2339164.title: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal confers SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026
2339164.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal confers SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026
Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh among the leading States recognised for their performance in implementing the Scheme
Assam, Sikkim , Mizoram , Tripura awarded among North-Eastern and Hilly States
Describing street vendors as ‘Street Wonders’, Shri Manohar Lal acknowledged their entrepreneurial spirit, resilience and ability to transform small livelihood activities into successful enterprises
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India, organised the SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 on 20 November 2026 at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The awards were conferred by Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, in the presence of Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, as Guest of Honour, to recognise the outstanding contributions of States/UTs, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Lending Institutions and partner organisations in strengthening street vendors’ livelihoods and advancing financial inclusion, digital adoption and social security under the PM SVANidhi Scheme.

Featuring 52 awards and 5 special recognitions, the awards celebrated excellence across States, cities, banks and other stakeholders. Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh were among the leading States recognised for their performance in implementing the Scheme and expanding its outreach. Cities and ULBs were also recognised for their contribution to effective grassroots implementation, improved outreach and digital adoption.

 

Among the Lending Institutions, State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank and Union Bank were recognised for their lending performance and contribution towards extending accessible formal credit to street vendors.

Since its launch in June 2020, PM SVANidhi has enabled around 81 lakh street vendors to access over 1.21 crore loans amounting to approximately ₹20,000 crore. Following the restructuring of the Scheme in August 2025, around 22 lakh loans worth ₹6,294 crore were disbursed to 10.6 lakh new beneficiaries in the first year. The Scheme has also expanded access to formal credit through an UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card, offering eligible beneficiaries who have repaid their second loan tranche a credit limit of up to ₹30,000.

Under SVANidhi se Samriddhi, socio-economic profiling of over 52 lakh beneficiary families has been completed, resulting in more than 1.62 crore sanctions under eight Central Government welfare schemes. The Scheme is also strengthening the street vending ecosystem through initiatives such as the development of 50 Street Food Hubs and capacity-building programmes, including food safety and hygiene training.

The awards covered the Scheme's implementation ecosystem across 35 States/UTs, over 4,900 ULBs and more than 120 Lending Institutions. The assessment was based on category-specific Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), using data primarily from the PM SVANidhi and SVANidhi se Samriddhi portals. Performance following the Scheme's restructuring was assessed for the period from 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2026, while overall performance was evaluated from the Scheme's inception up to 31 August 2026.

The SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 recognise the collective contributions of stakeholders towards strengthening the street vending ecosystem and improving the livelihoods of street vendors. These efforts will further promote inclusive urban development and contribute towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

 

Key Highlights from Addresses

Shri Manohar Lal emphasised that the vision of Antyodaya, leading towards Viksit Bharat @2047, can be realised by ensuring that the benefits of PM SVANidhi reach every eligible street vendor. He highlighted that the Scheme enables street vendors to progress from small loans to higher bank credit and expand their businesses, thereby promoting livelihood opportunities, financial inclusion and social security.

The Minister underscored that the success of PM SVANidhi is driven by the collective efforts of the Central and State Governments, banks and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). He noted that the SVANidhi Samman Awards recognise the contributions of States, cities, institutions and officials in translating the objectives of the Scheme into tangible outcomes at the grassroots level.

Describing street vendors as ‘Street Wonders’, Shri Manohar Lal acknowledged their entrepreneurial spirit, resilience and ability to transform small livelihood activities into successful enterprises.

Referring to the Scheme's song, “Har mehnatkash ka saath diya, PM SVANidhi ne samman diya”, the Minister highlighted how PM SVANidhi has extended support to hardworking street vendors while strengthening their dignity, recognition and respect in society.

 

MOS Shri Tokhan Sahu  Speech Highlights

Addressing the gathering, Minister of State Shri Tokhan Sahu emphasised that the transformation in the lives of the poor should be viewed through the collective impact of various Government welfare initiatives rather than through any single scheme. Referring to the World Bank’s October 2026 report, he highlighted that approximately 50 crore people in India have moved out of poverty, reflecting the impact of sustained and coordinated efforts towards inclusive development.

The Minister also highlighted Chhattisgarh’s achievement of receiving four awards, particularly appreciating the recognition of Dantewada and Bade Bacheli, erstwhile Naxal-affected areas. He noted that this achievement reflects the reach of the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the positive transformation taking place in regions progressing towards becoming Naxal-free.

2339157.title: Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Chairs Plenary Session of ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’
2339157.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Chairs Plenary Session of ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’
Calls For Whole-Of-Government Approach To Build An Inclusive, Accessible And Drug-Free India
Centre And States Identify Time-Bound Action Points On Drug Demand Reduction, Scholarships, Early Intervention And Accessibility; Summit Reinforces Collective Commitment Towards Viksit Bharat @2047
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi applauded the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for organizing the Departmental Summit and facilitating meaningful deliberations. The Prime Minister emphasized the importance of collective action and a ‘Whole of Government’ approach in achieving the objectives of social justice, social empowerment and a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

Addressing the plenary session of the two-day Departmental Summit titled ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’, at the Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, in the National Capital here on Thursday, Shri Modi highlighted the transformative impact of the Government’s welfare initiatives, he observed that nearly 50 crore people lifted out of poverty have experienced genuine social empowerment.

Calling for the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to be transformed into a nationwide Jan Andolan, the Prime Minister stressed that every citizen, family, educational institution and community must contribute to building a drug-free India.

Shri Modi encouraged schools to organize essay competitions and undertake awareness initiatives, while sensitizing parents to recognize early signs of substance abuse and addiction.

Emphasizing the importance of rehabilitation and social reintegration, the Prime Minister observed that the journeys of individuals who have successfully overcome substance dependence carry a powerful message of hope.

“These journeys carry the strongest message of hope. They show that recovery is possible and that a life free from drugs is a life of dignity,” he said.

The Prime Minister also urged farmers to shun illicit crop cultivation and called for coordinated efforts involving all Ministries, State Governments, district administrations and spiritual organizations to strengthen the national campaign against drug abuse.

Recognising the influence of spiritual leaders, the Prime Minister said that spiritual gurus and organisations have a vital role to play in the mission. Their guidance, he noted, can inspire millions to choose a life free from drugs.

On the empowerment of persons with disabilities, the Prime Minister highlighted the significance of the term ‘Divyang’, noting its contribution towards enhancing the dignity, respect and self-esteem of persons with disabilities.

Shri Modi encouraged its wider use and popularization to foster a positive outlook towards Divyangjan across society. He also emphasized the need to identify, nurture and recognize their inherent talents and abilities by providing appropriate opportunities and platforms for their participation and contribution.

The Prime Minister’s address reinforced the need for sustained cooperation between the Centre and States, institutional convergence and effective implementation of welfare programmes to ensure that the benefits of development reach every section of society.

The Summit was attended by Union Ministers for Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministers from 27 States and Union Territories, Secretaries of both Departments, Secretaries from 35 States and Union Territories, and senior officers of the Ministry and participating State/UT administrations, to deliberate on key priorities and strengthen collaborative efforts towards inclusive social development and empowerment.

Four thematic priorities deliberated at the Summit

The two-day Departmental Summit commenced on November 18, 2026, with the inaugural session addressed by Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar. Context-setting remarks were delivered by the Secretaries of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), outlining the policy priorities and implementation challenges relating to drug demand reduction, scholarships, early intervention and accessibility.

The first day featured four thematic deliberations focusing on Re-imagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction for Nasha Mukt Bharat; Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students; Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden; and Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat.

Four parallel breakout sessions provided a platform for Ministers and senior officials from States and Union Territories to exchange best practices, discuss implementation challenges and identify actionable measures with clearly defined timelines.

1. Re-imagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction for Nasha Mukt Bharat

The session, chaired by Dr. (Col.) Dhani Ram Shandil, Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Himachal Pradesh, and co-chaired by Shri Avinash Gehlot, Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Rajasthan, focused on transforming drug prevention and awareness efforts into a sustained Jan Andolan.

The key action points included observing the 10th of every month as Nasha Mukti Sankalp Diwas, beginning December 2026; making drug prevention a standing agenda item in every Gram Sabha and Municipal Ward; and establishing at least one de-addiction centre in every district by March 2029.

States shared several innovative initiatives, including Chandigarh’s VADA Clubs, Punjab’s SOORMA Ambassadors, Meghalaya’s DREAM Solace Home, Jammu and Kashmir’s 100 Days Campaign and Haryana’s STARS Rating for rehabilitation centres.

Dr. Shandil underscored the importance of structured and continuous interventions through families, schools and communities, observing that prevention is both sound public health policy and sound economics.

Shri Gehlot emphasised the need to move beyond government-led programmes towards community-driven participation.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma affirmed that the outcomes of the deliberations would inform the national action plan.

2. Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students

Chaired by Shri Asim Arun, Minister in the Government of Uttar Pradesh, and co-chaired by Shri Kishan Kumar Bedi, Minister in the Government of Haryana, the session focused on developing an integrated, accessible and student-centric scholarship delivery ecosystem.

The deliberations emphasized simplification of application procedures, secure digital integration between the Centre and States, assisted application facilities, timely disbursement of scholarships and strengthened grievance redressal mechanisms. Suggestions relating to revision of income eligibility criteria and scholarship amounts were also discussed.

States highlighted successful initiatives, including common scholarship platforms in Odisha, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh; Andhra Pradesh’s One Stop Scholarship Portal; prior scrutiny of applications in Madhya Pradesh; and auto-approval mechanisms adopted by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

The discussions underscored the importance of technology-enabled service delivery, intergovernmental coordination and transparent processes to ensure that eligible students receive scholarship assistance in a timely and hassle-free manner.

3. Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden

The session, chaired by Dr. Shweta Gupta, Minister in the Government of Bihar, and co-chaired by Ms. Pi Lalrinpuii, Minister in the Government of Mizoram, focused on strengthening early identification, timely assessment and intervention for children with developmental delays and disabilities.

The key priorities included strengthening convergence among health, nutrition, education and disability-related services; expanding tele-rehabilitation and mobile outreach facilities; developing integrated digital tracking systems; and enhancing the availability of trained human resources.

West Bengal presented its SANSPARSH model, which facilitates community-level screening for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) through a 20-point questionnaire.

Dr. Gupta highlighted that early identification and convergence of existing services are critical to reducing the burden of disability and ensuring that support reaches beneficiaries at the grassroots level.

Ms. Lalrinpuii emphasised the importance of parental awareness, continuous follow-up and shared responsibility among families, institutions and service providers.

4. Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat

The fourth thematic session focused on mainstreaming universal accessibility and inclusive design in public infrastructure, transport systems and digital services from the planning stage itself. The discussions highlighted the need for regular accessibility audits, effective monitoring mechanisms and active participation of persons with disabilities in the design and evaluation of public facilities.

States showcased several good practices, including Kochi Metro and Water Metro in Kerala, with Indian Sign Language-trained staff and accessible amenities; accessibility upgrades at Chennai Egmore and suburban railway stations in Tamil Nadu, including Braille-enabled lifts, tactile pathways and induction loops; accessible tourist spaces in Goa; level-boarding Ahmedabad Janmarg buses in Gujarat; and mandatory barrier-free infrastructure in schools in Assam.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma emphasised that accessibility is not an additional facility but the foundation of equal opportunities and a life of dignity, particularly in the context of the national vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Goa Minister Shri Subhash Faldessai advocated incorporating accessibility at the design and planning stage rather than relying on retrofitting.

Assam highlighted proposals for a dedicated National Mission, district-level monitoring and appropriate penalties for non-compliance with accessibility requirements.

Knowledge-sharing and exhibition of best practices

During the full-house sessions, experts Dr. Varsha Gathoo (formerly AYJNISHD) and Prof. J. S. Thakur (PGIMER) presented global best practices from the US, Australia, Switzerland, Iceland, Thailand, and the African Union alongside national policies.

An exhibition at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan showcased schemes, initiatives, success stories, digital applications and portals of both Departments, providing participants with an opportunity to understand innovative interventions and effective models of service delivery.

Renewed commitment to inclusive and empowered India

The deliberations culminated in a renewed commitment to strengthen Centre-State cooperation, institutional convergence and time-bound implementation of the agreed action points.

The Summit provided an important platform for translating policy priorities into coordinated action, leveraging successful State-level practices and addressing implementation gaps through collective responsibility.

With a shared focus on drug demand reduction, equitable access to educational opportunities, early intervention for persons with disabilities and universal accessibility, ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’ reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to building an inclusive, empowered, accessible and drug-free India in keeping with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

2339042.title: Strengthening Educational Opportunities for OBC Students through Dedicated Hostel Infrastructure
2339042.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strengthening Educational Opportunities for OBC Students through Dedicated Hostel Infrastructure
Ministry-Supported 150-Seat OBC Hostel at Alagapur, North Tripura, to Strengthen Access to Safe Residential Facilities and Quality Education
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 3:52PM by PIB Delhi

Access to safe and affordable accommodation plays an important role in enabling students, particularly those from rural and socially and economically weaker backgrounds, to continue their education. The proposed hostel seeks to address accommodation-related challenges by providing essential boarding facilities and a healthy environment conducive to learning, personal development and academic advancement.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, has initiated the establishment of a 150-seat hostel for students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community at Alagapur Gram Panchayat in North Tripura. The initiative aims to strengthen educational opportunities by providing suitable residential infrastructure and creating a supportive environment for students to pursue their academic aspirations.

Starting during the financial year 2025–26, the hostel project has a planned accommodation capacity of 150 students. Once completed and operational, the hostel is expected to provide accommodation for up to 150 eligible OBC students and contribute to improved access to educational opportunities in North Tripura. This will also provide them facility of a structured and supportive living environment.

The project is being implemented by the Rural Development Department, Government of Tripura, on behalf of the OBC Welfare Department, with funding support from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. This collaborative initiative reflects the importance of Centre-State coordination in expanding educational infrastructure and promoting inclusive socio-economic development.

The proposed hostel will provide essential amenities, including electricity, proper sanitation and hygiene facilities, safe drinking water and adequate security arrangements. These facilities are intended to ensure a safe, healthy and supportive residential environment, allowing students to concentrate on their educational pursuits.

Beyond residential accommodation, the hostel is envisaged as a space for nurturing academic excellence, leadership qualities and skill development among OBC students. The initiative also seeks to encourage participation in refresher programmes and skill-orientation courses, helping students develop competencies that can support their future educational and professional aspirations.

The initiative reflects the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s continued commitment towards inclusive education, equitable access to opportunities and the development of supportive educational infrastructure for disadvantaged communities, contributing to the broader vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

2339017.title: Hon’ble Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Flags Off ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ from New Delhi
2339017.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Hon’ble Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Flags Off ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ from New Delhi
Over 1,100 students embark on a special train journey to Somnath under Somnath Swabhiman Parv
More than 35,000 devotees have visited Somnath under the initiative
Yatra to connect young people with India's historical and spiritual legacy
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 3:26PM by PIB Delhi

The ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’, organised under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv, was flagged off by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat from Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi. More than 1,100 students from various colleges and institutions have embarked on this special train journey to Somnath, Gujarat.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that despite repeated attacks over a thousand years, the Somnath Temple continues to stand as a symbol of India's enduring cultural heritage. He highlighted how earlier generations protected not only their faith but also the country's rich traditions and heritage. He said that the history of Somnath reflects India's faith, resilience and cultural continuity.

Addressing the young participants, the Minister said that this is not an ordinary journey but an opportunity to understand India's history of struggle and resilience, and to carry forward its glorious legacy. He encouraged the students to take pride in India's intellectual wealth, architectural heritage and cultural achievements, which have influenced the world and continue to do so.

Under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv, more than 35,000 devotees have so far had the opportunity to visit Somnath Mahadev. The initiative highlights the historical and cultural significance of the Somnath Temple and its enduring place in India's heritage.

Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Shri Samar Nanda said, “Under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv, devotees from 17 states have visited Somnath Mahadev. The 75th anniversary of the reconstruction of the Somnath Temple was also commemorated on 11 May 2026 in the presence of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The Yuva Somnath Yatra is an important initiative to connect the younger generation with Somnath and its rich historical and spiritual significance.”

Before the departure of the train, Sadho Band presented devotional musical performances at the railway station, creating a spiritual and enthusiastic atmosphere. The devotional performances filled the young participants with enthusiasm and added to the spirit of the occasion.

A ceremonial Guard of Honour was also presented by NCC women cadets, adding to the significance of the occasion.

The initiative aims to connect the younger generation with India's rich cultural heritage and historical legacy, while creating greater awareness about the historical significance of Somnath.

Scheduled from 20 to 25 November 2026, the special train will travel from Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi, to Veraval Junction in Gujarat. From there, the students will proceed to Somnath to experience the historical and spiritual significance of the revered temple.

2339014.title: Secretary, DoUD, MoHUA chairs 11th meeting of CSMC under PMAY-U 2.0
2339014.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Secretary, DoUD, MoHUA chairs 11th meeting of CSMC under PMAY-U 2.0
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 3:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India has sanctioned 1.75 lakh houses under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) and an additional in-principle approval for 1.5 lakh houses was also given during the 11th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), held under the chairmanship of Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) on 19th November 2026.

Shri Kumar Ravikant Singh, Joint Secretary and Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All (HFA); Shri Sanjeet, Joint Secretary and Financial Advisor (JS&FA); Shri Vaibhav Rundwal, Director (HFA), officials from the Ministry; and Mission Directors, representatives from States/UTs were among those present in the meeting.

1.75 lakh houses have been approved in Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals of PMAY-U 2.0 in States/UTs of Assam (4,841), Goa (06), Gujarat (5,793), Madhya Pradesh (10,913), Maharashtra (19,778), Odisha (2,681), Puducherry (937), Rajasthan (4,572), Tamil Nadu (14,350), Uttar Pradesh (1,01,493) and West Bengal (10,159). Furthermore, in-principle approval has been given for 1,27,349 houses in State of Andhra Pradesh and 22,484 houses in State of Maharashtra, subject to submission of necessary compliance and adherence to Scheme Guidelines by the respective States. This takes the total count of houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0 to more than 24.15 lakh. The latest approval marks another significant step towards expanding access to pucca houses for eligible urban families, particularly those belonging to the Economically Weaker Section (EWS).

Secretary, DoUD directed States/UTs to accelerate expenditure and ensure optimal utilisation of sanctioned funds, along with ensuring timely release of funds to beneficiaries and implementing agencies for seamless implementation of scheme. He further mentioned about strengthening monitoring, geo-tagging of houses and complete verification of all pending applications within stipulated timelines.

Promoting inclusive and equitable housing, the scheme places women empowerment at its core while also prioritising housing needs of vulnerable sections of society.

A beneficiary family from Gujarat outside their house constructed under PMAY-U 2.0

Meanwhile in the meeting, States/UTs were also advised to formulate comprehensive Affordable Housing Policies and undertake mandatory reforms to create an enabling ecosystem for affordable housing.

PMAY-U 2.0, launched in September 2024, aims to support 1 crore additional eligible EWS/Low Income Group (LIG) and Middle Income Group (MIG) families in constructing or purchasing pucca houses through different verticals. Moreover, the scheme also caters to rental housing needs of urban migrants/working women/urban poor by providing affordable and dignified rental accommodation in cities.

Together under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, 1.29 crore houses have been sanctioned while 1.01 crore houses have been completed.

2339007.title: A new recipe to shape magnetisation that could open new doors to storing quantum information
2339007.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
A new recipe to shape magnetisation that could open new doors to storing quantum information
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi

Scientists have cracked a way to tune an exotic form of quantum magnetism in a network by changing the connectivity of the network. This may have applications in quantum devices, for example, in storing quantum information.

Many systems are composed of interacting objects, and that can range from gas in the room to social networks. The hub-and-spoke diagrams showing flight routes in aeroplane magazines illustrate how connectivity allows people to move across cities. Another relatable example is that of superspreaders during COVID, who acted as hubs in spreading the disease.

These are familiar instances that show how different patterns of connections can determine collective behaviour. But these are all classical systems.

A team from the Raman Research Institute (RRI), an Autonomous Institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), explored what happens when many quantum objects interact with each other, what sets the collective ordering and how the quantum units organise themselves. 

To understand the system, Revathy B. S., the lead author of the new study and a postdoctoral fellow at RRI, and Shovan Dutta, co-author and assistant professor in the Theoretical Physics group at RRI, pictured a square lattice with one vacant site (hole) and all other sites occupied by one electron.

Fig 1: The top row shows the possible magnetic ordering of a many-body quantum system within a single square lattice. The bottom shows that the introduction of a diagonal in the square lattice yield

The electrons have an intrinsic property called spin, which can point up or down. The hole can hop from one site to another, and this motion of the hole can influence how the electron spins arrange themselves, giving rise to what scientists’ call “kinetic magnetism”. Unlike conventional magnetism which arises from direct interactions between the spins, kinetic magnetism arises from the quantum motion (kinetic energy) of particles. Kinetic magnetism is a true quantum-mechanical effect with no classical counterpart.

If all the spins point along the same direction, it is called ferromagnetic order, and if adjacent spins have opposite directions, it is called antiferromagnetic ordering. For a square lattice with one hole, it has been shown before that the lowest-energy state is ferromagnetic.

Revathy and Dutta showed that the magnetic ordering can be varied by the connectivity of the network. For example, introducing a diagonal bond in the square lattice makes the spins of the two electrons involved antiparallel, creating a quantum-mechanically anti-aligned pair of spins, called a “singlet”. The remaining sites retain the ferromagnetic ordering, and the hole keeps hopping across the network.

“What’s amazing is that I can almost deterministically predict that wherever I [introduce a diagonal bond], I will get [singlets],” said Revathy. By introducing a diagonal bond and changing the connectivity locally, they could engineer the global magnetic order. These findings demonstrate that collective quantum order can be shaped by geometry alone.

Fig 2: Global magnetic order can not only be determined in a quantum many-body system, but also engineered

“This is far from obvious, because if you had a classical system, similar changes in geometry do not really affect the magnetic order,” said Dutta.

The computational complexity involved prevented physicists from tackling the problem for decades. A lattice with 20 sites yields a mind-boggling two million configurations. Revathy and Dutta used a combination of advanced numerical and analytical approaches to uncover these microscopic patterns and their physical origin.

The research published in Physical Review B is also particularly timely because experimental advances are reaching a stage where researchers can possibly observe the complex theory in action.

Although this work is theoretical, it opens new avenues for shaping quantum states of interacting particles, which may have applications in quantum devices. Our familiar hard drives, for example, use magnetic patterns to store information, but only as classical bits. The singlets in these networks are entangled quantum states and may be used to store quantum information.

Publication Link: https://doi.org/10.1103/stj9-srp1

2339006.title: Pollen from wetland of Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve regenerative capacity of tropical forest ecosystems
2339006.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Pollen from wetland of Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve regenerative capacity of tropical forest ecosystems
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 3:13PM by PIB Delhi

A new study carried out at Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve shows that in 2700- and 2300-years BP, the region experienced a strong Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM), while between 2300- and 1600-years BP, it underwent multiple climatic phases, including periods of high humidity and prolonged drought significantly influencing the composition, structure, distribution of forest vegetation and shifts in regional landscape through time.

This was followed by stable monsoon and increasing evidence of human activity between 1600 and 820 years BP and strengthening of monsoons during the last 400 years resulting in recovery of forests.

This indicated the resilience and regenerative capacity of tropical forest ecosystems that populated the region, under favourable climatic conditions.

Understanding the long-term variability of the ISM is essential because it is a key driver of India's climate, ecosystems, and water resources. As Indian agriculture is highly dependent on monsoon rainfall, even small changes in monsoon intensity or timing can affect crop productivity, food security, and the national economy. Reconstructing past climate and vegetation changes provides valuable long-term insights into natural monsoon variability and ecosystem responses.

However, there is a lack of high-resolution Late Holocene palaeoclimate records from the Core Monsoon Zone (CMZ) of central India.

Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), an Autonomous Institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), used pollen-based records from Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve in central India's Core Monsoon Zone and integrated them with the Earth System Paleoclimate Simulation (ESPS) model to reconstruct vegetation and Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) variability over the past ~2700 years.

Fig 1: Three-dimensional (3D) elevation model of the Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve, located in the Core Monsoon Zone, Madhya Pradesh, India.

This combination allowed researchers to reconstruct historical Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) patterns for the past 3000 years, correlating climate changes with significant events in Indian history.

Dr. Anjali Trivedi, along with Anupam Nag and Prof. M. G. Thakkar from BSIP) studied sediment core from the Chakradhara Wetland of Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve, located in Umaria district of Northeastern Madhya Pradesh, India, segmented the core and prepared samples for radio carbon dating and pollen analysis.

They also generated Earth System Palaeoclimate Simulation (ESPS) models to reconstruct climatic conditions over the past three millennia. These models were then used to compare the pollen dataset, ensuring the authenticity and reliability of the research findings.

They found that between approximately 2700- and 2300-years BP, a strengthened Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) supported widespread dense moist deciduous forests dominated by Sal (Shorea robusta). Its proliferation indicates sustained rainfall of around 1100–1200 mm or more annually, along with a timely monsoon onset.

Fig 2: Digital elevation model (DEM) of the Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve showing the location of the study site in the Core Monsoon Zone, Madhya Pradesh, India.

 

Between around 2300- and 1600-years BP, the region experienced multiple climatic phases, including periods of high humidity, prolonged drought, gradual environmental recovery, and a subsequent strengthening of the Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM). These climatic fluctuations significantly influenced the composition, structure, and distribution of forest vegetation, resulting in shifts in the regional landscape through time.

The period 1600 and 820 years BP saw relatively stable monsoon conditions supported dense tropical forests. From 820 to 400 years BP, weakening of the ISM led to reduced moist deciduous forests and expansion of dry deciduous vegetation, accompanied by increasing Cerealia and other cultivated pollen, indicating growing agricultural activity, land-use change and human influence.

Over the past ~400 years, strengthening monsoon conditions promoted the recovery and expansion of moist deciduous forests, demonstrating the resilience and regenerative capacity of tropical forest ecosystems under favourable climatic conditions.

The findings published in Quaternary Research can improve our understanding of climate–environment interactions and can contribute to better climate adaptation strategies, sustainable agriculture, and future climate resilience.

Publication link: https://doi.org/10.1017/qua.2026.10093

2338981.title: Vice President calls for strengthening constitutional values through responsible citizenship; says duties are as important as rights
2338981.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice President calls for strengthening constitutional values through responsible citizenship; says duties are as important as rights
Constitution is much more than a legal document; it is the moral compass of our Republic: Vice President
Achievements under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi translate constitutional aspirations into tangible outcomes in people’s lives: Vice President
Technology must serve humanity and remain guided by constitutional values: Vice President
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurates the 5th Edition of Constitution Week 2026 organised by Bennett University’s School of Law in New Delhi.
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the 5th Edition of Constitution Week Celebrations 2026, organised by the School of Law, Bennett University, at the Constitution Club of India, New Delhi.

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the 5th Edition of Constitution Week 2026, organised by the School of Law, Bennett University, at the Constitution Club of India, New Delhi. Addressing the gathering, he said that the Constitution is much more than a legal document; it is the moral compass of our Republic. He emphasised that constitutional values must become part of everyday public life and that duties are as important as rights. Highlighting India’s achievements over the last decade, he described them as a silent revolution, translating constitutional aspirations into tangible improvements in people’s lives. Union Minister Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal; Attorney General for India, Shri R. Venkataramani; Chancellor, Bennett University and MD, Times Group, Shri Vineet Jain; and Vice-Chancellor, Bennett University, Dr. Raj Singh, and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 20, 2026

Addressing the gathering, the Vice President said that the Constitution of India is much more than a legal document; it is the moral compass of the Republic. He said that constitutional values must not remain confined to institutions and legal texts but must become an integral part of everyday public life. He observed that democracy flourishes when institutions remain accountable, dissent is respected, and citizens exercise their rights and duties responsibly. He stressed that duties deserve as much importance as rights, observing that responsible discharge of duties is essential to safeguarding the rights of all citizens.

Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled Dr. B. R. Ambedkar’s definition of democracy as a form of government through which revolutionary changes in the economic and social life of people are brought about without bloodshed. He said that India’s achievements over the last decade reflect the realisation of constitutional aspirations through tangible improvements in people’s lives. Citing the lifting of around 50 crore people out of poverty, the construction of four crore pucca houses for the poor, and rural tap water coverage crossing 82 per cent under the Jal Jeevan Mission, he said that even border villages, once at the lowest rung of development, are now emerging as vibrant villages. He observed that these achievements represent a silent revolution made possible under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Highlighting women’s participation in nation-building, the Vice-President recalled the valuable contributions of the 15 women members of the Constituent Assembly. He noted that their vision is being carried forward through initiatives such as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam. He also expressed happiness at witnessing the growing participation of women and their achievements across the country. Describing this progress as another revolution, he said India is steadily moving from women’s development to women-led development, with women becoming active participants in shaping the nation’s destiny.

Speaking about the dynamism of the Constitution, Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan cited Article 21, which has evolved over the years to encompass a wide range of rights relating to dignity, livelihood, health, shelter, privacy, education and environmental protection.He called for a balanced approach towards development and environmental conservation, emphasising that natural resources must be utilised to improve living standards while ensuring their sustainability for future generations. He cautioned against mindless consumerism and stressed the need for responsible consumption. He called for greater public awareness about sustainable lifestyles.

The Vice President said that India’s constitutional jurisprudence has made significant contributions to global environmental thought by recognising environmental protection as an integral part of sustainable development. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s initiative, Mission LiFE, he said it inspires individuals and communities across the world to adopt environmentally responsible lifestyles. 

Referring to India’s progress in digital public infrastructure, artificial intelligence and technological innovation, the Vice President underscored that technology must serve humanity and remain guided by constitutional values. Innovation, he said, should empower citizens, strengthen transparency and expand access to opportunities.He highlighted the important role of universities and institutions of higher learning in this journey, observing that legal education must go beyond professional competence. He said that it should cultivate constitutional sensitivity, ethical leadership, critical thinking and a deeper understanding of social realities.

Shri C.P.Radhakrishnan urged the students to become informed and responsible citizens who engage in reasoned dialogue and contribute constructively to democratic institutions. As India moves towards Viksit Bharat @2047, he said, constitutional values must remain the foundation of the nation’s progress.He concluded by calling upon everyone to strengthen the Constitution through the values they practise and the responsibilities they discharge.

Union Minister of State for Law and Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal; Attorney General for India, Shri R. Venkataramani; Chancellor, Bennett University and Managing Director, Times Group, Shri Vineet Jain; and Vice-Chancellor, Bennett University, Dr. Raj Singh, were among the dignitaries present on the occasion.

2338974.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES 12TH CONVOCATION OF ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES AND DR RAM MANOHAR LOHIA HOSPITAL
2338974.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES 12TH CONVOCATION OF ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES AND DR RAM MANOHAR LOHIA HOSPITAL
COLLABORATION AMONG HUMAN MEDICINE, VETERINARY MEDICINE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE IS ESSENTIAL FOR ACHIEVING THE GOAL OF ONE HEALTH: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 2:21PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu graced the 12th convocation of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences and Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in New Delhi today (November 20, 2026).

 

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that today the concept of 'One Health' is of paramount importance in the field of global health. Due to the constant contact between humans, animals, plants, and the environment, a health issue arising in one domain can affect others as well. Many infectious diseases spread from animals to humans, while air and water pollution, climate change, and environmental imbalances also pose serious challenges to human health. It is, therefore, essential to work in collaboration with experts from the fields of human medicine, veterinary medicine, and environmental science. This integrated approach will not only facilitate disease prevention and timely detection but also enhance our preparedness to address future health crises.

 

The President said that understanding the social, economic, nutritional, and environmental conditions is crucial for the prevention and treatment of diseases, as these factors have a direct impact on human health. Research into treatment and preventive measures tailored to local health challenges and circumstances should be encouraged.

 

The President said that, in assessing the evolving health needs, the Government of India has revised the Health Policy in 2017. Within this comprehensive and inclusive Health Policy, greater emphasis was placed on preventive and promotive services, alongside curative solutions. The focus on rehabilitative and palliative care was also strengthened.  In view of the rapid rise of non-communicable diseases such as mental stress, diabetes, and cancer, special emphasis is being placed on various aspects related to their prevention.

 

President said that the initiatives undertaken by the Government of India in the health sector over the past decade are yielding far-reaching effects. These have led to a significant expansion of healthcare services, spanning from primary to tertiary levels.

The President told graduating doctors that through their research and efforts, healthcare services can become more effective, accessible, affordable, and people-centric. She underlined that their expertise should also benefit marginalized communities in remote areas, as well as the country’s primary healthcare services. Their thinking and actions should be such that the benefits of their skills can reach the underprivileged sections of society.

2338972.title: ‘Stories Without Borders’: IFFI 57 to celebrate cinema beyond geographical and socio-cultural boundaries
2338972.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
‘Stories Without Borders’: IFFI 57 to celebrate cinema beyond geographical and socio-cultural boundaries
Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker outlines vision for the 57th edition; urges media to explore diverse cinematic sections and showcase the festival’s global appeal
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 2:09PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 20 November 2026

 

A media briefing was held today at the PIB Media Centre, Panaji, Goa on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). The session brought together Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director, IFFI 57, and Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC). It was moderated by Smt. Smita Vats Sharma, Director General (West), Press Information Bureau (PIB).

Addressing the media, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker outlined his vision for the 57th edition of IFFI, centred on the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’. He explained that the theme extends beyond geographical and territorial boundaries to explore divisions within families and societies, including those arising from caste, social differences and other socio-cultural realities. The festival seeks to bring together stories that transcend such boundaries and reflect shared human experiences across cultures.

Highlighting the festival's diverse cinematic offerings, Shri Gowariker announced the introduction of three new sections this year i.e. Animation, Documentary and Films about Films. He underscored the growing significance of documentaries and the need to provide greater visibility and opportunities to documentary filmmakers. As part of this initiative, IFFI will host a special gala presentation featuring films by winners of the recently concluded Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF).

Emphasising the significance of the festival's varied programming, he noted that every section, including retrospectives, curated showcases and special screenings, contributes to presenting the richness and diversity of cinema. He encouraged media professionals to explore the festival beyond their individual film preferences and attend gala screenings, red-carpet events, international press conferences and Panorama interactions. Such engagements, he observed, offer filmmakers and visiting delegates an opportunity to present their work while enabling audiences to discover diverse cinematic perspectives.

Underscoring the role of media in amplifying the festival's reach, Shri Gowariker urged media representatives to watch and cover films across different sections, including retrospectives, while retaining their independent judgement and critical perspectives. He emphasised that media engagement plays an important role in taking the stories and cinematic offerings of IFFI to audiences across the country.

He also expressed his willingness to facilitate meaningful and informal interactions between the festival team and media representatives throughout the event. Noting the professional commitments of media personnel, he said that the scheduling of interactions had been adjusted to provide greater flexibility and adequate time for coverage of festival activities.

During the briefing, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker also unveiled the official brochure of the 57th International Film Festival of India.

The media interaction provided an overview of the festival's vision and programming priorities, while highlighting the importance of media engagement and collective efforts in strengthening IFFI as an international platform for cinema and cross-cultural exchange.

2338970.title: From Creative Ideas to Global Opportunities: WAVES Film Bazaar 2026 Begins in Goa
2338970.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
From Creative Ideas to Global Opportunities: WAVES Film Bazaar 2026 Begins in Goa
Two decades of connecting filmmakers, nurturing stories and fostering international partnerships
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 2:03PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 20 November 2026

 

The 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar was inaugurated today at Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon, Goa, marking two decades of fostering connections between Indian and international film industries. Organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), under the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, the five-day marketplace brings together filmmakers, producers, writers, investors, distributors and other industry professionals to explore collaborations and take creative projects towards global markets.

In the keynote address during the inauguration, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, highlighted the remarkable growth of Film Bazaar from 204 delegates representing 18 countries in 2007 to more than 2,500 delegates in recent editions. He described WAVES Film Bazaar as a platform that transforms creative conception into commercial opportunities.

Referring to the vision of ‘Create in India, Create for the World’, articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at WAVES 2025, he emphasised the importance of providing Indian creative talent with greater access to international markets and opportunities. He described Film Bazaar as a platform for collaboration and discovery, inviting filmmakers from across the world to make full use of the marketplace, where stories can evolve into partnerships and creativity can generate enduring economic and cultural value.

Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting

Addressing the gathering as Guest of Honour, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director highlighted the unique role of Film Bazaar in bringing Indian filmmakers and international industry professionals together.

Emphasising that the platform engages with filmmakers at every stage of their creative journey, he said WAVES Film Bazaar does not wait for a film to be completed but meets filmmakers wherever they are in the process. Whether a filmmaker has an unfinished script or a completed film seeking an audience, the marketplace brings together people who can help take the project forward. He described how a simple conversation, often beginning with an invitation to have coffee, could open doors to meaningful collaborations.

Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director

Highlighting the transformative power of cinema, he observed that enabling people to see things differently was a gift. He urged delegates to make the most of the four days, interact with strangers, share their ideas, particularly unfinished projects, and pursue opportunities with the hope of finding a ‘yes’.

Welcoming the gathering, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director NFDC described Film Bazaar as an integral part of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI), noting that the platform had maintained this association over the past two decades. He observed that Film Bazaar had grown into a much bigger and wider platform, expanding its scope and opportunities for the film industry.

From right- Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, MIB, G Krishnakumar, Chairman, NFDC, Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, MIB, Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director NFDC

Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, delivered the vote of thanks. The inaugural ceremony was also attended by G Krishnakumar, Chairman, NFDC.

As WAVES Film Bazaar marks two decades, its role extends beyond bringing the film industry together to creating possibilities for stories to travel further. By connecting filmmakers with producers, writers, investors and distributors from across the world, the marketplace seeks to ensure that promising ideas find the right collaborators and that diverse Indian stories have opportunities to reach international audiences. The emphasis remains on creating a space where conversations lead to collaborations and creative possibilities find their way to the screen.

2338963.title: Union Health Ministry’s Health Pavilion at IITF 2026 Records Over 12,189 Stall Visits in First Five Days, Promoting Health Awareness and Preventive Healthcare
2338963.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2338963.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry’s Health Pavilion at IITF 2026 Records Over 12,189 Stall Visits in First Five Days, Promoting Health Awareness and Preventive Healthcare
39 Stalls Representing 24 National Health Programmes and Participating Organisations Offer Free Health Screenings, Medical Consultations, Counselling and Diagnostic Services
Themed ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’, the Pavilion Features Interactive Health Awareness Activities, Cultural Performances, Doctors’ Talk Shows and Live CPR Demonstrations
Dedicated Kids’ Zone Encourages Screen-Free Engagement, Physical Activity and Learning Through Traditional Games and Play
Health Pavilion at Bharat Mandapam to Remain Open for Public Until 27th November 2026
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 1:53PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is witnessing encouraging public participation at its Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, being organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 14th to 27th November 2026. The Pavilion has recorded over 12,189 cumulative stall visits during the first five days (14th –18th November 2026), reflecting strong public interest in healthcare awareness, preventive screening and information about various healthcare initiatives of the Government.

The Health Pavilion was inaugurated on 14th November 2026 by Dr. M. Srinivas, Member, NITI Aayog, in the presence of the Union Health Secretary, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava. Themed ‘युवा भारत, स्वस्थ भारत’, the Pavilion has emerged as an important platform for public engagement, health education and dissemination of information on Government healthcare programmes and services. Visitors, including children, youth, families and other sections of society, are actively participating in the activities being organised across the Pavilion.

Interactive Activities and Cultural Performances Promote Health Awareness

As part of the ongoing public outreach initiatives, Nukkad Natak performances are being organised under the ‘TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan’, alongside awareness activities on vector-borne diseases and filariasis. These performances aim to sensitise visitors about tuberculosis, its symptoms, modes of transmission, prevention, early diagnosis and timely treatment.

Magic shows are also being organised to communicate important health messages through innovative and engaging presentations. Doctors’ talk shows and health awareness sessions provide visitors with opportunities to interact with medical professionals, understand common health concerns and seek guidance on preventive measures and healthy lifestyle practices.

Live Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) demonstrations, interactive quizzes and other stage activities are further familiarising visitors with essential health practices, emergency response techniques and disease prevention. These activities are transforming the Pavilion into an interactive learning space, promoting health awareness through information, demonstration and public participation.

 

Free Health Screening, Medical Consultations and Counselling Services

Spread across an area of 989 square metres in Hall No. 4(G), Ground Floor, Bharat Mandapam, the Health Pavilion brings together 39 stalls representing 24 National Health Programmes, Programme Divisions and participating organisations.

Visitors are being provided access to a wide range of healthcare services, basic health screenings, medical consultations, counselling and information, free of cost. These include BMI assessment, blood sugar testing, blood pressure measurement, routine eye check-ups, oral health screening, hearing assessments and blood grouping services.

The Pavilion also provides information on maternal and child healthcare, immunisation, the U-WIN digital vaccination platform and services under the Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram. Visitors can access awareness and counselling on HIV/AIDS, sexually transmitted infections, tuberculosis, vector-borne diseases, viral hepatitis, leprosy and other public health concerns.

Digital healthcare initiatives, including eSanjeevani teleconsultation services, Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), are also being showcased to familiarise visitors with the availability and benefits of Government healthcare services.

Mental health awareness and counselling services, including information on Tele-MANAS, are being provided alongside specialised services related to eye and vision care, hearing, dental health and organ donation awareness. Visitors are also receiving guidance on nutrition, physical activity, tobacco cessation, food safety and other healthy lifestyle practices.

Representatives of participating organisations and programme divisions are facilitating direct interaction with visitors, helping them understand the healthcare services, benefits and support mechanisms available under various Government initiatives.

Dedicated Kids’ Zone Encourages Healthy Habits Through Play

A dedicated Kids’ Zone has been set up to provide children with opportunities to participate in traditional games and recreational activities. With an emphasis on screen-free engagement, the zone encourages physical activity, social interaction and learning through play. The initiative aims to familiarise children with the importance of healthy habits while offering an engaging and enjoyable experience for families visiting the Pavilion.

The Health Pavilion will continue to host a range of interactive activities, health screening facilities, awareness sessions and public engagement initiatives throughout IITF 2026, which concludes on 27th November 2026.

2338955.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Organises Mega Camp Under Digital Life Certificate Campaign 5.0 in New Delhi
250 Pensioners submitted their Life Certificate through Jeevan Pramaan App
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways organised a Mega Camp under Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 5.0 on 19th November 2026 in New Delhi. The camp was organised jointly by Northern Railway Headquarters and Delhi Division to facilitate pensioners in submitting their Digital Life Certificates conveniently through the Jeevan Pramaan App using face authentication.

Over 250 pensioners participated in the Mega Camp and registered themselves for submission of their Digital Life Certificates. A total of 58 Digital Life Certificates were generated on the spot through face authentication using the Jeevan Pramaan App.

Railway staff and representatives of participating banks assisted pensioners throughout the process to ensure smooth and convenient submission of their Digital Life Certificates. Teams from 12 banks participated in the camp. UIDAI officials were also present at the camp to assist pensioners with Aadhaar verification and updation. In addition, a health camp was organised for the participating pensioners as part of the initiative.

Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW), Shri Harsh Khare, AGM, Northern Railway, Smt. Rekha Yadav, PED/IR, Railway Board, Shri Sujit Kumar Mishra, PCPO, Northern Railway, and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

The Mega Camp reflects Indian Railways' continued efforts to facilitate pensioners through digital services and ensure easy access to essential pension-related facilities.

2338943.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported transportation of the dead bodies of a woman and her daughter in a garbage vehicle for post-mortem after hospital staff failed to provide a hearse in Faridabad, Haryana
2338943.body_html:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported transportation of the dead bodies of a woman and her daughter in a garbage vehicle for post-mortem after hospital staff failed to provide a hearse in Faridabad, Haryana
The Commission reiterates right to life, fair treatment and dignity under Article 21 also extends to the dead; reaffirms its 2021 Advisory on their respectful treatment
Issues notices to the Secretary, Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Haryana and District Magistrate, Faridabad, calling for detailed reports on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 1:31PM by PIB Delhi

 

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that the dead bodies of a woman and her daughter were carried in a garbage vehicle from a hospital to the mortuary of Civil Hospital, Ballabhgarh in Haryana for post-mortem examination. They had succumbed to their injuries caused in a road accident in the Ballabhgarh area of Faridabad on 14th November 2026. Reportedly, the hospital staff failed to provide their family members with a hearse to carry the bodies.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. The right to life and human dignity under Article 21 of the Constitution of India extends to the deceased, requiring authorities and institutions to treat dead bodies with respect. The Commission also issued an Advisory in this regard on 14th May 2021 to all States and Union Territories for compliance. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Secretary, Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of Haryana and District Magistrate, Faridabad, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

According to the media report, carried on 17th November 2026, the woman, who worked at the Nawada garbage dumping yard of the Municipal Corporation, was returning home with her husband and daughter on a motorcycle when they met with an accident on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway.

2338934.title: President Droupadi Murmu Addresses 12th Convocation of ABVIMS and Dr. RML Hospital in Presence of Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda
2338934.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2338934.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
President Droupadi Murmu Addresses 12th Convocation of ABVIMS and Dr. RML Hospital in Presence of Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda
President Urges Young Doctors to Uphold Medical Ethics and Place Compassion, Sensitivity and Service to Humanity at the Heart of Healthcare
President Highlights India's Remarkable Progress in Healthcare Delivery, Medical Education and Expansion of Healthcare Infrastructure
Medical Education Is Both a Privilege and a Profound Responsibility Towards Society: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda
Union Health Minister Highlights ₹15,000 Crore Government Initiative to Add 10,000 Medical Seats, Strengthening India's Healthcare Workforce
324 Medical Graduates Awarded Degrees Across Undergraduate, Postgraduate and Super-Specialty Disciplines; 58 Gold Medals Conferred for Academic Excellence
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 1:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) and Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi, celebrated its 12th Convocation Ceremony today at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, addressed the gathering on the occasion in the presence of Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri J.P. Nadda.

The convocation ceremony marked an important milestone in the academic journey of the graduating students, recognising their dedication, perseverance and commitment to the medical profession.

Addressing the gathering, the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, congratulated the graduating students and appreciated the significant representation of female graduates, observing that the achievements of the daughters reflected the growing participation of women in medical education and the healthcare sector. She highlighted the important role played by Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital in providing extensive clinical exposure to medical students. Referring to the hospital's patient footfall, she noted that more than 19 lakh patients availed its OPD services in 2025, providing students with valuable hands-on experience and strengthening their clinical knowledge and confidence.

Highlighting India's transformation in healthcare over the past decade, the President observed that sustained government initiatives had strengthened healthcare delivery from the grassroots to advanced tertiary care. She noted that approximately 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were operational across the country, expanding access to primary healthcare services. She also highlighted the expansion of tertiary healthcare and medical education beyond metropolitan cities into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, enabling people, particularly those from rural and underserved communities, to access specialised healthcare services closer to their homes. She emphasised the importance of telemedicine in bridging geographical barriers and ensuring that quality medical consultations reach people in remote areas.

The President highlighted the shift in India's healthcare approach towards preventive and promotive healthcare, in line with the National Health Policy, 2017. She emphasised the growing importance of early screening, detection and management of non-communicable diseases, including diabetes, mental health conditions and various forms of cancer. She observed that large-scale screening initiatives undertaken across the country were essential to identifying health conditions at an early stage and ensuring timely treatment, particularly among vulnerable populations.

Referring to the Government's initiatives towards strengthening financial protection in healthcare, the President highlighted the role of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), which provides health coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year, helping reduce the financial burden of hospitalisation and improving access to quality healthcare for economically vulnerable families. She also highlighted the Ayushman Vaya Vandana Yojana, which extends the benefit of ₹5 lakh health coverage to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their socio-economic status.

The President also underscored the importance of integrating traditional systems of medicine with modern healthcare. She noted that efforts to promote Ayurveda and Yoga, alongside modern medical practices, had strengthened the country's holistic approach to health and well-being. She highlighted the co-location of Ayush services in government healthcare institutions and the growing emphasis on collaborative research. She also referred to international cooperation through the Ministry of Ayush and the World Health Organization's Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in advancing research and promoting evidence-based traditional healthcare practices.

Addressing the graduating medical professionals, the President urged them to uphold the highest standards of professional ethics, sensitivity and compassion in their careers. She emphasised that access to quality healthcare must not remain limited to urban centres and privileged sections of society, and called upon the doctors to extend their services to people living in remote and underserved areas. She encouraged the graduates to contribute not only to clinical care but also to medical research, innovation and the development of solutions suited to India's specific socio-economic, nutritional and environmental conditions.

The President further emphasised the transformative potential of emerging technologies, particularly Artificial Intelligence, in improving the accessibility, affordability and efficiency of healthcare delivery. Drawing lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, she called upon medical professionals to remain adaptable and embrace technological advancements while ensuring that healthcare remains people-centric.

Emphasising the significance of the One Health approach, the President observed that human health was closely interconnected with animal health, vegetation and the environment. Referring to emerging zoonotic diseases, environmental pollution and climate change, she stressed the need for coordinated efforts among medical professionals, veterinarians, environmental scientists and other stakeholders. She called for greater interdisciplinary collaboration to strengthen disease surveillance, enable early detection and build resilience against future public health challenges.

Addressing the Convocation, Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda, described ABVIMS and Dr. RML Hospital as a pioneering institution and a beacon of excellence in medical education and healthcare. Furthermore, Shri Nadda appreciated its contributions to medical research, infrastructure development and specialised clinical services.

He highlighted that the institution provides an exceptional learning environment by combining a high volume of patient care with quality medical standards, thereby offering students invaluable clinical exposure and practical experience. He also appreciated the institution's achievements in organ donation, organ retrieval and complex surgical procedures, along with the continuous development of its infrastructure and various departments.

Emphasising that professional medical education is a privilege accompanied by significant social responsibility, the Union Health Minister stated that while primary and secondary education are fundamental rights, medical education is supported by a substantial ecosystem of public investment, institutional resources and societal contributions. Referring to the initiatives undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he highlighted the Government's allocation of ₹15,000 crore towards the creation of 10,000 undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats, underscoring the significant investment made in strengthening India's medical education infrastructure. He urged the graduating doctors to recognise this investment as a responsibility to serve society with dedication, compassion and professional excellence.

Shri Nadda further emphasised that students must remain grateful to their teachers for their guidance and acknowledge the sacrifices and support of their parents throughout their academic journey. He observed that the achievements of medical graduates are not solely the result of their individual efforts but also reflect the collective contribution of families, teachers and the larger society.

Highlighting the transformation of medical education in India over the past decade, the Union Health Minister noted the expansion of the country's healthcare and medical education infrastructure, including the establishment and operationalisation of 23 All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). He observed that these institutions are equipped with modern infrastructure and advanced facilities, strengthening India's capacity to provide quality medical education and specialised healthcare services.

Concluding his address, Shri Nadda reiterated the Government of India's commitment to providing world-class medical education infrastructure and healthcare facilities across the country. He urged the graduating doctors to carry forward the values of professional integrity, compassion and service, and to dedicate their knowledge and skills towards the health and well-being of the nation.

As part of the ceremony, the Union Health Minister released the Annual Report (2025–26) and the ABVIMS Journal, highlighting the institution's academic, clinical, research and institutional achievements.

The convocation formally inducted 324 graduating medical professionals into the healthcare workforce across undergraduate, postgraduate and super-specialty disciplines. The graduating cohort comprised 100 MBBS students from the Batch of 2020, including 79 male and 21 female students. A total of 177 students graduated from MD/MS programmes across 17 broad specialties from the batches of 2022–2025, comprising 115 male and 62 female students. In the super-specialty disciplines, 47 students graduated from DM/M.Ch./DrNB programmes across 13 specialties from the batches of 2022–2025, including 35 male and 12 female students.

A total of 58 Gold Medals were conferred upon top-performing graduates in recognition of their outstanding academic performance and clinical excellence.

Infrastructure and Clinical Milestones

The occasion also highlighted significant advancements in the institution's healthcare infrastructure and clinical capabilities. These included the commissioning of the new 666-bed Super-Specialty Block, featuring dedicated departments for Radiotherapy, Nuclear Medicine, Surgical Oncology and Gastrointestinal Surgery. The new facility has further strengthened the availability of specialised and advanced healthcare services.

Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital also achieved a significant milestone in 2025 by becoming the first Central Government hospital in India to receive full accreditation from the National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH), reflecting its commitment to quality healthcare, patient safety and institutional excellence.

The occasion celebrated the achievements of the graduating students and reaffirmed the institution's commitment to excellence in medical education, research and patient care. It also encouraged the next generation of medical professionals to uphold the highest standards of professional ethics, compassion and dedication in their service to the nation.

Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family welfare; Dr. Abhijat Seth, Chairman, National Medical Commission (NMC); Dr. (Prof) Akhilandeswari Prasad, Director, RML and other senior officials of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, faculty members, healthcare professionals, graduating students and their family members, among others present at the event.

Newsletter to capture festival highlights, cinematic conversations and behind-the-scenes moments
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 12:53PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 20 November 2026

 

As the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) gets underway in Goa, Festival Director and acclaimed filmmaker Shri Ashutosh Gowariker today launched Volume 5, Issue 1 of IFFILOID, the daily festival newsletter published by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

Returning for another edition of IFFI, IFFILOID offers its readers a glimpse into the vibrant world of cinema, bringing together films, filmmakers, conversations and memorable moments that make the festival a celebration of storytelling.

The newsletter will feature festival highlights, engaging articles, photographs, programme schedules and updates on key events. From cinematic showcases and interactions with filmmakers to screenings and other festival activities, it will capture the diverse experiences unfolding throughout the festival.

Reflecting the theme of the 57th IFFI, ‘Stories Without Borders’, the newsletter celebrates the power of cinema to connect people, cultures and perspectives. It seeks to take the festival beyond its screening venues, enabling cinema enthusiasts and readers to stay connected with the latest happenings at IFFI.

Published daily during the festival from November 20 to 29, IFFILOID complements PIB's official coverage of IFFI by presenting festival updates and highlights in an accessible and visually engaging format.

The first issue of IFFILOID is available on the official PIB IFFI portal. Interested readers can access the newsletter and follow subsequent editions throughout the festival.
