2338907.title: From Indian Fields to Global Markets: Agri-Exports Gather Pace
2338907.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
From Indian Fields to Global Markets: Agri-Exports Gather Pace
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 12:32PM by PIB Delhi

India's agricultural exports recorded strong growth during April-September FY 2026-27, led by Basmati rice, processed frozen potatoes and yellow dent corn. Basmati rice exports increased 25.4%, while processed potato exports rose 20.8%. Yellow dent corn exports surged around 12-fold. Strong growth in exports across West Asia, East and Southeast Asia, and other international markets reflects the widening geographical reach of India's agricultural and processed food exports.

 

Introduction

India's agricultural exports recorded strong growth across key commodities during April–September FY 2026–27, with Basmati rice, prepared or preserved frozen potatoes and yellow dent corn registering significant increases. The performance reflects a combination of stronger demand in traditional markets, rapid growth in emerging destinations and the increasing geographical diversification of India's agricultural exports.

Basmati rice exports increased across several West Asian markets, including Iran, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Yemen and Oman. The United States also recorded growth during the period. Meanwhile, processed potato exports gained momentum across East and Southeast Asia, particularly in Indonesia, and Japan.

Yellow dent corn registered a particularly sharp increase in exports, with Vietnam, Bangladesh and the Philippines emerging as major destinations. Growth across these agricultural commodities highlights the widening geographical spread of India's exports and its expanding presence in international markets.

Basmati Rice Exports Rise 25% to US$ 1.60 Billion

Exports of Basmati rice increased around 25.4%, from US$ 1.28 billion during April–September FY 2025–26 to US$ 1.60 billion in the corresponding period of FY 2026–27. The increase was recorded across several important markets in West Asia, North America and other regions.

  • Iran emerged as the largest destination among the reported markets, with exports increasing 44.1%, from US$ 129.8 million to US$ 187.1 million.
  • Saudi Arabia recorded growth of 7.9%, with exports rising from US$ 161.6 million to US$ 174.4 million.
  • The United States registered an increase of 27.7%, with shipments rising from US$ 109.5 million to US$ 139.8 million.
  • The UAE recorded growth of more than 50%, with exports reaching US$ 138.3 million during the period.
  • Yemen registered a substantial increase of 66.8%, with exports rising from US$ 74.7 million to US$ 124.6 million.
  • Oman also recorded strong growth of 65.3%, with shipments increasing from US$ 44.9 million to US$ 74.2 million.
  • Among smaller markets, Jordan recorded a sharp increase of 444.4%, with exports rising more than five-fold from US$ 6.3 million to US$ 34.3 million.

Other destinations, including Canada, Qatar, Nepal, Mauritius and Italy, also registered increases in Basmati rice exports during the period, reflecting the widening geographical reach of Indian Basmati rice across international markets.


Processed Potato Exports Rise 21% to US$ 179.4 Million

India's exports of prepared or preserved frozen potatoes increased 20.8%, from US$ 148.5 million to US$ 179.4 million during April–September FY 2026–27. Growth was recorded across several markets, particularly in East and Southeast Asia.

  • The Philippines remained the leading export destination, with shipments reaching US$ 36.7 million, followed by Saudi Arabia at US$ 24.3 million.
  • Indonesia registered strong growth of 75%, with exports rising from US$ 7.6 million to US$ 13.3 million.
  • Japan recorded a significant increase of 112.9%, with exports more than doubling from US$ 6.2 million to US$ 13.2 million.
  • Oman and Australia also registered notable gains. Exports to Oman reached US$ 9.6 million, while shipments to Australia more than doubled to US$ 6.0 million, representing growth of over 100%.
  • South Korea recorded a nearly 100% increase, with exports rising from US$ 1.0 million to nearly US$ 2.0 million.
  • China registered substantial growth of 160%, with exports increasing from US$ 0.5 million to US$ 1.3 million.

Yellow Dent Corn Exports Surge 1,156%

Exports of yellow dent corn recorded a sharp increase of approximately 1,156%, from US$ 9.78 million during April–September FY 2025–26 to US$ 122.82 million in the corresponding period of FY 2026–27. The sharp increase was driven by substantial growth in shipments to several Asian markets.

  • Vietnam emerged as the largest export destination, with shipments increasing approximately 3,49,600%, from US$ 0.02 million to US$ 69.94 million, reflecting exceptional growth.
  • Bangladesh recorded exports of US$ 30.84 million. The Philippines emerged as another important destination, with exports reaching US$ 8.55 million during the period.
  • The UAE registered a substantial increase of approximately 3,867%, with exports rising from US$ 0.18 million to US$ 7.14 million.
  • Malaysia also recorded strong growth of approximately 903%, with shipments increasing from US$ 0.34 million to US$ 3.41 million.

Diversification Strengthens India's Agricultural Export Story

India's agricultural export performance during April–September FY 2026–27 reflects growth across selected traditional staples and processed food products. Basmati rice recorded increased shipments across West Asia, North America and other markets, while processed potatoes registered gains across East and Southeast Asia.

Yellow dent corn contributed to this expansion, with exports rising sharply to Vietnam, Bangladesh, the Philippines and other destinations. The increase in shipments across these markets highlights the growing geographical diversification of India's agricultural exports.

Growth across established and emerging markets demonstrates the expanding international market base for Indian agricultural commodities and value-added processed food products.

Reference

Ministry of Commerce and Industry

2338898.title: NFDC Partners with Svayam to Make 57th IFFI Accessible and Inclusive for All
2338898.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
NFDC Partners with Svayam to Make 57th IFFI Accessible and Inclusive for All
Collaboration to focus on accessibility audits of festival venues, sensitisation of volunteers and an interactive simulation zone to promote an inclusive cinematic experience
Initiative aims to set a benchmark for accessibility and inclusion at cultural events
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 12:12PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 20 November 2026

 

The National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) has partnered with Svayam to make the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) more accessible and inclusive for all cine-goers, including persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility. This marks the third collaboration between the two organisations, following their partnerships at the 55th IFFI and the 18th Mumbai International Film Festival (MIFF).

As the Accessibility Partner, Svayam is undertaking accessibility audits across festival venues to identify potential barriers and recommend measures to ensure safer, more comfortable and independent access for visitors.

The partnership also includes sensitisation workshops for festival volunteers on disability and accessibility. The sessions will focus on respectful communication, inclusive assistance and practical ways to support persons with diverse accessibility needs.

An Accessibility Simulation Zone will further provide visitors and festival stakeholders with an interactive opportunity to understand the everyday barriers faced by persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility. The initiative aims to foster greater awareness, empathy and understanding of the importance of accessible public spaces.

Speaking about the partnership, Ms. Sminu Jindal, Managing Director, Svayam, said, “Accessibility is not merely about creating ramps or making physical spaces barrier-free; it is about ensuring that every individual has the dignity, independence and opportunity to participate equally in society. Cinema is a powerful medium that brings people together, transcends boundaries and celebrates diverse human experiences. It is therefore essential that film festivals are equally welcoming and accessible to everyone. Our collaboration with NFDC for the 57th IFFI is an important step towards making inclusion an integral part of the festival experience. We envision an IFFI where reduced mobility, whether due to age, temporary injury or permanent disability, does not become a barrier to experiencing the joy of cinema.”

Emphasising the importance of the initiative, Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, NFDC, said, “The International Film Festival of India celebrates the universal language of cinema, and it is important that this celebration is truly open to everyone. Our partnership with Svayam is a significant step towards making the 57th IFFI more accessible, inclusive and welcoming for all cine-goers. Through accessible venues and trained and sensitised volunteers, we aim to create an environment where everyone can participate in the festival with dignity, comfort and independence. We hope this initiative will set a meaningful benchmark for inclusive cultural and cinematic events in India.”

The collaboration marks another step towards making India's premier film festival a truly inclusive celebration of cinema, ensuring that persons with disabilities and persons with reduced mobility can participate, connect and experience the power of storytelling with dignity and independence.

2338841.title: Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Chairs Plenary Session of ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’
2338841.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Chairs Plenary Session of ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’
Calls For Whole-Of-Government Approach To Build An Inclusive, Accessible And Drug-Free India
Centre And States Identify Time-Bound Action Points On Drug Demand Reduction, Scholarships, Early Intervention And Accessibility; Summit Reinforces Collective Commitment Towards Viksit Bharat @2047
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 10:34PM by PIB Delhi

Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today applauded and commended the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for organizing the Two Day Departmental Summit and facilitating meaningful deliberations. The Prime Minister emphasized the importance of collective action and a ‘Whole of Government’ approach in achieving the objectives of social justice, social empowerment and a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

Addressing the the plenary session of the two-day Departmental Summit titled ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’, at the Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, in the National Capital here late this evening , Shri Modi highlighted the transformative impact of the Government’s welfare initiatives, he observed that nearly 50 crore people lifted out of poverty have experienced genuine social empowerment.

Calling for the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to be transformed into a nationwide Jan Andolan, the Prime Minister stressed that every citizen, family, educational institution and community must contribute to building a drug-free India. He encouraged schools to organize essay competitions and undertake awareness initiatives, while sensitizing parents to recognize early signs of substance abuse and addiction.

Emphasizing the importance of rehabilitation and social reintegration, Shri Modi observed that the journeys of individuals who have successfully overcome substance dependence carry a powerful message of hope. “These journeys carry the strongest message of hope. They show that recovery is possible and that a life free from drugs is a life of dignity,” he said.

The Prime Minister also urged farmers to shun illicit crop cultivation and called for coordinated efforts involving all Ministries, State Governments, district administrations and spiritual organizations to strengthen the national campaign against drug abuse.

Recognising the influence of spiritual leaders, the Prime Minister said that spiritual gurus and organisations have a vital role to play in the mission. Their guidance, he noted, can inspire millions to choose a life free from drugs.

On the empowerment of persons with disabilities, the Prime Minister highlighted the significance of the term ‘Divyang’, noting its contribution towards enhancing the dignity, respect and self-esteem of persons with disabilities.

Shri Modi encouraged its wider use and popularization to foster a positive outlook towards Divyangjan across society. He also emphasized the need to identify, nurture and recognize their inherent talents and abilities by providing appropriate opportunities and platforms for their participation and contribution.

The Prime Minister’s address reinforced the need for sustained cooperation between the Centre and States, institutional convergence and effective implementation of welfare programmes to ensure that the benefits of development reach every section of society.

The Summit was attended by Union Ministers for Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministers from 27 States and Union Territories, Secretaries of both Departments, Secretaries from 35 States and Union Territories, and senior officers of the Ministry and participating State/UT administrations, to deliberate on key priorities and strengthen collaborative efforts towards inclusive social development and empowerment.

Four thematic priorities deliberated at the Summit

The two-day Departmental Summit commenced on November 18, 2026, with the inaugural session addressed by Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar. Context-setting remarks were delivered by the Secretaries of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), outlining the policy priorities and implementation challenges relating to drug demand reduction, scholarships, early intervention and accessibility.

The first day on November 18 featured four thematic deliberations focusing on Re-imagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction for Nasha Mukt Bharat; Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students; Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden; and Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat.

Four parallel breakout sessions provided a platform for Ministers and senior officials from States and Union Territories to exchange best practices, discuss implementation challenges and identify actionable measures with clearly defined timelines.

1. Re-imagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction for Nasha Mukt Bharat

The session, chaired by Dr. (Col.) Dhani Ram Shandil, Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Himachal Pradesh, and co-chaired by Shri Avinash Gehlot, Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Rajasthan, focused on transforming drug prevention and awareness efforts into a sustained Jan Andolan.

The key action points included observing the 10th of every month as Nasha Mukti Sankalp Diwas, beginning December 2026; making drug prevention a standing agenda item in every Gram Sabha and Municipal Ward; and establishing at least one de-addiction centre in every district by March 2029.

States shared several innovative initiatives, including Chandigarh’s VADA Clubs, Punjab’s SOORMA Ambassadors, Meghalaya’s DREAM Solace Home, Jammu and Kashmir’s 100 Days Campaign and Haryana’s STARS Rating for rehabilitation centres.

Dr. Shandil underscored the importance of structured and continuous interventions through families, schools and communities, observing that prevention is both sound public health policy and sound economics.

Shri Gehlot emphasised the need to move beyond government-led programmes towards community-driven participation.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma affirmed that the outcomes of the deliberations would inform the national action plan.

2. Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students

Chaired by Shri Asim Arun, Minister in the Government of Uttar Pradesh, and co-chaired by Shri Kishan Kumar Bedi, Minister in the Government of Haryana, the session focused on developing an integrated, accessible and student-centric scholarship delivery ecosystem.

The deliberations emphasized simplification of application procedures, secure digital integration between the Centre and States, assisted application facilities, timely disbursement of scholarships and strengthened grievance redressal mechanisms. Suggestions relating to revision of income eligibility criteria and scholarship amounts were also discussed.

States highlighted successful initiatives, including common scholarship platforms in Odisha, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh; Andhra Pradesh’s One Stop Scholarship Portal; prior scrutiny of applications in Madhya Pradesh; and auto-approval mechanisms adopted by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

The discussions underscored the importance of technology-enabled service delivery, intergovernmental coordination and transparent processes to ensure that eligible students receive scholarship assistance in a timely and hassle-free manner.

3. Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden

The session, chaired by Dr. Shweta Gupta, Minister in the Government of Bihar, and co-chaired by Ms. Pi Lalrinpuii, Minister in the Government of Mizoram, focused on strengthening early identification, timely assessment and intervention for children with developmental delays and disabilities.

The key priorities included strengthening convergence among health, nutrition, education and disability-related services; expanding tele-rehabilitation and mobile outreach facilities; developing integrated digital tracking systems; and enhancing the availability of trained human resources.

West Bengal presented its SANSPARSH model, which facilitates community-level screening for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) through a 20-point questionnaire.

Dr. Gupta highlighted that early identification and convergence of existing services are critical to reducing the burden of disability and ensuring that support reaches beneficiaries at the grassroots level.

Ms. Lalrinpuii emphasised the importance of parental awareness, continuous follow-up and shared responsibility among families, institutions and service providers.

4. Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat

The fourth thematic session focused on mainstreaming universal accessibility and inclusive design in public infrastructure, transport systems and digital services from the planning stage itself. The discussions highlighted the need for regular accessibility audits, effective monitoring mechanisms and active participation of persons with disabilities in the design and evaluation of public facilities.

States showcased several good practices, including Kochi Metro and Water Metro in Kerala, with Indian Sign Language-trained staff and accessible amenities; accessibility upgrades at Chennai Egmore and suburban railway stations in Tamil Nadu, including Braille-enabled lifts, tactile pathways and induction loops; accessible tourist spaces in Goa; level-boarding Ahmedabad Janmarg buses in Gujarat; and mandatory barrier-free infrastructure in schools in Assam.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma emphasised that accessibility is not an additional facility but the foundation of equal opportunities and a life of dignity, particularly in the context of the national vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Goa Minister Shri Subhash Faldessai advocated incorporating accessibility at the design and planning stage rather than relying on retrofitting.

Assam highlighted proposals for a dedicated National Mission, district-level monitoring and appropriate penalties for non-compliance with accessibility requirements.

Knowledge-sharing and exhibition of best practices

During the full-house sessions, experts Dr. Varsha Gathoo (formerly AYJNISHD) and Prof. J. S. Thakur (PGIMER) presented global best practices from the US, Australia, Switzerland, Iceland, Thailand, and the African Union alongside national policies.

An exhibition at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan showcased schemes, initiatives, success stories, digital applications and portals of both Departments, providing participants with an opportunity to understand innovative interventions and effective models of service delivery.

Renewed commitment to inclusive and empowered India

The deliberations culminated in a renewed commitment to strengthen Centre-State cooperation, institutional convergence and time-bound implementation of the agreed action points.

The Summit provided an important platform for translating policy priorities into coordinated action, leveraging successful State-level practices and addressing implementation gaps through collective responsibility.

With a shared focus on drug demand reduction, equitable access to educational opportunities, early intervention for persons with disabilities and universal accessibility, ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’ reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to building an inclusive, empowered, accessible and drug-free India in keeping with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

2338781.title: PM chairs valedictory session of Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment
2338781.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM chairs valedictory session of Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment
PM calls for a whole-of-nation approach for success of Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan
PM calls for greater Jan Bhagidari in early identification of disabilities and overcoming social stigma
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 9:09PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the valedictory session of the Departmental Summit on Social Justice and Empowerment at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan earlier today.

The Summit brought together Ministers and senior officials from States and Union Territories for focused deliberations on strengthening social inclusion, empowerment of people with disabilities, prevention of substance abuse and innovative approaches to public participation.

Prime Minister appreciated the extensive deliberations and observed that the discussions and action points emerging from the Summit reflected a shared sense of purpose among the Centre and States. He emphasised that the spirit of competitive and cooperative federalism should guide implementation, with States learning from one another’s experiences and innovations.

Emphasising the importance of Jan Bhagidari, Prime Minister observed that community participation could play a significant role in creating awareness among parents about developmental disabilities and the importance of early identification. He noted that hesitation, fear of social stigma and lack of awareness often prevent parents from recognising or seeking timely support for their children. He observed that a community-based approach could help address parental hesitation and make early intervention more acceptable. He called for innovative approaches to awareness generation, particularly by leveraging technology to communicate important messages in simple and accessible ways. He also suggested that States could organise start-up competitions to encourage young innovators to develop affordable aids and assistive devices, particularly for improving mobility, accessibility and participation in sports and everyday activities.

Discussing the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, Prime Minister emphasised that efforts to address substance abuse must go beyond routine and symbolic activities. He suggested involving schools through essay-writing, debates, oratory competitions and other activities to generate awareness among young people and encourage wider societal participation. He also highlighted the importance of sharing the experiences of individuals who have successfully overcome addiction.

Emphasising a whole-of-nation approach, Prime Minister called for greater involvement of communities, spiritual organisations, educational institutions and Ministries in efforts towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat. He stressed that lasting behavioural change could be achieved only when society itself became an active participant in the movement.

Prime Minister reiterated that the Centre and States are partners in a common national endeavour, and that the collective commitment demonstrated during the Summit should be carried forward in the spirit of competitive and cooperative federalism, contributing towards an inclusive and empowered Viksit Bharat.

 

***

2338801.title: ویوز فلم بازار عالمی فلمی تعاون کو فروغ دینے کے 20 سال مکمل ہونے کی نشان دہی کرتا ہے
2338801.ministry: 2007 میں 18 ممالک کے 204 مندوبین کے ایک معمولی مجمع سے لے کر 2025 میں 40 سے زیادہ ممالک کے 2,500 سے زیادہ مندوبین کا خیرمقدم کرنے والے ایک بڑے بین الاقوامی بازار تک، فلم بازار بھارتی سنیما کو عالمی فلمی صنعت سے جوڑنے والا ایک اہم پلیٹ فارم بن گیا ہے۔ اپنے 20 ویں سال کی نشان دہی کرتے ہوئے، ویوز فلم بازار 2026 تخلیقی تعاون کو فروغ دینے، نئی کہانیوں کو دریافت کرنے اور بھارتی سنیما کے لیے عالمی مواقع کھولنے کی دو دہائیوں کا جشن منا رہا ہے۔
2338801.body_html:
सूचना और प्रसारण मंत्रालय
ویوز فلم بازار عالمی فلمی تعاون کو فروغ دینے کے 20 سال مکمل ہونے کی نشان دہی کرتا ہے
20 واں ایڈیشن بھارتی فلم سازوں کو عالمی منڈیوں سے جوڑے گا؛ افتتاحی تقریب کل گوا میں منعقد ہوگی
प्रविष्टि तिथि: 19 NOV 2026 8:22PM by PIB Delhi

2007 میں 18 ممالک کے 204 مندوبین کے ایک معمولی مجمع سے لے کر 2025 میں 40 سے زیادہ ممالک کے 2,500 سے زیادہ مندوبین کا خیرمقدم کرنے والے ایک بڑے بین الاقوامی بازار تک، فلم بازار بھارتی سنیما کو عالمی فلمی صنعت سے جوڑنے والا ایک اہم پلیٹ فارم بن گیا ہے۔ اپنے 20 ویں سال کی نشان دہی کرتے ہوئے، ویوز فلم بازار 2026 تخلیقی تعاون کو فروغ دینے، نئی کہانیوں کو دریافت کرنے اور بھارتی سنیما کے لیے عالمی مواقع کھولنے کی دو دہائیوں کا جشن منا رہا ہے۔

اطلاعات و نشریات کی وزارت کے تحت نیشنل فلم ڈیولپمنٹ کارپوریشن (این ایف ڈی سی) کے ذریعے، انٹرنیشنل فلم فیسٹیول آف انڈیا (اِفی) کے حصے کے طور پر منعقد ہونے والا، ویوز فلم بازار وسیع تر ورلڈ آڈیو ویژول اینڈ انٹرٹینمنٹ سمٹ (ویوز) پہل کا حصہ ہے۔ ’بھارت میں تخلیق کریں، دنیا کے لیے تخلیق کریں‘ کے وژن کی رہ نمائی میں، یہ پلیٹ فارم مشترکہ پروڈکشن، فنانسنگ، تقسیم اور بین الاقوامی شراکت داری کے ذریعے بھارت کی تخلیقی صلاحیتوں کو عالمی مواقع میں تبدیل کرنے کی کوشش کرتا ہے۔

ویوز فلم بازار کا 20 واں ایڈیشن 20 نومبر 2026 کو دی بال روم، تاج سیڈیڈ ڈی گوا ہورائزن میں اِفتتاح کیا جائے گا۔ جناب چنچل کمار، سکریٹری، اطلاعات و نشریات کی وزارت، خیرمقدمی خطاب دیں گے، جس کے بعد مہمانِ خصوصی جناب آشوتوش گواریکر، فیسٹیول ڈائریکٹر، خطاب کریں گے۔ جناب جی کرشنا کمار، چیئرمین، این ایف ڈی سی، افتتاحی خطاب دیں گے، جب کہ جناب پربھات کمار، ایڈیشنل سکریٹری، اطلاعات و نشریات کی وزارت، شکریہ کی تحریک پیش کریں گے۔ جناب دھیرج سنگھ، منیجنگ ڈائریکٹر، این ایف ڈی سی، بھی موجود ہوں گے۔ رسمی کارروائیوں کے بعد فلم بازار ٹیم کے ذریعے ’ویوز فلم بازار کو نیویگیٹ کرنا‘ پر ایک پریزنٹیشن ہوگی۔

کہانیوں اور مواقع کے لیے ایک بازار

دو دہائیوں کے دوران، فلم بازار ایک نیٹ ورکنگ ایونٹ سے ایک منظم بازار میں تبدیل ہو گیا ہے جو فلم سازوں، پروڈیوسروں، سرمایہ کاروں، تقسیم کاروں، سیلز ایجنٹوں اور فیسٹیول پروگرامرز کو جوڑتا ہے۔ اس کے پروگرام این ایف ڈی سی اسکرین رائٹرز لیب، کو-پروڈکشن مارکیٹ اور ورک اِن پروگریس لیب جیسی پہل قدمیوں کے ذریعے ترقی کے مختلف مراحل میں فلموں کی حمایت کرتے ہیں۔ ویونگ روم، مارکیٹ اسکریننگز، کیوریٹڈ بی 2 بی میٹنگز اور نالج سیریز مزید پروجیکٹ کی دریافت، صنعت کی شمولیت اور ممکنہ تعاون کو آسان بناتے ہیں۔

2025 کا ایڈیشن، جو 20 سے 24 نومبر تک گوا میں 56 ویں انٹرنیشنل فلم فیسٹیول آف انڈیا (اِفی) کے ساتھ منعقد ہوا، 40 سے زیادہ ممالک کے 2,500 سے زیادہ مندوبین کو یکجا کیا۔ اس میں 320 پروجیکٹس کی نمائش کی گئی اور 220 سے زیادہ خریداروں کو شامل کرتے ہوئے 1,200 سے زیادہ ون ٹو ون کاروباری میٹنگز کو آسان بنایا گیا۔ کاروباری گفت و شنید اور مذاکرات کی مالیت تقریباًً 1,050 کروڑ روپے تھی، جس میں ایونٹ کے موقع پر تقریباًً 100 کروڑ روپے کے مفاہمت نامے (ایم او یو) بھی شامل تھے۔

ویوز بازار: سالانہ بازار سے آگے بھارت کی تخلیقی رسائی کو وسعت

ویوز پہل ویوز بازار کے ذریعے سالانہ فلم بازار سے آگے بڑھتی ہے، جو جنوری 2025 میں شروع کیا گیا ایک سال بھر کا بین الاقوامی بی 2 بی پلیٹ فارم ہے۔ فلم، ٹیلی وژن، او ٹی ٹی، اینیمیشن، وی ایف ایکس، گیمنگ، موسیقی اور دیگر تخلیقی شعبوں کا احاطہ کرتے ہوئے، یہ تخلیق کاروں اور کاروباروں کو ممکنہ خریداروں اور معاونین سے جوڑتا ہے۔

اکتوبر 2026 کے پیش رفت نوٹ کے مطابق، ویوز بازار میں 12,500 سے زیادہ فعال صارفین تھے، جن میں 5,000 سے زیادہ خریدار اور تقریباًً 6,500 فروخت کنندگان شامل تھے، جن کے پاس 2,800 سے زیادہ فعال پروجیکٹس تھے۔ اے آئی سے چلنے والی سیمنٹک سرچ، میچ میکنگ، ورچوئل پچنگ اور آن لائن بی 2 بی میٹنگ کی سہولیات تخلیق کاروں اور کاروباروں کو ممکنہ شراکت داروں کی شناخت کرنے اور جسمانی ایونٹس سے آگے صنعت کی شمولیت کو برقرار رکھنے میں مدد کرتی ہیں۔

آسٹریلیا، جاپان، جنوبی کوریا، اٹلی، جرمنی، کینیڈا، فرانس اور اسپین جیسے ممالک میں اس کی بین الاقوامی رسائی نے بھارتی تخلیقی اداروں کے لیے مزید راستے کھولے ہیں۔ گیمز کام، ٹورنٹو انٹرنیشنل فلم فیسٹیول، وینس اور ایم آئی پی کام سمیت عالمی صنعت کے پلیٹ فارمز میں شرکت نے بین الاقوامی اسٹیک ہولڈروں کے ساتھ تعلقات کو مضبوط کیا ہے۔

یہ پہل قدمیاں بھارتی تخلیقی صلاحیتوں کو ’دستکاری سے تجارت‘ تک لے جانے کی ایک وسیع تر کوشش کی عکاسی کرتی ہیں، جس سے مواد کی تخلیق، دانش ورانہ ملکیت اور تخلیقی صنعتوں کے لیے ایک عالمی مرکز کے طور پر بھارت کی پوزیشن مضبوط ہوتی ہے۔

جیسا کہ ویوز فلم بازار اپنے سفر کی دو دہائیوں کو مکمل کر رہا ہے، یہ آزاد فلم سازوں، علاقائی زبان کے سنیما اور ابھرتی ہوئی تخلیقی صلاحیتوں کے لیے بین الاقوامی منڈیوں تک رسائی حاصل کرنے، شراکت داری قائم کرنے اور بھارتی کہانیوں کو دنیا بھر کے سامعین تک پہنچانے کے لیے ایک اہم پلیٹ فارم کے طور پر کام کرتا رہے گا۔

2338737.title: Decoding the Language of Cinema: PIB-FTII Film Appreciation Course Explores the Art, Craft and Grammar of Filmmaking Ahead of IFFI 2026
2338737.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Decoding the Language of Cinema: PIB-FTII Film Appreciation Course Explores the Art, Craft and Grammar of Filmmaking Ahead of IFFI 2026
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:57PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 19 November 2026

 

The Press Information Bureau (PIB), in collaboration with the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), organised a Film Appreciation Course for accredited media delegates and students of mass communication ahead of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026. The course sought to equip participants with a deeper understanding of cinema as an art form, introducing them to its language, aesthetics and creative processes to enable more informed engagement with the festival and its films.

Addressing the inaugural session, Director General, PIB, Ms. Smita Vats Sharma emphasised the importance of looking at cinema beyond entertainment and appreciating its grammar, philosophy and visual language. Shri Mahesh Kumar described cinema as a spatial-temporal and techno-industrial art form, drawing attention to the interplay of visual techniques, technology and creative processes in shaping its cultural and social influence.

Ms. Smita Vats Sharma highlighted the need for greater depth and quality in media coverage of cinema, urging media professionals to look beyond the volume of stories and engage with the artistic and technical dimensions of filmmaking. She also emphasised the value of bringing mass communication students into the programme and encouraged participants to make full use of the sessions, screenings and opportunities to interact with filmmakers and other cinema professionals.

The course was led by FTII faculty members Prof. Dr. Indranil Bhattacharya, Professor, Screen Studies & Research, and Prof. Vaibhav Abnave, Associate Professor, Film Direction. The sessions combined lectures, screenings, discussions and analytical exercises to familiarise participants with film form, cinematic history and the aesthetics of global filmmaking. Key themes included ‘Time and Space in Cinema’, ‘Animated Documentaries’ and ‘Structural Analysis’. The programme culminated in a session on film criticism, in which participants analysed Lifeline, drawing upon the concepts and critical approaches explored during the course.

In recognition of their contribution, the FTII faculty members were felicitated with specially curated artworks reflecting Goa’s rich cultural heritage. Certificates were presented to participating media delegates by Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Shri Prabhat Kumar; FTII Vice-Chancellor and NFDC Managing Director, Shri Dhiraj Singh; and PIB Director General, Ms. Smita Vats Sharma.

By bringing together academic perspectives and practical engagement with cinema, the course sought to strengthen participants’ ability to appreciate and interpret films, adding an informed critical dimension to their engagement with the 57th IFFI.

.@PIB_India, in association with @FTIIOfficial, organised a Film Appreciation Course in Panaji, Goa today, ahead of the commencement of the 57th @IFFIGoa, offering participants an opportunity to deepen their understanding and appreciation of cinema before the festival begins. The session was attended by mediapersons coming for coverage of IFFI from all over India, and also mass-communication students from two colleges in Goa. Ms. Smita Vats Sharma, Director General, PIB West Zone, delivered the opening remarks for the day-long session, which was conducted by Prof. Dr. Indranil Bhattacharya and Prof. Vaibhav Abnave. FTII's distinguished faculty members shared their expertise, offering media delegates deeper insights into film form, history, aesthetics and cinematic storytelling through lectures, screenings and discussions. The session ended with distribution of certificates to the participants, in the presence of the Additional Secretary, @MIB_India Shri Prabhat, and @FTIIOfficial Vice-Chancellor Shri Dhiraj Singh.

— PIB in Goa 🇮🇳 (@PIB_Panaji) November 19, 2026

 

* * *

Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, chaired the 32nd meeting of the Central Supervisory Board (CSB) today to review the implementation of the Pre-conception and Pre-natal Diagnostic Techniques (Prohibition of Sex Selection) Act, 1994 (PC&PNDT Act), and deliberate on measures to address Gender-biased Sex Selection and prevent the misuse of diagnostic technologies.

Addressing the Central Supervisory Board, the Union Minister underscored the need to bring in relevant perspectives in tune with the changing technology landscape so as to bring in the effectivity for reaching the desired objective of the PC&PNDT Act, 1994. He also took note of the various implementation activities undertaken by the States/UTs for prevention of sex selection and sex determination.

While steering the meeting, Hon’ble Minister called upon policymakers, regulatory authorities, State Governments, enforcement agencies and other stakeholders for continued constructive dialogue for meaningful recommendations to strengthen the Act.

Smt. Anupriya Patel, Hon’ble Minister of State, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare mentioned about various action points which had been taken to reduce the gender gap and raised concerns about the importance of ensuring that all efforts should be taken to reduce the gender balance. With women-led development being a key priority, a balanced sex ratio is critical to ensure holistic development. In this regard, the focus on education and changing mindset is essential to bring in gender balance.

Smt. Savitri Thakur, Union Minister of State for Women and Child Development, highlighted the role of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao initiative in promoting the value of the girl child and addressing gender-based discrimination. She underscored the importance of sustained awareness and community participation in fostering positive social attitudes towards girls.

The Board deliberated on the recommendations of the High-Level Committee (HLC) on Non-Financial Regulatory Reforms, in the broader context of strengthening the implementation of the PC&PNDT Act. The Union Health Minister called upon States/UTs to ensure regular inspections of registered facilities and prompt follow-up on violations.

Union Health Secretary, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, highlighted the importance of coordinated efforts between the Centre and States/UTs and leveraging the various digital initiatives within the Ministry for an integrated approach. She emphasised that effective implementation of the PC&PNDT Act requires sustained engagement with stakeholders, including medical professionals, and continued attention to the rights and value of the girl child.

Members of the Board deliberated on key implementation challenges and measures to improve the functioning of the PC&PNDT framework. Discussions covered the use of digital processes, capacity building of Appropriate Authorities, engagement with medical professionals, and need for targeted interventions and sharing of good practices among States/UTs. Members gave suggestions on the various interventions, ensuring that the PC&PNDT Act keeps pace with the current emerging challenges, which should be considered for enabling effective implementation of the Act.

Concluding the meeting, Shri Nadda emphasised that technology must be leveraged to advance healthcare and social inclusion, and must not be allowed to facilitate sex selection or gender discrimination.

2338724.title: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026 Records Cumulative Sales of ₹44.55 Lakh
2338724.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026 Records Cumulative Sales of ₹44.55 Lakh
Cumulative Sales Register Approximately 51% Increase Over Previous Day; Additional Sales of ₹14.99 Lakh Recorded in a Single Day Reflecting Growing Consumer Appreciation for Indigenous Products
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:45PM by PIB Delhi

The pavilion of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment at the ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, in the National Capital here, continues to witness an encouraging response from visitors, with cumulative sales reaching approximately ₹44.55 lakh as of November 18, 2026.

The increase reflects  growing consumer appreciation for India’s traditional craftsmanship and indigenous products.

The cumulative sales have registered a significant increase of approximately 51 per cent over ₹29.56 lakh recorded as of November 17, 2026, with additional sales of approximately ₹14.99 lakh in a single day.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to reaffirm its commitment to promoting indigenous craftsmanship, strengthening traditional livelihoods, fostering entrepreneurship and building an inclusive and self-reliant India in line with the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047.

 

Notably, cumulative sales have increased more than eightfold from ₹5.50 lakh recorded as of November 15, 2026, reflecting sustained consumer patronage, growing demand for indigenous products and expanding economic opportunities for participating artisans and entrepreneurs.

The Ministry’s pavilion, located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, has emerged as a vibrant platform for celebrating India’s diverse artistic traditions, indigenous skills and entrepreneurial talent, while facilitating direct engagement between traditional artisans and consumers.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said more than 130 artisans from 19 States are showcasing their products at the ongoing Trade Fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

The sustained growth in sales reflects the potential of traditional craftsmanship as a driver of entrepreneurship, economic self-reliance and sustainable livelihood generation, the Official noted.

He said the pavilion showcases an extensive range of traditional handlooms, intricately designed handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products, representing the distinctive artistic identities and rich cultural heritage of different regions of the country.

Beyond facilitating direct sales, participation in national-level exhibitions such as IITF enables artisans to enhance their product visibility, understand evolving consumer preferences, establish business networks and explore newer market opportunities, the Official said.

 

He said the participation of the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations underscores their continued efforts towards strengthening market linkages, promoting entrepreneurship and advancing the socio-economic empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalised communities.

 

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, the Ministry continues to facilitate greater economic participation and self-reliance among artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs), the Official said.

The Official said a significant highlight of the Ministry’s participation at IITF 2026 is the promotion of the TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) brand, which seeks to establish a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhance their recognition among domestic and international consumers.

The TULIP initiative was recently launched by Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, during the Shilp Samagam Mela at Dilli Haat in the National Capital, he said.

 

Through the promotion of the TULIP brand, the Ministry seeks to bridge the gap between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation, strengthen entrepreneurial capabilities and create sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans, the Official said.

He said the Ministry’s pavilion offers visitors a unique opportunity to experience India’s diverse cultural and artistic heritage, interact directly with artisans and actively contribute to their economic empowerment by purchasing authentic, indigenous and handcrafted products.

The ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, 2026, provides a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange, bringing together producers and consumers from diverse backgrounds.

2338712.title: ‘Stories Without Borders’ to Come Alive as 57th IFFI Opens Tomorrow in Goa
2338712.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
‘Stories Without Borders’ to Come Alive as 57th IFFI Opens Tomorrow in Goa
Goa all set to welcome global film community as 57th IFFI opens tomorrow
A Celebration of Cinema, Music and Culture to Mark Opening of 57th IFFI in Goa
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:14PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa 19 November 2026

 

The grand Opening ceremony to bring together filmmakers, artists and delegates from India and abroad for an evening of music, cultural performances and cinematic celebration under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’

Goa is all set to welcome filmmakers, artists, delegates and cinema enthusiasts from India and across the world as the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) commences tomorrow, November 20, bringing together the world of cinema for nine days of films, cultural exchange and creative engagement.

Organized under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, this year’s festival will bring together films and creative voices from different countries, cultures and cinematic traditions, celebrating the universal language of cinema.

The opening ceremony at Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium, Goa, will feature musical presentations, cultural performances and ceremonial proceedings, marking the commencement of the nine-day festival.

The ceremony will begin with a sound and light presentation, followed by the National Song and National Anthem. The ceremonial opening will include the lighting of the lamp and watering of the Tulsi plant, symbolising light, life and new beginnings.

Prominent personalities at the opening ceremony

The ceremony will feature addresses by the Chief Minister of Goa, Dr. Pramod Sawant, and senior dignitaries from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

The opening ceremony will also bring together prominent personalities from Indian cinema, including Member of Parliament Ravi Kishan, filmmaker and Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker, filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar and filmmaker Aanand L. Rai, among other distinguished members of the Indian and international film fraternity.

Ricky Kej's symphonic orchestra

A major highlight of the evening will be a symphonic orchestra presentation by three-time Grammy Award-winning composer and environmentalist Ricky Kej, titled ‘A World of Cinema Through Music’. The performance will bring alive the universal language of cinema through a musical journey across cultures and storytelling traditions.

The musical presentation will be followed by ‘Music Without Borders’, bringing together musicians from different countries in a celebration of musical traditions, harmony and cultural exchange, reflecting the festival's theme.

The peacock motif associated with IFFI will come alive through ‘Beyond the Frame’, a special dance presentation, bringing the festival's iconic emblem to life through movement and artistic expression.

The ceremony will also feature the felicitation of the Indian Panorama and International Competition juries, recognising the filmmakers and cinema professionals entrusted with selecting films for the festival's competitive sections.

International Competition Jury

The International Competition Jury will be chaired by filmmaker Aanand L. Rai and will comprise distinguished cinema professionals from across the world, including Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière (Argentina), Bogdan Muresanu (Romania), María Alejandra Rojas (Colombia) and Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke (Thailand). The jury will be felicitated during the opening ceremony.

Indian Panorama Jury

The Feature Film Jury is chaired by National Award-winning filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar, while the Non-Feature Film Jury is chaired by filmmaker and former Director of the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, Himansu Sekhar Khatua.

A special presentation marking two decades of WAVES Film Bazaar will showcase its evolution as a platform connecting Indian filmmakers with the international film industry and facilitating creative and business collaborations.

Nine days of cinema from across the world

From acclaimed international films to emerging voices and diverse Indian stories, IFFI 2026 will offer audiences a wide-ranging cinematic experience. The festival will screen over 150 international films from 86 countries, bringing diverse storytelling traditions and perspectives to Goa.

The festival will open with Fatherland, directed by acclaimed Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski, whose work received the Best Director Award at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. The Mid-Fest Film will be I Matter, directed by Alina Șerban, a Romania-Germany-Belgium co-production featuring dialogues in Romanian and Romani. The festival will conclude with We Are All Strangers, directed by Singaporean filmmaker Anthony Chen, bringing the nine-day celebration of world cinema to a close on 28th November. The festival will also spotlight international cinema through competitions, curated showcases and country presentations, with Spain as the Country of Honour and Russia as the Partner Country.

Indian cinema will find a prominent place through Indian Panorama, featuring 76 films in 18 languages. A special focus on BRICS cinema will further bring films from member and partner countries into the spotlight.

The festival will celebrate emerging filmmakers through the Best Debut Feature Films Competition, alongside other competitive sections, including the International Competition and ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal, recognising cinematic excellence across diverse categories.

New Segments in IFFI 2026

This year’s festival introduces two new segments to broaden its cinematic offerings and celebrate diverse forms of storytelling. The first segment, Animation, will feature five outstanding films, showcasing creativity and innovation in animated cinema. The second segment, Films About Films, presents five films with the objective of bringing the art and craft of filmmaking to the forefront.

Golden Peacock and Silver Peacock Awards

The festival's competitive sections will recognise cinematic excellence through the prestigious Golden Peacock and Silver Peacock Awards, comprising six awards. The Golden Peacock will be presented for Best Film, while the Silver Peacock Awards will recognise Best Director, Best Actor (Male), Best Actor (Female), Special Jury Award and Best Debut Feature Film of a Director. The festival will also present the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal for a film promoting tolerance, intercultural dialogue and a culture of peace.

Through Creative Minds of Tomorrow, young aspiring filmmakers will have opportunities to learn from industry professionals, collaborate and explore the world of filmmaking through masterclasses, workshops, interactive sessions and a 48-hour filmmaking challenge.

Beyond film screenings, the festival will facilitate wider engagement among filmmakers, artists, students and industry professionals through curated interactions and industry initiatives. WAVES Film Bazaar, being held alongside IFFI, will provide a platform for creative exchange, collaboration and industry opportunities, connecting filmmakers and producers with buyers, distributors and other stakeholders.

Established in 1952, IFIF continues to serve as an important platform for showcasing Indian and international cinema, fostering cultural exchange and bringing filmmakers, industry professionals and audiences together from across the world.

2338703.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference in New Delhi
2338703.body_html:

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference in New Delhi
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have adopted ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy towards terrorism, and this policy is yielding positive results
Following the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Latif Bhat, Kashmir is now free of locally recruited terrorists born in India, this marks a major milestone in the fight against terrorism

Every state's ATS should strengthen its cyber expert unit
By expanding the scope of MAC to include cyber security, narco-terrorism, and emerging radicalisation hotspots, and by establishing a National Memory Bank, we have laid a new foundation for strengthening our preparedness
Not only have legal powers of NIA been enhanced, but its national presence has also been expanded, approval has been granted for 16 new branch offices and two zonal offices simultaneously
NIA has been empowered to conduct investigations to protect the interests of Indians residing abroad
Dismantling of PFI network is a significant example of how effective coordinated operations by police forces across India can be
In a single night, police forces from 11 states, along with central agencies, jointly dealt a major blow to PFI network, this operation is now a case study for the entire world
Shahzad Bhatti network has been designated a terrorist organisation under UAPA, more than 40 of its modules have been dismantled across the country, over 100 cases have been registered, and more than 271 arrests have been made
Union Home Minister released NIA publication ‘Fail-Safe Investigation’, laid the foundation stone for NIA office complex in Chandigarh, and inaugurated residential complex at Maidan Garhi i
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the inaugural session of two-day counter-terrorism conference organised in New Delhi. On the occasion, Union Home Minister released the publication ‘Fail-Safe Investigation’ brought out by National Investigation Agency (NIA). He also laid the foundation stone of NIA office complex in Chandigarh and inaugurated NIA residential complex built at Maidangarhi in Delhi. In addition, Union Home Minister e-launched the NIA’s ‘Pushti’ portal and conferred decorations on seven officers and personnel of the National Investigation Agency.

On this occasion, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Union Home Secretary Shri Govind Mohan, Director Intelligence Bureau (IB) Dr. Mahesh Dikshit, Special Secretary (Internal Security) in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Anand Swarup, and Director General National Investigation Agency (NIA) Shri Rakesh Aggarwal, along with several other senior officers, were present. Senior police officers from the states and Union Territories, officers from counter-terrorism agencies, and experts from related fields including law, forensics and technology are participating in this conference.

Addressing the conference, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that India has been a victim of terrorism and we have been confronting terrorism for a long time. He noted that police forces of different states had made various kinds of efforts, but a lack of coordinated action was clearly visible. Over time, during the tenures of successive governments, gradual efforts were made to overcome these shortcomings. Today, we can say with satisfaction that in this vast country — from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and from Dwarka to Kamakhya — we are putting in place a system under which a uniform strategy to combat terrorism will operate right down to the level of every police station.

Shri Amit Shah said that some successful operations have recently been carried out against terrorism, which has strengthened the confidence of our country. He stated that just yesterday we achieved a significant milestone in the fight against terrorism. With the elimination of Lashkar terrorist Latif Bhat, the entire Kashmir has become free from the presence of India-born terrorists. Shri Shah noted that this situation has come about after 35 years.

Shri Amit Shah said that the Shahzad Bhatti network has been declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). More than 40 of its modules have been neutralised across the country. In the action taken against this network, over 100 cases have been registered and more than 271 arrests have been made. Shri Shah stated that the hallmark of a successful agency is to apprehend terrorists and put them behind bars even before they can execute a terrorist incident. He said that the police of every state should analyse this model, accept it, and implement it in their respective areas.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that since 2019 we have launched a special drive to bring fugitives back to India, and so far 303 fugitives have been brought back from 36 countries, thereby strengthening the security of our nation. He noted that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the Ministry of Home Affairs have made special efforts in this regard. Our intelligence agencies have made outstanding efforts in bringing back fugitives living abroad through scientific methods. Shri Shah stated that if we are to completely eliminate the three menaces— terrorism, organised crime and drugs, it is essential to bring the culprits and masterminds who have taken shelter abroad before Indian courts.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, we have adopted ‘Zero Tolerance’ policy against terrorism, and positive results of this are being achieved. He stated that, as part of continuous efforts in this direction, NIA Act was first amended on 2nd August 2019. New offences were brought under the jurisdiction of NIA and additional jurisdictions were granted to it. Shri Shah added  that UAPA was amended on 14th August 2019, under which NIA was empowered to seize the properties of terrorists and a process was initiated to declare individuals as terrorists. Union Home Minister noted that in September 2019 a unified action plan was prepared to counter radicalisation, which was finalised in December 2019 after discussions with various ministries. In September 2022, PFI network was dismantled. He said that the destruction of PFI network is a striking example of how effective a joint operation by the Indian police can be. In a single night, coordinated action was carried out simultaneously in 11 states, completely dismantling the entire PFI network and breaking its backbone. By destroying the PFI network, we have preemptively eliminated several serious problems that the country could have faced in the future. He added that the dismantling of PFI network is the key to preventing many potential incidents that could have occurred in the times to come.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the functioning of the Multi-Agency Centre (MAC) has been reorganised. Cyber security, narcotics, organised crime networks and emerging radicalisation hotspots have been brought under the purview of the MAC. In 2023, the methodology of the MAC was restructured using state-of-the-art technology. A National Memory Bank was established and efforts were made to create a centralised database. He further stated that during this period, not only were the legal powers of NIA enhanced, but its national character was also expanded. Almost simultaneously, 16 new branch offices and two zonal offices were approved. NIA was empowered to conduct investigations for the protection of the interests of Indians residing abroad. A ban was imposed on the glorification of terrorism. A 25-point integrated action plan was formulated to control the funding of terrorists, and this is being effectively monitored.

Shri Amit Shah said, NIA officers have been trained to gain international exposure, and 70 new NIA Special Courts have been established across the country. He stated that peace had been established in three major hotspots, networks such as PFI and Shahzad Bhatti had been dismantled, and a scientific mechanism had been developed to bring back fugitives from abroad. He also highlighted the implementation of a new comprehensive approach to border security, the complete removal of illegal religious structures along the borders, and improved coordination among various agencies to strengthen economic security. Shri Shah stated that the government had worked simultaneously and effectively on all these fronts.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah stated that we are moving forward with an ecosystem-based approach to combating terrorism through cooperation between the Centre and the States, and that this cooperation needs to be further strengthened. He said that we have strengthened the provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) on the legal front, and that the flow of information needs to be made smoother and more robust at the institutional level. He emphasised that we must also change our work culture to achieve victory in this fight. On the operational front, agencies must enhance their capabilities while also undertaking modernisation. We must target the entire chain of terror financing, which requires better coordination with financial investigation agencies. Shri Shah stated that we will not achieve success unless we strike at the entire terrorist network in a coordinated and comprehensive manner.

Shri Amit Shah stated that in the fight against terrorism, our approach must be based on shared and collective goals, along with clearly defined accountability. He emphasised that unless our goals are shared and accountability for achieving them is clearly established, success cannot be achieved. He further said that this conference must be made outcome-oriented, which will be possible only when all participants make concerted efforts in this direction.

Union Home Minister said that India needs to strengthen the concept of proactive action in its counter-terrorism policy, with greater emphasis on structural and operational capabilities. Shri Amit Shah stated that the entire terrorist network must be investigated and its capabilities dismantled. He said that by investigating the entire network, many incidents could be prevented before they occur. Shri Shah emphasised the need to develop a mechanism through which police station-level intelligence is transmitted through multiple levels to the Director General of Police (DGP), enabling the extraction of actionable intelligence. He also said that the Anti-Terrorism Squads (ATS) of every state need to strengthen their cyber expert units, as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes. Union Home Minister further stated that establishing a Quadrangular Regional Security Grid in Border States should be a key priority. He also stressed the need to enhance the capabilities of the ATS units across all states.

2338701.title: Raksha Mantri and Japan’s Minister of Defense hold bilateral talks in Tokyo
2338701.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri and Japan’s Minister of Defense hold bilateral talks in Tokyo
India & Japan agree to deepen defence cooperation across key domains and reaffirm commitment to peace & stability in Indo-Pacific
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh held a bilateral meeting with the Minister of Defense of Japan Mr Shinjiro Koizumi in Tokyo on November 19, 2026. The two Ministers welcomed the steady materialisation of India-Japan defence cooperation through close communication between them, including the holding of their third Defence Ministers’ Meeting within a short period of time, following their interactions in August and October this year.

Both the leaders welcomed the signing of LOI (Letter of Intent) toward the utilisation of firing ranges in India, whereby Japan Self-Defense Forces would, for the first time, conduct live-fire training etc., including those involving surface-to-ship missiles, at firing ranges in India. They concurred on accelerating coordination between the defence authorities of the two countries toward its early realisation.

The two Ministers welcomed the steady progress in materialising maritime security cooperation under the ‘Memorandum of Arrangement on Maritime Security Cooperation’ signed in August this year. In particular, they confirmed that the Working Group, headed at the JS/DG level, would follow up on working level talks on areas including enhancing mine counter-measures capabilities and exploring the possibility of joint development in naval shipbuilding and design.

The two Ministers agreed to further deepen cooperation towards creating an environment that would facilitate information sharing between the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force and the Indian Navy.

The two Ministers welcomed the deepening of cooperation through joint exercises between the respective Services, including the multilateral naval exercise ‘Malabar 2026’ involving Japan, the United States, India and Australia, and the Japan-India Maritime Exercise ‘JAIMEX26’, both conducted in Japan this month. They also concurred on further advancing exchanges between their respective Special Operations Forces.

Regarding defence equipment and technology cooperation, the two Ministers shared their expectation for an early conclusion of the UNICORN related arrangements, and the Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) by India by February 2027. They also affirmed that they would materialise defence R&D cooperation between DRDO and ATLA in the field of state-of-the-art missile and defence technologies.

 

The two Ministers concurred on promoting cooperation between the two air services in the field of Air Domain Awareness and confirmed that the working level talks would also be followed through the Working Group, headed at the JS/DG level.

Amid an increasingly complex and uncertain security environment in the Indo-Pacific region, the two Ministers concurred on further promoting multilateral defence cooperation, including trilateral cooperation, in addition to bilateral defence cooperation between Japan and India, and on advancing practical cooperation for peace and stability in the region.

The two Ministers shared their determination to steadily implement these concrete areas of cooperation and elevate Japan-India defence cooperation to greater heights, thereby contributing together to the peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific.

2338698.title: Strengthening Rehabilitation and Livelihood Opportunities through NAPDDR
2338698.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strengthening Rehabilitation and Livelihood Opportunities through NAPDDR
Mr. Sudesh Kumar Of Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh Treated And Rehabilitated Under Ministry-Supported De-Addiction Treatment, Counselling And Rehabilitation Assistance
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi

Access to comprehensive de-addiction treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services plays a significant role in promoting individual well-being, strengthening family relationships, economic self-reliance and social reintegration among individuals affected by substance dependence.

Mr. Sudesh Kumar (name changed), a 42-year-old resident of Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh, belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, has successfully overcome alcohol addiction with rehabilitation support under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.

Having studied up to high school, Rajesh worked as a driver and also undertook daily wage labour to support his wife and two children. However, alcohol addiction gradually affected his personal, professional and financial well-being, resulting in irregular employment, financial instability and strained family relationships.

With a determination to lead a healthier life and secure a better future for his children, and with encouragement from his family members, Sudesh Kumar approached the Sarvodaya Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) in Annamayya district of Andhra Pradesh.

On February 5, 2026, Sudesh received comprehensive de-addiction treatment and rehabilitation assistance under the NAPDDR Scheme, which included individual counselling, family counselling, group counselling, yoga, meditation, motivational sessions and psychosocial support.

For individuals undergoing recovery from substance dependence, access to structured rehabilitation and sustained counselling is an important enabler of personal and social transformation. These interventions helped Sudesh understand the harmful effects of alcohol addiction, rebuild his self-confidence and develop a positive outlook towards life. Family counselling further strengthened his relationships with family members.

As per the follow-up conducted on April 27, 2026, Sudesh had completely abstained from alcohol consumption and was leading a sober and responsible life. He had also established a small tea shop in Kadapa, enabling him to earn a stable income, support his family and work towards economic self-reliance.

Beyond providing de-addiction treatment, the NAPDDR Scheme seeks to promote behavioural transformation, emotional well-being, social reintegration and sustainable rehabilitation, thereby enabling individuals to lead healthy, productive and dignified lives.

Sudesh’s  journey from alcohol dependence to recovery and entrepreneurship highlights the significance of targeted rehabilitation interventions in restoring self-confidence, strengthening livelihood opportunities and bringing positive changes in the lives of individuals and their families.

The initiative reflects the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s sustained commitment towards holistic rehabilitation, social empowerment, economic self-reliance and inclusive socio-economic development, contributing to the larger vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047.

2338694.title: Advancing Global Statistical Partnerships: MoSPI’s Vision for Knowledge Exchange and Institutional Cooperation
2338694.body_html:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Advancing Global Statistical Partnerships: MoSPI’s Vision for Knowledge Exchange and Institutional Cooperation
MoSPI’s transformative Initiatives on SDGs and Statistical Database Stewardship for fortifying the architecture of India’s National Statistical System showcased
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:55PM by PIB Delhi

Reaffirming India’s abiding commitment to partnership and shared progress in the field of official statistics, the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA)- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), in collaboration with the National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD), organised an interaction of international participants from twenty-six partner countries of the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Programme on 17 November 2026. The engagement offered the visiting delegates a meaningful vantage point on the manner in which India builds, governs and sustains its statistical institutions.

The occasion was graced by the eminent presence of Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics) and Dr. Purnendu Kishore Banerjee, Director General (Data Governance)-In-Charge, MoSPI, along with senior officers of the Ministry, including Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division and Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, Social Statistics Division. Dr. P. C. Parida, Director, NILERD and faculty of NILERD also participated.

Setting the tone for the day’s deliberations, Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division recalled India’s timeless message that the world is one family and that all people are one’s own kin. Anchored in this civilisational outlook, he stressed that the country has consistently striven to extend its support to other nations in improving and strengthening their statistical systems. Ms. Reena Singh, Deputy Director General, NSSTA, while moderating the interaction, emphasized the crucial role of MoSPI in strengthening the country’s official statistical system ensuring the availability of reliable, credible and timely statistical information, and supporting evidence based policymaking across sectors. She also emphasized the pivotal role of NSSTA for strengthening the capacity of the statistical system in India.

The keynote address, delivered by Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), furnished the delegates with a comprehensive panorama of the National Statistical System of India. In the course of his address, he elaborated on the institutional framework, the organisational structure and the functioning of the Statistical System, thereby giving an overview of the various statistical products and varied surveys undertaken by MoSPI.

The substantive core of the interaction consisted of two technical sessions. The first session on “Overview of SDG Monitoring in India” was led by Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, SSD, Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, SSD, and Shri Indradeep Roy Chaudhary, Director, SSD. The session provided an overview of more than 270 national indicators identified by MoSPI for monitoring SDGs and its continuous process of alignment with the Global Indicator Framework. The session on “Developing and Managing Statistical Database” was presented by Shri Vishnu Mishra, Director, Data Innovation and Information Division (DIID), MoSPI which provided insights into the e-Sankhyiki portal, microdata portal, semantic search, Model Context Protocol (MCP) micro and macro datasets etc.

Bringing the proceedings to a close, Shri P. K. Banerjee, Director General (Data Governance)-In-Charge, engaged with the international participants and shared valuable perspectives on India’s statistical ecosystem in his concluding remarks. He urged the delegates to carry the learnings of the interaction back with them and apply them towards strengthening the statistical systems of their respective countries.

India reaffirms its unwavering commitment to all participating nations through sustained technical cooperation, knowledge-sharing and institutional partnership to translate shared learning  into actionable outcomes.

2338683.title: ​​​​​​​Union Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari Calls for Greater Focus on Road Safety, Construction Quality and Sustainable Technologies
2338683.body_html:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
​​​​​​​Union Minister Shri Nitin Gadkari Calls for Greater Focus on Road Safety, Construction Quality and Sustainable Technologies
At the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress in Hyderabad, Minister emphasises innovation, use of alternative materials, scientific planning and accountability in road infrastructure development
Posted On: 19 NOV 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari today addressed the 85th Annual Session of the Indian Roads Congress (IRC) in Hyderabad, Telangana, and called upon engineers, contractors, consultants and policymakers to work collectively towards improving the quality, safety, durability and sustainability of India's road infrastructure.

The event was attended by Telangana Chief Minister Shri A. Revanth Reddy, Minister for Roads and Buildings, Telangana, Shri Komatireddy Venkat Reddy, President IRC Shri L K Padhi, Director General (Road Development) & Special Secretary, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Shri Sudip Chaudhary, and Secretary General, Indian Roads Congress, Shri Rahul Gupta, among other dignitaries, senior government officials, engineers and industry representatives.

Congratulating the engineers, contractors and officials for their contribution to the development of the country's National Highway network, Shri Gadkari acknowledged their dedicated efforts and technical expertise. He emphasised that continuous upgradation of knowledge, research, innovation and adoption of global best practices are essential for developing future-ready infrastructure.

Highlighting the role of the Indian Roads Congress in setting technical standards for the road sector, the Minister noted that IRC has developed several technical codes, guidelines, manuals and publications that guide road infrastructure development in the country. He urged the organisation to strengthen international cooperation and facilitate greater exchange of knowledge, technology and successful practices to keep Indian standards aligned with evolving global developments.

Focus on Construction Quality and Road Safety

The Minister stressed that quality, safety and durability must remain the foremost priorities in road construction. He called for greater accountability among contractors, consultants and engineers and stated that any compromise in construction quality must invite appropriate action. He also emphasised transparent, time-bound and result-oriented implementation of highway projects.

Shri Gadkari underlined the need to improve the quality of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), strengthen technical supervision and ensure effective implementation of road safety audits. He urged engineers to identify and rectify accident-prone locations through proper planning, improved junction design, and provision of flyovers and underpasses wherever required. Emphasising the importance of protecting human lives, he called for a collective commitment towards reducing road accidents and eliminating black spots through better engineering and design.

Innovation and Sustainable Construction Practices

Emphasising the need to reduce construction costs while improving quality, the Minister called for greater use of innovative and alternative construction materials. He highlighted the potential of plastic waste, used tyres, steel slag, municipal solid waste and agricultural residue in road construction, wherever technically suitable.

He also referred to the use of bio-bitumen developed from rice straw and highlighted the potential of research and field applications of alternative materials in promoting sustainable highway construction and reducing dependence on conventional resources.

The Minister encouraged wider adoption of alternative fuels and biofuels in construction equipment, including electric, ethanol, biodiesel, CNG, LNG and hydrogen-based technologies. He highlighted their potential to reduce pollution, lower dependence on imported fossil fuels and create additional opportunities for farmers through the diversification of agricultural produce towards the energy sector.

Shri Gadkari also called for greater use of treated wastewater in construction activities, particularly in view of increasing water stress. He highlighted the importance of recycling municipal waste and reusing available resources in infrastructure development. He further encouraged research into tree transplantation and plantation along highways to strengthen environmental protection.

Road Infrastructure as an Enabler of Economic Growth

The Minister highlighted the role of quality road infrastructure in improving connectivity, reducing travel time and logistics costs, and supporting trade, industry, agriculture and tourism. Referring to the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, he underlined the importance of connecting rural areas through all-weather road networks to improve access to markets and economic opportunities.

He also stressed the need to explore innovative financing mechanisms, including public-private partnerships and monetisation of existing highway assets, to mobilise resources for infrastructure development.

Shri Gadkari urged the Indian Roads Congress to focus not only on developing technical standards and guidelines but also on their effective implementation across the country. He called for greater collaboration among the Central and State Governments, research institutions, industry stakeholders and engineering professionals to address emerging challenges in the road sector.

The Minister expressed confidence that the deliberations at the 85th Annual Session would contribute to the development of safer, more durable, sustainable and technologically advanced road infrastructure in the country.
