2338087.title: Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026 concludes with recommendations to strengthen climate resilience, ecological planning and municipal finance in Himalayan cities
2338087.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026 concludes with recommendations to strengthen climate resilience, ecological planning and municipal finance in Himalayan cities
Two-day Regional Conclave brings together representatives from 11 Himalayan states to address integrated water and sanitation management, climate resilience and ecosystem-based urban development
Ten initiatives, publications and learning resources launched; 18 innovative urban solutions recognised under अrban Learnathon 2.0
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:51PM by PIB Delhi

The Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026, convened by the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), concluded today in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, with recommendations to strengthen urban resilience, ecological planning and sustainable service delivery across the Indian Himalayan Region. The two-day Conclave, held from 17 to 18 November 2026, brought together policymakers, representatives from Himalayan states, urban local bodies, technical experts, academia, civil society organisations and development partners to deliberate on the distinct challenges of mountain urbanisation and identify practical approaches for resilient and sustainable urban development.

The Conclave was inaugurated on 17 November 2026 by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India, under the theme ‘From Water Security to Ecosystem-Based Urban Development: Mainstreaming Resilient Water and Sanitation for Himalayan Cities’.

Delivering the inaugural address, Shri Tokhan Sahu emphasised the importance of regional cooperation, institutional capacity building and knowledge-sharing in addressing the challenges faced by Himalayan cities. Stating that “by pooling knowledge, strengthening local capacities and learning from each other, we can advance solutions for water security, inclusive urban services and dignified sanitation, recognising that challenges do not stop at geographical boundaries”, he called for stronger collaboration among governments, institutions and regional stakeholders. Highlighting the importance of replicating successful urban innovations, he observed that “a solution confined to one city benefits only that city, but a solution shared and replicated has the potential to transform a hundred cities”.

Shri Nitesh Jha, Secretary, Urban Development, Government of Uttarakhand noted that as the source of the Ganga, the Yamuna and other major rivers, Uttarakhand bears a responsibility to every town and village downstream. For this reason, he said, the state treats the management of used water and faecal sludge as a commitment rather than a municipal chore. Tracing the state-led partnership with NIUA since 2019, he highlighted the Septage Management Protocol of 2017 and the co-treatment of septage at existing sewage treatment plants in Ganga towns. He also cited Rudrapur’s faecal sludge treatment plant, the first standalone facility in the state, which was built with support from NIUA. He called on partners, Union ministries and hill states to help design norms and financing that recognise the realities of mountain terrain.
Ms Nameeta Prasad, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), described the Himalayan region as the water tower of Asia, observing that its water crisis stems not from scarcity but from declining springs, pollution, inadequate infrastructure and growing urban demand. Emphasising that Himalayan cities cannot be water secure unless their surrounding ecosystems are healthy, she called for water security to be addressed within a wider ecological framework rather than through centralised infrastructure alone. She highlighted the National Mission on Himalayan Studies (NMHS) as a key platform in this effort, noting that it has supported over 255 projects, including more than 40 on water resource management.

Prof. (Dr) Debolina Kundu, Director, NIUA, highlighted the evolution of Parvat Manthan into a community of practice that brings together mountain states, institutions and regional partners to exchange knowledge, strengthen capacities and develop practical solutions. She noted that the platform has facilitated peer learning, regional cooperation and policy dialogue to support more responsive approaches to the unique challenges of mountain urbanisation.

Shri Vinod Goswami, Director, Urban Development Department, Government of Uttarakhand, emphasised the need for long-term, integrated and regionally coordinated planning. He observed that urbanisation must be understood beyond municipal boundaries, recognising its implications for surrounding rural areas and the wider region. He also highlighted the importance of strengthening the financial sustainability of urban local bodies by effectively utilising available resources and financing opportunities, including the 16th Finance Commission and the Urban Challenge Fund.

Key Areas of Technical Deliberation

The Conclave featured four technical sessions examining disaster resilience, integrated water management, ecological carrying capacity and municipal finance, with a focus on strengthening sustainable urban development in the Indian Himalayan Region.

Session 1: Living on the Edge: Disaster Risk, Fragility, and the Future of Hill Infrastructure

The session examined the vulnerability of Himalayan settlements to natural disasters, climate-related risks and increasing infrastructure pressures. Discussions focused on the need to integrate disaster risk assessments into urban planning, strengthen the resilience of critical infrastructure, adopt development practices suited to fragile mountain environments and improve institutional preparedness for climate-related and geological hazards.

Session 2: Water Beyond Boundaries: Integrated Water Management for Ecosystem Health in Hill Cities

The session focused on the need for integrated water resource management that extends beyond municipal boundaries and recognises the interdependence of urban settlements, watersheds and surrounding ecosystems. Discussions highlighted source sustainability, watershed conservation, integrated water and sanitation planning, improved coordination among institutions and the importance of ecosystem-based approaches to long-term water security.

Session 3: Within Limits: Carrying Capacity and Biodiversity in Hill City Planning

The session recommended institutionalising carrying capacity assessments within statutory master plans, establishing common planning parameters across Himalayan states and integrating water availability, biodiversity conservation and ecological sensitivity into land-use planning. Discussions emphasised regional planning beyond municipal boundaries, transparent environmental monitoring, sustainable mobility and construction practices appropriate to fragile mountain environments.

Session 4: Strengthening Municipal Finance for Sustainable Service Delivery in Hilly Regions

The session recommended predictable fiscal transfers, differentiated infrastructure costing for hill cities, lifecycle financing and stronger municipal own-source revenues. Discussions highlighted tourism-linked revenue instruments, cluster-based planning, project aggregation, institutional capacity building and greater transparency in municipal budgets, accounts and audits to strengthen financial sustainability and service delivery.

Launches and Releases

The inaugural session witnessed the launch of ten initiatives, publications and learning resources focused on sustainable urban development, water and sanitation management, climate resilience, inclusive service delivery and institutional capacity building.

  1. Carrying Capacity Assessment of Haridwar: A Ganga Town in Uttarakhand

The report examines the implications of tourism and population pressures on urban infrastructure and services, offering recommendations for sustainable land-use planning, resource management and urban development.

  1. Roadmap for Transitioning Towards Integrated Citywide Sanitation for Darjeeling Municipality

The report presents a phased approach for strengthening water supply, wastewater management, solid waste management and drainage through integrated planning suited to the geographical and environmental conditions of hill towns.

  1. Built for All: Let's Talk GEDSI in Sanitation

An interactive comic highlighting the importance of gender equity, disability and social inclusion in the planning and delivery of safe, accessible and dignified sanitation services.

  1. Four Seasons, One City: A Year of Climate Change

A story illustrating the impacts of climate-related disasters on urban water and sanitation systems, highlighting practical measures for improving community preparedness and infrastructure resilience.

  1. Himalayan Resilience: Darjeeling – Beyond Postcard

A coffee table book documenting the water, sanitation and waste management challenges experienced in Darjeeling, alongside community initiatives and priorities for sustainable urban development.

  1. Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) E-course

Launched on the National Urban Learning Platform (NULP), the course provides urban officials and sanitation practitioners with practical knowledge to improve workplace safety and promote dignified working conditions for sanitation workers.

  1. Gender, Equity, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) E-course

Launched on NULP, the course supports urban planners, engineers and government officials in incorporating equity, accessibility and inclusion into sanitation infrastructure planning and service delivery.

  1. Water and Sanitation: Sustainable and Resilient Urban Futures E-course

Launched on NULP, the course provides guidance on climate risk assessment, flood and drought preparedness, and the development of resilient and inclusive urban water and sanitation systems.

  1. Training Manual on GIS-based Spatial Mapping for Water and Sanitation Infrastructure Integrating Kobo Toolbox

The manual provides practical guidance on geotagged field data collection, spatial analysis using QGIS and the preparation of maps to support evidence-based water and sanitation planning.

  1. Himalayan Urban Bio-Sheds (HUBS) Initiative for Advancing Ecosystem-based Urban Development

Undertaken by NIUA with support from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the National Mission on Himalayan Studies (NMHS), in partnership with the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), the initiative seeks to integrate water, waste, biodiversity and ecosystem health into a unified urban planning framework. Planned for pilot implementation in three towns across Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Sikkim, HUBS aims to promote urban development approaches that respect ecological boundaries while strengthening essential urban services.

अrban Learnathon 2.0: Recognition of Innovative Urban Solutions

The inaugural session also marked the announcement of the results of अrban Learnathon 2.0, with the awardees felicitated by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs.

Launched on 08 January 2025 during the Capacity for Change Conclave 2025 by Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Union Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, अrban Learnathon 2.0 was designed to identify and recognise innovative solutions to urban challenges. The initiative received 201 entries, of which 84 were shortlisted and 18 solutions were selected for awards across categories covering government bodies, academia, industry and special mentions.

The second edition expanded participation to academia and industry, recognising the importance of collaboration among urban local bodies, research institutions and enterprises in developing innovative and replicable urban solutions. The results are available on the National Urban Learning Platform at https://nulp.niua.org/.

Delivering the closing remarks, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Mishra, Chief Advisor, NIUA, observed that institutional capacity had emerged as a common concern across the Conclave's four technical sessions. He highlighted the importance of genuine decentralisation, integrated planning, sustainable infrastructure financing and recognising the ecological sensitivity of Himalayan settlements. He emphasised that technical studies and knowledge products, including carrying capacity assessments prepared by NIUA, must inform policies, programmes and implementation practices.

Shri Vinod Kumar, Assistant Director, Urban Development Department, Government of Uttarakhand, acknowledged the contributions of NIUA and participating institutions towards strengthening regional cooperation on mountain urbanisation. Highlighting the distinct development challenges of Himalayan settlements, he called for continued collaboration among states, innovation and the adoption of technologies appropriate to mountain environments. He stated, “May the spirit of Parvat Manthan inspire us to deepen cooperation among the Himalayan states, encourage innovation and promote the adoption of appropriate technologies for mountain settlements. Our ultimate objective must be to ensure prosperity and a better quality of life for the people living in these regions.”

Dr Mahreen Matto, Team Lead, NIUA, acknowledged the long-standing partnership of the Government of Uttarakhand and the participation of representatives from 11 Himalayan states. She emphasised the importance of continued collaboration in translating the Conclave's deliberations into actionable knowledge and institutional learning. Stating that “we will ensure that the deliberations of this conclave are carried forward into our forthcoming knowledge products and reports”, she informed participants that the outcomes would be documented and shared for their suggestions and feedback.

The recommendations emerging from the two-day Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026 will inform subsequent efforts to strengthen sustainable urban development across the Indian Himalayan Region.

About Parvat Manthan

Launched by NIUA in 2023, the Parvat Manthan Hill Forum is a regional platform for dialogue, knowledge exchange and collaboration on sustainable mountain urbanisation. Building on earlier editions that addressed decentralised water and sanitation services, waste management and sustainable settlements, Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026 expanded the discussions to include disaster resilience, ecological carrying capacity, biodiversity conservation and long-term infrastructure financing, with the objective of supporting sustainable and resilient urban development in the Indian Himalayan Region.

2338081.title: Union Health Ministry Observes World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026, Calls for Collective Action against AMR
2338081.ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
2338081.body_html:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Ministry Observes World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026, Calls for Collective Action against AMR
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Emphasises One Health Approach under This Year's Theme, ‘One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now’
Smt. Srivastava Urges Responsible Antimicrobial Use and Stronger Infection Prevention Practices to Contain AMR
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, today, inaugurated the national observance of the World Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Awareness Week 2026 at Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi. The week-long observance is significant as it seeks to build greater awareness and collective action against antimicrobial resistance, one of the most urgent threats to public health.

Addressing the event virtually, Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava drew attention to the growing threat of Antimicrobial Resistance, describing it as one of the most serious public health challenges of our time. She noted that medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse. She cautioned that if left unchecked, AMR could undermine decades of medical progress, making even common infections difficult to treat and posing a serious threat to human health.

Referring to this year's theme, ‘One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now’, Smt. Srivastava underscored the need for coordinated action across sectors. Drawing attention to the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, she stressed on the importance of adopting a One Health approach that recognises the interconnectedness of human health, animal health, plant and food systems and the environment. She noted that the improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance, underscoring the need for coordinated action to address this growing threat.

The Union Health Secretary highlighted that the Government of India has accorded high priority to AMR containment. She said that the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025–2029, launched by Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda during World AMR Awareness Week in November 2025, provides a comprehensive framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action across sectors.

She also highlighted the efforts being undertaken by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare through the National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), which focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation.

Highlighting the role of healthcare professionals, Smt. Srivastava stressed that antibiotics should be prescribed only when clinically indicated and in accordance with appropriate treatment guidelines. She also underscored the responsibility of pharmacists in ensuring appropriate dispensing of antimicrobials against valid prescriptions and counselling patients on their correct use.

Urging the public to adopt responsible practices, she advised against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines. She reminded citizens that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza. She also highlighted the importance of hygiene and sanitation, safe water, safe food and vaccination in preventing infections, thereby reducing the need for antibiotic use.

Smt. Srivastava concluded her address by encouraging States and Union Territories, healthcare institutions, educational institutions and community organisations to take the message of AMR awareness to every section of society. She emphasised that the commitment to combat antimicrobial resistance must extend beyond the awareness week, with its success reflected in everyday practices relating to the prescription, dispensing and use of antimicrobials, and effective infection prevention. Calling for collective action, she urged all stakeholders to work together to preserve the effectiveness of essential antimicrobial medicines and safeguard the health of present and future generations.

The meeting participants, which included representatives of various stakeholder organisations, took note of the fact that more than half of antimicrobial sales in India occur without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate. They underscored the urgent need to address these practices and identified several measures that could be scaled up across the country. These include public awareness campaigns; preventing self-prescription of antibiotics; proper disposal of antibiotics and expired medicines; displaying legal warnings at drug shops against the sale of antimicrobials without prescriptions; curbing the production of substandard and spurious medicines; promoting the appropriate use of antibiotics in veterinary medicine, particularly for food-producing animals; and maintaining quality standards in healthcare facilities to prevent the occurrence and spread of infections.

The event was attended by senior officers from the National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC), Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), Department of Animal Husbandry, Indian Medical Association and All India Association of Druggists and Chemists. Senior officers from States and Union Territories also attended the event virtually.

About World Anti Microbial Resistance Awareness Week

World AMR Awareness Week is a global campaign celebrated from 18th to 24th November every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and encourage best practices among the public, One Health stakeholders and policymakers. All these stakeholders play a critical role in reducing the further emergence and spread of AMR.

2338083.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE VALEDICTORY CEREMONY OF THE CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS OF SHRI RAM COLLEGE OF COMMERCE
2338083.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE VALEDICTORY CEREMONY OF THE CENTENARY CELEBRATIONS OF SHRI RAM COLLEGE OF COMMERCE
INDIA HAS THE BEST POOL OF YOUNG TALENT IN THE WORLD AS DEMONSTRATED IN COLLEGES LIKE SRCC: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the Valedictory Ceremony of the Centenary Celebrations of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) in New Delhi today (November 18, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the country's leading educational institutions must evolve into world-class institutions. It will not only help in realizing the national vision of transforming India into a Global Knowledge Superpower but also attract talented students from both within India and abroad for higher education.

 

The President said that during the last ten years, India has remained one of the fastest-growing large economies in the world. The country has achieved unprecedented expansion of infrastructure, revolutionary digital transformation, financial inclusion and social development. There is a conducive start-up ecosystem. ‘Ease of Doing Business’ has been given high priority. At the same time, effective welfare measures have been implemented with the approach of leaving no targeted beneficiary uncovered. Around 50 crore fellow citizens have come out of extreme poverty in recent years. These achievements have been made possible amidst several challenges in the global environment, characterised by uncertainties and ongoing conflicts. The students at this college are fortunate to witness the resilience and success of our economy and learn from it. They will utilise this learning to further accelerate our journey of development.

 

The President said that Bharat is expanding its economic role on the global stage with a new energy and outlook. Our youth will be driving our ambitious endeavours. India has the largest young population in the world and  it also has the best pool of young talent in the world as demonstrated in colleges like SRCC.

 

The President said that ‘Of India, by India, and for India’ is the approach with which our youth should define their aspirations and roles. In this context, ‘by India’ implies that the society and institutions have contributed to the development of capabilities of students. Therefore, they have a special responsibility towards the society and the country.

 

The President was happy to note that the students of SRCC have been scoring high marks and securing top positions in examinations. She said that students of SRCC should demonstrate that wealth creation leads to nation-building; should do well for themselves and also create opportunities for others, especially for the less privileged; should achieve world-class excellence while remaining rooted in the noble Indian values; should use state-of-the-art technologies responsibly with sensitivity; and should pursue professional excellence with empathy, ethics and morality. She expressed confidence that members of the SRCC family will continue to contribute towards the building of Viksit Bharat by 2047 and the glorious journey of our country even beyond.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah congratulates brave Jawans of JKP, Army and CRPF and intelligence agencies for neutralizing Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley, Lateef Bhat
One of his terrorist associates, Umar Nisar, was also neutralised in Kulgam, the day before

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah has congratulated brave Jawans of JKP, Army and CRPF and intelligence agencies for neutralizing Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley, Lateef Bhat, in an operation in Kulgam in the early morning hours today.

2338073.title: Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia to participate in Letter of Intent Distribution Ceremony in Bhopal for upcoming Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior
2338073.body_html:
Ministry of Communications
Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia to participate in Letter of Intent Distribution Ceremony in Bhopal for upcoming Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior
Letters of Intent for land allotment to be distributed to prospective investors
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards realising the vision of establishing Asia’s first Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior, a Letter of Intent (LoI) Distribution Ceremony will be held in Bhopal on November 19, 2026. The programme will be graced by Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Dr. Mohan Yadav and the Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia along with representatives of the telecom industry and industry associations.

The ceremony will mark an important step towards translating investment interest into concrete opportunities for establishing telecom manufacturing facilities in the region. The distribution of Letters of Intent for land allotment will provide prospective investors with an opportunity to participate in the development of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone and contribute to strengthening India's domestic manufacturing capabilities.

The proposed Telecom Manufacturing Zone in Gwalior is envisioned as Asia's first integrated telecom manufacturing cluster. The zone will provide an enabling ecosystem for manufacturing, research and development, innovation and technology partnerships in areas such as mobile devices, optical fibre, telecom equipment and next-generation 5G and 6G technologies.

Under the initiative, the Central Government is providing 100 per cent funding support of ₹493 crore for Phase-I of the project, while the Government of Madhya Pradesh has provided approximately 170 acres of land free of cost, along with investor-friendly incentives. A Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) has also been established for the development of the project, with 51 per cent equity participation from the Government of Madhya Pradesh and 49 per cent from the Department of Telecommunications.

The initiative is aligned with the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and aims to strengthen domestic value chains, promote indigenous design and manufacturing, reduce import dependence, boost exports and position India as a trusted global destination for telecom products and technologies.

The programme will feature a presentation on the project and its roadmap by the Government of Madhya Pradesh, followed by an address on the Government of India's vision for telecom manufacturing. Industry representatives will share their perspectives on investment opportunities and industry participation. The ceremony will also include the distribution of Letters of Intent, followed by addresses by the Union Minister of Communications and the Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh.

The development of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone is expected to strengthen Madhya Pradesh's industrial ecosystem, encourage investment, promote technology-driven entrepreneurship and create new opportunities for skilled employment. It will also contribute to India's broader ambition of emerging as a global hub for telecom manufacturing, innovation and technological advancement.

Through this initiative, the Government of India is reaffirming its commitment to building a robust, self-reliant and globally competitive telecom manufacturing ecosystem under the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat.

2338065.title: Strengthening Educational Opportunities for OBC Girls through Dedicated Hostel Infrastructure
2338065.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Strengthening Educational Opportunities for OBC Girls through Dedicated Hostel Infrastructure
Ministry-Supported 200-Seat OBC Girls Hostel Project at Women’s Polytechnic, Hapania, Tripura to Strengthen Access to Safe Residential Facilities and Higher Education
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi

The OBC Girls Hostel project at Women’s Polytechnic, Hapania, West Tripura, is an initiative supported by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, aimed at strengthening educational opportunities for girl students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community.

Access to safe and affordable residential facilities plays a significant role in promoting higher education among young women, particularly those belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged communities and residing in distant and rural areas.

Initiated during the financial year 2024–25, the hostel project envisages a dedicated residential facility with a planned capacity of 200 seats. The facility is expected to strengthen boarding arrangements for eligible OBC girl students and provide a conducive environment for pursuing their academic aspirations.

For students residing far from educational institutions, access to suitable residential facilities is an important enabler of academic advancement. The hostel seeks to address accommodation-related challenges and create an environment where students can focus on their education, skill development and personal growth.

The project is being implemented by the Rural Development Department, Government of Tripura, on behalf of the OBC Welfare Department, with funding support from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. The initiative reflects the importance of Centre-State collaboration in strengthening educational infrastructure and promoting inclusive socio-economic development.

The hostel will have essential amenities, including electricity, proper sanitation and hygiene facilities, safe drinking water and adequate security arrangements, to ensure a safe, healthy and supportive residential environment for students.

Beyond providing residential accommodation, the hostel project also seeks to encourage leadership qualities, healthy competition, voluntary participation, social harmony, mutual cooperation and a spirit of national integration among students.

The hostel facility is expected to strengthen educational accessibility for OBC girls and encourage their participation in higher education.

The initiative reflects the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s sustained commitment towards women’s empowerment, inclusive education and equitable access to opportunities through targeted infrastructure development, contributing to the larger vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

2338056.title: Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports invites citizens to participate in Constitution Day Quiz 2026 from Nov 18 to 26; 500 Winners to Receive Cash Rewards
2338056.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2338056.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports invites citizens to participate in Constitution Day Quiz 2026 from Nov 18 to 26; 500 Winners to Receive Cash Rewards
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, in collaboration with MyGov and My Bharat, has invited citizens to participate in the Constitution Day Quiz 2026, being organised on the occasion of Constitution Day on 26th November. The quiz will be open from 18th November 2026 to 26th November 2026. A total of 500 winners will be selected, with the top 100 winners receiving a cash reward of INR 5,000 each and the next 400 winners receiving INR 2,000 each. All participants will receive an E-Participation Certificate.

The Constitution of India is the cornerstone of the world's largest democracy, reflecting the ideals of Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity. It safeguards the rights of citizens, defines their fundamental duties and strengthens the democratic values that unite the nation.

Continuing the endeavour to promote constitutional awareness, the quiz encourages citizens to test their knowledge and learn more about the making of the Indian Constitution, their voting rights and the values that shape the country's democracy. It will provide an opportunity to celebrate India's constitutional heritage, understand citizens' rights and reaffirm their duties towards building a Viksit Bharat.

Citizens can participate in the quiz through https://www.quiz.mygov.in and https://mybharat.gov.in/quizzes/yuva/. It will be available in English and Hindi.

2338048.title: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Chairs 13th Governing Body Meeting of National Institute of Unani Medicine
2338048.body_html:
AYUSH
Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Chairs 13th Governing Body Meeting of National Institute of Unani Medicine
Shri Jadhav Calls for Timely Action, Accountability and Expansion of Unani Education and Research
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:06PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State in the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Shri Prataprao Jadhav, today chaired the 13th Governing Body meeting of the National Institute of Unani Medicine (NIUM) at Kartavya Bhawan-I, New Delhi.

Highlighting NIUM's role in advancing Unani education, research and healthcare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav noted that the institute currently has 71 students across 10 postgraduate departments. He highlighted the proposed expansion through five additional postgraduate departments, 35 additional seats and a Department of Integrative and Translational Research.

Shri Jadhav also highlighted the development of NIUM's second campus at Ghaziabad, near Delhi, with a proposed 200-bed referral hospital, postgraduate education and research facilities. Welcoming the proposal for 24 seats for foreign students within the existing intake capacity, he said it would strengthen international academic engagement and reflect the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम् ).

The Minister outlined three key expectations from NIUM — timeliness, accountability and service — stressing that pending matters should be addressed promptly and clear timelines and responsibilities assigned to every project. Union minister emphasised that healthcare services and treatments developed by the institute must reach even the poorest sections of society.

Prof. Saiyad Shah Alam, Director, National Institute of Unani Medicine (NIUM), Bengaluru, welcomed the Union Minister and the Secretary, Ministry of Ayush. He also made a presentation highlighting the institute’s activities, achievements and proposed initiatives.

The meeting was attended by Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha; Additional Secretary and Financial Adviser, Shri Hoyeeda Abbas; Additional Chief Secretary, Department of Finance, Government of Karnataka, Shri Ritesh Kumar Singh; Advisor (Unani), Ministry of Ayush, Dr. M.A. Qasmi; President, Board of Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa, Prof. Asim Ali Khan; and Director General, Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), Dr. N. Zaheer Ahmed, among other senior officials.

The meeting concluded with a focus on strengthening institutional governance, ensuring effective implementation of approved initiatives and enhancing coordination among stakeholders for the institute's future development.

2338038.title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches Curtain Raiser for India International Science Festival (IISF) 2026, Calls for Taking Science Beyond Labs to Empower Youth and Startups
2338038.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches Curtain Raiser for India International Science Festival (IISF) 2026, Calls for Taking Science Beyond Labs to Empower Youth and Startups
Pune to Host the 12th Edition of IISF Across Five Premier Research and Academic Campuses from December 19–22 Under the Theme "India’s Science, World’s Future"
Under PM Modi’s Vision of Vishwa Bandhu Bharat, Indian Science Is Delivering Solutions for All Humanity, From Indigenous Bio-Experiments on the ISS to Frontier Biotech: Dr. Jitendra Singh
India Has Reimagined Its National Science Calendar Around Two Distinct Flagship Pillars, Academic Conclave ESTIC in New Delhi and Public-Centric Festival IISF Across the Country, Says Union Minister
Nationwide Build-Up Across 13 Cities with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA) Will Connect Students, Women, Farmers, and Entrepreneurs with Working Laboratories Ahead of Pune Mega Event: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today formally launched the Curtain Raiser for the 12th edition of the India International Science Festival (IISF) 2026, alongside unveiling the official festival website and brochure, at the National Media Centre in New Delhi.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that IISF 2026, scheduled to be held in Pune from December 19 to 22 under the theme "India’s Science, World’s Future" (Bharat ka Vigyan, Vishwa ka Bhavishya), embodies Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Vishwa Bandhu Bharat, where Indian scientific breakthroughs serve the welfare of the entire humankind. Explaining that the theme is already being translated into action rather than remaining a slogan, the Minister cited indigenous research kits developed by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and carried to the International Space Station (ISS) by Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla, whose experimental outcomes will benefit the whole world. As India moves toward a frontline global position on the path to Viksit Bharat 2047, Dr. Jitendra Singh added, Indian science will increasingly shape the global scientific ecosystem.

The curtain raiser ceremony, organised by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Ministry of Science & Technology, in collaboration with Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA), was graced on the dais by Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood; Secretary, Department of Biotechnology, Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale; and National Organising Secretary, Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA), Dr. Shiv Kumar Sharma.

Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) and Director General, CSIR, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi; Secretary, Department of Science and Technology (DST), Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare; Secretary, and Director, BRIC–National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), Pune, Dr. Thomas Pucadyil, along with senior scientists, institutional directors, and officials from participating departments, also attended the event.

Speaking on the strategic transformation of India’s scientific engagements over the past few years, Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that the government took a conscious decision to replace scattered, repetitive gatherings, including the erstwhile Indian Science Congress, with two flagship national events carrying distinct identities. While the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC), inaugurated annually by the Prime Minister in New Delhi with the participation of over 13 ministries and Nobel Laureates, serves as an academic-driven conclave exploring frontier themes, IISF brings a festive, public-facing character with international resonance. By rotating the venue to different regions, after Chandigarh, Hyderabad, Goa, and Delhi, bringing IISF for the first time to Pune leverages the western hub’s vibrant academic, research, and industrial ecosystem.

Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that IISF 2026 is designed to communicate complex, futuristic domains, ranging from gene editing, antibodies, and insulin production to next-generation energy sources and an immersive, larger-than-life walk-through 3D cell, in an engaging format tailored for diverse stakeholders. Beyond academic talks, including a special lecture by 2001 Nobel Laureate Sir Tim Hunt, the festival creates dedicated pathways for children, youth, women, existing and aspiring startups, entrepreneurs, and industry through B2B meetings, hackathons, and science safaris so young minds can discover their aptitudes and turn ideas into enterprises.

Commending Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA) and Dr. Shiv Kumar Sharma for championing a "whole-of-government, whole-of-science, whole-of-nation, and whole-of-society" approach, Dr. Jitendra Singh lauded VIBHA’s pivotal role in spearheading curtain raiser events across 13 cities, including Chennai, Kolkata, Dehradun, Thiruvananthapuram, Pune, Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Imphal, Indore, Mohali, and Ahmedabad, leading up to the Pune festival. He also urged media representatives to actively participate in and travel to Pune to carry India’s science story to every corner of the country.

Principal Scientific Adviser Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood described IISF 2026 as a unique celebration of science as a collective national endeavour aimed at bringing young people into the scientific fold and embedding scientific temper into public consciousness beyond research laboratories. Connecting the tagline Bharat ka Vigyan, Vishwa ka Bhavishya with India’s timeless philosophy of VasudhaivaKutumbakam, Prof. Sood stated that India has repeatedly demonstrated its willingness to share homegrown innovations at scale, from Vaccine Maitri to Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), and expressed confidence that the energy of IISF 2026 will inspire youth to drive cutting-edge, people-centric innovations for Viksit Bharat.

In his welcome remarks, DBT Secretary Dr. Rajesh S. Gokhale stated that since its inception in 2015, IISF has belonged to the people, uniting curious students, inspiring teachers, small-town innovators, and farmers practising everyday soil engineering. Describing IISF at its core as a platform connecting Samaj, Sarkar, aur Bazaar (Society, Government, and Market) through science, where societal needs guide research, government empowers innovation, and markets convert discoveries into public goods, Dr. Gokhale informed that the 2026 edition brings together major science departments alongside the Department of Atomic Energy and NITI Aayog’s Atal Innovation Mission (AIM).

During the programme, BRIC–NCCS Director Dr. Thomas Pucadyil presented the detailed blueprint of IISF 2026, which will be held under the banner "One Nation, One Science Festival" across five closely located campuses in Pune: BRIC–National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), CSIR–National Chemical Laboratory (NCL), Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Pune, Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), and COEP Technological University.

Spanning 26 programmes across 17 working laboratory venues with the participation of seven Union Ministries and Departments and 16 national institutions, the four-day festival will feature a Global Summit on Biomanufacturing aligned with the BioE3 Policy, a Clinicians–Academia Conclave, "The New Nalanda" Science and Technology Village for 1,800 students and 200 teachers, a Student–Scientist Interaction Programme for 1,200 students, "The Gurukula" teachers' workshop, an eight-zone Science Safari, and a public Science–Technology–Defence–Space Expo showcasing Chandrayaan-3, Gaganyaan, INS Vikrant, Mission Shakti, and national missions in quantum, semiconductors, and deep ocean exploration.

Concluding with a strong policy and global outreach agenda, IISF 2026 will also host Vision Sansad for 150 institutional heads, a Science Diplomacy Conclave, a Global S&T Alliance spanning three continents, the National Social Organisations and Institutions Meet (NSOIM) with 150 NGOs, Nari Shakti, Vigyanika, and SHIV-DURG celebrating the engineering heritage of Maratha forts. The festival is expected to yield concrete national deliverables, including the Vision Sansad Declaration 2026, the NSOIM Declaration, an IISF 2026 Statement on Science Diplomacy with a bio-diplomacy roadmap, and a National Roadmap for Biomanufacturing, while identifying promising student innovations for mentoring and incubation.

2338016.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
MoD inks Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for upgradation & obsolescence management of Barak Point Defence Missile System for Indian Navy
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Defence has signed a contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgradation and obsolescence management of Barak Point Defence Missile System onboard Indian Navy ships at an overall cost of Rs 1,976.40 crore. The contract, under Other Capital Procurement Procedure, was inked in the presence of Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi on November 18, 2026.

The upgradation of the system would ensure enhanced features and potent range anti-air defence capability of the Indian Naval platforms. As part of the contract, a comprehensive upgrade of hardware and software of the system would be undertaken.

2337997.title: Raksha Mantri visits Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Naval Base in Yokosuka
2337997.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri visits Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force Naval Base in Yokosuka
Growing India-Japan maritime cooperation is a reflection of deep trust & shared commitment towards a free, open & rules-based Indo-Pacific: Shri Rajnath Singh
“India has emerged as one of the fastest-growing major economies despite global challenges, defence sector is witnessing unprecedented growth”
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi

“The growing maritime cooperation between India and Japan is a reflection of the deep trust and shared commitment of the two nations towards a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh in a post on X following his visit to the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (JMSDF) Naval Base in Yokosuka on November 18, 2026, along with Japan’s Minister of Defense Mr Shinjiro Koizumi. Upon his arrival in Japan, Raksha Mantri commenced his engagements with a visit to the Ministry of Defense, where he was received by his Japanese counterpart.

Shri Rajnath Singh was accorded a ceremonial Guard of Honour, following which the two Ministers interacted briefly at the Ministry. They, later, travelled to the JMSDF Naval Base in a Japan Self-Defense Forces (JSDF) helicopter. At the Naval Base, the two Ministers toured the Mogami-class multi-mission frigate JS Natori.

本日小泉進次郎防衛大臣(@shinjirokoiz)とともに 横須賀の海上自衛隊基地を訪問し、もがみ型多機能護衛艦「なとり」を視察しました。 インドと日本の海洋分野における協力関係の進展は自由で開かれた法の支配に基づくインド太平洋の実現に向けた、両国間の深い信頼と共通の決意を反映するものです。

— Rajnath Singh (@rajnathsingh) November 18, 2026

Raksha Mantri also interacted with members of the Indian diaspora in Tokyo at an event organised by the Embassy of India. Addressing the gathering, he highlighted India's remarkable economic transformation, asserting that the country has emerged as one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, despite challenges arising from the situation in West Asia.

Highlighting the unprecedented growth in India’s defence sector, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that domestic defence production has crossed a record Rs 1.80 lakh crore, up from Rs 48,000 crore a decade ago. He added that defence exports have registered a remarkable increase from Rs 600 crore to an all-time high of Rs 38,000 crore, reflecting India's growing indigenous capabilities and expanding footprint in the global defence market.

Emphasising the Government's zero-tolerance policy towards corruption, Raksha Mantri stated that corruption has been significantly curbed over the last 12 years, with benefits of welfare schemes reaching their intended beneficiaries. “No one can question the integrity of our Government,” he added. He also highlighted the Government's efforts towards poverty alleviation and the significant improvements in sanitation and cleanliness across the country.

Raksha Mantri is on a two-day visit to Japan. On November 19, 2026, he will participate in the 4th India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers' Dialogue (2+2) and hold bilateral discussions with Japan's Minister of Defense. The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by Raksha Mantri and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar, along with Mr Shinjiro Koizumi and Japan's Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Toshimitsu Motegi. The bilateral meeting between Shri Rajnath Singh and Mr Shinjiro Koizumi will be their third meeting this year.

2337988.title: NAMASTE Scheme Promotes Safer Working Conditions And Dignity For A Sanitation Worker Mr Sinu In Palakkad, Kerala
2337988.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NAMASTE Scheme Promotes Safer Working Conditions And Dignity For A Sanitation Worker Mr Sinu In Palakkad, Kerala
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi

For 47-year-old Sinu (name changed), the PPE kit represents more than protective equipment. It reflects recognition of the occupational risks faced by sanitation workers and reinforces the importance of safety, dignity and respect for those who play an essential role in maintaining clean and healthy communities.

For years, Mr Sinu, sanitation worker from Palakkad, Kerala, had carried out his duties while facing daily exposure to waste, dust and potentially harmful gases. The absence of adequate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) exposed him to occupational health risks, including respiratory conditions, skin infections and other work-related illnesses.

As the primary earning member and sole financial support for his family, any health setback could have affected the well-being and financial stability of his household. Despite these challenges, he remained committed to his work and aspired to perform his duties in safer conditions, with dignity and confidence.

Mr Sinu got opportunity on 7 October 2025, when he received a complete PPE kit under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. This proved a significant step towards improving his working conditions. The kit included a safety helmet, safety goggles, a gas mask with filter, nitrile gloves, gum boots and full-body protective clothing.

The protective equipment has helped reduce his direct exposure to hazardous substances while carrying out sanitation-related activities. With access to essential safety gear, he is now able to perform his duties with greater confidence and an improved sense of workplace security.

The intervention has brought a meaningful improvement to his working conditions by addressing a longstanding concern about occupational safety. Although the assistance did not result in a direct change in income, it has helped lower potential health risks and strengthened his confidence in continuing his livelihood while taking better precautions for his well-being.

Through the NAMASTE Scheme, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote the safety, dignity and well-being of sanitation workers by facilitating access to protective equipment and safer working practices. The initiative reflects the Government’s commitment to ensuring that sanitation workers can carry out their essential duties with greater protection and dignity.

2337978.title: MSDE Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on advancing inclusive skilling and economic participation of persons with disabilities
2337978.ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
2337978.body_html:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on advancing inclusive skilling and economic participation of persons with disabilities
Dialogue focuses on accessible training, meaningful employment and pathways to economic independence
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) held an interaction with Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, on strengthening disability inclusion in skill development and expanding pathways to employment and entrepreneurship. The engagement formed part of the Special Rapporteur’s official visit to India.

The interaction provided an opportunity to examine how skill development systems can support the dignity, autonomy and economic participation of persons with disabilities. The dialogue centred on addressing barriers across the journey from access to training and certification to employment, retention and career progression, in keeping with the principles of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD).

Speaking on the engagement, Shri Niranjan Kumar Sudhansu, Additional Secretary, MSDE said, “An inclusive skill ecosystem must recognise both the diversity of learners and the equal worth of their aspirations. For persons with disabilities, access to training must translate into the freedom to choose a vocation, demonstrate competence and progress in the world of work. Our endeavour is to embed accessibility across the skilling journey and strengthen the connection between learning and livelihoods. The measure of our progress must be the opportunities people are able to exercise and the economic independence they are able to achieve.”

The engagement brought into focus the importance of accessible training infrastructure, digital learning platforms, learning materials and assessment processes. Reasonable accommodation, assistive technologies and the capacity of trainers and assessors were identified as important considerations in enabling learners with different disabilities to participate on an equal basis. The discussions also underscored the importance of embedding accessibility and appropriate support within mainstream training programmes, alongside disability-specific interventions, to enable greater participation and inclusion.

The dialogue also addressed the relationship between skilling and labour market inclusion. Industry engagement, accessible workplaces and support during the transition from training to employment are critical to ensuring that acquired skills lead to sustained livelihoods. The discussions also emphasised upon the enabling measures to enhance the participation of persons with disabilities in skill training and government employment, while encouraging greater inclusion and employment opportunities in the private sector.

Entrepreneurship and self-employment were also discussed as important pathways to economic independence, including the role of access to finance, mentoring, technology and markets in supporting entrepreneurs with disabilities.

Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities said, “The right to work begins with having a real opportunity to learn, choose and participate. Inclusive vocational training must equip persons with disabilities for the full range of opportunities in a changing economy, with accessibility and reasonable accommodation built into its design. Meaningful participation of persons with disabilities and their representative organisations is essential to this process. Their experience and expertise can help institutions translate commitments into practical changes that advance equality and independence.”

The dialogue also highlighted the role of evidence in strengthening disability inclusion, including through better understanding of participation, training outcomes and pathways to employment. Particular attention was drawn to addressing barriers faced by women with disabilities and persons in rural and underserved areas.

The engagement situated inclusive skilling within the wider objective of enabling persons with disabilities to participate as equal contributors to economic and social development. It provided a platform for exchanging perspectives on how policy, institutional practice, technology and employer participation can work together to expand opportunity.

The United Nations Special Rapporteur on the rights of persons with disabilities is an independent expert appointed by the Human Rights Council. The mandate promotes the rights of persons with disabilities through dialogue, country visits, recommendations and the exchange of good practices.

2337970.title: National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction Strengthens India’s Efforts Towards a Drug-Free Society
2337970.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction Strengthens India’s Efforts Towards a Drug-Free Society
Focuses on Preventive Education, Awareness, Identification, Counselling, Treatment, Rehabilitation and Social Reintegration
Article 47 of the Constitution Mandates the State to Endeavour to Prohibit Consumption of Intoxicating Drinks and Drugs Injurious to Health
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been implementing a scheme for the prevention of alcoholism and substance abuse since 1985-86, reflecting its sustained commitment towards addressing substance dependence through preventive, therapeutic and rehabilitative interventions. This is in accordance with its Constitutional mandate and commitment to address alcoholism and substance abuse while building a healthy, inclusive and socially empowered society.

The Article 47 of the Constitution directs the State to endeavour to bring about prohibition of the consumption, except for medicinal purposes, of intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the magnitude of the challenge was highlighted by the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India, conducted in 2018 by the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, New Delhi, and released in February 2019. The survey provided important insights into the extent and pattern of substance use across the country and underscored the need for comprehensive interventions, he said.

According to the survey, approximately 16 crore people consumed alcohol in India, of whom more than 5.7 crore required assistance for harmful or dependent use. Around 3.1 crore people used cannabis products, while 2.26 crore used opioids. Of these, approximately 25 lakh individuals were dependent on cannabis, while nearly 77 lakh required assistance for opioid use, the Official informed.

The Official added the survey further revealed that more than 7 crore individuals were affected by substance use disorders, including nearly 1.2 crore children and 58 lakh women, highlighting the importance of sustained awareness, early intervention, accessible treatment and rehabilitation services.

The Official said the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) has been designed to address the multifaceted challenges associated with substance use through a comprehensive and coordinated approach.

 

The Ministry continues to strengthen preventive and rehabilitative efforts while promoting a compassionate, supportive and inclusive approach towards individuals affected by substance use disorders, he added.

He said that NAPDDR is implemented as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with Central Sector components and focuses on two key objectives.

The Official said the first objective is to reduce drug demand through preventive education, awareness generation, identification, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation. The second objective is to reduce the stigma and discrimination associated with drug dependence, which often create barriers to the social acceptance and reintegration of affected individuals, he said.

He said the Plan recognises that addressing substance dependence requires not only treatment and rehabilitation but also an enabling social environment in which individuals can seek assistance without fear of discrimination or exclusion.

The Official said the awareness generation and preventive education play a significant role in informing individuals, families and communities about the harmful consequences of substance use. Early identification and timely counselling, along with access to appropriate treatment and rehabilitation facilities, are essential components of the national response, the Official said.

He further said that reducing stigma and discrimination is equally important to ensure that individuals recovering from substance dependence can return to their families and communities and participate meaningfully in society.

The Official said with its focus on prevention, awareness, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration, the Ministry is working towards building a healthier and drug-free society, in alignment with the constitutional vision and the broader goal of inclusive socio-economic development.

2337946.title: Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue strong financial performance in first half of FY2026-27
2337946.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue strong financial performance in first half of FY2026-27
PSBs’ profitability soars to highest ever with aggregate net profit of Rs. 1,09,540 crore, growing by 16.9% y-o-y
Total PSBs business crosses Rs. 300 lakh crore; with y-o-y growth at 15.5%
Gross advances of PSBs grew to ₹127 lakh crore, registering a robust growth of 18.8% evenly panned across retail, agriculture and MSME segments
PSBs record historic low stressed assets, with gross NPA ratio declining to 1.69% and net NPA ratio to 0.33% as on 30.09.2026
Systemic reforms, improved governance and Government’s commitment of healthy PSBs manifest through improved financial performance of PSBs in profitability, business growth, asset quality and capital position
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

The sustained improvement in financial health across different financial parameters, including, inter alia, capital adequacy, business growth, low slippages, healthy asset quality and outstandingly improved profitability, establishes the complete turnaround in overall functioning of Public Sector Banks (PSBs). It shows that PSBs are not only making profit but also meeting the requirements of credit supply need with improved underwriting capabilities, aided by technology and higher governance standards.

PSBs’ aggregate net profit reached ₹1.10 lakh crore with 16.9% y-o-y growth and aggregate operating profit reached ₹1.81 lakh crore with 13.9% y-o-y growth. Return on assets of PSBs continue to improve, reaching 1.11% with y-o-y improvement of 3bps. The continued improvement in profitability in both net and operating profit for the fifth consecutive year shows fruitful outcome of enablement of deeply engaged reforms drive and establishment of better governance standards by the Government.

Aggregate business of PSBs grew by 15.5% y-o-y to ₹301.6 lakh crore as on 30.9.2026, crossing the ₹300 lakh crore business mark for the first time. While aggregate deposits grew by 13.1% y-o-y to reach ₹275 lakh crore, the aggregate advances grew at 18.8% y-o-y to reach ₹136.4 lakh crore. The robust credit growth having evenly panned out across different segments, i.e. Retail, Agriculture, MSME, shows PSBs’ continued support to grassroot economic development, inculcation of entrepreneurship and deepening financial inclusion. Credit growth for retail, agriculture and MSME loans was recorded at 17%, 19.5%, 20.4%, respectively.

PSBs’ asset quality remains in continual improvement, recording another long-time low, with Gross NPA ratio declining to 1.69% and Net NPA ratio declining to 0.33%. Low levels of NPAs are aided by better underwriting standards visible through low slippages of 0.62% and continually focused collections efforts visible through improved recoveries and upgradations of 21.1%. All PSBs are now having provisioning coverage ratio of above 90%, reflecting prudent banking practices and resilient financial performance.

Capital buffers of PSBs remain well above regulatory minimum benchmark through higher retained earnings and strong capital raising, showing availability of adequate cushion to support credit growth while also having capability to absorb systemic shocks. CRAR of PSBs was at 16.89% as on 30.9.2026, improved by 93bps y-o-y. The improvement was also aided by decline in RWA density by 94bps y-o-y to 47.9%.

Cost to income ratio of PSBs also improved by 191 bps y-o-y to 47.38% for H1FY2026-27, aided by decline in cost per asset to 1.60% by 14bps y-o-y. The improved operational efficiency shows gains of investment in technologies and digital transformation, a reflection of efficient cost management.

Performance of PSBs is true reflection of outcomes of institutionalisation of reforms by the Government in PSBs, primarily aimed at better governance standards, improved operational efficiency, prudency in banking practices, enhanced risk management and continual adaptability of technology. The steps taken by the Government in improving operational standards of PSBs is now being reflected in the financial performance, aimed supporting India’s growth aspirations of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
One-day capacity building workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” organised in Kolkata, West Bengal
MoSPI is accelerating India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 through robust Sustainable Development Goal monitoring framework at the State and UT levels
The workshop focuses on strengthening State/UT Indicator Frameworks by supporting States/UTs currently developing their indicator frameworks and featuring sub-national monitoring best practices
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), in collaboration with the Department of Planning, Statistics and Programme Monitoring, Government of West Bengal and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), organised a one-day Capacity Building Workshop on “Strengthening Sub-National SDG Monitoring” in Kolkata, West Bengal on 18th November, 2026. The workshop brought together government officials from States and Union Territories that are in process of development of their respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks (SIFs/UTIFs) and the three (3) States/UT sharing best practices, with the aim of strengthening institutional capacities and providing targeted technical support to advance the process. Around 50 participants attended the workshop, comprising officers from MoSPI, UNDP, and States/UTs-West Bengal, Maharashtra, Delhi, Odisha, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

 

With around four years remaining to achieve the 2030 Agenda, strengthening sub-national monitoring systems is critical to advancing SDG localisation and translating national commitments into measurable outcomes at the State/UT levels. State/UT-level monitoring enables governments to track progress against SDG targets, identify development gaps and align policies and interventions with local priorities.

As per SDGs-National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2026, 33 States and Union Territories have developed their respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks. Strengthening the remaining frameworks and improving existing monitoring systems is important to ensure comprehensive SDG monitoring across the country.

In the inaugural session, Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, Social Statistics Division, MoSPI, emphasised the importance of strengthening monitoring systems at the State and local levels. She highlighted that national-level data alone cannot capture the diversity of development challenges across India. State and District Indicator Frameworks are essential to translate national SDG commitments into locally relevant priorities and measurable outcomes. She also underlined the need to strengthen statistical capacities and improve the quality and timeliness of data.

Shri Pawan Kadyan, Senior Special Secretary, Department of Finance, Government of West Bengal, highlighted the need for State Indicator Frameworks to reflect ground realities and local development priorities. He emphasised that monitoring should extend to districts, blocks and Gram Sabhas. He also stressed the need to move beyond tracking scheme implementation and fund utilisation towards measuring actual development outcomes, enabling a shift towards outcome-oriented governance. Representative of UNDP, Mr. Jaimon Uthup, Policy Specialist emphasized the commitment to supporting the Government of India and States/UTs in building robust data systems, technical capacities, and inclusive monitoring mechanisms.

Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, highlighted the ongoing statistical reforms undertaken by MoSPI to address emerging data needs and strengthen the evidence base for development planning. He emphasised the importance of linking Indicator Frameworks not only with the SDGs but also with India's longer-term development goals under Viksit Bharat. He noted that updated base years and new statistical surveys to capture the unorganised sector and services economy are strengthening the country's statistical system.

The technical sessions commenced with a presentation by Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, Social Statistics Division, MoSPI, on strengthening the SDG monitoring architecture at national and sub-national levels. The session covered the National Indicator Framework (NIF), its alignment with State/UT Indicator Frameworks, principles for indicator selection, data sources, reporting periodicity and institutional responsibilities.

A key component of the workshop was the sharing of good practices and experiences from States that have made progress in strengthening SDG monitoring and localisation. Representatives from Maharashtra, Delhi and Odisha presented their approaches, highlighting institutional arrangements, data systems and lessons that could inform the development and strengthening of State/UT Indicator Frameworks.

Officials from the participating State and UT administrations presented their progress, institutional preparedness, data readiness and challenges in developing their respective frameworks. The discussions helped identify State/UT-specific priorities, institutional requirements and data-related gaps.

The workshop also included a facilitated group exercise led by MoSPI and UNDP, focusing on the development and refinement of draft State/UT Indicator Frameworks. Participants reviewed potential indicators for each SDG, identified State/UT-specific indicators reflecting local development priorities, mapped responsible departments and data sources, and assessed data availability and gaps. The exercise also emphasised the integration of gender-responsive and disaggregated indicators, wherever relevant, and the prioritisation of indicators based on relevance and monitoring requirements.

The workshop concluded with discussions on key recommendations and next steps for finalising and strengthening the respective State/UT Indicator Frameworks. MoSPI and UNDP reaffirmed their commitment to providing continued technical support to the all States/UTs.

The workshop reiterated the importance of robust sub-national statistical systems in advancing SDG localisation and evidence-based policymaking. State and UT Indicator Frameworks provide a common basis for tracking progress against the SDGs while reflecting local development priorities and longer-term Vision 2047 agendas. These frameworks can also strengthen planning, monitoring and decision-making at State and sub-State levels

2337930.title: In line with PM Shri Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah to inaugurate two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on 19th November 2026
2337930.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
In line with PM Shri Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah to inaugurate two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on 19th November 2026
Organised by National Investigation Agency (NIA), this year’s Conference will hold discussions on 'Cross-Border Terrorism' theme
Conference to serve as a platform for collective deliberation among security agencies, investigators and experts on emerging terror threats
The conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders with the 'Whole of Government approach'
Subjects like, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations and effective management of trials, will be discussed
Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, espionage, and emerging hybrid threats to national security
The deliberations will enable LEAs to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:31PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s policy of Zero Tolerance against terrorism, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah will inaugurate the two-day 'Anti-Terror Conference' in New Delhi on Thursday, 19th November 2026. The conference is being organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, as a part of a continued effort to bolster the nation's collective response to terrorism. This year's conference will deliberate on the theme 'Cross-Border Terrorism'.

Held annually, the conference has steadily grown into a significant gathering of operational forces, agencies working in the field of counter-terrorism, and experts from the technical, legal and forensic domains. It offers the agencies / forces, an opportunity to collectively examine matters that have bearing on national security and the threats arising from terrorism.

In keeping with the 'Whole of Government approach', the conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders. It seeks to establish formal as well as informal channels that enable coordinated and concerted action against terrorism. The conference also aims at contributing substantive inputs towards the formulation of future policy.

The conference sessions will address a range of subjects, including, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations, and the effective management of trials. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, and emerging hybrid threats to national security. Further sessions will examine the tools, techniques and case experiences involved in disrupting terror financing networks, as well as the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges.

This year, the conference will also host a capacity-building training programme for State police personnel and practising professionals. The programme has been designed to equip participants in several areas. These include applying the new criminal laws in terror investigations, using digital evidence in prosecution, and trial strategy and management. The programme will also cover special provisions relating to the investigation of terror cases, common challenges posed by the defence, the protection of witnesses, and the initiatives taken by the Government to improve prosecution.

Over the two days, the deliberations will enable law enforcement agencies to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations.

The conference will be attended by senior police officers of States and Union Territories, officers of Central agencies and departments dealing with counter-terrorism, and experts from allied fields including law, forensics and technology.

2337921.title: India positions CDRI as a key Global Platform for Climate-resilient Infrastructure; Calls for translating Commitments into Action at COP31, in Antalya (Türkiye)
2337921.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2337921.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India positions CDRI as a key Global Platform for Climate-resilient Infrastructure; Calls for translating Commitments into Action at COP31, in Antalya (Türkiye)
CDRI provides a Global Platform for Strengthening Disaster-resilient Infrastructure through International Cooperation: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 18 NOV 2026 4:23PM by PIB Delhi

Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today highlighted India's leadership in advancing global cooperation on disaster-resilient infrastructure at the CDRI Ministerial Dialogue on ‘Disaster Resilient Infrastructure for Climate Adaptation’ at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. He emphasised that climate action must go hand in hand with climate negotiations, with the success of international commitments ultimately measured by their translation into concrete action on the ground.

Shri Yadav stressed the need for practical outcomes in adaptation, mitigation and resilience, backed by stronger international cooperation and collective efforts. He highlighted the importance of knowledge sharing, technical expertise and capacity building, particularly for developing countries, to strengthen institutional capabilities and facilitate access to proven technologies. The Minister underscored that affordable and sustainable finance, complemented by strong institutional frameworks and technical capacities, is essential for developing resilient infrastructure.

Describing the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) as a unique global initiative, Shri Yadav highlighted its role in bringing together governments, international institutions, development partners and technical experts to promote collaboration, exchange best practices and strengthen infrastructure resilience. He noted that discussions at COP31 had reinforced resilience as a key priority and called for translating shared commitments into collaborative initiatives and tangible outcomes.

Representatives from participating countries highlighted their respective priorities and challenges. Trinidad and Tobago stressed the importance of grant and affordable finance, risk assessment tools and cooperation with the Government of India in agro-processing. Namibia highlighted the severe impact of drought on rural livelihoods and called for adequate funding to strengthen infrastructure resilience. Japan emphasised accelerating the deployment of Early Warning Systems, sharing disaster risk reduction expertise and strengthening regional networks in vulnerable countries. Guatemala underscored the need for affordable finance, while Jordan called for greater cooperation in facilitating access to finance and strengthening infrastructure planning.
