2337287.title: Prime Minister visits Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila, Philippines
2337287.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister visits Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila, Philippines
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 12:01PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila today and led the foundation-stone laying ceremony for the redevelopment of the Gurudwara in the presence of Panj Pyare. On the occasion, several dignitaries including Senator H.E. Francis Joseph Escudero and Hon’ble Mayor of Manila City, Mr. Francisco Isko Moreno were present.

Originally established in 1901 and formally organised in 1903, the institution was registered as Khalsa Diwan in 1924. The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara holds a unique distinction of being the oldest Gurudwara in the Philippines. It continues to play an important role through its spiritual, cultural and philanthropic activities for the Sikh and other communities in Manila.

The Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara continues to stand as a vital bridge between the Indian-Sikh community and Philippine society.

2337279.title: Raksha Mantri to attend 4th India-Japan 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue and hold bilateral talks with his Japanese counterpart in Tokyo
2337279.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Mantri to attend 4th India-Japan 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue and hold bilateral talks with his Japanese counterpart in Tokyo
Posted On: 17 NOV 2026 11:38AM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will participate in the 4th edition of India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue (2+2) and hold bilateral discussions with his Japanese counterpart during his official visit to Japan from November 18 to 19, 2026. The 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by Raksha Mantri and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar, along with Japan’s Minister of Defense Mr Shinjiro Koizumi and Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Toshimitsu Motegi. The dialogue will review the full spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, exchange views on regional & global developments, and reaffirm the shared commitment of the two nations to a free, open, inclusive, and rule-based Indo-Pacific.

The bilateral talks between Raksha Mantri and the Japanese Minister of Defense will be their third meeting this year. Building on the momentum from their interactions in New Delhi in August 2026 and on the margins of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October 2026, the two Ministers will deliberate on advancing defence equipment and technology collaboration, maritime security, enhancing the scale & complexity of joint exercises across all three services, and deepening industrial partnerships.

India and Japan share a Special Strategic and Global Partnership rooted in shared democratic values, mutual trust & converging strategic interests. The upcoming visit aims to further deepen bilateral defence ties and chart the roadmap for enhanced operational & industrial synergy between the two countries.

2337223.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah visits the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune and reviews its functioning and progress of various initiatives
2337223.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah visits the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune and reviews its functioning and progress of various initiatives
Shri Amit Shah interacts with officials and reviews activities related to registration, regulation, monitoring and good governance of Multi-State Cooperative Societies
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation emphasises transparent, accountable and systematic development of cooperative societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy
Shri Amit Shah stresses the need for effective monitoring of cooperative societies and strict compliance with regulatory provisions to prevent potential irregularities
CRCS Regional Office in Pune oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
Of the 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across the country, 420 have been registered since the formation of the Ministry of Cooperation
Regional Offices in Pune, Lucknow, Chennai and Kolkata will strengthen monitoring, grievance redressal and regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 9:59PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi', transparency, accountability, good governance and institutional strengthening in the cooperative sector are being continuously promoted under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. As part of these efforts, Shri Amit Shah today visited the Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) in Pune, Maharashtra. During the visit, he interacted with officials and reviewed the progress of various initiatives relating to the registration, regulation, monitoring and reform of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. Shri Amit Shah particularly sought information regarding the functioning of cooperative societies in Maharashtra, their registration status and measures being taken to further strengthen the regulatory framework. The establishment of Regional Offices of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies is a significant initiative towards ensuring effective regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and decentralisation of cooperative administration across the country.

During the review, Shri Amit Shah emphasised that the development of Multi-State Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra and the Western Region must be aligned with the objectives and guidelines of the National Cooperation Policy. He stated that the role of the Regional Office should not remain confined merely to registration-related activities but should extend to ensuring effective supervision, regulatory compliance, transparency and accountability in the functioning of cooperative societies.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also reviewed ongoing activities with the officials and emphasised that registration, inspection, auditing, grievance redressal and other statutory processes relating to cooperative societies must be carried out in a transparent and time-bound manner. He underscored the importance of an effective regulatory framework to promote good governance in cooperative institutions and safeguard the interests of all stakeholders, including members and depositors.

The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) is a statutory authority under the Ministry of Cooperation, appointed under Article 243ZH(f) of the Constitution and Section 4(1) of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002. It regulates cooperative societies whose objectives and areas of operation extend beyond the boundaries of a single State. The CRCS is entrusted with important statutory powers and responsibilities, including registration and regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, amendments to their registered bye-laws, supersession of Boards in accordance with statutory provisions, inquiries, inspections, audits, settlement of disputes, and liquidation and winding up of defunct societies.

At present, a total of 1,872 Multi-State Cooperative Societies are registered across the country. Of these, 420 societies have been registered since the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation on 6 July 2021. In view of the increasing number of Multi-State Cooperative Societies and their expanding geographical presence, Regional Offices are being established to ensure effective monitoring, regulatory compliance and good governance.

The first Regional Office of the CRCS, established in Pune for the Western Region, oversees matters relating to 818 Multi-State Cooperative Societies registered across Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. These include 756 societies in Maharashtra, 59 in Gujarat, two in Goa and one in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu. Thus, a substantial proportion of the country's registered Multi-State Cooperative Societies falls within the jurisdiction of the Pune Regional Office.

The Pune Regional Office commenced its operations on 15 April 2026. The Department of Expenditure has sanctioned 10 posts for the office. Arrangements are being made for the deployment of officers and essential support personnel to ensure effective and timely execution of regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies.

To further strengthen the monitoring and administrative framework for Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Ministry of Cooperation has initiated steps to establish additional Regional Offices in Lucknow for the Northern Region, Chennai for the Southern Region and Kolkata for the Eastern and North-Eastern Regions, in addition to the Pune office. These offices will facilitate decentralisation of regulatory administration, faster approval processes, improved monitoring and compliance, greater financial inclusion, effective grievance redressal and expansion of digital services.

The Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies has also undertaken several important initiatives for the digitisation, reform and strengthening of Multi-State Cooperative Societies. These include the development of an online system for processes such as registration of societies, amendments to bye-laws, filing of annual returns and opening of branches. Other significant measures include amendments to the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, computerisation of the offices of the Cooperative Election Authority and the Cooperative Ombudsman, and the establishment of the Cooperative Rehabilitation, Reconstruction and Development Fund (CRRDF).

In a significant step towards strengthening financial discipline, transparency and accountability in Multi-State Cooperative Societies, the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2026 (MSCARO, 2026) has also been issued. These reforms aim to ensure better financial management, effective regulatory oversight and protection of the interests of members of cooperative institutions.

The visit of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to the Pune Regional Office marks an important step towards strengthening the regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies, enhancing the effectiveness of regional monitoring mechanisms and promoting transparency, accountability and good governance in the cooperative sector in accordance with the National Cooperation Policy.

2337215.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses Ramoji Excellence Awards Ceremony – 2026 in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh
2337215.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses Ramoji Excellence Awards Ceremony – 2026 in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh
Only a few individuals, like Ramoji Rao, transform themselves into institutions during their lifetime; their contributions continue to inspire the nation forever
Ramoji Rao was well-informed about developments from every corner of country, and his views on resolving every problem were clear, forthright and fearless
Born into a poor farming family, Ramoji Rao launched 'Eenadu' without any backing and ensured that first voice of morning reaching every Telugu household was voice of truth
Ramoji Rao kept pace with technological advancements in every era, built the ETV network in Telugu and several other Indian languages, and took television channels to mobile platforms as well
Many people struggle to build their careers, but it is those who struggle to uphold values who truly become great, Shri Ramoji Rao not only fought for values but also established them
Padma Vibhushan was not merely an honour for Ramoji Rao; it was a recognition of journalism, literature and Telugu identity, through his enterprise, he built an institution that continues to uphold his values even in his absence
He did not run newspapers and news channels merely for profit, despite financial losses and immense pressure, he upheld journalism as fourth pillar of democracy
He also made immense contributions to film industry, it is difficult to imagine a film studio for any regional-language film industry without Ramoji Film City
Under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modi, country has witnessed decisive leadership after a long time, with era of policy paralysis giving way to the politics of performance
World's longest and most powerful hydrogen-powered train has been developed in India using entirely indigenous technology and has also begun running on tracks
Under the leadership of Shri Narendra Modi, 98% of Gram Panchayats have been connected through 4G connectivity, and 50 crore Indians have come out of poverty over the past 12 years—a fact also acknowledged by the World Bank
Andhra Pradesh will emerge as most developed state in the country over next 10 years
USD 15 billion AI hub being developed by Google in Visakhapatnam will be its largest hub outside the United States, which is a matter of pride for the entire country
Shri Chandrababu Naidu has successfully translated investments worth ₹30 lakh crore into reality on the ground in just two and a half years, which is a matter of great pride
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 9:52PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed the Ramoji Excellence Awards Ceremony – 2026 in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh. On the occasion, Governor of Andhra Pradesh Shri S. Abdul Nazeer, Chief Minister Shri Chandrababu Naidu, Union Ministers Shri G. Kishan Reddy and Shri K. Ram Mohan Naidu, Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri K. Pawan Kalyan, and several other dignitaries were present.

Addressing the award ceremony, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today marks the 90th birth anniversary of Ramoji Rao, who is no longer among us. He said that there are individuals who, through their dedicated work during their lifetime, evolve into institutions, and the institutions they establish continue to inspire the nation forever. Shri Shah said that he had met Ramoji Rao on four occasions and he remained well-informed about developments from every corner of the country. He had a clear understanding of every problem facing the nation and its possible solutions. He held firm convictions of his own and had the courage to express them fearlessly and candidly. He said that Ramoji Rao had an excellent understanding of ground realities. He said that Ramoji Rao continues to serve as a role model for young people in several fields, including agriculture, education, filmmaking and media.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao had an in-depth understanding of the geographical situation, population, challenges and root causes of insurgency in the Northeast. Shri Amit Shah said more he came to know about Ramoji Rao, the greater his respect for him became.

Shri Amit Shah said that when one looks back at the 90-year life of Ramoji Rao, it becomes evident that hardly anyone else could have made such an extensive contribution to the nation across so many fields. He said that Ramoji Rao was born into a poor family in Krishna district and had no inheritance, resources or formal degree in journalism. However, he possessed vision in his eyes and mind, along with unwavering determination. Shri Shah said that by launching the newspaper Eenadu, Ramoji Rao sought to make the voice of truth resonate among readers. He said that if Ramoji Rao's contribution were to be assessed today, it could be said that in the world of journalism, the only media group chairman with whom he could be compared was Ram Nath Goenka.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao always kept pace with changing times and evolving technology. He said that when private news channels were first introduced, no one other than Ramoji Rao could have envisioned the possibility of running 24-hour news channels in regional languages. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao launched ETV not only in Telugu but also in almost all the regional languages of the country. He added that Ramoji Rao not only enriched the country's regional languages but also took the innovative initiative of making the voice of truth resonate among people across the country through the ETV network.

Shri Amit Shah said that on one occasion, when he asked Ramoji Rao what he wished to accomplish with the time he had left, the latter had replied that he wanted to launch a TV channel on mobile phones. He said that today, his mobile channels are available in all languages. It is this passion to keep contributing and the zeal to constantly strive and overcome challenges that make Ramoji Rao truly great.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that when we look at the owners of today's newspapers and news channels, their business objectives and their focus on profits, we realise what a towering personality Ramoji Rao was. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao must have firmly believed that journalism, in its true sense, constitutes the fourth pillar of democracy. He made numerous sacrifices and faced many struggles throughout his life to uphold this conviction.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao spent two major phases of his life in struggle. Despite significant financial losses and numerous challenges, he maintained the impartiality of his news channel and upheld its role as a true fourth pillar of democracy. Shri Shah said that those who struggle to build their careers are also great individuals. Struggle is a unique quality that makes a person great. However, those who struggle to uphold values are even greater. Ramoji Rao always fought for values and worked to establish them.

Shri Amit Shah said that when Ramoji Rao was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2016, a renowned Gujarati newspaper from Gujarat had written that the honour was not merely a recognition of Ramoji Rao, but also an honour for journalism, literature, education and Telugu pride. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao had not merely built a news industry; he had created institutions rather than businesses. Institutions are those that continue to function and uphold the same values even after their founders are no longer present.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that Ramoji Rao also made significant contributions to the film industry. He said that it is difficult to imagine the film industry of any language without Ramoji Film City. Shri Shah said that Ramoji Rao assured filmmakers that if they came with the funds and their creative vision, everything else would be available at his studio, and they would not need to go anywhere else.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that several individuals have been selected for the Excellence Awards this year. People who have made significant contributions to the nation in fields such as science and technology, young icons, service to humanity, art and culture, education, medicine and healthcare, rural development, journalism and women's achievements are being honoured on this occasion. He said that he would like to tell all nine award recipients, who are being recognised for their contributions in these nine fields crucial to the country's development, that they may receive many more awards in their lives, but an award associated with the name of Ramoji Rao holds a special significance of its own.

Shri Amit Shah said that under the able leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is moving forward on the path of progress. He said that over the past 13 years, the country has witnessed stability, continuity and decisive leadership after a long period. The era when policy paralysis was widely discussed has now given way to performance-driven politics and development based on sound policies. Union Home Minister said that significant progress has been made in several areas, including the abrogation of Article 370, ending the five-decade-old problem of Naxalism, driving the country's economic growth and ensuring national security. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India's economy is advancing rapidly, while opportunities are expanding at an equally fast pace across all sectors.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that despite the prolonged wars between Russia and Ukraine, and between the United States and other countries, positive projections have emerged regarding India's economic growth.  Moody’s has recently raised its growth forecast for India for 2026–27 from 6.5% to 7%. In 2025–26, India recorded exports worth a record USD 863 billion, and our next target is USD 1 trillion. He expressed confidence that we would achieve this target.

Shri Shah said that India has become the world's second-largest producer in the manufacturing sector. India now produces more steel than the United States and Japan combined. This achievement has been accomplished over the past 12 years. He further said that earlier, only 58 Gram Panchayats had internet connectivity, whereas today, 2 lakh 15 thousands Gram Panchayats have been connected through 4G services, accounting for approximately 98 per cent of the total Gram Panchayats.

Shri Amit Shah said that India has made significant progress in the economic sector as well. The world's longest and highest-capacity hydrogen train has been built in India using completely indigenous technology, and its operations have also commenced.

He said that in 2014, the country had only 76 airports, whereas today, India has made significant strides, with the number of airports reaching 150. Shri Shah further said that, according to a World Bank report, during the 12 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's tenure, 50 crore Indians have come out of poverty, which is a matter of great satisfaction for everyone.

Union Home Minister said that for nearly 40 years, the country witnessed more than 2,000 Naxal attacks every year. However, today, it is a matter of satisfaction that not a single Naxal attack is taking place. He said that this is a collective achievement of all of us.

He said that Andhra Pradesh, too, is progressing rapidly under the leadership of Shri Chandrababu Naidu. He added that he has been consistently studying the data from Shri Chandrababu Naidu's second term in office and can confidently say that Andhra Pradesh will become the most developed state in the country over the next 10 years.

Shri Shah said that Google's USD 15 billion AI hub is a matter of pride not only for Andhra Pradesh but also for the entire country. The establishment of a USD 15 billion AI hub by Google in Visakhapatnam is a matter of pride for the people of India as well as Andhra Pradesh. Both the one-gigawatt data centre and Google's largest AI hub outside the United States are significant achievements for the country. A new gateway for undersea cables will also be established in Andhra Pradesh.

He said that the foundation stone of the state's first semiconductor unit has been laid, and major steel plants have been established. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has recently inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, and on the same day, foundation stones were laid for projects worth ₹18,000 crore.

Shri Shah said that a closer examination of all these initiatives reveals that Shri Chandrababu Naidu has facilitated the grounding of investments worth ₹30 lakh crore in Andhra Pradesh in just two-and-a-half years.

Shri Amit Shah said that once the Polavaram Dam is completed and water reaches every part of Andhra Pradesh, it will create an unparalleled opportunity for the farmers of the state. He said that taking the project forward with firm determination and a time-bound approach is a significant achievement.

****

2337158.title: India calls for Country-Driven Just Transition Mechanism at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye); Emphasizes Adequate Finance, Technology Transfer and Capacity Building for Developing Countries
2337158.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2337158.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
India calls for Country-Driven Just Transition Mechanism at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye); Emphasizes Adequate Finance, Technology Transfer and Capacity Building for Developing Countries
Shri Bhupender Yadav calls for a Two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism that respects National Sovereignty and diverse National Circumstances
India stresses that Just Transition must address Employment, Social Protection, Adaptation, Poverty Eradication and Energy Access
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 8:23PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for moving the global just transition agenda from dialogue and exchange of experiences towards practical, country-driven implementation. Addressing the Fourth Annual High-Level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition under the UAE Just Transition Work Programme at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye), the Minister reiterated India's commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind.

Presented India's views at the 4th Annual High-level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye today. Underlined the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning. India supports the operationalisation of a two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism, responsive to developing-country needs and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances.

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) November 16, 2026

Shri Yadav emphasised that just transition must follow a whole-of-economy and whole-of-society approach, addressing employment, social protection, adaptation, poverty eradication, energy access and sustainable development. He highlighted that adequate financial support, technology transfer and capacity-building are essential to enable developing countries to implement their national priorities. 

Noting that there can be no one-size-fits-all approach, he cited India's sub-national heat action and disaster management plans, which address vulnerabilities of workers and communities, as well as the country's renewable energy expansion that seeks to combine low-carbon development with affordable energy access. These examples underline the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning, he added.

The Minister underlined the need for clearly defined and complementary roles for the UAE Just Transition Work Programme and the proposed Just Transition Mechanism. While the Work Programme should continue to provide a platform for dialogue and exchange of experiences, the Mechanism should facilitate practical support through technical assistance, capacity-building and cooperation, translating the learnings from ongoing discussions into action, he stated.

Reaffirming India's support for operationalising a two-tier, Party-guided Just Transition Mechanism, Shri Yadav stressed that it must be responsive to the needs of developing countries and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances. The Mechanism should build on existing efforts, avoid duplication and facilitate access to adequate means of implementation. It must neither prescribe uniform sectoral pathways nor create new obligations, but enable countries to pursue their own just transition pathways in accordance with national priorities, while ensuring that workers, communities and vulnerable groups are not left behind, the Minister stressed.

Shri Yadav observed that COP31 presents an important opportunity to move from exchanging experiences to practical, country-driven implementation. India stands ready to work constructively with all Parties towards an inclusive outcome that advances just transition while safeguarding the developmental priorities of developing countries, the Minister concluded.

2337144.title: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) Renew Scientific Partnership to Promote Joint Research, Innovation and Technology Development
2337144.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) Renew Scientific Partnership to Promote Joint Research, Innovation and Technology Development
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

India and Belarus took an important step towards strengthening their bilateral scientific and technological partnership with the signing of the Second Programme of Cooperation (PoC) for the period 2027–2029 between the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) of India, and the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus (NASB) at New Delhi on 16th November 2026.

The Programme of Cooperation was signed during a meeting between Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, and Dr. A. V. Trukhanov, Deputy Chairman of the Presidium of NASB, who is visiting India from 15–18 November 2026 in connection with the 12th Meeting of the Belarusian-Indian Intergovernmental Commission on Cooperation in Economy, Trade, Industry, Science, Technology and Culture and the India-Belarus Business Forum.

The signing of the Second PoC builds upon the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Scientific and Technical Cooperation signed between CSIR and NASB on 22 May 2023. Under the first Programme of Cooperation (2024–2026), the two institutions launched a Joint Call for Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) proposals in October 2024, resulting in the approval seven joint projects.These projects are currently progressing through their second year of implementation.

The Second Programme of Cooperation (2027–2031) provides a renewed framework for expanding bilateral scientific collaboration, facilitating joint research and development initiatives and strengthening linkages between research institutions and scientists of both countries. It is expected to provide an impetus to collaborative research, technology development, knowledge exchange and innovation-driven partnerships through focused cooperation in mutually identified areas of science and technology.

As a key initiative under the Second Programme of Cooperation, CSIR and NASB propose to launch the Second Joint Call for Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Proposals from 27 November 2026 inviting proposals from researchers and scientists of both countries for undertaking collaborative research projects in mutually identified priority areas. The call is expected to provide fresh impetus to bilateral research partnerships, encourage scientific exchanges and facilitate the development of innovative solutions through joint research and technological collaboration.

Speaking on the occasion, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, DSIR, highlighted the importance of sustained scientific partnerships in addressing emerging global challenges and advancing innovation-led development. The DG, CSIR emphasised the significant potential for Indian and Belarusian researchers to work together by leveraging their respective scientific strengths and institutional capabilities.

Dr. A. V. Trukhanov, Deputy Chairman of the Presidium of NASB, highlighted the importance of continued scientific engagement between India and Belarus and expressed interest in further strengthening institutional cooperation and expanding opportunities for joint research and technological collaboration, specifically through organizing Joint Laboratories between NASB and CSIR and exploring mechanisms to support cooperation activities targeting upscaling and translational research activities.

The signing of the Second Programme of Cooperation marks an important milestone in India–Belarus scientific relations. The renewed partnership is expected to further strengthen research collaboration, promote institutional linkages and create new opportunities for scientific exchange and innovation, contributing to the broader objectives of bilateral cooperation between the two countries.

2337140.title: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment’s Participation at 45th IITF 2026 Reinforces Commitment to Inclusive Economic Empowerment, Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Livelihoods
2337140.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment’s Participation at 45th IITF 2026 Reinforces Commitment to Inclusive Economic Empowerment, Entrepreneurship and Sustainable Livelihoods
Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Showcase Handicrafts, Handlooms and Traditional Products
Cumulative Sales Reach Approximately ₹5.50 Lakh as of November 15, Reflecting Encouraging Market Opportunities for Participating Artisans
TULIP Brand Promoted to Strengthen National and International Market Access for Traditional Artisans and Entrepreneurs
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, continues to promote traditional craftsmanship, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities through its participation in the ongoing 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, in the National Capital here.

The Ministry's pavilion has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹5.50 lakh as of November 15, 2026, highlighting the market opportunities being created for artisans and entrepreneurs from disadvantaged and marginalised sections of society.

The Ministry's pavilion, located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, provides a prominent platform for showcasing India's rich artistic traditions, indigenous craftsmanship and entrepreneurial capabilities. The participation of artisans from different regions of the country reflects the Ministry's continued efforts to strengthen market linkages and facilitate direct engagement between traditional producers and consumers.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in the Trade Fair through the Ministry's three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), and National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

He said the participating artisans are showcasing a diverse collection of handicrafts, handloom products, handmade articles and other traditional products that reflect India's rich cultural heritage and indigenous skills.

The pavilion provides opportunities for artisans to interact directly with visitors, understand consumer preferences, explore emerging market trends and generate income through the sale of their products, he said.

 

The Official said the cumulative sales of approximately ₹5.50 lakh recorded up to November 15, represent an encouraging development in the Ministry's efforts to promote market-oriented livelihood opportunities, that is also helping artisans enhance the visibility of their products and establish connections with a wider consumer base.

The Official said guided by the vision of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of 'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas', the Ministry is providing opportunities to artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs) to showcase their skills and participate more actively in mainstream economic activities.

He said the significant highlight of the Ministry's participation in IITF 2026 is the promotion of the TULIP (Traditional Artisans' Upliftment Livelihood Programme) brand, which seeks to strengthen the visibility, recognition and market reach of products developed by traditional artisans.

 

The TULIP initiative was recently launched by Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, during the Shilp Samagam Mela at Dilli Haat in the National Capital, the Official said.

 

The initiative aims to create an enhanced platform for promoting artisan-made products and facilitating access to national and international markets, he added.

The Official said through TULIP, the Ministry seeks to connect traditional craftsmanship with contemporary consumer preferences and emerging market demands. The initiative also focuses on preserving India's artistic heritage while encouraging innovation, entrepreneurship and economic self-reliance among artisans.

He said the Ministry's participation in the Trade Fair demonstrates the importance of national-level exhibitions in expanding marketing opportunities for small entrepreneurs and traditional craftspeople.

The Official said the platforms enable artisans to showcase their capabilities, interact with potential customers, strengthen their market presence and explore opportunities for long-term business development.

The ongoing exhibition also highlights the role of the Ministry's Apex Corporations in supporting livelihood promotion and economic empowerment. By facilitating participation in prominent trade fairs and exhibitions, these Corporations are contributing to improved market access, increased product visibility and greater opportunities for income generation among their beneficiaries.

The Ministry's pavilion adds an important dimension of social and economic inclusion to IITF 2026 by bringing the products, skills and entrepreneurial potential of artisans from diverse social and geographical backgrounds into the mainstream marketplace.

The 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, 2026, serves as a prominent platform for trade, commerce, industry and cultural exchange. The Ministry's continued participation reflects its commitment to ensuring that traditional artisans and entrepreneurs benefit from expanding market opportunities and contribute meaningfully to the country's economic development.

 

Through initiatives such as TULIP and participation in national exhibitions, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment remains committed to strengthening sustainable livelihoods, promoting indigenous craftsmanship and advancing inclusive socio-economic development in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

2337121.title: India and Thailand Review Bilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation at 14th Joint Trade Committee Meeting in Nonthaburi, Thailand
2337121.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India and Thailand Review Bilateral Trade and Economic Cooperation at 14th Joint Trade Committee Meeting in Nonthaburi, Thailand
India-Thailand Bilateral Trade Grows 12.6% to USD 21.49 Billion in FY 2025-26
India and Thailand Discuss UPI Linkage, Local Currency Settlement and FinTech Cooperation
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi

The 14th Meeting of the India-Thailand Joint Trade Committee (JTC) was held on 16 November 2026 at the Ministry of Commerce, Nonthaburi, Thailand. The meeting was co-chaired by Additional Secretary, Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Nitin Kumar Yadav, and Director-General, Department of Trade Negotiations, Ministry of Commerce, Thailand, Ms. Chotima Iemsawasdikul. Representatives of concerned Ministries, Departments and organisations of both countries also participated.

Both sides noted the encouraging momentum in bilateral trade, which reached USD 21.49 billion in FY 2025–26, registering a growth of 12.6 per cent over the previous year. Thailand accounted for 16.7 per cent of India's total trade with ASEAN. The co-chairs acknowledged the role of the JTC in facilitating trade and investment, and reiterated their commitment to expanding bilateral trade and investment and facilitating market access.

India highlighted investment opportunities in infrastructure and logistics, automotive and electric vehicles, food processing and agro-industry, electronics and semiconductors, and tourism, hospitality and wellness. Thailand shared its economic outlook and investment facilitation measures and presented its “Co-Creation Co-Investment” approach. India welcomed the approach and agreed to examine it further in consultation with the concerned Ministries and Departments.

The meeting discussed enhancing the utilisation of the ASEAN–India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) and the India–Thailand Early Harvest Scheme. Both sides also explored a mechanism for the annual exchange of bilateral trade data and data on the utilisation of preferences to identify areas for enhancing preferential trade and addressing implementation-related challenges. They underlined the importance of an early and meaningful conclusion of the AITIGA Review.

The discussions focused on ensuring effective market access and resolving issues faced by traders, including market access for agricultural, livestock and marine products, sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures and certification processes, quality and regulatory requirements, and the removal of non-tariff barriers.

Both sides explored opportunities for cooperation in pharmaceuticals and healthcare, AYUSH and traditional medicine, textiles, plastics and petrochemicals, gems and jewellery, as well as the services sector. Collaboration between trade promotion organisations was also discussed.

The two sides also deliberated on payment and financial connectivity, including the linkage of India's UPI with Thailand's PromptPay, local currency settlement and FinTech cooperation between the Reserve Bank of India and the Bank of Thailand.

The meeting reaffirmed the commitment of both sides to strengthening the India–Thailand economic partnership. The co-chairs encouraged officials to continue discussions and convene working-level meetings before the next JTC meeting to sustain the momentum. The next meeting of the JTC will be held in India.

2337119.title: Special Handloom and Handicraft Exhibition Themed ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ Inaugurated by Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh at IITF 2026
2337119.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
Special Handloom and Handicraft Exhibition Themed ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ Inaugurated by Union Minister Shri Giriraj Singh at IITF 2026
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:29PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Giriraj Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister of Textiles, Government of India, inaugurated the “Special Handloom & Handicraft Exhibition cum Sale” at the India International Trade Fair (IITF), Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 16th November 2026. The inauguration took place in the august presence of Smt. Arti Kanwar, Additional Secretary, Smt. Amrit Raj, Development Commissioner Handicrafts, Sh. Rajiv Ashok, MD, NHDC (National Handloom Development Corporation Ltd) and other senior officials from the Ministry and NHDC.

This year’s pavilion is themed “Vikas Aur Virasat”, celebrating India’s timeless craft legacy through a geographical journey across North, South, East and West—highlighting the unique handloom and handicraft traditions of different regions.

The pavilion showcases India’s cultural diversity through four regional representations:

  • North – Reflection & Ancestral Grace: Featuring traditional motifs of Ganesha, Ram Darbar and the luminous Banarasi weave, symbolising lineage and inherited excellence.
  • South – Precision, Devotion & Sculptural Discipline: Showcasing Karnataka and Tamil Nadu’s mastery in wood, silk and metal crafts, along with the cosmic rhythm of Natraj.
  • East – Memory, Continuity & the Handwoven Heartbeat: Highlighting the traditional weaving heritage of Odisha and Bengal, reflecting cultural identity and continuity.
  • West – Radiance, Celebration & Desert Brilliance: Showcasing mirrorwork, Lippan art and carved wood, representing desert resilience and festive spirit.)

Shri Giriraj Singh interacted with participating weavers and artisans after the inauguration formalities. He emphasized on the Government of India’s continuous efforts to strengthen the entire value chain—from raw material support to technology integration, design interventions and market linkages. He reiterated the Ministry’s commitment to expanding income and livelihood opportunities for weavers and craftspeople, reinforcing India’s leadership as the world’s largest and most sustainable handloom and handicraft ecosystem.

The Union Minister of Textiles highlighted that development must go hand in hand with heritage, noting that handloom, handicrafts and jute have been an integral part of India's heritage for over 5,000 years. Emphasising their contribution to economic growth and employment generation, he said that the handloom and handicrafts sectors alone are associated with over one crore artisans, supporting millions of livelihoods both directly and indirectly. He further highlighted their significant contribution to the domestic market and exports, expressing confidence that sales at this year's International Trade Fair would reach new heights, with both domestic demand and export opportunities expected to grow in the coming years.

The event, scheduled from 13th to 27th November 2026, is open to the public from 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM in Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. With 200 stalls representing 100 Handloom and 100 Handicraft artisans. Representing more than 21 States and Union Territories showcasing various types of  distinct crafts, the pavilion is managed by the National Handloom Development Corporation (NHDC) to provide direct market access to handloom weavers and handicraft artisans The textile theme pavilion also features distinguished master artisans, including 7 National Awardees, 3 State Awardees, 2 Sant Kabir Awardees, and more than 5 multiple award holders, with a total of 17 awardees from both the Handloom and Handicraft sectors. whose exceptional craftsmanship enriches the cultural experience of the pavilion and reflects the artistic excellence of India’s textile heritage.

2337105.title: CBDT Chairman Shri Ravi Agrawal inaugurates Taxpayers' Lounge at the India International Trade Fair (IITF), 2026, celebrating the spirit of Vikas aur Virasat
2337105.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
CBDT Chairman Shri Ravi Agrawal inaugurates Taxpayers' Lounge at the India International Trade Fair (IITF), 2026, celebrating the spirit of Vikas aur Virasat
CBDT releases 18 informative brochures and a children's book introducing basics of Income Tax through games, puzzles and quizzes
Senior Citizens' Helpdesk introduced this year; immersive installations and interactive games make taxpayer awareness engaging for visitors of all ages
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), today inaugurated and dedicated the Taxpayers' Lounge at the India International Trade Fair (IITF), 2026, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, to the general public from 13th to 27th November, 2026.

Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT, along with senior officers, marking the formal opening of the Taxpayers' Lounge at Hall No. 4, Bharat Mandapam.

 

Spread across an expansive 507 sq. metres, the Taxpayers' Lounge brings alive the spirit of Vikas aur Virasat, blending India's rich cultural heritage with contemporary technology and immersive experiences.

 

 

The Lounge reflects the evolution of India's tax administration and the Department's vision of a progressive, transparent and citizen-centric tax ecosystem. Its key attractions include:

 

  • Triveni Kinetic LED: The Lounge's digital centerpiece, combining movement, light and dynamic visual storytelling to symbolise the convergence of tradition, technology and transformation. It is complemented by a Kar-Sathi Holobox that interacts with visitors and answers their queries.
  • Tree of Life: At the heart of the Lounge stands the Tree of Life, whose deep, timeless roots symbolise Virasat – India's heritage, enduring values and collective good. The Archway of Growth represents the nation's journey of progress and aspirations, while the Canopy of Hope signifies protection, inclusivity and collective well-being, conveying how responsible taxation contributes to nation-building.
  • Heritage-inspired entrance: The entrance draws inspiration from the iconic Toran of the Sanchi Stupa, reimagined in a contemporary design language. Symbolising auspicious beginnings, it marks the dawn of a new era of tax reforms under the Income-tax Act, 2025. The two pillars at the entrance carry the Department's guiding motto on one side and 'Prarambh – The New Income-tax Act, 2025' on the other.
  • Dynamic LED Fascia: A running LED fascia across the Lounge gives it a vibrant digital identity, showcasing key messages and departmental initiatives.
  • Interactive experiences: Digital and VR games on the theme of Income Tax, including 'Little Bee: Big Nation', VR bowling, along with Nukkad Natak, magic shows and quizzes, make taxpayer awareness engaging for visitors of all ages.

The Tree of Life installation at the heart of the Taxpayers' Lounge.

 

Among other things, the Lounge also offers dedicated taxpayer services through six helpdesks providing assistance on:

 

  • e-Filing of returns and related queries
  • PAN and PAN-related services
  • Use of the AI Chatbot
  • Grievance redressal through CPGRAM
  • International Taxation
  • A Senior Citizens' Helpdesk, introduced for the first time this year

 

As part of its knowledge and awareness initiatives, the Department released 18 informative brochures on taxpayer services, along with a specially designed children's book that introduces the fundamentals of Income Tax through games, puzzles and quizzes, promoting early tax awareness and financial literacy among the next generation.

 

 

The Income Tax Pavilion at the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 (13–27 Nov), was dedicated to the general public today by Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman CBDT, in the presence of other senior officers of the Department. Spread across an expansive 507 sq. metres, the Pavilion brings alive the spirit of “Vikas Aur Virasat”, blending India's rich cultural heritage with contemporary technology and showcasing the Department’s journey towards a trust-based and citizen-centric tax ecosystem. Key attractions include: 🔹 Triveni Kinetic LED: A digital installation symbolising the convergence of tradition, technology and transformation, complemented by a Karsathi Holobox to engage with visitors and answer their queries. 🔹Tree of Life: A specially designed installation symbolising heritage, enduring values, sustainable growth and the contribution of responsible taxation to nation-building. 🔹Interactive experiences for kids and adults: Digital and VR games, including 'Little Bee: Big Nation' and VR bowling, along with Nukkad Natak, magic shows and quizzes. 🔹Dedicated taxpayer helpdesks: Six helpdesks to provide guidance on e-Filing, PAN, AI Chatbot, grievance redressal (CPGRAM), International Taxation and a specially introduced Senior Citizens' Helpdesk. 🔹Knowledge and awareness initiatives: Release of 18 informative brochures and a specially designed children's book introducing the fundamentals of Income Tax through games, puzzles and quizzes, promoting early tax awareness and financial literacy. The Pavilion reflects the Income Tax Department's commitment to ease of compliance, citizen engagement and nation-building, rooted in India's rich heritage and empowered by technology. Visitors are invited to explore the Pavilion and experience its diverse range of interactive activities, exhibits and taxpayer services, offering an engaging and informative experience for people of all age groups.

2337092.title: Sarbananda Sonowal Pitches $10 Billion Shipbuilding Opportunity to Global Maritime Leaders
2337092.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2337092.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Sarbananda Sonowal Pitches $10 Billion Shipbuilding Opportunity to Global Maritime Leaders
India’s shipbuilding Order Book Tops $1.7 billion across 150-plus Ships, with Exports Driving over 80%: Sarbananda Sonowal
Minister launches “Naukosh” portal & sets Goal of Top 10 Shipbuilding Nation by 2030
Cochin Shipyard & Damen sign MoU pact for a new Shipbuilding
30 foreign shipyards, including South Korea's three largest, join talks on five coastal clusters; 10 delegations to visit sites
Build in India, for India & for the world: Sarbananda Sonowal
5 Greenfield Shipbuilding Clusters in Dugarajapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, Kuchhadi in Gujarat, Dighi in Maharashtra, Kendrapada in Odisha & Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi

​​​​New Delhi, 16 November 2026: Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal invited the global shipbuilders, shipping lines and financiers for investment as projections estimate nearly $10 billion of investment in the five new Greenfield coastal shipbuilding clusters, saying India aims to rank among the world's top 10 shipbuilding nations by 2030 and the top five by 2047.

Sonowal made the pitch at the India Shipbuilding Investment Conclave 2026, hosted by the MoPSW here today. He also launched Naukosh, a digital portal for the shipbuilding and ship repair industry, and the conclave saw Damen Shipyards and Cochin Shipyard sign a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on future shipbuilding projects.

"India is ready to build the ships of the world," Sarbananda Sonowal said. "Build in India, for India and for the world.” The conclave builds on the $8 billion shipbuilding financial package the government approved last year under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal cited domestic and export demand as the case for investors. Identified domestic demand covers more than 400 vessels, representing an investment opportunity of nearly $24 billion, the minister said. The active order pipeline holds more than 150 vessels valued at over $1.7 billion, and export orders account for more than 80% of that value.

The investment push centers on five greenfield clusters that officials described as ready to build: Dugarajapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, Kuchhadi in Gujarat, Dighi in Maharashtra, Kendrapada in Odisha and Thoothukudi in Tamil Nadu. Central and state teams took investors through available land, supporting policies and joint Centre-state backing for shipyards, component makers and allied marine businesses.

Sonowal said the clusters would open opportunities in manufacturing, technology, employment and exports. “Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, cooperative federalism is powering the next chapter of Make in India. Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha and Tamil Nadu have shown that India’s coastal states are partners in this mission, not just hosts. We move this as Team India so that investors get land, approvals and policy support without delay,” Sonowal said.

Executives from 30 international shipyards joined shipping companies, equipment makers, banks, investors and diplomatic missions, along with Indian industry leaders. Among those taking part were HD KSOE, Samsung Heavy Industries, Hanwha Ocean, Fincantieri, Meyer Werft, Damen, Royal IHC, Everllence, Mitsui Engines, Wartsila, Kongsberg, Drydocks World Dubai, Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, MOL and DP World.

The Korean Ambassador to India also led a large delegation after Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal's recent visit to South Korea. HD KSOE, Samsung Heavy Industries and Hanwha Ocean are South Korea's three largest shipbuilders; shipping company HMM also attended. Their participation builds on VOYAGES, short for Vision for Operation of Yard Assisted Growth with Efficiency and Scale, the partnership PM Narendra Modi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung signed April 2026 to pair Korean shipbuilding expertise with India's Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.

Naukosh, developed by the ministry's Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA), brings policies, approvals and investment opportunities onto one digital platform, which Sarbananda Sonowal said would promote transparency and ease of doing business. It serves shipyards, repair facilities, equipment makers, design agencies, classification societies, research and training institutions, financiers, insurers and regulators.

Its modules cover an industry directory, shipyard capability data, a collaboration hub, finance and insurance information, a technical library, an innovation centre, training and certification, and regulatory guidance. A public homepage dashboard will show shipyard and capacity indicators, ships delivered and on order, and sector updates.

At a Global Maritime Leaders' Open House, executives gave government officials direct feedback on policy and long-term plans. Delegations then held one-on-one meetings with state cluster teams, central ministries and financial institutions to work toward specific deals. State governments have arranged site visits tomorrow (Tuesday on Nov. 17), for 10 international delegations to inspect the cluster locations.

"The participation of global leaders today reflects growing confidence in India as a shipbuilding destination," Sonowal said. "With assured demand, strong policy support, dedicated financing and five ready coastal clusters, India offers a compelling case for long-term investment. Our priority now is to convert today's discussions into projects on the ground."

Sonowal tied the effort to PM Modi's leadership, saying shipbuilding had become a pillar of the Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat journey. He said growth in the sector would create opportunities for Indian industries, enterprises and young people.

Vijay Kumar, Secretary, MoPSW said the discussions were "focused and practical.” He further added, ”Each investor now has a clear point of contact across the cluster special purpose vehicles, state governments and the ministry, and we will follow up closely on every engagement in the weeks ahead.”

Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal was also joined by the Secretary, along with senior officials from central ministries, state governments and major ports.

2337086.title: From Alcohol Dependence to Financial Stability
2337086.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Alcohol Dependence to Financial Stability
 A Journey of Recovery and Self-Reliance Through IRCA in Karnataka
Counselling, Therapeutic Interventions and Family Support Help 33-Year-Old Ramesh Gowda from Kolar Rebuild His Life
Ministry-Supported De-addiction Centre Helps Beneficiary Restore Family Relationships and Revive Business Activities
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of 33 year Ramesh Gowda (name changed) from alcohol dependence and financial difficulties towards improved well-being, stronger family relationships and renewed livelihood opportunities, offers an encouraging example of recovery supported by individual determination, professional counselling and family involvement.

Mr. Ramesh Gowda, a resident of Kolar district in Karnataka, has made significant progress towards recovery from alcohol dependence through counselling and rehabilitation assistance at the Alcohol and Drug Abuse Free De-addiction Centre, an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA). His experience highlights the importance of timely professional support and family encouragement in rebuilding personal and professional life.

Belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, Ramesh previously ran his own business. What began as occasional alcohol consumption gradually became regular amid family-related difficulties and stress. His growing dependence affected the management of his business, weakened financial stability and strained relationships with family members. Recognising these challenges and determined to improve his circumstances, he voluntarily approached the IRCA centre in Kolar for assistance. He received support beginning on January 6, 2024, including regular counselling, motivational guidance and therapeutic interventions designed to help him understand his personal goals and responsibilities.

The counselling process helped Ramesh reflect on the effects of alcohol dependence, strengthen his motivation and build confidence in pursuing recovery. The centre also conducted family counselling sessions to improve communication and understanding among family members and encourage a supportive environment for rehabilitation.

With sustained guidance and family support, Ramesh showed significant improvement in his behaviour and overall well-being. As his confidence returned, he was able to regain focus on his business activities and work towards greater financial stability.

The progress was also reflected in his family relationships. Improved communication and renewed attention to his responsibilities helped him rebuild healthier connections with his loved ones and pursue a more stable daily routine.

Following counselling and rehabilitation support, Ramesh has regained stability in his personal and professional life and is now earning approximately ₹15,000 per month. This reported income reflects his renewed engagement with livelihood activities; the information provided does not specify his earlier monthly earnings.

The Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts in Kolar demonstrates the value of accessible counselling, therapeutic interventions and family-based support for individuals affected by substance dependence. Such assistance can help beneficiaries strengthen their well-being and participate more confidently in family and economic life.

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment supports rehabilitation and drug demand reduction interventions under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), including assistance through Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts.

Focuses on Strengthening Sericulture Research and Innovation
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

The 72nd Meeting of the Research Coordination Committee (RCC) of the Central Silk Board (CSB) was held on 16 November, 2026 at ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru, with a focus on strengthening research coordination, accelerating technological advancements and promoting innovation for the sustainable development of the sericulture sector.

The meeting was chaired by Dr. Mangi Lal Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR). Shri P. Sivakumar, IFS, Member Secretary, Central Silk Board, attended the meeting, along with Shri Purnesh Gururani, Director (Silk), Ministry of Textiles, Govt. of India.

The Committee reviewed the research achievements, ongoing programmes and future roadmap of CSB’s Research and Development Institutes and Seed Organizations. Detailed deliberations focused on strengthening research coordination, promoting technology development and ensuring the effective dissemination of research outcomes and innovations to stakeholders across the sericulture value chain.

The meeting brought together eminent Directors, scientists and subject matter experts from ICAR institutes, universities, including the University of Delhi, TERI, former Vice-Chancellors and other institutions, along with CSB scientists. Their valuable insights and recommendations contributed to the discussions on research priorities and future strategies for the sector.

The deliberations underscored the importance of quality research, inter-institutional collaboration and adoption of advanced technologies to enhance productivity, improve silk quality and strengthen the livelihoods of sericulture stakeholders. The meeting reaffirmed the importance of coordinated research and innovation in addressing emerging challenges and strengthening India's sericulture sector.

 

Source: Central Silk Board

2337070.title: 12th Session of India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission held in New Delhi
2337070.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
12th Session of India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission held in New Delhi
Minister of State Shri Jitin Prasada and Belarusian Foreign Minister Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov co-chair the Session
Both sides review bilateral cooperation and discuss measures to strengthen trade, economic and investment relations
India–Belarus Business and Investment Forum held alongside the Session to explore opportunities for greater business engagement
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi

The 12th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation was held on 16th November 2026 in New Delhi. Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada led the Indian delegation, while Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus H.E. Mr. Maxim Ryzhenkov led the Belarusian delegation.

The Session reviewed the progress of bilateral cooperation and discussed measures to further strengthen trade, economic and investment relations between the two countries. Both sides appreciated the longstanding and friendly relations between India and Belarus and highlighted the importance of regular exchanges, closer institutional engagement and greater participation of businesses in taking the partnership forward.

Discussions covered several important areas of economic cooperation, with a focus on expanding bilateral trade and investment. Both sides also discussed the Roadmap for Cooperation for 2027–2031 as an important step towards identifying future priorities and providing direction to bilateral economic engagement. Key sectors discussed included industry, financial and banking services, agriculture and food processing, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, tourism, education, culture, science and technology, construction and customs cooperation.

The Protocol of the 12th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission was signed by both Co-Chairs, reaffirming the commitment of the two countries to deepen bilateral cooperation.

Addressing the business community, Minister of State for Commerce and Industry Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted India's growing economic and manufacturing capabilities and the opportunities they offer for closer engagement with Belarusian businesses. He emphasised that the longstanding friendship between the two countries provides a strong foundation for building practical and mutually beneficial economic partnerships. He also encouraged businesses to explore joint ventures, technology partnerships, investment opportunities and greater business-to-business engagement.

Shri Jitin Prasada highlighted the potential for collaboration in areas such as pharmaceuticals, agricultural and industrial machinery, engineering, chemicals, digital technologies and scientific research. He also encouraged businesses from both countries to explore opportunities for market access, local partnerships, co-development and cooperation in emerging areas, including unmanned aerial systems and advanced manufacturing technologies.

On the sidelines of the 12th Session of the Inter-Governmental Commission, the India–Belarus Business and Investment Forum was also organised in New Delhi on 16th November 2026. The Forum brought together business representatives, industry associations and government institutions from India and Belarus, providing an opportunity for direct interaction, exchange of ideas and exploration of new areas of trade, investment and commercial cooperation.

The Forum saw participation from Belarusian companies representing diverse sectors, including automotive and agricultural machinery, mining equipment, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, microelectronics, banking, agriculture and engineering. Discussions focused on possibilities for joint ventures, technology transfer, localisation of manufacturing, research and development, and stronger supply-chain linkages. Opportunities in agricultural and civil unmanned aerial systems, pharmaceutical cooperation, mining equipment, water treatment technologies and food processing were also highlighted as potential areas for future collaboration.

Both sides underlined the importance of maintaining regular engagement between their business communities and encouraged enterprises to take forward the opportunities identified during the discussions.

India and Belarus agreed to continue working together to expand cooperation across the identified sectors and strengthen their economic partnership. Both sides also agreed to hold the 13th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission in 2027, with the dates and agenda to be finalised through diplomatic channels.

2337069.title: MoSJE and Ministry of Defence Join Hands to Strengthen Welfare of Senior Citizens in Cantonment Areas Across The Country
2337069.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
MoSJE and Ministry of Defence Join Hands to Strengthen Welfare of Senior Citizens in Cantonment Areas Across The Country
MoU Signed between DoSJE and DGDE in the Presence of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar
New Day Care Centres to be Established in Cantonments; Existing Centres and Senior Citizen Homes to be Supported and Expanded under AVYAY
Youth from Cantonment Areas to Receive Training as Geriatric Caregivers; Partnership to Promote Dignified, Secure and Active Ageing through Better Care and Community Participation
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Directorate General Defence Estates (DGDE), Ministry of Defence, in the National Capital here today, to strengthen the welfare and well-being of senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas.

The MoU was signed in the presence of Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar.

Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sudhansh Pant, Director General, Defence Estates, Smt. Shobha Gupta, Joint Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, and other senior officers from both Ministries were present on the occasion.

The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was formally exchanged between Ms Kajal Singh, Director, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and Shri Mane AmitKumar B., Deputy Director General (Cantonments Division-II), Directorate General Defence Estates, Ministry of Defence, in the presence of the Union Ministers and senior officials of both Ministries.

Speaking at the event, Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar reaffirmed the Government's commitment under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to ensuring dignified, secure and active ageing for every senior citizen.

Dr Kumar highlighted that through the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY), the Ministry is supporting Senior Citizen Homes, Day Care Centres, Geriatric caregiver training, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens (ELDERLINE – 14567) and other welfare initiatives. He stated that the MoU would extend better care, welfare services and opportunities for active ageing to senior citizens living in Cantonment areas.

The Minister also appealed to citizens, particularly youth, officers and staff of Cantonment Boards and members of Cantonment communities, to register as Vayo SAATHI volunteers.

Launched on November 4, 2026, alongside the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, Vayo SAATHI encourages citizens aged 18 years and above to spend time with senior citizens, assist them in their daily needs and facilitate their access to welfare schemes, the Minister said.

Emphasising the importance of inter-generational companionship, Dr. Virendra Kumar said, “Every Vayo SAATHI is a bridge between generations. I urge citizens to register as a Vayo SAATHI and become a companion to our elders.”

Dr Kumar reiterated the Government’s commitment to the welfare of senior citizens and enumerated the initiatives taken by MoSJE, including the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), to improve the quality of life of the elderly.

He stated that the MoU marks an important step towards strengthening the support system for senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas by ensuring access to better care, welfare services and opportunities for active and dignified ageing.

Addressing the gathering, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that senior citizens are not merely members of families but also carriers of experience, traditions and social values. He observed that their guidance and wisdom would play an important role in the journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Shri Singh said their experience, wisdom and guidance will be invaluable in the journey to create peaceful, harmonious and knowledgeable societies.

Highlighting their lifelong contribution to building families, society and the nation, he termed it a social and moral responsibility to ensure that they are accorded respect, security and a sense of belonging.

Recalling the Indian ethos of “Matru Devo Bhava, Pitru Devo Bhava”, he emphasised that caring for senior citizens is a social and moral responsibility as well as a national duty, extending beyond the boundaries of individual families.

While acknowledging the progress made in senior citizen welfare, Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the need for continuous improvement in the delivery of services to the elderly.

The Raksha Mantri also called for regular social audits of Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes to assess the quality of services, identify areas requiring further improvement and address gaps through continuous monitoring.

In his closing remarks, Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sudhansh Pant said that the MoU represents a shared commitment towards ensuring companionship, dignity and care for senior citizens closer to their homes.

Joint Secretary, MoSJE, Shri Sajeesh Kumar N, stated that a Joint Working Group would work closely with DGDE to ensure that the new Day Care Centres become operational and caregiver training programmes commence in the identified Cantonments at the earliest.

The MoU aims to promote the welfare of senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY). The partnership envisages the establishment of new Day Care Centres and Senior Citizen Homes with residential facilities of 25/50-bed capacity, wherever feasible. It will also support and strengthen existing facilities run by Cantonment Boards.

Under the arrangement, DGDE will facilitate the provision of infrastructure, premises and basic civic amenities, while the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment will extend financial assistance, technical guidance, training and operational support.

The partnership will also focus on training youth from Cantonment areas as geriatric caregivers, along with awareness generation, skill development and promotion of inter-generational bonding. A Joint Working Group will be constituted to monitor implementation, facilitate coordination and ensure effective execution of the initiatives. The MoU will remain valid for five years, with a provision for renewal.

The MoU comes at a significant juncture as the Defence Estates Department marks its centenary, commemorating 100 years since its establishment in 1926. The partnership reflects the expanding role of the Defence Estates Department from administration to community welfare.

By bringing together the infrastructure and civic facilities of Cantonment Boards with the policy, technical and financial support of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the initiative exemplifies the Whole of Government approach towards ensuring the welfare, dignity and well-being of senior citizens.
