2337054.title: Self-Enumeration for Phase II of Census 2027 Commences in Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Non-Snow-Bound Areas of Uttarakhand
2337054.body_html:
Ministry of Home Affairs
Self-Enumeration for Phase II of Census 2027 Commences in Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Non-Snow-Bound Areas of Uttarakhand
Corresponding house-to-house Population Enumeration in these States and areas will be conducted from December 1, 2026 to January 4, 2027 followed by a revisional round from January 5 to 9, 2027
To participate in Self-Enumeration during Phase II, residents can log in to official portal se.census.gov.in using their mobile number (preferably the one registered during Phase I)
While Self-Enumeration allows residents to provide their details online at their convenience, Enumerators will continue to carry out door-to-door visits in all allocated blocks
Households that do not opt for Self-Enumeration will be covered during house-to-house visits by Enumerators
All information collected under Census Act, 1948, remains strictly confidential and is used solely for statistical purposes and development planning
 Residents are encouraged to actively participate in this important national exercise and extend their cooperation to Enumerators
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Self-Enumeration (SE) process for Phase II of Census 2027 i.e. Population Enumeration (PE) has commenced today in the States of Goa, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and the non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. Residents can submit their household details online till November 30, 2026.

The corresponding house-to-house Population Enumeration in these States and areas will be conducted from December 1, 2026 to January 4, 2027 followed by a revisional round from January 5 to 9, 2027. The reference date for these States/areas will be 00:00 hours of January 5, 2027.

In the remaining States and Union Territories, Population Enumeration will be conducted from January 25 to February 28, 2027 followed by a revisional round from March 1 to 5, 2027. The provision for Self-Enumeration in these States/UTs will be available from January 10 to 24, 2027, prior to the commencement of house-to-house visits by Enumerators. The reference date for Census in these States/UTs will be 00:00 hours of March 1, 2027.

The Houselisting and Housing Census (HLO) under Phase I of Census 2027 have been completed across 35 States and Union Territories, except Manipur, marking the completion of first phase of the Census exercise.

For the first time, Census 2027 is being conducted using digital tools, with Self-Enumeration introduced as an additional facility. It is a secure, convenient and user-friendly web-based facility available in 16 Indian languages. To participate in Self-Enumeration during Phase II, residents can log in to the official portal se.census.gov.in using their mobile number (preferably the one registered during Phase I) along with basic details and answer 40 notified questions covering household and individual particulars. Upon successful submission, a unique Self-Enumeration ID (SE ID) is generated, which is to be shared with the Enumerator during the subsequent field visit to complete the process.

While Self-Enumeration allows residents to provide their details online at their convenience, Enumerators will continue to carry out door-to-door visits in all allocated blocks. Households that do not opt for Self-Enumeration will be covered during the house-to-house visits by Enumerators.

All information collected under the Census Act, 1948, remains strictly confidential and is used solely for statistical purposes and development planning. Residents are encouraged to actively participate in this important national exercise and extend their cooperation to Enumerators.

2337050.title: Ministry of Minority Affairs Organises Workshop on AI for Digital Transformation to Strengthen AI-Enabled Governance
2337050.body_html:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Ministry of Minority Affairs Organises Workshop on AI for Digital Transformation to Strengthen AI-Enabled Governance
Senior officials participated in expert-led sessions, hands-on exercises and demonstrations exploring AI-powered tools, agentic workflows and their applications in research, document processing and administrative decision-making
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 5:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Minority Affairs organised a one-day workshop on ‘AI for Digital Transformation,’ in collaboration with the Wadhwani Government AI Academy, on 16th November, 2026, to familiarise senior officials with the evolving AI landscape and explore its potential to transform public administration. The workshop was chaired by Dr. Srivatsa Krishna, Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs, and was attended by senior officials of the Ministry.

The programme focused on the ongoing emphases towards AI-enabled governance, highlighting the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Generative AI and Agentic AI in enhancing administrative processes and institutional efficiency.

Addressing the inaugural session, Dr. Srivatsa Krishna emphasised the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence and the need for government institutions to proactively understand and embrace its applications. Drawing a parallel with the advent of the internet, he described AI as a defining technological shift that would have a far-reaching impact on society.

 

Highlighting the importance of practical learning over theoretical discussions, Dr. Krishna emphasised that the workshop should provide officers with hands-on exposure to AI tools, their applications and potential limitations, including the risks of AI-generated inaccuracies or hallucinations. He encouraged participants to actively engage with experts, raise questions and understand how these technologies could be responsibly leveraged in government functioning.

The workshop featured expert-led sessions, interactive discussions, hands-on exercises and demonstrations of AI-powered tools and agentic workflows. The sessions covered practical applications of AI in research, information extraction, document processing, administrative decision-making and other government functions. Participants also gained insights into the effective and responsible use of these tools in public administration.

 

 

The capacity-building programme is being undertaken in phases to facilitate wider participation across different levels of the Ministry's administrative hierarchy. Following the session for senior management, a dedicated programme for officials below the rank of Deputy Secretary is scheduled for 18th November, 2026. A more detailed follow-up workshop is also envisaged in December 2026 to further strengthen practical understanding and application of AI tools.

This initiative reflects the Ministry's commitment to institutional capacity building, administrative modernisation and the adoption of emerging technologies. Through structured learning opportunities and practical exposure, the Ministry aims to equip its officials with the knowledge and capabilities required to harness artificial Intelligence for more efficient, responsive and citizen-centric governance.

2337049.title: 10 Films to Compete for ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at 57th IFFI
2337049.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
10 Films to Compete for ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at 57th IFFI
Four-member international jury headed by Dr. Prof. Ahmed Bedjaoui to adjudicate the entries
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 5:52PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 16 November 2026

 

Ten Indian and international fiction feature films will compete for the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), scheduled to be held in Goa from 20th to 28th November, 2026. The selected films explore themes of peace, tolerance, empathy, social justice and intercultural dialogue, in keeping with the festival's overarching theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’.

Instituted at the 46th edition of IFFI in collaboration with the International Council for Film, Television and Audiovisual Communication (CICT-ICFT), Paris, under the aegis of UNESCO, the award recognizes films that reflect Mahatma Gandhi's ideals of non-violence, tolerance, intercultural understanding and a culture of peace.

The four-member international jury will be headed by Prof. (Dr.) Ahmed Bedjaoui of Algeria, a University professor, filmmaker, producer and film critic. The other members are Maria Cristina Iglesias of Argentina/France, former Head of Programme at UNESCO's Cultural Sector; Georges Dupont of Luxembourg, former Director-General of CICT-ICFT; and Manouj Kadaamh of India, an internationally acclaimed filmmaker and member of ICFT.

The ten films selected for this year's competition bring together stories from diverse cultural backgrounds, highlighting human relationships, social challenges and shared values.

The international line-up includes Call Me Queen, directed by Emily Atef, a Germany-France-UK-Kenya production set in 1990s Nairobi. It follows a single mother who finds strength in an unexpected friendship while confronting an AIDS diagnosis and social injustice. The film will have its India Premiere at IFFI.

India is represented by three films. Kabir Sir ka Akhri Lesson (Kabir Sir), directed by Sarfaraz Alam and starring Vinay Pathak, explores the challenges faced by veteran educators in the age of technology and will have its World Premiere. Scroll, directed by Kannan S, examines smartphone addiction through the disturbing experiences of a young man using an app-based game to control his screen time. Sev Micchar, the debut feature of Muskan Asthana, explores family tensions, rivalry and reconciliation through the story of a shopkeeper facing financial and personal challenges.

The Haiti-France-Belgium-Luxembourg-Canada production Marie Madeleine, directed by Gessica Généus, explores faith, social conventions and personal freedom through the evolving relationship between an independent woman and a young evangelist. The film won the Grand Prix du Jury at the Festival de Cabourg 2026 and will have its Asia Premiere at IFFI.

Ghanaian-American filmmaker Amartei Armar's Our Time Will Come (Ego Reach We All) follows two orphans travelling to Accra in search of their last living parent. The film won the Pardo for Change and Pardo for Best Performance at the Locarno Film Festival 2026 and will have its Asia Premiere.

Turkish filmmaker Faysal Soysal's Rahma tells the story of an archaeologist whose unexpected bond with a nine-year-old Syrian orphan brings emotional healing and changes her outlook on life. The film will have its Asia Premiere.

Strawberries (La más dulce), directed by Laïla Marrakchi, follows two Moroccan women working as seasonal strawberry pickers in Spain who find the courage to stand against workplace abuse and exploitation. The France-Morocco-Spain-Belgium production will have its India Premiere.

Another Turkish entry, The Farm (Süt Çiftliği), directed by Elif Eda, follows a 12-year-old girl who, disturbed by the separation of newborn calves from their mothers at a dairy farm, joins an orphaned veterinary apprentice to free the pregnant cows. The film will have its International Premiere at IFFI.

The Taiwan-Singapore production, Will You Still Be My Friend (Ri guang), directed by Lu Po-Shun, explores the friendship between two 13-year-old boys from different backgrounds, as tensions among adults threaten to drive them apart. The film will have its India Premiere.

Through this diverse selection, the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal competition at the 57th IFFI brings together cinematic narratives that promote compassion, mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and shared human values across cultures and geographical boundaries.

2337040.title: Marathi Cinema Takes Centre Stage at 57th IFFI
2337040.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Marathi Cinema Takes Centre Stage at 57th IFFI
Diverse film selections accompany special tributes to Legends Suryakant Mandhare and Nana Patekar
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 5:46PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 16 November 2026

 

Mumbai, the heart of India’s mainstream Hindi film industry, is also home to a vibrant Marathi cinema tradition that has evolved alongside Bollywood, carving out a distinct identity through its rich content driven storytelling, grounded realism, and deep literary roots. Celebrating this enduring cinematic legacy, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) brings the diversity of Marathi cinema into focus through a selection of contemporary feature and non-feature films, alongside tributes to its celebrated personalities and cinematic heritage.

This year at IFFI, seven Marathi films have been selected for the Indian Panorama, while a celebrated classic will be presented in its restored version under the Centenary Tributes section. Another Marathi film will be showcased under the Gala Premieres section.

Among the feature-film selections, Aadi Anant, directed by Mahesh Limaye, explores the emotional bond between an aspiring actor and his grandfather. The film which highlights the challenges of caregiving, family responsibilities and the meaning of success, features Ashok Saraf, Sankarshan Karhade, Sakhi Gokhale and Yogesh Shirsat.

The Mainstream Cinema section of Indian Panorama brings together Deool Band 2 (Temple Closed 2), written and directed by Pravin Vitthal Tarde, which portrays agrarian distress through the story of a woman who loses her farmer husband and Baapya (The Man), directed by Samir Tewari, that  follows a transgender protagonist returning to their hometown, weaving together themes of family and gender identity.

Another notable selection is Tighee, directed by Jeejivisha Kale, which is among the films featured in the Best Debut Director of Indian Feature Film category at IFFI. This poignant family drama delves into relationships, sacrifice and the pain of unspoken emotions.

The Indian Panorama non-feature section further showcases three Marathi films, each offering a distinct narrative. Amyth Patkar’s Punishment (Shiksha) examines guilt and its consequences through two seemingly unrelated thefts. Santosh Davakhar’s Sky Tree (Abhal-Vriksh) portrays a villager’s hopes amid drought, while Nipun Dharmadhikari’s The Moon (Chandoba) captures a teenager’s struggle with vitiligo and the social judgement surrounding the condition.

Beyond the Indian Panorama selections, Tu Aahes Na (You Are There, Right?), directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Deepak Gawade, will be presented under the Gala Premieres section. The film touches upon grief, loneliness and identity, highlighting the unexpected human connections that bring meaning to life.

Marathi storytelling also finds a place in IFFI’s Best Web Series Award category through Devkhel, directed by Chandrakanth Lata Gaikwad. This gripping crime thriller is set in a coastal village where a series of mysterious ritual-linked murders unfold, with superstition concealing a chilling truth.

   

The festival also celebrates Marathi cinema’s rich legacy through the Centenary Tributes section, commemorating legendary actor Suryakant Mandhare on his birth centenary. As part of the tribute, his 1965 Marathi film Sadhi Manase will be presented in its restored version by the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) under the National Film Heritage Mission. A Homage section dedicated to the late Nana Patekar, renowned for his intense and memorable performances in Hindi and Marathi cinema, is also part of the 57th IFFI. The screening of his Hindi film Diksha and open air screening of his iconic Marathi film Natsamrat at Miramar Beach will offer audiences an opportunity to celebrate the legendary actor’s enduring contribution to Indian cinema.

2337025.title: Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and Kanpur MP Shri Ramesh Awasthi Flag Off New Kanpur Express Between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar Terminal
2337025.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Railway Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and Kanpur MP Shri Ramesh Awasthi Flag Off New Kanpur Express Between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar Terminal 
Kanpur Express to Directly Connect Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh’s Premier Industrial, Leather and Educational Hub, with Delhi’s Major Multimodal Transit Gateway
Kanpur to Get Permanent Relief from Decades-Old Traffic Congestion at Railway Crossings Through 16-km Elevated Railway Track: Ashwini Vaishnaw
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting, and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, and Member of Parliament, Shri Ramesh Awasthi,  flagged off the inaugural run of the new Kanpur Express today. The train will operate between Kanpur Central and Anand Vihar Terminal, providing connectivity in both directions.

माननीय रेल मंत्री श्री @AshwiniVaishnaw एवं उत्तर प्रदेश के माननीय जनप्रतिनिधियों द्वारा कानपुर-दिल्ली (आनंद विहार) एक्सप्रेस का हरी झंडी दिखाकर शुभारंभ किया गया। #RailInfra4UttarPradesh https://t.co/G2jLLNwIkV

— Ministry of Railways (@RailMinIndia) November 16, 2026

The occasion was attended by Smt. Pramila Pandey, Mayor, Kanpur Nagar Nigam; and Shri Devendra Singh Bhole, Member of Parliament, Akbarpur, along with other dignitaries and senior railway officials.

The new daily train service will strengthen rail connectivity between Uttar Pradesh and the National Capital Region (NCR), providing an additional travel option for passengers travelling between Kanpur and Delhi.

New Train Service to Boost Connectivity Across Major Industrial and Commercial Centres

Covering a distance of 428 km, the train will comprise 22 modern LHB coaches and connect several important towns and economic centres along its route.

The train service will benefit passengers from Phaphund, serving the industrial areas of Auraiya, including NTPC Auraiya and GAIL Pata; Etawah, an important agricultural centre; and Tundla, providing connectivity to the Firozabad region, renowned for its glass industry.

The train will further connect Hathras, known for its hing processing, brassware and agro-based industries, and Aligarh, an important centre for the lock industry and home to Aligarh Muslim University. It will also strengthen connectivity to Khurja, renowned for its ceramic and pottery industry.

Further, the train service will connect Dadri, an important logistics and industrial hub, with Ghaziabad, one of the major industrial centres of the NCR, before reaching Anand Vihar Terminal, a major multimodal transport hub in Delhi.

Boost to Regional Development and Passenger Convenience

The new train service will establish a direct rail link between Kanpur, one of Uttar Pradesh’s premier industrial, leather and educational hubs, and Anand Vihar Terminal in Delhi, a major multimodal transit gateway connecting passengers to various parts of the National Capital Region. This connectivity will facilitate convenient travel for business professionals, students, workers and other passengers travelling between the two important urban centres.

Shri Vaishnaw congratulated the people of Kanpur on the introduction of the new train service. He said that Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath has also extended his best wishes to the people of Kanpur for this new train service.

Upcoming Major Railway Projects

Highlighting the upcoming railway infrastructure projects in the city, the Railway Minister said that the construction of a 16-kilometre elevated railway track between Anwarganj and Mandhana would provide a permanent solution to Kanpur’s decades-old problem of traffic congestion at railway crossings. He further informed that the Detailed Project Report (DPR) had been completed and the necessary approvals for the project had been obtained. Construction work is expected to commence shortly.

 

On the proposed Bullet Train project, the Railway Minister said that the Bullet Train North Corridor would open a new chapter in Kanpur’s development. The proposed corridor will connect Delhi, Agra, Kanpur, Varanasi, Lucknow and Ayodhya, extending further to Patna, Siliguri and Guwahati. Once operational, the bullet train will reduce the travel time between Delhi and Kanpur to approximately 1 hour and 45 minutes. The journey between Lucknow and Kanpur will take around 27 minutes, while Kanpur and Prayagraj will be connected in approximately 1 hour and 15 minutes.

He further highlighted that high-speed rail connectivity would strengthen Kanpur’s links with major cities and give a boost to regional and economic development.

Speaking about the redevelopment of Kanpur Central Railway Station, Vaishnaw said that work is progressing at a rapid pace. He highlighted the ongoing redevelopment efforts and stated that several additional railway infrastructure development initiatives would be undertaken in Kanpur in the coming period.

 

Addressing the gathering, Shri Awasthi, said that the resolve to restore Kanpur’s lost glory was now beginning to take shape on the ground. He said that the announcement of a Bullet Train halt at Kanpur had brought immense joy to the people of the city. He said the Railways has approved the long-pending demand of Kanpur residents for the construction of an elevated corridor on the Anwarganj-Mandhana railway section (2017-18). Shri Awasthi expressed happiness over the redevelopment of Kanpur Central railway station and the introduction of a new train service named after Kanpur.

The introduction of this service reflects Indian Railways’ continued commitment to strengthening passenger connectivity and providing modern, comfortable and reliable rail travel facilities.

*****

2336782.title: TDB-DST Signs Agreement with NeoSeeker Metals under RDI Fund to Advance Indigenous Critical Minerals Recovery Technology
2336782.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST Signs Agreement with NeoSeeker Metals under RDI Fund to Advance Indigenous Critical Minerals Recovery Technology
Advancing Indigenous Critical Minerals Recycling Technology from TRL-5 to TRL-9
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi

As India expands its footprint in electric mobility, clean energy, electronics and advanced manufacturing, the demand for critical minerals is set to grow significantly. This growing demand also brings into focus an important national challenge—securing access to these strategic resources sustainably while addressing the increasing volume of electronic and end-of-life battery waste.

Recognising this potential, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Neo Seekermetals Pvt. Ltd., Hyderabad, Telangana, under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The agreement will support the development and commercialisation of an indigenous technology for the extraction of critical metals through the recycling of e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste.

The project, titled “Extraction of Critical Metals by Recycling of E-Waste and Lithium-Ion Battery Waste,” has a total project cost of ₹20 crore, with ₹10 crore approved under the RDI Fund. The financial assistance will be extended through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).

Neo Seekermetals is addressing this challenge through an integrated and patented recycling process designed to process both e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste. The technology seeks to recover valuable metals and battery materials from these complex waste streams, creating a pathway where materials that would otherwise be discarded can be brought back into the productive economy.

The project aims to advance the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-5 to TRL-9, taking it towards commercial-scale deployment. The proposed process is designed to support the recovery of a range of valuable materials, contributing to the development of a more resilient domestic ecosystem for critical minerals and metals.

Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, Technology Development Board, said, “India's transition towards clean energy and advanced technologies will require secure and sustainable access to critical minerals. Developing indigenous capabilities to recover these resources from e-waste and end-of-life batteries is an important part of this larger effort. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting technologies that can combine innovation with strategic relevance, helping transform waste streams into valuable resources and strengthening the foundations of a circular economy.”

An authorised representative of Neo Seekermetals said, “The support from TDB under the RDI Fund will help us take our technology forward towards commercial deployment. Our focus is on building an efficient and sustainable process for recovering critical and valuable materials from e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste. This partnership will provide an important impetus to our efforts to build indigenous capabilities in resource recovery and contribute to India's growing circular economy.”

2336781.title: Vice-President addresses Orientation Programme for Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar
2336781.body_html:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President addresses Orientation Programme for Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar
Vice-President urges legislators to uphold democratic values and strengthen public trust through dedicated service
Healthy debate, constructive cooperation essential for strengthening democracy: Vice-President
Vice-President calls for greater use of AI and digital technologies in legislative functioning
Odisha’s progress will be central to India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047: Vice-President
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 12:39PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the Orientation Programme for the Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar. Calling upon legislators to uphold the rich democratic traditions of Bharat, he emphasised the importance of constructive debates, informed discussions, legislative efficiency and people-centric governance in strengthening democratic institutions.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Orientation Programme for the Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar today. He emphasised the importance of constructive debates, informed discussions, adherence to legislative procedures and embracing emerging technologies to strengthen democratic institutions. He urged legislators to uphold Bharat’s rich democratic traditions and work towards a developed Odisha, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; Chief Minister, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Speaker of the Odisha Legislative Assembly, Smt. Surama Padhy;along with Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly were present on the occasion.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 16, 2026

The Vice-President appreciated the Speaker, Smt. Surama Padhy, for organising the orientation programme, describing such initiatives as instrumental in strengthening democratic institutions and enabling legislators to discharge their constitutional responsibilities effectively.

Referring to India’s ancient democratic traditions, the Vice-President cited the democratic institutions of Vaishali and the Chola-era Kudavolai system, observing that democracy has deep roots in Bharat’s civilisational history. He said that Bharat rightly takes pride in being the ‘Mother of Democracy’ and called upon the legislators of Odisha to live up to this distinguished legacy.

Emphasising that electoral victories must translate into meaningful public service, the Vice-President said, “We win in the elections by votes, but we can earn the respect of the people only through our service." He observed that the Legislative Assembly is much more than a forum for debate, as every policy framed, question raised and law enacted has the potential to improve the lives of countless citizens.

Referring to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said that Odisha’s progress would be central to India’s progress. With Odisha approaching the centenary of its formation as a province in 2036, he highlighted the significance of Vision Odisha 2036 in transforming the State into a developed, prosperous and inclusive State. He expressed confidence that legislators would play an important role in creating opportunities for the youth and ensuring that development reaches every village and every family.

Addressing the issue of disruptions in legislative proceedings, the Vice-President emphasised that differences of opinion should not come in the way of the larger commitment to the people and the Constitution. He remarked, “In a democracy, we may agree to disagree, but we should all agree towards one thing – our commitment to the people and the Constitution.” Reiterating that “debate, discussion or even sometimes disruption must lead to a decision”, he called for healthy debates and constructive cooperation to strengthen democracy and advance national development.

Underscoring the importance of continuous learning and preparation, the Vice-President urged Members to familiarise themselves thoroughly with legislative rules and procedures, budgetary processes, committee systems, parliamentary conventions and ethics.

He particularly highlighted the importance of Question Hour and Zero Hour, describing them as crucial opportunities for individual Members to raise constituency-related concerns and important policy matters. He urged Members to cooperate with the Chair to ensure that these important parliamentary instruments function without disruption.

The Vice-President also emphasised the role of the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) in building consensus on the business of the House. He observed that greater agreement within the Committee would contribute to smoother and more productive legislative proceedings.

Highlighting the growing role of technology in legislative functioning, the Vice-President welcomed the inauguration of the Digital House in the Odisha Legislative Assembly under the National e-Vidhan Application. Referring to the increasing use of digital platforms in the Rajya Sabha, he noted that parliamentary papers, questions and debates were now available in multiple languages with the support of technology. He urged legislators to embrace emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing, to make legislative institutions future-ready.

Concluding his address, the Vice-President reminded legislators of the immense responsibility and transformative potential of their office. He observed that a thoughtful intervention could bring about a change in policy, while a compassionate decision could restore hope in the lives of countless citizens. He wished all Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly a fruitful orientation programme and an enriching legislative journey.

The programme was attended by Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Speaker of the Odisha Legislative Assembly,Smt. Surama Padhy; Deputy Speaker of Odisha Legislative Assembly Shri Bhabani Shankar Bhoi; and Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly, among other dignitaries.

2336751.title: NICDC Showcases Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Progress and Investment Opportunities at 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam
2336751.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
NICDC Showcases Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Progress and Investment Opportunities at 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam
CEO & MD, NICDC, Briefs Dignitaries on Progress of Three Industrial Nodes in Andhra Pradesh
Summit Focuses on Strengthening Global Partnerships, Attracting Investments and Positioning India as a Global Manufacturing Hub
NICDC Pavilion Showcases Andhra Pradesh’s Industrial Potential, Investment Opportunities and Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 11:33AM by PIB Delhi

The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) organised the 31st edition of the CII Partnership Summit 2026 on 12–13 November 2026 in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, under the theme “Navigating the New World Order: Trade | Technology | Trust | Thought Leadership.” Organised in association with the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, and hosted by the Government of Andhra Pradesh, the Summit brought together policymakers, international delegates, global business leaders and investors to deliberate on emerging opportunities in trade, technology and economic cooperation.

The inaugural session was attended by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal; Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu; Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri Konidala Pawan Kalyan; and Union Minister of Civil Aviation Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu. Shri Nara Lokesh, Minister for Human Resources Development, IT, Electronics & Communication and RTG, Government of Andhra Pradesh, also delivered a special address.

The inaugural session also witnessed the participation of several senior leaders, Union and State Ministers, overseas trade ministers, senior government officials, policymakers and prominent industry representatives from India and abroad, reflecting the strong participation in efforts to strengthen international trade, investment, industrial cooperation and strategic partnerships.

The Summit provided a platform for deliberations on international trade, global value chains, resilient supply chains, advanced manufacturing, defence technology, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, smart manufacturing, green energy, future mobility and emerging technologies. Discussions focused on strengthening international partnerships, attracting investments and positioning India as a competitive destination for global manufacturing and innovation.

During the Summit, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu visited the National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) pavilion. Shri Rajat Kumar Saini, CEO & MD, NICDC, briefed the dignitaries on the development and progress of NICDC's three Greenfield Industrial Smart City nodes in Andhra Pradesh: Krishnapatnam, Orvakal and Kopparthy.

The NICDC pavilion showcased India's evolving industrial infrastructure landscape and investment opportunities through various initiatives and digital platforms. Key highlights included the development of Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities, BHAVYA (Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana), the Industrial Corridor Land Platform (ICLP), which enables investors to discover and compare verified industrial land opportunities across India, and Koyla Shakti, a Smart Coal Analytics Dashboard. The pavilion also featured a 360-degree Virtual Reality (VR) Tour, offering visitors an immersive overview of NICDC's industrial corridor projects.

Shri Rajat Kumar Saini apprised the dignitaries of the development progress of the three industrial nodes. The updates highlighted the progress of infrastructure development across the projects and NICDC's continued efforts towards creating investment-ready industrial destinations in the State.

The pavilion also showcased Andhra Pradesh's industrial potential, highlighting the three nodes' combined project area of 7,223 acres, investment potential of ₹31,360 crore and employment potential of 2 lakh. The three nodes are being developed under different industrial corridors and are envisaged as integrated industrial ecosystems supported by world-class infrastructure and connectivity. Their development is aimed at facilitating large-scale investments, strengthening manufacturing capabilities, generating employment and accelerating industrial growth in Andhra Pradesh.

Through these displays and interactions, NICDC highlighted investment opportunities across manufacturing and emerging sectors, positioning Andhra Pradesh as an attractive destination for domestic and international investors.

During the Japan Country Session, H.E. Mr Keiichi Ono, Ambassador of Japan to India, highlighted the growing India–Japan economic partnership, noting that 31 Japanese companies across three cities in Andhra Pradesh have generated over 8,000 local jobs. He also highlighted opportunities for collaboration in steel, pharmaceuticals, clean energy and semiconductors.

Shri T. G. Bharath, Minister for Industries & Commerce and Food Processing, Government of Andhra Pradesh, highlighted the State's industrial infrastructure, strategic ports, sectoral opportunities and focus on translating investment commitments into project implementation.

Shri Rajat Kumar Saini delivered the opening remarks, outlining five key areas for deeper cooperation: manufacturing and industrial corridor development, resilient supply chains, advanced technologies, sustainable industrial development, and MSME partnerships and skill development. He emphasised the need to translate investment opportunities into actionable partnerships, highlighting Japan's commitment to facilitate investments of JPY 10 trillion in India over the next decade.

Mr Kiyotaka Doho, Director General, JETRO Chennai, highlighted the growing interest among Japanese companies in India and Andhra Pradesh, with over 80 per cent of surveyed companies planning to expand their operations. Mr Rajesh Mittal, President & MD, Isuzu Motors India, underscored the importance of Japanese manufacturing practices, quality standards, skill development and local supplier ecosystems.

Through the development of Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities across various industrial corridors, NICDC is working towards strengthening India's manufacturing ecosystem, enhancing logistics efficiency and creating investment-ready industrial destinations. Its initiatives aim to attract domestic and international investments, generate employment and facilitate the integration of Indian industries with global value chains.

Other distinguished dignitaries present at the event included Shri T. G. Bharath, Minister for Industries and Food Processing, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri B. C. Janardhan Reddy, Minister for Roads and Buildings, Infrastructure and Investments, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri G. Sai Prasad, Chief Secretary to the Government of Andhra Pradesh; Shri R. Mukundan, President, CII and Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Limited; and Shri Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII.

NICDC's participation in the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 provided an opportunity to showcase the progress of its industrial corridor projects, engage with global stakeholders and highlight investment opportunities in Andhra Pradesh. These efforts contribute to the Government of India's vision of strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities and achieving Viksit Bharat @2047.

National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation Limited (NICDC), under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, is mandated to develop world-class Greenfield Industrial Smart Cities across the country. Through integrated industrial infrastructure and digital initiatives, NICDC aims to enhance manufacturing competitiveness, attract investments and promote sustainable economic development.

2336726.title: India and Egypt Hold Ministerial-Level 7th Joint Trade Committee Meeting to Strengthen Bilateral Economic Ties
2336726.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India and Egypt Hold Ministerial-Level 7th Joint Trade Committee Meeting to Strengthen Bilateral Economic Ties
Both sides agree to set up a Joint Working Group to explore Terms of Reference for a Preferential or Free Trade Agreement
India–Egypt bilateral trade grows 35% to USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26; trade during April–September 2026 rises 65% to USD 5.04 billion
More than 300 Indian and Egyptian companies participate in India–Egypt Business Forum to explore trade, investment and manufacturing partnerships
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 9:37AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, co-chaired the 7th session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital today. The meeting marked the first occasion on which this important bilateral institutional mechanism was convened at the ministerial level, underscoring the priority both governments attach to strengthening the economic dimension of the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of USD 12 billion. They emphasised the need to diversify trade, promote value-added exports and address trade-related challenges. As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries.

The meeting was preceded by bilateral discussions between the two Ministers on expanding trade, facilitating investments and developing long-term industrial and commercial linkages. The JTC provided an opportunity to review existing trade ties, assess challenges faced by businesses and identify new areas for closer collaboration.

The Committee reviewed the growth in India–Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to reach USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26 (April 2025–March 2026). Trade during April–September 2026 also grew by 65% to reach USD 5.04 billion, compared to USD 3.08 billion during the corresponding period in 2025. The increase reflects the growing momentum in commercial exchanges and the potential for further diversification of the trade basket. Significant complementarities exist for enhanced trade in industrial goods, energy and fertilisers, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, engineering, textiles and agricultural products.

The discussions primarily focused on expanding trade, developing supply chains and establishing predictable trade pathways. Both sides considered measures to address non-tariff barriers, facilitate customs processes, strengthen standards and conformity assessment, and improve market access. They also discussed practical issues affecting business operations, including product registrations and trade-related regulatory procedures.

Discussions also focused on strengthening business exchanges and encouraging joint manufacturing and investment. Priority sectors included pharmaceuticals and medical devices, engineering and electrical equipment, fertilisers, textiles, renewable energy and emerging technologies. Opportunities for Indian investment in Egyptian industrial zones, as well as Egyptian investment in India's expanding manufacturing and services sectors, also formed an important part of the agenda.

Both sides expressed interest in strengthening the framework agreement between Invest India and Egypt’s General Authority for Investment and Free Zones, including a proposed digital platform for sharing investment information and facilitating business linkages.

Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains. India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships.

Speaking at the Joint Trade Committee meeting, Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted five areas of strong complementarity between India and Egypt: pharmaceuticals and healthcare, leveraging India’s strengths in affordable medicines, vaccines and medical technology; engineering and automobiles, covering machinery, auto components and industrial manufacturing; agriculture and food processing, including food security, fertilisers, irrigation and cold-chain infrastructure; digital and fintech, through UPI linkages, local currency trade and India’s Digital Public Infrastructure; and culture and museums, through proposed collaboration between the Grand Egyptian Museum and India’s upcoming Yuge Yugeen Bharat National Museum in conservation, curation and digitisation.

The ministerial-level JTC is an important step towards advancing the economic priorities of the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership. It was held against the backdrop of the meeting between President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the BRICS Summit in India in September 2026. The JTC seeks to translate this political momentum into stronger trade flows, new investments, joint manufacturing, greater market access and more resilient supply chains connecting India, Egypt and wider regional markets.

The next JTC meeting was agreed to be held in New Delhi in 2028, or earlier at a mutually convenient date.

The India–Egypt Business Forum brought together more than 300 companies from India and Egypt today, providing a platform to strengthen business engagement under the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, addressed the Forum, which was attended by industry leaders and senior business representatives from a wide range of sectors.

The Forum was organised on the sidelines of Shri Piyush Goyal’s official visit to Egypt from 15 to 16 November 2026. The opening session was addressed by Dr. Mohamed Awad, Chief Executive Officer of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); Mr. Vijay Sankar, President of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and Chairman of Sanmar Group; and Mr. Ahmed ElWakil, President of the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce.

Addressing the session, Shri Goyal proposed a four-point action agenda ahead of the 80th anniversary of India–Egypt diplomatic relations in 2027. The agenda included resolving identified trade barriers within a time-bound framework; encouraging Egyptian investments in Indian states and industrial clusters, with Invest India facilitating opportunities; bringing suppliers of large companies into the partnership to create opportunities for smaller businesses; and institutionalising annual reviews to track progress and translate business discussions into concrete contracts.

Underscoring the ambition of the partnership, Shri Goyal said, "Years from now, when someone studies this decade, let them find factories with labels that say: Made in Egypt, with India. Made in India, with Egypt."

A dedicated session on investment opportunities in Egypt brought together senior representatives of GAFI and the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE), who presented the country’s industrial and investment opportunities. Egypt’s strategic location linking the Mediterranean and Red Seas, its expanding ports and logistics infrastructure, and its access to African, Arab and European markets offer opportunities for Indian businesses seeking to establish manufacturing and export-oriented operations.

The Forum also featured a session on the experiences of Indian companies operating in Egypt, including TCI Sanmar, Galaxy Chemical and Abdos. Their presence illustrated the potential for Indian investments to contribute to Egyptian industrial production, employment, technology development, exports and integration into regional supply chains. Representatives of the two business communities explored areas of cooperation in engineering and electrical equipment, chemicals and fertilisers, pharmaceuticals, textiles, food processing, automotive components, renewable energy and logistics.

A special panel on the digital economy brought together stakeholders from Egypt’s digital technology and transformation ecosystem and leading Indian startups and technology companies. Moderated by Eng. Ayman El Gohary, Chairman of Global for Smart Solutions, the panel included experts and industry leaders from both countries. The Egyptian participants included Eng. Mahmoud Sofrata of the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), Mr. Fady Ismaeel of AGX, Dr. Kareem Hamza of National System and Dr. Sideek Ahmed of Eram Holding. Indian industry representatives included Mr. Rajesh Ranganathan of Zoho and Mr. Pradeep Gilbile of Datamorphosis. The discussions focused on opportunities in enterprise technology, digital solutions, innovation and industry partnerships.

Earlier in the day, the 6th India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) meeting was held at the New Administrative Capital. Shri Goyal and Minister Saleh addressed the Council. The Council was co-chaired by Mr. Ganesh Kumar, Executive Vice Chairman, TCI Sanmar Chemicals SAE, on the Indian side, and Mr. Khaled Aboul Makarem of Makarem Tex on the Egyptian side. Mr. Vijay Sankar, President of FICCI, also addressed the Council.

The Joint Business Council provided a platform for focused discussions on priority sectors, including chemicals and petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, food processing and agri-business, renewable energy and green hydrogen, infrastructure, ports and logistics, information technology and digital services, textiles and automotive manufacturing. The Council also examined ways to strengthen institutional links between business organisations, including the possibility of establishing sectoral working groups, customs and trade facilitation, business visas and a calendar of reciprocal trade missions for 2026-27.

The two engagements highlighted the complementarities between the Indian and Egyptian economies. India offers a large and growing market, competitive manufacturing, engineering and digital capabilities, while Egypt offers an established industrial base, strategic connectivity, skilled human resources and access to markets in Africa and the wider region. Bilateral trade exceeds USD 6.5 billion, while Indian investments in Egypt already exceed USD 5.5 billion. Both sides see significant potential for deeper two-way investment, joint manufacturing, technology partnerships and the development of supply chains serving domestic and international markets.

Shri Goyal’s visit follows the meeting between President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during the September 2026 BRICS Summit in India. The high-level visit, the India–Egypt Business Forum involving more than 300 companies and the India–Egypt Joint Business Council engagements reflect the shared ambition to further strengthen economic engagement under the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership.

Shri Piyush Goyal held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, to review bilateral trade and investment relations and explore avenues for further economic cooperation. Discussions covered trade expansion, market access, investment opportunities, pharmaceuticals, fertilisers and challenges faced by Indian businesses in Egypt, including visa-related issues. Shri Goyal emphasised the importance of facilitating Indian investments and strengthening bilateral supply chains and business-to-business linkages.Shri Piyush Goyal also held a bilateral meeting with H.E. Eng. Khaled Hashem, Minister of Industry of Egypt, to discuss opportunities for strengthening industrial cooperation, promoting manufacturing partnerships and enhancing investment linkages. Both sides discussed potential cooperation in industrial development, technology partnerships, MSME development, industrial automation and advanced manufacturing.

India and Egypt have exciting opportunities to work together in transforming transport, logistics and supply chain infrastructure. Had an excellent meeting with Lt. Gen. Eng. Kamel Al-Wazir, Egypt’s Minister of Transport, to explore greater collaboration in railways, highways, ports and multimodal connectivity. 2336707.title: Prime Minister’s Departure Statement Ahead of His Visit to the Philippines
2336707.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister’s Departure Statement Ahead of His Visit to the Philippines
Posted On: 16 NOV 2026 7:53AM by PIB Delhi

Today, I am embarking on a visit to Manila to participate in the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit on 17 November 2026, at the invitation of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

Our relationship with ASEAN countries is at the heart of India's Act East Policy and occupies a central place in our MAHASAGAR vision. Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilizational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations.

At the ASEAN-India Summit, I look forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and give further momentum to our shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity.

The East Asia Summit provides an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges. I look forward to exchanging views with participating leaders on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific.

I also look forward to interacting with the vibrant Indian community in the Philippines, whose contributions strengthen the bonds of friendship between our two countries.

I am confident that the visit will impart new energy to India's partnership with ASEAN and reinforce our collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific.

2336674.title: Akashvani Launches ‘AIR Rising Stars’ to Provide National Platform to Young Musical Talent
2336674.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Akashvani Launches ‘AIR Rising Stars’ to Provide National Platform to Young Musical Talent
26 Musical Concerts to Be Organised Across the Country from 17th to 30th November 2026
AIR Rising Stars to Promote Young Musical Artists Below 30 Years of Age as Part of Akashvani’s 90-Year Celebrations
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:56PM by PIB Delhi

In a major initiative to encourage young musical talent and carry forward India’s rich and diverse musical heritage, Akashvani is launching the inaugural season of the “AIR Rising Stars”, a nationwide series of special musical concerts exclusively by the young artists below 30 years of age. The first season of the concert series will be organised at 26 locations across the country from 17th November to 30th November 2026. These concerts will provide distinguished national platform to young and emerging musical artists to showcase their talent and connect with wider audiences.

The initiative is being undertaken as part of the celebrations marking 90 years of Akashvani and reflects its continued commitment to identifying, nurturing and promoting musical talent across generations. AIR Rising Stars seeks to carry this legacy forward by placing the spotlight on the next generation of performers.

Focus on Young Graded and Emerging Artists

The concerts will primarily feature young graded artists of Akashvani below 30 years of age, representing different genres and musical traditions. In cases where suitable graded young artists are not available in a particular category, deserving ungraded young artists may also be provided an opportunity, subject to the prescribed guidelines and selection by the concerned Akashvani Station.

The concerts will showcase the diversity of India’s musical heritage through Hindustani Classical Music (Vocal and Instrumental), Carnatic Classical Music (Vocal and Instrumental), Light and Folk Music, Western Music and other regional musical forms, as appropriate to the participating stations.

Nationwide Celebration at 26 Locations

The concerts will be organised by 26 participating Akashvani Stations at Shimla, Dehradun, Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi, Jaipur, Jalandhar, Suratgarh, Hyderabad, Vijayawada, Dharwad, Bengaluru, Mysuru, Madurai, Thiruvananthapuram, Tiruchirappalli, Kolkata, Imphal, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Sangli, Nagpur, Puducherry, Jammu, Guwahati and Rampur.

Each participating station will organise a musical concert at a suitable venue, featuring promising young artists from the respective region. Eminent personalities, music connoisseurs, youth icons, students and members of the public will also be invited to encourage the participating artists and make the initiative a nationwide celebration of young musical talent.

Multi-Platform Broadcast and Digital Outreach

A key feature of AIR Rising Stars: Season-1 will be its extensive multi-platform broadcast and digital outreach, taking the performances of young artists beyond the concert venues to audiences across the country.

The concerts will be broadcast through the network of Akashvani Stations and will also receive coverage on Doordarshan, on “Raagam” Youtube channel of Akashvani, youtube channels of 26 Akashvani Stations, “NewsOnAir” mobile app and Prasar Bharati’s “WAVES OTT” platform. This integrated broadcast strategy will provide participating artists wider visibility through radio, television and digital platforms.

Cash Prizes for Top Three Performances

To encourage young artists and promote wider digital engagement, cash prizes and certificates will be awarded to the three participating artists whose performances secure the highest number of views on YouTube by 15th January 2027.

First Prize: ₹20,000

Second Prize: ₹15,000

Third Prize: ₹10,000

This initiative will provide additional recognition to young performers and encourage them to reach out to wider audiences through digital platforms.

It may be noted that Akashvani has a long tradition of organising the Akashvani Sangeet Sammelan , which has successfully completed 67 editions. Akashvani Sangeet Sammelan provides an esteemed platform for renowned Top Grade and A Grade artists to showcase their musical excellence, whereas AIR Rising Stars is an exclusive initiative aimed at providing a dedicated platform to young graded artists, who otherwise have limited opportunities to perform in such prestigious concert platforms organised by Akashvani.

Through “AIR Rising Stars:”, Akashvani aims to create a distinctive national platform for the next generation of musicians while strengthening the connection between India’s enduring musical traditions and its youth. The initiative will further reinforce Akashvani’s longstanding role as a promoter of India’s rich cultural and musical heritage and a nurturing ground for emerging musical talent.

*****

2336673.title: Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Inaugurates EPFO Lounge and ESIC Pavilion at IITF 2026
2336673.body_html:
Ministry of Labour & Employment
Union Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Inaugurates EPFO Lounge and ESIC Pavilion at IITF 2026
Kiosks showcase citizen-centric initiatives for accessible social security and healthcare
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, today inaugurated the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) Lounge and the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) Pavilion at the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Central Provident Fund Commissioner (CPFC) Shri Ramesh Krishnamurthi, Director General, ESIC, Shri Ashok Kumar Singh, and other senior officers from both EPFO and ESIC were present on the occasion.

Following the inauguration, Dr. Mandaviya witnessed the initiatives and facilities being offered at the respective kiosks, and also interacted with visitors.  The Union Minister expressed his appreciation for the citizen-centric, technology-driven initiatives aimed at making social security services more accessible, efficient, and engaging for workers, pensioners, employers and the general public.

EPFO Lounge

The EPFO Lounge features an engaging puppet show (Raja Rancho) highlighting EPFO’s benefits. It also showcases dedicated kiosks offering a wide range of support, including the Nidhi Aapke Nikat / Grievances kiosk for grievance resolution; an E-services Desk for online guidance, claim filing, and KYC correction; a Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana / Face Authentication Technology kiosk; an information kiosk on New Schemes of EPFO; a Pension Help Desk for pension queries and Digital Life Certificates; and a National Career Services (NCS) / e-Shram kiosk for employment and social security services.

ESIC Pavilion

At the ESIC Pavilion, visitors have access to public-friendly facilities such as free health check-ups (including blood pressure monitoring and blood glucose tests), on-the-spot Aadhaar seeding, and across-the-counter grievance resolution, alongside face-to-face interactions with senior ESIC officers from Delhi and Haryana. To make awareness interactive and engaging, the pavilion features digital screens, audio-visual presentations, a Know ESIC quiz, an interactive Take a Selfie and Become a Doctor activity, as well as daily goody bags and merchandise for lucky participants. Additionally, a unique QR-code-based direct feedback mechanism has been introduced, with responses monitored daily by the Insurance Commissioner to ensure citizens' suggestions directly reach senior management.

Both spaces will remain open to visitors throughout IITF 2026 from 14th to 27th November 2026 at Hall No. 4, Bharat Mandapam, with the EPFO Lounge located on the Ground Floor (Stall No. 8A) and the ESIC Pavilion on the First Floor (Stall No. 4F-05-A). Workers, pensioners, employers, their families, and the general public are cordially invited to visit both stalls to avail of on-the-spot services, participate in interactive activities, and learn more about the government's social security initiatives.

***

2336671.title: Agriculture Pavilion in IITF 2026 Witnesses Massive Footfall
2336671.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Agriculture Pavilion in IITF 2026 Witnesses Massive Footfall
Pavilion to remain open every day till November 27, 2026, to showcase its unique display of modern agriculture
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:54PM by PIB Delhi

The Agriculture Pavilion set-up by Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoA&FW) in the 'India International Trade Fair (IITF)' 2026 has emerged as a major crowd-puller at Pragati Maidan. Commencing from November 13 and to be  continued till November 27th 2026, the pavilion today witnessed  extraordinary public participation. The momentum received a major boost with the visit of the Joint Secretary (Extension), who interacted extensively with exhibitors, farmers, and tech innovators, praising their efforts towards awareness creation about sustainable and modern agriculture.

The theme of the pavilion beautifully reflects the progress of MoA&FW in empowering farmers through farmer-centric  interventions of flagship schemes, technology transfer and direct market linkages from 'Seed to Market'.

Strategic Display of Key initiatives and Achievement of MoA&FW Schemes in Agriculture Pavilion include :

• Digital Agriculture & Public Infrastructure: A cornerstone of the pavilion depicts the live demonstration of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for Agriculture, featuring AgriStack, Decision Support System (DSS) for geospatial intelligence, and AR/VR-based Digital Crop Surveys.

• National Mission on Natural Farming & Core Missions: The pavilion spotlights the shift toward eco-friendly farming with full-scale models on Natural Farming, alongside interactive displays from the Pulses Mission and Oilseeds Development ("Save Oil" campaign), stepping towards self-reliance.

• Millets for Nutrition: Backed by the Directorate of Millets Development, this zone attracts massive crowds to  visualise live seed samples, nutritional education, and counters for processed and value-added millet products, as a super food.

• Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY): A dedicated area showcases the success milestones, and the security net provided by the government's premier Crop Insurance Scheme to millions of Indian farmers.

• Per Drop More Crop (PDMC): Underlining the conservation of water through Micro Irrigation automation set-ups display, high-efficiency water conservation techniques and smart irrigation systems.

• Empowering FPOs & Agri-Marketing: Giving regional agriculture a global platform, several Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and the e-NAM (electronic-National Agriculture Market) network are showcasing their high-quality produce.

The Major highlights include:

            • Kashmiri Saffron & Spices: Saffron, Kahwa, and pure essential oils directly from FPO Pampore.

            • Organic & Native Grains: Multi-flavored Jaggery from Hargaon FPO, and unique Black and Basmati rice varieties showcased by FPO, Dasuya.

            • North-East Organic Bounty: Exotic fruit wines, Lakadong turmeric, and bamboo shoot pickles brought by Tangsim Agro FPO from Meghalaya.

• Advanced Horticulture & Allied Sectors: Live hydroponic farming display by  'National Horticulture Board (NHB)', cocoa processing techniques, and high-interest live Beehive & Honey Extraction demonstrations by 'National Bee Board' are keeping families and children highly engaged.

• Plant Protection & Modern Agriculture Machinery: Interactive zones on safe pesticide use, the Pest Surveillance System (NPSS), Mobile App, and actual display of advanced mechanical farm tools emphasize smart farming.

The Agriculture Pavilion remains open every day till November 27, 2026, to showcase its unique display of modern agriculture to the urban visitors, industry professionals, and visiting farmers with a profound, technology driven to depict the resilient and sustainable future of Indian agriculture.

2336665.title: National Zoological Park organises 21st Sunday Bird Walk to Promote Citizen Science and Biodiversity Documentation
2336665.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2336665.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
National Zoological Park organises 21st Sunday Bird Walk to Promote Citizen Science and Biodiversity Documentation
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park (NZP), New Delhi, organised the 21st edition of ‘Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP’ on 15 November 2026, from 7:30 AM to 10:30 AM promoting public participation in biodiversity monitoring and wildlife conservation. The walk was conducted under the expert guidance of Shri Vineet Kumar, Bird Expert, with the support of dedicated volunteers.

A total of eight participants, comprising bird enthusiasts, nature lovers, students, wildlife photographers and citizens with an interest in biodiversity, took part in the programme. The walk was also attended by the zoo officials and the resource expert, who interacted with participants and shared their knowledge and insights throughout the activity.

During the walk, participants recorded 42 bird species, with more than 600 individual birds observed in the designated area. A significant highlight of this edition of Sunday Bird Walk was the addition of a new species to the bird checklist of the National Zoological Park —Northern Shoveler (Spatula clypeata). This addition represents a valuable contribution to the ongoing documentation of the Zoo's avian diversity and underscores the importance of systematic bird monitoring and citizen science in understanding and conserving biodiversity.

The walk also provided participants with a hands-on learning experience in bird identification and field-based biodiversity documentation. Shri Vineet Kumar shared valuable insights into bird ecology, behaviour and conservation, highlighting the ecological significance of birds, particularly their role in natural pest control and their importance as indicators of ecosystem health.

Through initiatives such as Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP, the National Zoological Park continues to foster environmental awareness, encourage citizen participation in biodiversity conservation and strengthen public engagement in documenting the rich avian diversity of the Zoo.

To ensure meaningful learning and effective participation, each Sunday Bird Walk is limited to 20–25 participants. Prior registration is mandatory, and places are allotted on a first-come, first-served basis. The registration form remains open from Monday to Friday each week. The link is available on the official website of the National Zoological Park and through the NZP Saathi mobile application.
