2336647.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah performs Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society, virtually inaugurates Western Regional Office of Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies and launches Bharat Taxi services in Pune, Maharashtra
2336647.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah performs Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society, virtually inaugurates Western Regional Office of Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies and launches Bharat Taxi services in Pune, Maharashtra
Pioneers like Vitthalrao Vikhe Patil and Vaikunthbhai Mehta laid the foundation of the cooperative movement in Maharashtra, establishing a system to ensure that the benefits of agricultural trade reach farmers
The sugar mill and machinery manufacturing facility established by our cooperative pioneers in Pune as National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Limited (NHEC) is being revived today
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, several significant initiatives have been undertaken to strengthen PACS, dairy cooperatives and cooperative sugar mills following the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi attended a programme in Gadchiroli, a region that has recently witnessed significant progress towards freedom from Naxalism, on the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda
Western Regional Office for regulation of Multi-State Cooperative Societies inaugurated in Pune; Shri Amit Shah congratulates cooperative leaders of Maharashtra
Bharat Taxi, envisioned as a nationwide cooperative-based transport service, launched in Pune; Sarathis to receive their entire earnings without any commission deductions through a fully transparent system
The idea of cooperative-based Bharat Taxi emerged from the need to address the exploitation faced by drivers over the years; Sarathis are now becoming owners of their own transport enterprise
Bhoomi Pujan performed for the revival of National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Limited (NHEC), a pioneering manufacturer of sugar mills and centrifugal machinery, with the support of cooperative institutions
The revived NHEC facility will manufacture sugar mills, power generation plants, ethanol and CBG plants, dairy processing equipment and containers, with every rupee of earnings accruing to cooperative institutions
Circular economy in the dairy and sugar sectors will generate additional income for farmers from cattle dung and other by-products while helping reduce t
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 7:49PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of 'Sahkar se Samriddhi' and further strengthening, modernising and making the cooperative movement in the country more inclusive, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today performed the Bhoomi Pujan for the revival of NHEC (National Heavy Engineering Cooperative) Multi-State Cooperative Society at Talegaon Dabhade in Pune district, Maharashtra. On the occasion, he also virtually inaugurated the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) and launched Bharat Taxi services in Pune. Deputy Chief Ministers of Maharashtra Shri Eknath Shinde and Smt. Sunetra Ajit Pawar, Union Minister of State for Cooperation Shri Krishan Pal Gurjar, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol, Maharashtra Minister for Higher and Technical Education and Parliamentary Affairs Shri Chandrakant Patil, Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani, and several other dignitaries were present at the event.

In his address, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah paid tribute to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and said that the land of Maharashtra has not only played a significant role in establishing and strengthening the spirit of Swaraj but has also given a new direction to the cooperative movement in the country. He said that Maharashtra, particularly Pune, can rightly be described as the fountainhead of the cooperative movement in western India. Pioneers of the cooperative movement, including Padma Shri Vitthalrao Patil and Vaikunthbhai Mehta, had endeavoured even before Independence to develop a system in which the maximum benefits arising from agriculture and trade would reach farmers.

Shri Amit Shah said that farmers, rural women, milk producers and those associated with the cooperative movement had long been demanding the establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation at the Centre. He said that this demand remained unfulfilled during the tenure of previous governments, while the Central Government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi established a dedicated Ministry of Cooperation, giving a new direction to the cooperative sector. He said that Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), district-level cooperative institutions and the dairy sector are steadily becoming stronger. The Central Government has undertaken several significant measures, including providing relief of approximately Rs. 15,000 crore to cooperative sugar mills and extending income tax relief of approximately Rs. 3,000 crore annually.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a major manufacturing facility producing machinery and equipment for sugar mills once operated on the very land where today's programme was being held. The factory had ceased operations during the tenure of a previous government. He said that the reconstruction of the same industrial complex is now being initiated, marking an occasion of pride and satisfaction for the cooperative sector.

Shri Amit Shah extended his greetings to the people of the country, particularly mothers and sisters, on the occasion of Chhath Mahaparv. Paying tribute to Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his 151st birth anniversary, he said that Bhagwan Birsa Munda had ignited the spirit of resistance against colonial rule from the land of Jharkhand even before the wider freedom movement gathered momentum. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi decided to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. Shri Shah also referred to the progress made towards eliminating Naxalism in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, and the programme held there. Paying homage to Acharya Vinoba Bhave, he said that Vinoba Ji dedicated his life to cow welfare, Sarvodaya, the Bhoodan Movement and strengthening Indian languages through the Devanagari script. He recalled that Vinoba Bhave, a devoted follower of Mahatma Gandhi, spent a significant part of his life in Wardha, Maharashtra.

Referring to the inauguration of the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS), the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a large number of Multi-State Cooperative Societies operate across the western region, including Maharashtra and Gujarat. He said that there had been demands from different regions for the establishment of this office, which has now been set up in Pune. Shri Shah informed that the office would undertake regulatory functions relating to Multi-State Cooperative Societies in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, and Daman and Diu.

Referring to the launch of Bharat Taxi services in Pune, Shri Amit Shah said that cooperative-based Bharat Taxi services would be expanded across the country. He said that for many years, drivers associated with several taxi companies had to surrender a portion of their earnings as commission and, in many instances, faced exploitation. The concept of Bharat Taxi, based on the cooperative model, was developed to address this situation. He said that through Bharat Taxi, the Sarathi brothers and sisters, who were earlier recognised merely as drivers, are now becoming owners of their own company. The system ensures complete transparency, with the entire earnings of Sarathis being credited directly to their bank accounts without any commission deductions. He said that Bharat Taxi services should also be introduced in Nagpur, Nashik, Kolhapur and Solapur after Pune.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, referring to the Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC (National Heavy Engineering Cooperative), said that the institution had previously operated from the same location and supplied sugar mills and centrifugal machinery across the world. He said that over time, the industrial unit ceased operations, and its approximately 110 acres of land increasingly faced the threat of illegal encroachment. The Ministry of Cooperation initiated efforts to revive this important cooperative industrial asset and began the process of its restoration with the support of institutions such as the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), Amul, IPL, IFFCO and the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC).

Shri Amit Shah said that the manufacturing facility to be established at NHEC would not be limited to producing sugar mills. It would also manufacture power generation plants for sugar mills, Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants and various types of industrial equipment and plants related to the dairy sector. In addition, the facility would undertake container manufacturing for export to overseas markets. He said that the earnings generated from these industrial activities would accrue to cooperative institutions, thereby further strengthening the cooperative-based economic ecosystem.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that there was a time when sugar mills manufactured by NHEC were exported to 11 countries, including Zambia, Ethiopia and Vietnam. The manufacturing facility had such a strong order book and demand that the delivery of new orders could take approximately four years. He said that these industrial operations subsequently came to a halt, but the Central Government has now decided to revive this important cooperative institution.

Shri Amit Shah informed that, as part of the revival process of NHEC, the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) initially took over the management of the institution as its administrator. Subsequently, all audits that had remained pending for the previous two years were completed. Institutions including Amul, NDDB, NCDC, IFFCO, NABARD and IPL contributed towards mobilising the investment required for the revival of the institution. Its Board of Directors was reconstituted, and at its first meeting held on 9 October 2026, a resolution was taken to rebuild the institution. The Bhoomi Pujan of the project was performed today as part of this process.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that a plan has been prepared to reschedule all liabilities and loans of NHEC and settle them in a transparent manner. He expressed confidence that production would commence at the facility before December 2027 and manufacturing of sugar mills would resume. He said that a circular economy would also be developed in the sugar and dairy sectors, creating additional income opportunities for farmers through the productive utilisation of resources such as cattle dung. Similarly, efforts would be made to reduce dependence on imports by increasing the utilisation of various by-products generated by sugar mills. He further informed that the second phase of the project envisages manufacturing containers for the railways, defence sector and exports.

Shri Amit Shah expressed confidence that, like successful cooperative institutions such as Amul, IFFCO and KRIBHCO, NHEC would also emerge as an important example for the cooperative movement in the country in the coming years. He congratulated all the institutions associated with the revival of NHEC and the farmers of Maharashtra on this initiative.

In his address, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation also referred to the country's democratic system and the role of political parties, observing that the principal opposition party has faced successive electoral defeats in recent years. Referring to 'Bharat Summit 2026' held in Hyderabad, he said that the remarks made by the Leader of the Opposition at the international conference concerning India's development journey, democratic system and national leadership were inappropriate. Shri Shah said that the electoral success or failure of political parties depends on their leadership, performance and the confidence reposed in them by the people.

Shri Amit Shah referred to the tenure of the previous government and said that several allegations and controversies relating to corruption had emerged during that period, whereas development across various sectors has gained momentum over the past 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He highlighted achievements in agriculture, industrial development, India's historic accomplishment of reaching the Moon's south polar region, expansion of the startup ecosystem, modernisation of the railways, increase in the number of airports to approximately 150, expansion of the metro network, introduction of the National Education Policy and establishment of a separate Ministry of Cooperation.

The Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation advised the Leader of the Opposition that engaging with people in India's villages and understanding their concerns was more important than criticising the country on international platforms. He said that, in a democracy, the path to political power lies in reaching out to the people and earning their trust. Shri Shah said that all political parties, whether in government or in opposition, have a responsibility to safeguard the country's reputation, democratic institutions and national interests on international platforms. He also urged workers of the opposition party to reflect on the approach and political direction of their leadership, adding that the people of the country express their verdict through the democratic process.

Concluding his address, Shri Amit Shah said that a new beginning has been made in the cooperative sector today. Industrial production activities will resume at the approximately 110-acre complex that had remained closed for years. He extended his best wishes to cooperative sector workers and farmers across the country and expressed confidence that the revival of NHEC would give a new direction to cooperative-led industrial development in India.

During the programme, a Letter of Intent (LoI) was exchanged between NHEC and IDMC Limited, and share certificates were presented to Bharat Taxi Sarathis.

***

2336678.title: Dr M L Jat, DG ICAR inaugurates Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing and Farmers’ Training Centre at ICAR-IIHR, Bengaluru
2336678.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Dr M L Jat, DG ICAR inaugurates Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing and Farmers’ Training Centre at ICAR-IIHR, Bengaluru
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 6:59PM by PIB Bengaluru

Dr. M. L. Jat, Hon’ble Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), visited ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (ICAR-IIHR), Bengaluru, on 15 November 2026. During his visit, he inaugurated the Farmers’ Advanced Training Centre (ATC) and the Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing in Horticultural Crops, including a Biosafety Level-II (BSL-II) Laboratory.

Following the inauguration of the Farmers’ Advanced Training Centre, Dr. Jat interacted with progressive farmers, incubatees, entrepreneurs, nursery owners and practitioners of natural farming who have adopted ICAR-IIHR varieties and technologies. The interaction focused on natural farming practices, innovations in horticulture and strategies to mitigate the impact of El Niño and Super El Niño on horticultural crops. Farmers shared their experiences in adopting climate-resilient practices such as mulching, sprinkler irrigation, border cropping, intercropping with short-duration flower and vegetable crops, and green manuring. These interventions have helped improve crop yield, produce quality and farmers’ income.

Addressing the farmers, Dr. Jat emphasized the importance of encouraging educated youth, engineers and agricultural graduates to actively participate and invest in agriculture and horticulture by adopting scientific innovations. He highlighted the need to integrate modern scientific technologies with traditional wisdom and stressed that farmers must remain at the centre of all agricultural research and development initiatives. He also appreciated the role of ICAR institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) and Agricultural Technology Application Research Institutes (ATARIs) in popularizing innovative technologies through Government of India programmes, particularly the Khet Bachao Abhiyan (KBA). He assured that successful farmer innovations and experiences would be documented and disseminated widely to benefit farming communities across the country.

Subsequently, Dr. Jat inaugurated the Centre of Excellence for Genome Editing in Horticultural Crops, equipped with a Biosafety Level-II Laboratory, marking an important step towards strengthening advanced biotechnology research and genome-editing capabilities in horticultural crops. He emphasized that scientists should prepare for the future by developing self-reliance in genome resources for genome-editing research. He also highlighted the need for prioritization, better targeting, development of a strong data ecosystem and identification of opportunities where Indian agricultural research can achieve global standards and first-of-its-kind innovations.

During his interaction with postgraduate students, he stressed the importance of nurturing young scientific talent and strengthening human capital. He encouraged scientists to move beyond conventional approaches, embrace new opportunities and work towards making agriculture a major contributor to India's vision of a USD 30 trillion economy by 2047, with a targeted contribution of USD 6 trillion from agriculture. He also highlighted the potential of microbial technologies, biofertilizer start-ups and innovations in health and nutrition.

The visit also included interaction with postgraduate students, visits to research laboratories and a field visit to the institute's research facilities. The visit provided an important platform to strengthen the institute's research, innovation, farmer outreach and human resource development initiatives, reaffirming ICAR-IIHR's commitment to sustainable, climate-resilient and technology-driven horticultural development.

On this occasion Dr V B Patel, ADG Fruits and  spices, Director IIHR Dr Tusar Kanti Behera, Directors and Heads of the ICAR institutes in Bengaluru, Scientists of the institute, Postgraduate students, research scholars, Innovative farmers and Agri entrepreneurs were present.

2336597.title: At the Climate Summit, India Makes the Case for a Sunday Bike Ride
2336597.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2336597.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
At the Climate Summit, India Makes the Case for a Sunday Bike Ride
At COP31 in Antalya, Fit India presented Sundays on Cycle, a weekly ride that has not missed a Sunday since December 2024, and invited every country to host one community ride in the next year.
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi

Most of the talk at a United Nations climate summit is about energy, finance and technology. On Saturday afternoon, at the International Solar Alliance Pavilion at COP31, India’s Fit India Movement made a smaller argument: that the climate fight is also won on ordinary streets, one weekend ride at a time.

“A city can build a bicycle lane, but only if its citizens choose to ride on it,” Mayank Srivastava, deputy director general of the Sports Authority of India, told the audience. “Infrastructure alone does not change how people live.”

The hour-long session, “Sundays on Cycle: From a Weekly Ride to a Way of Life,” was held at the pavilion (D 610) on the summit’s Children, Youth, Education and Skills Day at COP31, the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. Launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 29 August 2019, the  Fit India Movement reflects his vision of building a healthy, active, and prosperous India. The movement aims to make fitness an integral part of every Indian’s daily life by encouraging people to adopt healthy lifestyles, engage in regular physical activities, practise yoga, and participate in sports.

The Fit India Movement of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports presented the ride as a working example of Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), India’s campaign for sustainable lifestyles, with a simple message: one pedal, one purpose, one healthier world.

Sundays on Cycle, a free community ride, has been held every Sunday since Dec. 22, 2024. “It has not missed a single Sunday,” Mr. Srivastava said. Participation has reached close to 3.7 million at more than 30,000 locations across India, he said, and on World Bicycle Day this year, held with cycling’s world governing body, the Union Cycliste Internationale, organisers planned for 100,000 riders and about 400,000 turned up.

“More than the numbers, people have begun to take cycling seriously,” he said. “They return Sunday after Sunday, and what began as a campaign is becoming a habit.”

He argued that timing matters for countries like India. Many cities in the Global South are still being built, he said, and most trips in them are short enough to cycle. “If cycling becomes a habit before car dependence takes hold, those emissions need never be produced,” he said. “Avoiding them now is far cheaper than removing them later.”

Lindita Xhaferi-Salihu, who leads sectors engagement for Global Climate Action at UN Climate Change, delivered the keynote. She described Fit India as “a great model that can be replicated everywhere,” and spoke about her husband, who arrived in a new country as an 18-year-old refugee and found a community through a local handball club. “A community is only a community if somebody brings it together,” she said. “We cannot talk about communities if we don’t have somebody like Fit India bringing together people who share the same purpose and can act collectively for the betterment of their societies.” Climate negotiations, she added, are so technical that it has been hard to bring people along, and sport can be the “connective tissue” that does it.

A short film on the ride’s journey followed. In it, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, India’s minister for youth affairs and sports, who launched Sundays on Cycle in December 2024, described cycling as “much more than exercise” and “a powerful medium to carry the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s message of Fit India.” “Through initiatives like Fit India Sundays on Cycle,” he said, “we must take this passion to every household and every community.”

A panel moderated by Dr. Bhairavi Joshi, an adviser to Fit India, asked whether a weekend ride can change how cities are built.

Jim Walker of the Walk21 Foundation, who joined a Sundays on Cycle ride in Delhi last month, pointed to Bogotá, Colombia, where a similar street opening began about 50 years ago and now draws about 1.6 million people every Sunday onto 125 kilometres of car-free streets. “We get stuck in the habits of our cities,” he said.

Felipe A. Ramírez Buitrago, director of urban mobility at the WRI Ross Center for Sustainable Cities, said such events “teach with example.” Once people enjoy the streets, he said, cities can make the case for protected lanes and links to mass transit.

Gashaw Aberra of ITDP Africa said car-free days in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, had helped produce the country’s first non-motorised transport strategy, which sets targets for walkways and cycle tracks. “Instead of what can we learn from Africa, I would say, what can Africa learn from India,” he said.

Sanjay Seth, executive director of The Energy and Resources Institute, said walking and cycling should be counted in India’s climate commitments and in state and city plans, not treated only as awareness campaigns. “We need to make sure that we build safely; then behaviour will follow,” he said.

Asked for one action every city should take in the next 12 months, the panellists answered in a word or two: Maud De Vries, chief executive of BYCS, said “just do it”; others named infrastructure, community engagement and obstruction-free pathways.

Closing the session, Ms. Amarjyoti, executive director of Fit India, invited every nation, city and partner present to host at least one community-led “active morning” over the next 12 months and to share the experience through the One Planet Network. The Turkish Cycling Federation, she said, was the first partner to join. “A cycling culture is not built in a day,” she said. “It is built week after week by people who keep showing up.”

The organisers also released an impact report on the first 97 editions of the ride.

Ashish Khanna, director general of the International Solar Alliance, delivered a special address. He said the session had drawn the largest attendance the pavilion had seen, and urged sports facilities, from stadiums to gyms, to adopt solar power. “We are so proud that we could fit something related to sports and cycling in our agenda,” he said.

The ride’s 100th edition will be held across India on Nov. 29. Fit India said it would share a Sundays on Cycle toolkit to help other cities start their own rides, and invited people around the world to ride that day in their own communities.

Fit India also invited COP31 delegates to a special Sundays on Cycle ride in Antalya on Sunday, Nov. 15, held with the Turkish Cycling Federation (Türkiye Bisiklet Federasyonu) from Konyaaltı to the old town of Kaleiçi, carrying the Sunday ride from India’s neighbourhoods to the summit’s host city. In India, the ride’s 98th edition on the same day marked Children’s Day with cycling and Zumba.

“Ride together, change together,” Ms. Amarjyoti said.

This special edition of Sundays on Cycle at COP31 was held under the banner “India Pedals & The World Joins In!”, and was organised in partnership with the Turkish Cycling Federation in Antalya, Türkiye, on Sunday, November 15, 2026. The route saw cyclists begin the rally at Konyaaltı Caddesi and conclude at Işıklar.

About Fit India – Sundays on Cycle

Launched by Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, in December 2024, Fit India – Sundays on Cycle is organised by the Sports Authority of India under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, in collaboration with the Cycling Federation of India, Navavrati Foundation, Fitspire, the Centre for Integrative Health, MY Bharat and other partners. Rides are held every Sunday in all States and Union Territories, including at SAI Regional Centres, National Centres of Excellence, SAI Training Centres, Khelo India State Centres of Excellence and Khelo India Centres.

The COP31 session was supported by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Sports Authority of India, Fit India, Mission LiFE, the International Solar Alliance and BYCS India Foundation.

***

2336573.title: 57th IFFI Celebrates Cinematic Ties with Partner Country Russia Through an Evocative Four-Film Showcase

2336573.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
57th IFFI Celebrates Cinematic Ties with Partner Country Russia Through an Evocative Four-Film Showcase
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 5:52PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 15 November 2026

 

Under the theme of "Stories Without Borders," the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), proudly spotlights Russia as its esteemed Partner Country. Scheduled to take place in Goa from 20th to 28th November 2026, the festival reinforces enduring Indo-Russian cultural diplomacy by presenting a specially curated four-film package that bridges contemporary Russian auteur sensibilities with a celebrated Soviet musical classic.

Bringing together emerging directorial voices alongside a masterwork of satirical operetta, the Partner Country Russia section reflects the emotional breadth, stylistic audacity, and thematic depth of Russian filmmaking. From intimate explorations of family fractures, societal alienation, and personal redemption to a buoyant, Shostakovich-scored satire on urban aspirations, the showcase will offer festival delegates and cinephiles an immersive journey into the human condition.

Anastasia Kuzina’s Bo Bo (98 min), making its India premiere at the 57th IFFI, is a poignant rural drama about identity, acceptance and prejudice. Through Nadia, a young girl facing mockery for her facial hemangioma, the film explores her search for self-expression through music, reminding us that true transformation lies not in changing appearances but in overcoming societal prejudice.

Sidney Lumet’s Birthday

Raul Geidarov’s Sidney Lumet’s Birthday (92 min), winner of the Grand Jury Prize at the Vyborg National Film Festival, makes its India Premiere at IFFI57. This heartfelt coming-of-age drama follows 17-year-old Dato as he navigates family tensions, abandonment and forgiveness, exploring the resilience needed to heal generational wounds.

New Home

Nikita Grushin’s New Home (101 min), set for its World Premiere at IFFI 2026, is a moving drama about second chances and redemption. Following seven years in prison, Anna struggles to rebuild her life with the help of social services and Roman’s support. Featuring powerful performances, the film explores the challenges of reintegration, healing and confronting the past to find a new beginning.

Cheryomushki

Herbert Rappaport’s Cheryomushki (91 min), making its India Premiere at IFFI, is a delightful musical satire set in post-war Moscow. Following four young couples dreaming of better homes, the film blends catchy melodies, lively choreography and humour to expose bureaucratic corruption while celebrating community spirit and solidarity.

Through this specially curated selection, IFFI 2026 reaffirms the enduring cultural ties between India and Russia, while offering audiences an opportunity to engage with the diversity and evolving expressions of Russian cinema. The four films, spanning different genres and generations of filmmaking, reflect cinema's ability to transcend geographical boundaries and foster mutual understanding through shared human experiences.

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), scheduled to be held in Goa from 20th to 28th November 2026, will bring together filmmakers, industry professionals and cinema enthusiasts from India and across the world under the theme “Stories Without Borders.” With a diverse line-up of Indian and international films, special country showcases, premieres, competitions and industry engagements, IFFI 2026 continues its tradition of celebrating cinematic excellence and promoting cross-cultural exchange through cinema.

2336519.title: India to strengthen engagement with Italy based 'International Physics Centre', says Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
2336519.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India to strengthen engagement with Italy based 'International Physics Centre', says Minister Dr Jitendra Singh
India and 'International Centre for Theoretical Physics' (ICTP) initiate ‘India- ICTP Co-operation Fund’ to institutionalise scientific collaboration and researcher mobility: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Letter of Intent signed between DST and ICTP to strengthen long-standing research partnership and create greater opportunities for Indian scientists, researchers and students
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi

India and the "International Centre for Theoretical Physics" (ICTP) have taken a significant step towards institutionalising their longstanding scientific partnership with the initiation of the ‘India-ICTP Co-operation Fund’, aimed at strengthening the engagement and mobility of Indian researchers with the international research centre.

A Letter of Intent (LoI) was signed between the Department of Science and Technology (DST) and ICTP in this regard during the visit of Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, to ICTP in Trieste, Italy. The LoI was exchanged from the Indian side by Dr Praveenkumar Somasundaram, Head of the International Cooperation in DST.

Welcoming the initiative, Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed the hope that the India-ICTP Co-operation Fund would give greater impact to the existing engagement between the two sides and benefit Indian researchers. He noted the importance of institutionalising the ongoing association to provide further impetus to scientific collaboration and researcher mobility.

The initiative builds upon India's longstanding partnership with ICTP, which has seen active participation by Indian scientists, researchers and students across multiple programmes. Through the proposed Co-operation Fund, DST and ICTP seek to provide a more structured framework for this existing engagement, with particular emphasis on creating further opportunities for Indian researchers.

ICTP is a leading global hub for advanced research, higher education and capacity-building in physics, mathematics and related fields. Its association with India extends across research collaboration, academic exchange, workshops and capacity-building activities involving several Indian institutions.

Institutions including the Department of Science and Technology (DST), CSIR, leading universities and IITs have collaborated with ICTP through joint research, workshops and exchange programmes. Indian researchers regularly benefit from ICTP's visiting fellowships, diploma programmes and postdoctoral opportunities, while ICTP experts frequently engage with India's scientific communities working in high-energy physics, astrophysics, climate modelling and computational science.

The initiation of the India-ICTP Co-operation Fund and the signing of the LoI mark an important step towards strengthening these existing avenues of engagement and advancing the researcher mobility component of the partnership.

The collaboration has contributed to strengthening global networks of scientific excellence, bringing together researchers and institutions and supporting fundamental discoveries as well as innovations with societal impact. The proposed initiative is expected to further enhance the impact of this engagement and benefit India's scientific research community.

Dr. Jitendra Singh's visit to ICTP, which included a welcome lunch and the initiation of the researcher mobility programme, formed part of his official visit to Italy from November 11 to 15, 2026.

2336512.title: Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy Unveil Logo and Mascot for 8th Edition of Khelo India Youth Games 2026
2336512.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2336512.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy Unveil Logo and Mascot for 8th Edition of Khelo India Youth Games 2026
Khelo India Youth Games to be held in Telangana from December 11 to 22 across six cities
Around 8,000 athletes and participants expected to take part
Edition to feature 29 disciplines, including 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events
Softball to make its debut as a competitive sport, while Sailing and Karra Samu will feature as demonstration sports for the first time
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 3:47PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Chief Minister of Telangana A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG), scheduled to be held in Telangana from December 11 to 22, 2026.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and integrating sports into the broader vision of the country’s development.

 

CM of Telangana, Shri @revanth_anumula Garu, Ministers in the Telangana government, Shri @Vakiti_srihari Garu, Shri @UttamINC Garu and Union Minister Dr. @mansukhmandviya met Prime Minister @narendramodi. @TelanganaCMO https://t.co/jBCB3PxWQa

— PMO India (@PMOIndia) November 15, 2026

 

“The Union Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, is committed to promoting sports. Various competitions, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of the younger generation in sports,” Dr. Mandaviya said.

The Union Sports Minister and the Telangana Chief Minister also expressed their gratitude to the Prime Minister for his guidance and support in organising the Khelo India Youth Games in Telangana.

Dr. Mandaviya further stated that the Union Government, in collaboration with the Telangana Government, would work towards encouraging and inspiring youth to take up sports and contribute to building a strong sporting culture in the country.

Telangana Chief Minister Shri A. Revanth Reddy said that events like the Khelo India Youth Games help advance the Prime Minister’s vision of a Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat, while encouraging young people to stay away from substance abuse and other social challenges.

Around 8,000 athletes and participants are expected to converge in Telangana for the Games, which will be held across six cities: Hyderabad, Khammam, Karimnagar, Hanumakonda, Mahabubnagar and Nizamabad, from December 11 to 22.

The Telangana edition of the Khelo India Youth Games will feature 29 disciplines, comprising 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events.

The competitive disciplines include Archery, Athletics, Badminton, Basketball, Boxing, Cycling, Fencing, Football, Gatka, Gymnastics, Hockey, Judo, Kabaddi, Kalaripayattu, Kho-Kho, Mallakhamb, Rowing, Shooting, Swimming, Softball, Table Tennis, Tennis, Thang-Ta, Volleyball, Weightlifting, Wrestling and Yogasana.

Sailing and Karra Samu will feature as demonstration sports.

Softball will be included as a competitive discipline in the Khelo India Youth Games for the first time. Sailing and Karra Samu will also make their debut in the Games as demonstration sports.

The launch event was attended by Shri Vakiti Srihari, Minister for Sports and Youth Affairs, Telangana; Shri N. Uttam Kumar Reddy, Minister for Irrigation and CAD, Telangana; Shri A.P. Jithender Reddy, Advisor to the Government on Sports Affairs and President of the Telangana Olympic Association; and Shri Sanjay Jaju, Chief Secretary, Government of Telangana.

Shri Hari Ranjan Rao, Director General, Sports Authority of India (SAI), and Secretary, Department of Sports, along with senior officials from the Union and Telangana State Governments, were also present.

Logo and Mascot:

The Khelo India Youth Games logo brings together Telangana’s rich cultural heritage and sporting aspirations through eight key elements.

The Khelo India emblem, featuring a saffron and green running figure, represents the national programme, youth and momentum. The Gandhi Tower, part of the proposed Gandhi Sarovar at Bapu Ghat, symbolises peace, unity and Hyderabad’s vision for the future, while the Kakatiya Kala Thoranam reflects the State’s rich heritage and spirit of welcome.

The Buddha statue at Hussain Sagar represents harmony, discipline and tranquillity, while the Tangedu flower reflects Telangana’s cultural identity and the spirit of Bathukamma. Seven sporting silhouettes form a sporting skyline alongside the heritage skyline, while the encircling blue, green and yellow ribbon symbolises movement, energy and inclusion.

The tagline, “Khel Ka Junoon, Telangana Ki Jaan Aur Pehchaan”, captures the passion for sports as an integral part of Telangana’s identity.

The mascot, “Neelamani”, represents energy, agility and determination, embodying the spirit of youth and sportsmanship. It reflects pride in cultural roots and the vision of a stronger, fitter and more united India.

Its crest symbolises energy and forward movement, while its eyes represent focus, intelligence and spirit. The beak signifies determination and leadership, and its blue and turquoise feathers convey vibrancy, freedom and confidence.

Neelamani embodies four defining qualities: Vibrant, Courageous, Agile and Pride, reflecting the values and aspirations of the Khelo India Youth Games.

2336498.title: Prime Minister pays tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda  on his Jayanti and extends greetings on Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
2336498.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister pays tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda  on his Jayanti and extends greetings on Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi

 Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today paid respectful tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his birth anniversary and extended warm greetings to the nation on the auspicious occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

Recalling Dharti Aaba's indomitable courage, struggle, and sacrifice, the Prime Minister noted that his legacy will continue to inspire every generation to protect self-respect, freedom, and rights. Inspired by him, Shri Modistated that the Government is leaving no stone unturned for the dignity, opportunities, and prosperity of tribal brothers and sisters, calling upon everyone to salute the invaluable contribution of the tribal society in nation-building.

The Prime Minister shared on X:

"भगवान बिरसा मुंडा जी की जयंती पर उन्हें समस्त देशवासियों की ओर से मेरा कोटि-कोटि नमन।

आप सभी को इस दिव्य अवसर से जुड़े जनजातीय गौरव दिवस की बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं।

धरती आबा का अदम्य साहस, संघर्ष और बलिदान देश की हर पीढ़ी को स्वाभिमान, स्वतंत्रता और अधिकारों की रक्षा के लिए प्रेरित करता रहेगा।

उनसे प्रेरणा लेकर हमारी सरकार जनजातीय भाई-बहनों के सम्मान, अवसर और समृद्धि के लिए कोई कोर-कसर नहीं छोड़ रही है।

आइए, सभी मिलकर राष्ट्र निर्माण में जनजातीय समाज के बहुमूल्य योगदान को नमन करें।"

2336496.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister extends greetings to people of Jharkhand on State Foundation Day
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today extended heartfelt greetings to the people of Jharkhand on the occasion of the State's Foundation Day.

Describing Jharkhand as a unique confluence of tribal pride, cultural diversity, and natural wealth, the Prime Minister noted that its dense forests, scenic waterfalls, and historical sites enrich its distinct identity, while its traditions draw continuous inspiration from the tales of Bhagwan Birsa Munda's valour and sacrifice. Highlighting the immense potential in the state ranging from minerals and energy to handicrafts and tourism, he expressed confidence that Jharkhand will scale new heights of development on the strength of the resolve and capability of its hardworking and talented citizens, and wished happiness and prosperity for all.

The Prime Minister shared on X:

"झारखंड के सभी भाई-बहनों को राज्य के स्थापना दिवस की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं!

हमारा यह प्रदेश जनजातीय गौरव, सांस्कृतिक विविधता और प्राकृतिक संपदा का अनूठा संगम है। यहां के घने वन, मनोरम जलप्रपात और ऐतिहासिक स्थल इसकी विशिष्ट पहचान को समृद्ध करते हैं।

भगवान बिरसा मुंडा जी की वीरता और बलिदान की गाथाओं से यहां की परंपराओं को निरंतर प्रेरणा मिलती रही है।

खनिज और ऊर्जा से लेकर हस्तशिल्प और पर्यटन तक इस राज्य में अपार संभावनाएं हैं।

मुझे विश्वास है कि यहां के मेरे मेहनती और प्रतिभाशाली परिवारजनों के संकल्प और सामर्थ्य के बल पर यह प्रदेश विकास की नई ऊंचाइयों को छुएगा।

मेरी कामना है कि यह विशेष अवसर यहां के सभी लोगों के जीवन में सुख-समृद्धि और खुशहाली लेकर आए।"

2336495.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra
2336495.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participates in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra
Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas celebrates the rich heritage, culture and contributions of India's tribal communities: PM
The tradition of celebrating Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, initiated on November 15, 2021, has today transformed into a national festival: PM
There was a time when many days and festivals in our country were determined from a foreign perspective. But today, India is remembering its heritage, its history, and its heroes with indigenous pride; This is a symbol of a major change in our national consciousness: PM
The nation's two monumental achievements are currently the topic of discussion everywhere; The first is the historic triumph over extreme poverty for nearly 50 crore citizens; The second is the country's absolute liberation from the menace of Naxalism, Maoist terror: PM
We have focused especially on those regions that had remained left behind in development for a long time; Special drives were launched in over 100 Aspirational Districts and more than 500 Aspirational Blocks across the country, which include a large number of tribal-populated areas;  Now, under the PM Krishi Dhan Dhanya Yojana, special focus is also being laid on 100 agriculturally backward districts: PM
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 2:59PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today participated in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra via video conferencing, where he inaugurated and laid the foundation stone for 246 development projects worth around ₹3,000 crore. Addressing the gathering on the occasion of the 151st birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, the Prime Minister greeted citizens across the nation with ‘Johar’, bowed in reverence to Bhagwan Birsa Munda, and stated that the nationwide celebrations reflect the pride of tribal communities and his enduring inspiration as the country remembers its tribal heroes and heroines. Highlighting the grand celebration in Maharashtra's Gadchiroli,a land of rich tribal culture associated with the heroic sagas of Raghoji Bhangre, Bhagoji Naik, and Veer Baburao Shedmake,he bowed to all tribal warriors. “I also felicitate all the Governors, Chief Ministers, Deputy Chief Ministers, and every public representative who are participating in this event from across the country,” said Shri Modi.

Noting that the observance of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, initiated on November 15, 2021, has evolved into a national festival that witnessed over two lakh events and the participation of crores of citizens during Bhagwan Birsa Munda's 150th birth anniversary last year. “Today India is remembering its heritage, its history, and its heroes with Swadeshi self-respect, which is a symbol of a major transformation that has come in our national consciousness,” observed PM Modi.

Recalling how tribal communities consistently raised their voices against colonial injustice,from Tirot Sing's struggle in the Khasi Hills, the Kol movement of Chota Nagpur, and the Santhal revolution led by Sido-Kanhu to the sacrifices of Govind Guru's followers at Mangarh and the courage of Rani Gaidinliu, Tantya Bhil, Alluri Sitarama Raju, and Rani Durgavati, the Prime Minister highlighted the overarching legacy of these freedom movements. “Along with all these sagas, the Ulgulan of Bhagwan Birsa Munda and his struggle at a young age is even today a very big inspiration for crores of us countrymen,” remarked Shri Modi.

Highlighting the inauguration of over 170 tribal development projects and the laying of foundation stones for more than 70 projects worth around 3,000 crore rupees across various states on Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, the Prime Minister noted the inauguration of a museum dedicated to freedom fighter Ropuiliani in Mizoram and the new building of the Tribal Research Institute in Arunachal Pradesh, alongside educational institutions, healthcare services, tribal product marketing centers, and rural infrastructure works. “I extend my heartiest congratulations to the country for all these projects,” affirmed PM Modi.

Observing that this year's celebration coincides with widespread discussion of two historic national milestones,nearly 50 crore citizens defeating extreme poverty and India achieving freedom from Naxalism and Maoist terror, the Prime Minister emphasized the significance of both accomplishments for tribal regions. “Both these achievements are deeply connected with the lives of our tribal brothers and sisters,” noted Shri Modi.

Referring to the recent World Bank report stating that nearly 50 crore Indians escaped extreme poverty over the past 12 to 13 years, the Prime Minister described this as one of India's greatest post-independence achievements driven not by any single government, but by the collective strength of society, the hard work of every citizen, and targeted Central tribal welfare schemes and decisions. “For this achievement, I extend my heartiest congratulations to all the countrymen, especially to my tribal brothers and sisters,” remarked PM Modi.

Describing the exit of millions from poverty as the fulfillment of a firm resolve to prioritize those deprived of development for decades, the Prime Minister noted that the government deployed its full strength in the most backward tribal regions that lacked basic necessities, allocating over one lakh crore rupees for the PM-JANMAN Yojana and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan. “Our effort was that the families whom facilities reached the latest after independence should now have facilities reached to them the fastest,” asserted Shri Modi.

Detailing the government's commitment to prioritizing the underprivileged by constructing over four crore pucca houses for the poor, electrifying 18,000 villages that had remained in darkness for decades after independence, providing free medical coverage up to five lakh rupees under Ayushman Bharat, and establishing over 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs that brought healthcare to remote tribal pockets, the Prime Minister also highlighted the impact of rural sanitation. “When poor families got toilets and sanitation facilities increased, the risk of numerous diseases also decreased,” noted PM Modi.

Emphasizing that eradicating poverty required expanding income opportunities for poor families, the Prime Minister stated that lakhs of crores of rupees in collateral-free loans were disbursed under the Mudra Yojana, benefiting the poor, Dalits, backward classes, and tribal communities alike. “Through this, a new self-confidence to move forward was born within them,” observed Shri Modi.

Highlighting targeted interventions in regions that had long lagged in development, including a special campaign across more than 100 Aspirational Districts and over 500 Aspirational Blocks with large tribal populations as well as a focused drive across 100 agriculturally backward districts under the PM Krishi Dhan Dhanya Yojana to create new opportunities for farmers, poor families, and tribal communities, the Prime Minister underscored the transformative power of collective effort. “These collective efforts and the mantra of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas gave a new self-confidence to the poor of the country, and crores of poor people demonstrated by defeating poverty,” asserted PM Modi.

Turning to the nation's second major milestone of freedom from Naxalism, which inflicted the greatest harm on tribal communities across Gadchiroli and other tribal belts, the Prime Minister noted that around 125 districts were affected by Naxalism, when hundreds of violent incidents occurred every year and claimed the lives of thousands of innocent people, mostly tribal brothers and sisters. Noting that with the end of Naxalism today, mothers and newly secure sisters are blessing the government while youth once robbed of their childhoods are accessing education and employment, the Prime Minister recalled celebrating Diwali a few days ago with security forces in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, a region people once feared to visit. “In all the formerly Naxal-affected areas, including Gadchiroli, this time on Diwali, along with earthen lamps, the light of hope has also reached the people,” observed PM Modi.

Spotlighting the enthusiastic contribution of tribal communities to India's progress and noting that the nation's highest office is held by a daughter of the tribal community, the Prime Minister expressed the nation's collective pride. “All of us are proud of President Droupadi Murmu ji,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Concluding his address with best wishes on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, the Prime Minister called upon citizens to draw inspiration from the life of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. “Today is the time that taking inspiration from Bhagwan Birsa Munda, we invest even more of our energy in fulfilling the dream of a Viksit Bharat,” asserted PM Modi.

2336497.title: IFFI 2026 celebrates Malayalam cinema, recalls Prem Nazir's legacy and spotlights new-generation filmmakers
2336497.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
IFFI 2026 celebrates Malayalam cinema, recalls Prem Nazir's legacy and spotlights new-generation filmmakers
Sarvam Maya, Ottanjaavalmaram and Ajayante Maranam: Oru Case Study among Malayalam films featured
Basil Joseph and K. S. Chithra to participate in special festival sessions
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 2:50PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 15 November 2026

 

From the enduring legacy of ‘evergreen romantic hero’ Prem Nazir to the contemporary storytelling of a new generation of filmmakers, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is bringing the richness and diversity of Malayalam cinema into focus in Goa.

A special attraction for Malayali cinema enthusiasts will be the centenary celebrations featuring Thulabharam, a film associated with legendary Malayalam actor Prem Nazir. The screening forms part of IFFI's wider celebration of the centenaries of distinguished personalities of Indian cinema, offering audiences an opportunity to revisit films and performances that have left an indelible mark on the country's cinematic history.

Contemporary Malayalam cinema finds representation through Sarvam Maya, directed by Akhil Sathyan and featuring Nivin Pauly, Aju Varghese, Riya Shibu and Priety Mukundan. Selected for the Indian Panorama feature-film section, the supernatural drama explores faith, love and self-discovery through the story of Prabhendu, an atheist musician who finds himself drawn into an unusual relationship with the spirit of a young woman.

The New Horizon section of Indian Panorama also features Malayalam films Ottanjaavalmaram (A Lone Jamun Tree), directed by Shruthi Sharanyam, and Ajayante Maranam: Oru Case Study, directed by Sreehari Haridas. The festival's non-feature selection includes Switch Off, an 11-minute Malayalam short film directed by Sandeep Francis. Adding to the Malayalam presence, Half, directed by Samjad, a filmmaker from Keralam, will be screened under the Gala Premieres section. Together, these selections reflect the diversity of themes and storytelling approaches that characterise Malayalam cinema.

   

Malayalam film personalities will also take centre stage in the festival's special interactions and sessions. Filmmmaker and actor Basil Joseph will participate in an 'In Conversation' session titled The Epic Genres – Mythologies, Superheroes & New Worlds, exploring the evolving landscape of epic storytelling in cinema. Acclaimed playback singer and 'Melody Queen' K. S. Chithra will lead a retrospective session paying tribute to evergreen singing legends Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki.

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) is all set to commence in Goa from 20 to 28 November 2026, under the theme “Stories without Borders”. The festival will bring together films, filmmakers and cinema enthusiasts from India and across the world on a common platform, fostering cultural exchange and celebrating the universal language of cinema.

2336493.title: WAVES Film Bazaar Celebrates 20 Years of Connecting Indian Cinema with Global Industry
2336493.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
WAVES Film Bazaar Celebrates 20 Years of Connecting Indian Cinema with Global Industry
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 2:40PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 15 November 2026

 

WAVES Film Bazaar, one of the region's most significant platforms for cinematic exchange, collaboration and business opportunities, will celebrate its 20th edition from 20th-24th November, 2026, at Taj Cidade de Goa Horizon, Goa, alongside the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI).

Key initiatives under Waves Film Bazaar include the Co-Production Market, which connects selected feature films and documentaries with international producers and financiers; the NFDC Screenwriters' Lab, which nurtures emerging writing talent; and the Work-in-Progress Lab, which provides expert feedback to filmmakers refining their projects. The Viewing Room, Market Screenings and Producers' Lab further facilitate industry networking, project development and opportunities to connect with potential buyers and distributors.

The Knowledge Series brings together industry leaders to discuss emerging trends, distribution, business models and international collaborations. Country and state pavilions, technology showcases and market stalls further promote cross-border partnerships and showcase opportunities across the global audiovisual industry.

Initiated by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) in 2007 to nurture South Asian storytelling, Film Bazaar has evolved into an important international platform connecting filmmakers, producers, financiers, distributors, sales agents and festival programmers. Over the years, it has contributed to the journeys of several acclaimed films, including Ship of Theseus (2012), Anhe Ghode Da Daan (2011), Miss Lovely (2012), Qissa (2013), The Lunchbox (2013), Liar's Dice (2013), Court (2014), Titli (2014), Margarita With A Straw (2014), Chauthi Koot (2015), Dum Laga Ke Haisha (2015), Thithi (2015), Newton (2017), Manto (2018), Fire in the Mountains (2021), In the Belly of the Tiger (2024), Girls Will be Girls (2024), Cactus Pears (2025), Shape of Momo (2026) and Little Thomas (2026), among others. The NFDC has also extended financial support to over 300 films across 21 regional languages, many of which have received national and international recognition.

Now operating under the broader WAVES Film Bazaar banner, the platform has expanded its vision to connect South Asian cinema with international markets and audiences. Its programmes support filmmakers at different stages of production through industry collaboration, mentorship, financing and distribution opportunities.

Marking two decades of its journey, the 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar aims to strengthen India's presence in the global film ecosystem by fostering creative partnerships, supporting emerging talent and creating new opportunities for Indian cinema on the international stage.

 

* * *

2336492.title: Spain as Country of Honour at the 57th IFFI: A Celebration of Contemporary Spanish Cinema and Storytelling
2336492.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Spain as Country of Honour at the 57th IFFI: A Celebration of Contemporary Spanish Cinema and Storytelling
The magic of Spanish cinema takes centre stage at the 57th IFFI with an exciting line-up of four contemporary films
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 2:24PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 15 November 2026

 

Cinema lovers attending the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) are in for a special treat as the festival celebrates the richness and diversity of Spanish cinema. With Spain designated as the Country of Honour, IFFI will present a specially curated selection of four contemporary Spanish films, featuring premieres at the World, Asian and Indian levels. The showcase promises to offer audiences a compelling glimpse into the vibrancy, creativity and evolving storytelling landscape of contemporary Spanish cinema.

The exciting line-up of the Spanish films at IFFI this year will include:

Bitter Christmas (Amarga Navidad)

Two-time Oscar winning film maker Pedro Almodóvar’s recent 2026 film explores the risks of using personal experiences and real events in filmmaking, asking how much of someone’s life a film maker can reveal in the search for an honest story. The story centres around a cult film maker Raul who is struggling to find ideas for next film, and then as the story progresses, he uses his experienced tragedy as inspiration for a new script.

The film was showcased in prestigious film festivals like Cannes, Toronto and San Sebastian this year, and is up for its India Premiere in IFFI.

 

Looking For Michael (Persiguiendo a Michael)

This 2026 film directed by Juana Macias, tells the story of a young woman diagnosed with Parkinson’s Disease. She bravely decides not to give in to the sadness life her thrown to her, and rather live life differently. With the support of her music therapy group, whose members have the same disease, she sets out to meet the renowned actor Michael J. Fox, who is known to live with Parkinson’s. This comedy drama genre film is set to mark its World Premiere at IFFI 2026.

 

The Bad Son (El Mal Hijo)        

Spanish actor-director Jaime Lorente’s directorial debut El Mal Hijo will make its Asia Premiere in IFFI 2026. The film is a poignant exploration of intergenerational trauma and family relationships.  Earlier showcased at the San Sebastian International Film Festival, it follows a man abandoned by his father at the age of 11, who moves in with a grandmother he barely knows. As he confronts painful memories and unravels his family’s troubled past, he attempts to break the cycle of emotional wounds passed down through generations.

 

Trinidad

Directed by Laura Alvea and José Ortuño, the 2025 film Trinidad follows the adventures of a young Spanish woman in the late 19th century who escapes to the Wild West. Wrongly accused of a crime, she joins forces with a band of female outlaws, embarking on an adventure marked by action, danger and revenge. The action movie is set to make its World Premiere at IFFI 2026. 

 

* * *

2336480.title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER TO INAUGURATE CONFERENCE OF COMMONWEALTH WOMEN PARLIAMENTARIANS INDIA REGION IN BENGALURU
2336480.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER TO INAUGURATE CONFERENCE OF COMMONWEALTH WOMEN PARLIAMENTARIANS INDIA REGION IN BENGALURU
CHIEF MINISTER, KARNATAKA; DEPUTY CHAIRMAN, RAJYA SABHA; PRESIDING OFFICERS OF KARNATAKA LEGISLATURE; CHAIRPERSON OF CWP INDIA REGION AND OTHER DIGNITARIES TO GRACE AND ADDRESS INAUGURAL SESSION
CONFERENCE TO DELIBERATE ON THE THEME: ‘STRONG FOUNDATIONS, STRONGER VOICES: INCLUSIVE CYBERSPACE AND MENTORSHIP PATHWAYS FOR NEW WOMEN LEGISLATORS’
PLENARY SESSIONS TO FOCUS ON DIGITAL EMPOWERMENT, SAFE CYBERSPACE, CAPACITY BUILDING AND MENTORSHIP FOR WOMEN LEGISLATORS; UN WOMEN INDIA TO HOLD SIDE EVENT ON MENOPAUSE
THE CONFERENCE TO CONCLUDE ON 18 NOVEMBER 2026 WITH VALEDICTORY ADDRESS OF GOVERNOR, KARNATAKA
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 2:16PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla will inaugurate the Conference of Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians (CWP) India Region at Vidhana Soudha, Bengaluru, Karnataka, on Tuesday, 17 November 2026.

The inaugural session will be graced by the Chief Minister of Karnataka, Shri D. K. Shivakumar, who will deliver the Keynote Address. The Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha Shri Harivansh; Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka, Dr. G. Parameshwara; Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, Shri G. S. Patil; and Chairperson, CWP India Region, Smt. Daggubati Purandeswari will also grace and address the gathering.

The Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, Shri Saleem Ahmed will deliver the Welcome Address, while the Deputy Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, Dr. Umashree will propose the Vote of Thanks. Women legislators from Parliament and State/UT Legislatures, along with other distinguished dignitaries, will participate in the Conference.

Theme of the two-day Conference is ‘Strong Foundations, Stronger Voices: Inclusive Cyberspace and Mentorship Pathways for New Women Legislators’. Two Plenary Sessions will be held during the Conference. The first, on ‘Empowering Women Digitally: Safe Cyberspace, Smart Choices’, will take place on 17 November 2026 and focus on enabling women to engage safely and effectively in the digital space. The second, on ‘Capacity Building and Mentorship for Women Legislators’, will be held on 18 November 2026 and explore pathways for strengthening legislative capabilities and supporting women legislators, particularly those newly entering legislative institutions. In a special initiative complementing the broader deliberations, UN Women India will organise a side event on menopause on 17 November 2026. The deliberations will provide an important platform for sharing experiences, exchanging best practices and exploring ways to strengthen the participation and leadership of women legislators through digital empowerment, capacity building and mentorship. The event will provide an important platform to foster awareness, encourage informed dialogue and bring greater attention to women's health, well-being and dignity across different stages of life.

The Conference will conclude on Wednesday, 18 November 2026, with the Valedictory Address by the Governor of Karnataka, Dr. Sudha Yadav. The Chief Minister of Karnataka; Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha; and Chairman, Karnataka Legislative Council, will also address the session. The Chairperson, CWP India Region, will present a statement on the outcome of the Conference. The Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, will deliver the Welcome Address, while the Deputy Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, will propose the Vote of Thanks.

The Conference is envisaged as a vibrant forum for dialogue, collaboration and collective reflection, reaffirming the indispensable role of women in strengthening democratic institutions. Through its deliberations on digital inclusion, legislative capacity and intergenerational mentorship, it seeks to advance a more enabling and supportive environment in which women legislators can amplify their voices, enrich parliamentary discourse and contribute meaningfully to the future of democratic governance.

Social Security Expenditure on Health Nearly Doubles as a Share of Total Health Expenditure, rising from 6% in 2013-14 to 11% in 2023-24, Strengthening Financial Protection
Government Investment in Primary Healthcare reaches ₹1.53 Lakh Crore, Reinforcing the Focus on Affordable and Accessible Healthcare at the Grassroots
Ayushman Bharat, Free Drugs and Diagnostics, Jan Aushadhi and Other Flagship Initiatives Support India's Progress Towards Universal Health Coverage
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 2:13PM by PIB Delhi

India has registered substantial progress towards making healthcare more affordable and reducing the financial burden on households, with Government Health Expenditure tripling and the share of Out-of-Pocket Expenditure borne directly by families declining sharply over the past ten years.

The National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates for India 2023–24, released by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, highlight a significant transformation in India's healthcare financing landscape. Between 2013-14 and 2023–24, Government Health Expenditure increased from approximately ₹1.30 lakh crore to ₹4.14 lakh crore, while Out-of-Pocket Expenditure as a share of Total Health Expenditure declined from 64.2% to 42.7%.

The simultaneous increase in public healthcare financing and decline in the proportion of spending borne directly by households reflects India's progress towards a more accessible, affordable and financially protective healthcare system.

The findings also underscore the Government's sustained efforts, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to strengthen public healthcare, provide comprehensive primary healthcare, expand financial protection, improve access to essential medicines and diagnostics, and bring quality healthcare services closer to communities.

Households' Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) Falls by 21.5 Percentage Points

One of the most significant findings of NHA 2023–24 is the substantial reduction in Out-of-Pocket Expenditure as a share of India's total healthcare spending.

OOPE declined from 64.2% in 2013-14 to 42.7% in 2023–24, marking a reduction of 21.5 percentage points.

This represents an important structural shift in healthcare financing, with a substantially lower proportion of total healthcare expenditure being financed through direct payments by households.

The decline has continued in the latest year, with OOPE reducing from 43.4% in 2022–23 to 42.7% in 2023–24.

The sustained downward trend reflects the expanding role of government-supported healthcare services and financial protection mechanisms. Initiatives aimed at improving access to free and affordable treatment, medicines, diagnostics and hospital services are supporting efforts to reduce dependence on direct household spending.

Government Health Expenditure Triples, Reaching ₹4.14 Lakh Crore

India's public investment in healthcare has witnessed substantial expansion over the period.

Government Health Expenditure rose from ₹1,29,778 crore in 2013-14 to ₹4,14,196 crore in 2023–24, representing a threefold increase.

Over the decade from 2013–14 to 2023–24, the Government’s share in Total Health Expenditure (THE) increased by nearly 52%, registering an increase of 14.9 percentage points.

This growing contribution signifies a major shift in the country's healthcare financing pattern, with public resources playing a considerably larger role in meeting healthcare expenditure.

The increase in Government Health Expenditure has been accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the share of household out-of-pocket payments, reinforcing the importance of sustained public investment in improving healthcare affordability.

Public Healthcare Spending Per Person Increases Nearly Threefold

The NHA estimates also point to a substantial increase in public healthcare expenditure on a per capita basis.

Per capita Government Health Expenditure increased from ₹1,042 in 2013-14 to ₹2,959 in 2023–24, representing an increase of approximately 2.8 times.

This increase highlights the significantly higher level of government expenditure on healthcare per person and reflects the expansion of public healthcare financing over the years.

Primary Healthcare Receives Major Boost; Government Spending Reaches ₹1.53 Lakh Crore

Strengthening primary healthcare has remained a central priority of India's healthcare reforms.

The NHA 2023–24 estimates show that Government expenditure on primary healthcare reached approximately ₹1.53 lakh crore, reflecting the substantial scale of public investment in essential and community-level healthcare services.

This investment is particularly significant in the context of the expansion of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, which are bringing comprehensive primary healthcare services closer to communities.

These facilities provide services relating to preventive and promotive healthcare, screening for non-communicable diseases, essential medicines, diagnostics and other primary healthcare interventions.

The emphasis on strengthening primary healthcare is helping build a more comprehensive healthcare system, with greater focus on early detection, disease prevention and accessible care at the grassroots.

Social Security Financing Strengthens; Share Rises to 11%

The NHA estimates also highlight substantial growth in social security financing for healthcare, an important component of financial protection.

Social Security Expenditure on Health increased from 6% of Total Health Expenditure in 2013-14 to 11% in 2023–24, an increase of 5 percentage points.

This growing share reflects the expanding contribution of organised financial protection arrangements, including Government-financed health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), State-specific health insurance schemes, social health insurance and medical expenditure for government employees.

The increase in social security financing is particularly significant as it strengthens mechanisms designed to protect individuals and families against financial risks associated with medical treatment.

Private Health Insurance Expenditure also increased from 3.4% of Total Health Expenditure in 2013-14 to 10.2% in 2023–24 which reflects deepening of health insurance penetration across the country. This coupled with the increase in GHE provides enhanced financial protection to the public at large.

Flagship Government Initiatives Expanding Access to Affordable Healthcare

India's progress in healthcare financing has been accompanied by a series of major initiatives aimed at making healthcare more accessible, affordable and inclusive.

The Free Drugs and Diagnostics Initiatives, Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme, Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana and Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment (AMRIT) pharmacies are supporting access to essential healthcare services, medicines and medical products at affordable costs.

Ayushman Arogya Mandirs are expanding comprehensive primary healthcare services closer to people's homes, while Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana is strengthening financial protection for eligible beneficiaries through cashless hospitalisation benefits.

These efforts are complemented by pharmaceutical price regulation undertaken by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority.

Together, these initiatives reflect a comprehensive approach combining stronger public investment, affordable medical treatment, primary healthcare expansion and financial protection.

A Decade of Transformation in India's Healthcare Financing

The National Health Accounts 2023–24 estimates bring out an encouraging picture of India's changing healthcare financing landscape.

Compared with 2013-14, the country has witnessed threefold growth in Government Health Expenditure, a substantial increase in the Government's share of Total Health Expenditure, a sharp reduction in the share of direct household spending and significant expansion in social security financing.

The most important development is the changing balance between public and household contributions to healthcare expenditure. A larger share of total healthcare spending is now being financed through government resources, while a considerably smaller share is being borne directly by households.

These trends represent important progress towards Universal Health Coverage and demonstrate the Government's continued commitment to building an affordable, equitable and accessible healthcare system.

About National Health Accounts 2023–24

The National Health Accounts Estimates for India 2023–24 constitute the eleventh round of estimates prepared by the National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat (NHATS) at the National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

The estimates are prepared using the internationally recognised System of Health Accounts 2011 framework.

The NHA Estimates 2023–24 may be accessed at: https://nhsrcindia.org/national-health-accounts-records
