2336477.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA, VICE PRESIDENT, PRIME MINISTER AND LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAY FLORAL TRIBUTES TO BHAGWAN BIRSA MUNDA ON HIS 151ST BIRTH ANNIVERSARY
2336477.body_html:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA, VICE PRESIDENT, PRIME MINISTER AND LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAY FLORAL TRIBUTES TO BHAGWAN BIRSA MUNDA ON HIS 151ST BIRTH ANNIVERSARY
BHAGWAN BIRSA MUNDA’S STRUGGLE PROVES THAT CULTURAL ROOTS & SOLIDARITY DEFINE SOCIETY’S TRUE STRENGTH: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
IDEALS OF BHAGWAN BIRSA MUNDA STRENGTHENED THE SENSE OF COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY & SELF-RESPECT: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 1:52PM by PIB Delhi

President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu; Vice President of India and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan; Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi; Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Om Birla; Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Law and Justice and Minister of State of the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal and other distinguished dignitaries paid floral tributes at the statue of Bhagwan Birsa Munda at Prerna Sthal in the Parliament House Complex today, on the occasion of his 151st birth anniversary, observed across India as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

Bhagwan Birsa Munda, revered as Dharti Aaba, holds a distinguished place in Indian history as a freedom fighter and a champion of tribal rights. Through the Ulgulan movement, he mobilised tribal communities against British colonial rule and exploitation, asserting their rights over water, forests and land. His leadership brought together the struggle for freedom with the defence of tribal identity, cultural dignity and self-respect. His courage, sacrifice and commitment to justice remains an enduring source of inspiration for all and his legacy occupies a place of honour in the nation’s collective memory.

Since 2021, 15 November has been observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas to honour the sacrifices of tribal freedom fighters and to recognise the contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle and national life. The occasion celebrates their rich history, culture and heritage and reaffirms the nation’s gratitude for their contribution to India’s freedom and progress.

As part of the celebrations, tribal folk artists from various states performed at Prerna Sthal, welcoming the dignitaries with their art forms and showcasing the richness of India’s tribal cultural traditions.

Earlier in the day, Lok Sabha Speaker observed in his message on X, as under: 

On the 151st birth anniversary of Dharti Aba Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji—the vibrant symbol of tribal identity, self-respect, and patriotism—bowing in utmost reverence, and extending warm greetings to all citizens on the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

At a young age, through his indomitable courage, visionary thought, and extraordinary leadership qualities, he awakened a new consciousness in tribal society. The 'Ulgulan' (revolt) led by him emerged as a powerful mass movement against the exploitative system, injustice, and oppression of British rule. This struggle was not merely political resistance, but a comprehensive pledge to protect the rights, cultural identity, and social justice of tribal communities over water, forests, and land. By making society aware of its traditions, heritage, and self-respect, he showed the path of unity, organization, and self-reliance.

Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji also spread public awareness against social evils, superstition, and exploitation. His ideals strengthened the sense of self-respect, collective responsibility, and vigilance towards their rights among tribal communities. His struggle underscores the truth that the true strength of any society lies in its cultural roots, community solidarity, and the resolve to protect its existence.

His life is such an inspiring saga of sacrifice, penance, struggle, and public service that will continue to illuminate the values of patriotism, social harmony, and justice for generations to come. Bhagwan Birsa Munda ji’s unique contribution is an invaluable heritage of Indian history. His ideals will continue to inspire us to remain steadfastly committed to the respect, rights, and holistic development of tribal society.

 

जनजातीय गौरव दिवस के पावन अवसर पर संसद परिसर स्थित प्रेरणा स्थल पर धरती आबा भगवान बिरसा मुंडा जी की प्रतिमा पर पुष्पांजलि अर्पित कर श्रद्धापूर्वक नमन किया। अपने अदम्य साहस, अद्वितीय नेतृत्व और अटूट संकल्प के बल पर उन्होंने जनजातीय समाज में अधिकारबोध, आत्मसम्मान और स्वाधिकारों के लिए संघर्ष का नया अध्याय रचा। उनका जीवन अन्याय एवं शोषण के विरुद्ध प्रतिरोध, सांस्कृतिक अस्मिता के संरक्षण और सामाजिक न्याय के प्रति अटूट प्रतिबद्धता का प्रतीक है। उनका संघर्ष किसी एक कालखंड तक सीमित नहीं, बल्कि राष्ट्र की सामूहिक स्मृति में अंकित प्रेरणादायी विरासत है। उनके विचार और आदर्श हमें जनजातीय समाज के सम्मान, अधिकारों एवं सर्वांगीण उत्थान के साथ समावेशी, सशक्त और आत्मनिर्भर राष्ट्र के निर्माण हेतु निरंतर संकल्पित होकर कार्य करने की प्रेरणा देते रहेंगे। #भगवान_बिरसा_मुंडा #जनजातीय_गौरव_दिवस

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 15, 2026

 

जनजातीय अस्मिता, स्वाभिमान और राष्ट्रभक्ति के ओजस्वी प्रतीक धरती आबा भगवान बिरसा मुंडा जी की 151वीं जयंती पर कोटिशः नमन एवं समस्त देशवासियों को जनजातीय गौरव दिवस की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ। अल्पायु में ही उन्होंने अपने अदम्य साहस, दूरदर्शी चिंतन और विलक्षण नेतृत्व क्षमता से जनजातीय समाज में नवजागरण की अलख जगाई। उनके नेतृत्व में हुआ ‘उलगुलान’ अंग्रेजी हुकूमत की शोषणकारी व्यवस्था, अन्याय और दमन के विरुद्ध एक सशक्त जनांदोलन बनकर उभरा। यह संघर्ष केवल राजनीतिक प्रतिरोध नहीं था, बल्कि जल, जंगल और जमीन पर जनजातीय समुदायों के अधिकारों, सांस्कृतिक अस्मिता और सामाजिक न्याय की रक्षा का व्यापक संकल्प था। उन्होंने समाज को अपनी परंपराओं, विरासत और स्वाभिमान के प्रति जागरूक करते हुए एकता, संगठन और आत्मनिर्भरता का मार्ग दिखाया। भगवान बिरसा मुंडा जी ने सामाजिक कुरीतियों, अंधविश्वास और शोषण के विरुद्ध भी जनचेतना का प्रसार किया। उनके विचारों ने जनजातीय समाज में आत्मसम्मान, सामूहिक उत्तरदायित्व और अपने अधिकारों के प्रति सजगता का भाव सुदृढ़ किया। उनका संघर्ष इस सत्य को रेखांकित करता है कि किसी भी समाज की वास्तविक शक्ति उसकी सांस्कृतिक जड़ों, सामुदायिक एकजुटता और अपने अस्तित्व की रक्षा के संकल्प में निहित होती है। उनका जीवन त्याग, तप, संघर्ष और जनसेवा की ऐसी प्रेरणादायी गाथा है, जो पीढ़ियों तक राष्ट्रप्रेम, सामाजिक समरसता और न्याय के मूल्यों को आलोकित करती रहेगी। भगवान बिरसा मुंडा जी का अद्वितीय योगदान भारतीय इतिहास की अमूल्य धरोहर है। उनके आदर्श हमें जनजातीय समाज के सम्मान, अधिकारों और सर्वांगीण विकास के प्रति निरंतर प्रतिबद्ध रहने की प्रेरणा देते रहेंगे। #भगवान_बिरसा_मुंडा #जनजातीय_गौरव_दिवस

2336469.title: English rendering of PM's address at the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra via Video Conferencing
2336469.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
English rendering of PM's address at the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra via Video Conferencing
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 1:23PM by PIB Delhi

Johar!

Heartiest greetings to all of you across the country who are connected with this celebration of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. On the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, I bow to him with deep reverence. Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas is a national occasion that is linked to the pride of the tribal community and to the inspiration of Bhagwan Birsa Munda. With this same spirit, programmes are being organized across the country today to mark Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. The nation is proudly remembering its tribal heroes and heroines. Especially in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra, such a massive gathering is taking place. As far as my eyes can see, there are people everywhere. Gadchiroli has a rich tribal cultural heritage. The heroic stories of Raghuji Bhangare, Bhagoji Naik, and Veer Baburao Shedmake are connected to this land. On this occasion, I respectfully pay tribute to all tribal heroes. I also congratulate all the Governors, respected Chief Ministers, Deputy Chief Ministers, and every public representative participating in this event from across the country.

Friends,

The observance of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, which began on 15 November 2021, has now become a national celebration. Last year, on the 150th birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, more than two lakh programmes were organised across the country. Crores of citizens participated in these events. There was a time when many commemorative days and celebrations in our country were shaped through a foreign perspective. But today, India is proudly remembering its heritage, its history, and its heroes with indigenous self-respect. This is a symbol of a major transformation in our national consciousness.

Friends,

Whether it was Tirot Sing’s struggle in the Khasi Hills, the Kol movement in Chota Nagpur, or the Santhal revolution led by Sidho and Kanho, the tribal community has always raised its voice against injustice. On the land of Mangarh, the followers of Govind Guru made the supreme sacrifice. Rani Gaidinliu, Tantya Bhil, and many other heroes and heroines inspired the nation through their courage. Great personalities such as Alluri Sitarama Raju and Rani Durgavati also energized tribal movements. Alongside all these stories of courage, Bhagwan Birsa Munda’s Ulgulan and his struggle at such a young age continue to inspire crores of Indians even today.

Friends,

On the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas today, more than 170 projects related to tribal development have been inaugurated across different states of the country, and foundation stones have been laid for more than 70 projects. In Mizoram, a museum dedicated to the great freedom fighter Ropuiliani Ji has been inaugurated. In Arunachal Pradesh, a new building of the Tribal Research Institute has also been inaugurated. In addition, among the projects being inaugurated and launched are educational institutions, healthcare facilities, marketing centres for tribal products, and numerous initiatives related to expanding basic amenities in villages. Across different states of the country, projects worth nearly ₹3000 crore have been inaugurated or had their foundation stones laid. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you and to the people of the country for these projects.

Friends,

Today’s programme is taking place at a time when two major achievements of the country are being discussed everywhere. The first achievement is that nearly 50 crore people have overcome extreme poverty and risen out of it. The second achievement is that the country has become free from Naxalism and Maoist terror. Both these achievements are deeply connected with the lives of our tribal brothers and sisters. A few weeks ago, the World Bank report stated that nearly 50 crore people in India have emerged from extreme poverty over the past 12–13 years. This is a very large number, 50 crore people. I consider this one of the greatest achievements of the country since Independence. This achievement belongs to the entire nation. The credit does not belong to any one government. Behind it is the collective strength of society, the effort and hard work of every citizen. The decisions taken by the central government and the schemes launched for tribal welfare in recent years have also played a major role in this achievement. I congratulate all the citizens of the country, especially my tribal brothers and sisters, for this accomplishment.

Friends,

Such a large number of people rising out of poverty is a major transformation in itself. This transformation is the story of a long journey from resolve to achievement. It has created confidence that India can fulfil its resolutions and that every Indian can achieve great goals. We had taken a pledge that those who had remained deprived of the benefits of development for decades would be given priority. As our resolutions began turning into reality on the ground, a chain of positive changes began to emerge. Our government devoted its full strength to those tribal regions that were among the most backward of the backward, where even the most basic facilities of life had not reached. For the PM-JANMAN Scheme and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan, we allocated a budget of more than ₹1 lakh crore. Our effort was that the families who received facilities the latest after Independence should now receive them the fastest.

Friends,

Priority to the deprived, priority to the deprived, this has been our priority. We built more than four crore permanent houses for poor families across the country. Electricity was provided to 18,000 villages where it had not reached even after so many decades of Independence. Through the Ayushman Bharat scheme, free healthcare worth up to ₹5 lakh was provided. More than 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were established across the country, allowing healthcare benefits to reach even remote tribal areas. When poor families received toilets and sanitation facilities improved, the risk of many diseases was also reduced.

Friends,

To defeat poverty, it was equally important to increase income opportunities for poor families. Through the Mudra Yojana, we provided collateral-free loans. Under this scheme, assistance worth lakhs of crores of rupees was provided. The benefits of all these schemes reached the poor, reached Dalits, reached backward communities, and reached our tribal brothers and sisters as well. This created a new confidence within them to move forward.

Friends,

We also gave special attention to those areas that had remained behind in development for a long time. A special campaign was launched in more than 100 Aspirational Districts and over 500 Aspirational Blocks for development, better facilities, and protection of citizens’ rights. A large number of these regions have significant tribal populations. Now, under the PM Krishi Dhan Dhanya Yojana, special attention is also being given to 100 districts that are backward in agriculture. Our effort is to create new opportunities for farmers, poor families, and tribal communities in these regions. These collective efforts, and the mantra of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, have given new confidence to the poor of the country, and crores of poor people have succeeded in overcoming poverty.

Friends,

The second achievement that I referred to is freedom from Naxalism and Maoism. The people of Gadchiroli, and of tribal regions across the country, know very well that Naxalite violence caused the greatest harm to our tribal communities. In 2014, nearly 125 districts of the country were affected by Maoism and Naxalism. Hundreds of incidents of violence occurred every year. Thousands of innocent people lost their lives in these incidents. A very large number of them were our tribal brothers and sisters.

But friends,

During that period, the people affected by Maoism and Naxalism, these very brothers and sisters of mine, had been left to their fate by the governments of that era. Their rights had been taken away. Everyone sat in silence and remained quiet. You would be shocked to know that these brothers and sisters from our tribal communities were not even allowed to vote. The governments of that time remained mere spectators and sat with their eyes closed. Maoists and Naxalites would take away small children from poor mothers, and nobody could do anything. Naxalites would abduct the daughters of our homes, and everyone could only watch helplessly in anguish.

Friends,

Now that Maoism and Naxalism have been defeated, those mothers, the mothers and sisters of my tribal community, are showering countless blessings upon us. The sister who now feels safe is blessing us. The child whose childhood was once snatched away is today joining us as a young person. He is receiving opportunities for education and employment. In Chhattisgarh, areas like Bastar, where people were once afraid to go, I myself celebrated Diwali with our security forces in the heart of that region just a short while ago. This Diwali, people in all former Naxal-affected regions, including Gadchiroli, have received not only the light of lamps but also the light of hope.

Friends,

Today, our tribal society, our Janjatiya community, is contributing enthusiastically to the progress of the nation. Today, even the leadership of the country is in the hands of a daughter from the tribal community. We are all proud of President Droupadi Murmu ji.

Friends,

Today is the time for us to draw inspiration from Bhagwan Birsa Munda and devote all our energy to fulfilling the dream of a Developed India. With this call, and while bowing to Bhagwan Birsa Munda, I once again extend my heartfelt greetings to all of you on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. And I urge you that every year, 15th November should be eagerly awaited. The birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda, and even more than that, Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, is the pride of the entire nation and the self-respect of the entire nation. Every 15th November, with greater strength than before, with greater enthusiasm than before, and on a greater scale than before, we should continue to celebrate this day. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, we should keep taking new resolutions and dedicate all our strength towards fulfilling those resolutions within a fixed timeframe. What could not be achieved during so many decades after Independence, we must accomplish within a short period. Once again, as I look at the screen and see people gathered at so many places, I can see the enthusiasm and excitement in all of them. This very sight has become the pride, glory, and grandeur of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. For such a successful effort, all of you from the tribal community deserve congratulations. I wholeheartedly congratulate all of you. I thank all of you very much.

Johar.

2336457.title: NITI Aayog to launch National Workshop Series drawing lessons for the nation from 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
2336457.body_html:
NITI Aayog
NITI Aayog to launch National Workshop Series drawing lessons for the nation from 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
Five National Workshops on leadership, delivery, inclusion, civilisational identity and India’s global role, from November 2026 to October 2027
First workshop on “Leadership as Mission” at Bharat Mandapam on 17 November
Accounts from Kutch, Covid-19, Lakhpati Didi and the Space Sector to open the series
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 12:19PM by PIB Delhi

NITI Aayog will launch a series of five National Workshops on 17 November 2026 to draw lessons from twenty-five years of the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, as Head of Government. The series will study this quarter century of public leadership so that its lessons become part of the nation’s shared knowledge. It will document the experiences of those who were part of this journey and translate them into knowledge that benefits all.

The Prime Minister assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat on 7 October 2001. After serving for more than twelve years in that office, he assumed office as Prime Minister of India in May 2014 and is now serving his third successive term. With the completion of twenty-five years on 7 October 2026, this marks the longest continuous tenure at the head of an elected government in India. Throughout this period, governance has been anchored in the idea of the Pradhan Sevak, under which every office of government exists to serve the citizens. Antyodaya has set the measure of progress at the last person. Jan Bhagidari has made development a people’s movement. The principle of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas has further strengthened this as a shared national undertaking. The goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047 has provided this approach a long horizon, asking every institution to plan and act for India as it approaches the centenary of Independence.

Much of what India has learnt about governing at this scale is held in the experience of the officers, institutions and citizens who took and carried through these decisions. The series will record their first-hand accounts and examine them with academic rigour. It will develop them into institutional learning material, including case studies, research papers and teaching material, for civil servants, training institutions, universities, students and the wider public.

The five National Workshops will be focus on the following governance themes: “Leadership as Mission” in November 2026, “Governance as Delivery” in January 2027, “Development as Inclusion” in April 2027, “Civilisational Identity” in July 2027 and “India as a Global Force” in September 2027.

The first National Workshop, “Leadership as Mission”, will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 17th November 2026. It will study leadership through the specific decisions in which it becomes visible and the manner in which those decisions are translated into outcomes for citizens. Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog, will welcome the participants and Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, will deliver the opening remarks. Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, will deliver the inaugural keynote address, and Shri Uday Kotak, Founder, Kotak Mahindra Bank, will deliver a keynote address. Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, will set out the framework of the workshop.

Four first-hand accounts from those who were directly part of significant decisions will form the core of the day. Shri Rajeev Topno, Additional Chief Secretary, Government of Gujarat, will speak on the reconstruction of Kutch following the 2001 earthquake. Ms. Preeti Sudan, former Union Health Secretary and former Chairman, UPSC, will speak on the response to Covid-19. Shri Shailesh Kumar Singh, former Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development, will speak on Lakhpati Didi. Dr. S. Somanath, former Chairman, ISRO, will share his experience on the opening up of the space economy.

A panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” will be moderated by Shri B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, former Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog. The panellists will include Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Cabinet Minister for Urban Development and Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Prof. Vishal Gupta, Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, Ms. Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, and Ms. Narayani Bhatia, Joint Magistrate, Hardoi.

Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, will close the workshop and launch the Karmayogi Sankalpa on the iGOT Karmayogi platform. Through the Sankalpa, civil servants across the country will commit to a specific change in their own leadership practice.

Around 900 participants are expected to attend the workshop, of whom 250 will participate directly in the deliberations. These will include 150 government officers, including Secretaries and senior officers of the Union and State Governments and District Collectors of Aspirational Districts. The participants will also include 25 students of leading institutions and universities, and 50 community partners and beneficiaries of national flagship schemes. The group discussions will be guided by 25 case facilitators trained under the Amrit Gyaan Kosh initiative of the Capacity Building Commission. The proceedings will be streamed on the iGOT Karmayogi platform.

2336452.title: The Lakhpati Didi Initiative
2336452.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
The Lakhpati Didi Initiative
From Household Income Enhancement to Women-Led Rural Entrepreneurship
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 12:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Lakhpati Didi Initiative promotes sustainable household incomes through women's entrepreneurship and diversified livelihoods. It is being implemented under the DAY-NRLM, which leverages the SHG network to provide rural women with financial access, skills and market opportunities. The initiative's implementation reflects a phased approach to policy planning, institutional strengthening and community mobilisation. As of June 2026, the initiative has enabled 3.76 crore Lakhpati Didis, with a target of six crore by March 2029.An independent assessment by IIM Ahmedabad reported a 61 percent rise in average monthly household income and a 61.7 percent increase in average monthly savings in Lakhpati Didi households.

 

From Subsistence to Sustainable Livelihoods

The Lakhpati Didi Initiative is a flagship effort to strengthen women's economic participation in rural India. It aims to improve household incomes through sustainable livelihood opportunities and enterprise development. The government announced this initiative on 15 August 2023. It initially targeted two crore women from Self-Help Group (SHG) households. The target was subsequently increased to three crore in February 2024. The initiative aims to create six crore Lakhpati Didis by March 2029. This target was envisioned in February 2026.

A Lakhpati Didi is an SHG member whose household earns at least ₹1 lakh annually. The benchmark considers total household income rather than individual earnings. Income from eligible farm and non-farm activities contributes towards this target. It is calculated after expenses and should remain sustainable across agricultural seasons or business cycles.

The initiative builds on the institutional network of the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). It seeks to move rural women beyond subsistence-based activities. Its approach combines livelihood diversification, financial inclusion, skill development and enterprise support.

 

3.76 Crore Rural SHG Women Enabled as Lakhpati Didis

By June 2026, 3.76 crore rural SHG women had been enabled as Lakhpati Didis and 5.70 crore women were identified as Potential Lakhpati Didis.

An independent evaluation of the Lakhpati Didi initiative by IIM Ahmedabad, covering 6,531 respondents in 17 states and UTs, reported improvements in household economic conditions. Average monthly household income increased by 61 percent, while average monthly savings increased by 61.7 percent.

 

Institutional Foundation: DAY-NRLM and the SHG Network

The Lakhpati Didi Initiative operates through DAY-NRLM. The government launched DAY-NRLM in June 2011. It organises women from poor rural households into SHGs. These groups promote regular savings and collective financial activities. They also connect members with banks, credit, training and markets. As of 12 November 2026, DAY-NRLM had mobilised approximately 10.13 crore SHG members into 94.40 lakh SHGs. SHGs function through a wider institutional structure. Village Organisations and Cluster Level Federations strengthen this network. This institutional foundation provided the delivery mechanism for the Lakhpati Didi Initiative. It enabled the government to build upon existing community institutions rather than establish a separate structure.

 

Evolution and Expansion of the Initiative

The initiative evolved through a series of policy decisions and implementation measures. In 2021, the government advised States to promote sustainable livelihoods and diversify farm and non-farm activities among SHG households. In August 2023, the government announced the target of enabling two crore rural SHG women as Lakhpati Didis. Recognising the need to strengthen community institutions for achieving this goal, the government conducted structured training for community cadres between November 2023 and March 2024. Approximately 5.5 lakh persons received training, which comprised of 12 modules delivered over 15 hours.

In February 2024, the Interim Budget increased the national target to three crore Lakhpati Didis. The Lakhpati Didi portal was also launched during this period. In May 2024, the Digital Aajeevika Register began recording the livelihoods and income of each household. Under this process, women are identified as ‘Potential Lakhpati Didis’ on the LokOS platform. Trained Community Resource Persons (CRPs) prepare business plans for individual households. Households then receive coordinated support in areas such as skills, finance, assets and markets. The national and state missions monitor progress through the same register. By August 2024, one crore women had achieved Lakhpati Didi status.

Further digital interventions followed in July 2025, with the introduction of the Didi Business Plan tool and a financial-literacy application for CRPs. The reported achievement in creating Lakhpati Didis increased to two crore women in August 2025. By December 2025, the initiative had achieved its three-crore target ahead of schedule. Subsequently, in February 2026, the government revised the national target to six crore Lakhpati Didis by March 2029.

 

 

Identification and Implementation Framework

The initiative follows a community-led identification and implementation process. It provides equal opportunities to SHG members across social and economic categories. Potential Lakhpati Didis are identified through consultations. Trained Community Resource Persons (CRPs) facilitate this process. They assess household livelihoods and support women in identifying additional income opportunities. The implementation framework follows several stages:

 

 

  1. Identification: Potential beneficiaries are identified through the SHG network and LokOS platform.
  2. Income Assessment: Household livelihoods, income and expenditure details are recorded. The Digital Aajeevika Register provides a common monitoring framework.
  3. Enterprise Planning: CRPs prepare individual business plans. These plans are consolidated to identify common requirements and sectoral opportunities.
  4. Implementation Support: Women receive coordinated assistance over three years. This includes training, finance, livelihood assets and market access.
  5. Monitoring: National and State missions review progress through digital records. State missions also validate reported achievements.

This process connects household-level planning with institutional support. It also allows interventions to respond to local livelihood requirements.

 

Leadership in Action: From Strategic Planning to Implementation

The initiative's implementation reflects a phased approach to policy planning, institutional strengthening and community mobilisation.

  • The groundwork began on21October 2021, when the government issued an advisory to States. It encouraged sustainable diversified farm and non-farm livelihoods among SHG households under DAY-NRLM. On 29 December 2021, the government requested States to establish time-bound targets.
  • Subsequently, a communication dated 10 June 2022 introduced a mobile application-based household income survey to provide an evidence base for identifying household income gaps and planning targeted interventions.
  • On 6 September 2023, the government organised a National Conclave, in which State missions, development partners and line ministries participated. The government released a Strategy Note on Enabling Two Crore Lakhpati SHG Didis. The strategy adopted an institutional approach by leveraging the existing DAY-NRLM network. The design recognised four critical considerations. Additional credit needed to support viable livelihoods and repayment capacity. Household income required a consistent measurement framework. State capacities varied and required context-specific support. Community institutions also needed adequate training to prepare household-level plans. These considerations were presented to the Prime Minister on 10 October 2023. The Ministry of Rural Development subsequently submitted a detailed action plan to the Prime Minister's Office. It issued implementation action points on 16 October 2023.
  • Consultations with States also identified 12 priority livelihood sub-sectors. These included bamboo, honey, goat rearing, poultry and tasar silk.
  • During 2024, the initiative received continued leadership attention through national addresses and direct interactions. The Prime Minister referred to it during Mann Ki Baat and other national addresses. He also interacted with SHG women, drone operators and entrepreneurs. A Performance Review Committee meeting took place in July 2024. The government also organised regional consultations across Guwahati, Srinagar, Jaipur, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Raipur during 2024-25. These engagements facilitated interaction with State missions and enabled discussions on implementation progress.
  • In January 2025, a Lakhpati Didi tableau featured in the Republic Day parade on Kartavya Path. The government conducted refresher training during February-March 2025. In March2025, it initiated discussions with the Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and MSME departments. These discussions focused on convergence between their respective schemes. The government also introduced a learning portal and chatbot in October 2025.
  • The government also strengthened data governance during 2025-26. It introduced checks to identify unusual income entries. State missions were asked to reconcile discrepancies and certify reported figures. This helped strengthen the credibility of progress assessments. In 2026, implementation support expanded further through digital and institutional interventions. An application for individual enterprise loans was introduced on 21 February 2026. An upgraded version of LokOS followed in May 2026. Regional workshops were organised at Gaya and Pushkar. A review involving all States took place during the Rashtriya Grameen Vikas Sammelan on 28-29 June 2026. On 29 June 2026, a platform for producer groups and enterprises and a public Lakhpati Didi dashboard were also launched.

Overall, the implementation approach demonstrates the importance of leadership beyond target-setting. The government combined evidence-based planning with institutional capacity building. It leveraged existing community networks and promoted interdepartmental convergence. Regular reviews, digital tools and data validation strengthened monitoring and accountability. This combination enabled a nationally coordinated initiative to function through decentralised, community-led institutions.

 

Building Women-Led Rural Prosperity

The Lakhpati Didi Initiative represents an approach to rural livelihood development centred on women. It combines existing community institutions with enterprise planning and financial support. Its focus extends beyond increasing household income. It also promotes diversified livelihoods, entrepreneurship and community leadership. By enabling women to become active economic contributors, the initiative seeks to strengthen rural households. It also creates pathways for broader rural economic development.

2336442.title: President of India, Vice President, Prime Minister And Lok Sabha Speaker Pay Floral Tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda in Parliament Premises
2336442.body_html:
Rajya Sabha Secretariat
President of India, Vice President, Prime Minister And Lok Sabha Speaker Pay Floral Tributes to Bhagwan Birsa Munda in Parliament Premises
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 11:22AM by PIB Delhi

President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu; Vice President of India and Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan; Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi; Lok Sabha Speaker, Shri Om Birla; Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Law and Justice; and Minister of State in the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal; Members of Parliament and other distinguished dignitaries paid floral tributes at the statue of Bhagwan Birsa Munda on his birth anniversary, Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, at Prerna Sthal in the Parliament premises today.

During the day, Shri C.P. Radhakrishnan in a message on X wrote, "A symbol of courage and resistance, he led the tribal community against British rule, championing their rights, dignity and identity. His clarion call of Ulgulan became a powerful voice of the struggle for freedom and justice. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, we honour his enduring legacy and the invaluable contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle and nation-building. It was inspiring to witness vibrant cultural performances celebrating his legacy and the invaluable contributions of tribal communities to Bharat’s freedom struggle and nation-building."

Since 2021, November 15 has been observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas to honour the sacrifices of tribal freedom fighters. Tribal communities played a crucial role in India’s freedom struggle, contributing through numerous revolutionary movements. This day celebrates their rich history, culture and heritage, with nationwide events aimed at fostering unity, pride, and recognition of their significant contributions to India’s freedom and progress.

As part of celebrations, welcoming the dignitaries, six tribal folk artists from various states, showcased their talent at Prerna Sthal in  Parliament premises.

2336431.title: NIELIT to organize 3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026) to be held in New Delhi on November 16–17, 2026
2336431.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
NIELIT to organize 3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026) to be held in New Delhi on November 16–17, 2026
NCCDFI 2026 to Bring Together Key Stakeholders to Strengthen India’s Cybersecurity and Digital Forensics Ecosystem
The conference will be held under the theme “Cyber Secure Bharat: Fortifying India’s Digital Future”
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 11:06AM by PIB Delhi

The National Institute of Electronics & Information Technology (NIELIT), under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is organising the 3rd National Conference on Cyber Security, Digital Forensics & Intelligence (NCCDFI 2026) on November 16-17, 2026, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, 15 Janpath, New Delhi, centered around the theme “Cyber Secure Bharat: Fortifying India’s Digital Future.

The conference assumes noteworthy significance in the present digital era, wherein the increasing dependence on digital technologies, the emergence of sophisticated cyber threats and the evolving nature of cybercrime have made cyber security and digital investigation critical areas of national importance.

The journey of NCCDFI began in 2024 with its inaugural edition in Kohima, Nagaland, held from 25–26 July 2024 at the Capital Convention Centre, Organised by NIELIT Kohima in collaboration with the Nagaland Police and the Department of Information Technology & Communication, Government of Nagaland. Building on the foundation laid in Kohima, the second edition of NCCDFI was held in 2025 at Gauhati University, Guwahati, Assam. Drawing on the success of its preceding editions, the conference expanded its reach from a regional initiative into a broader national platform. The third edition aims to further strengthen this platform through wider participation, technology demonstrations, knowledge exchange and stronger collaboration among key stakeholders.

NCCDFI 2026 will provide a knowledge-sharing platform for stakeholders from government, law enforcement, defence, judiciary, technology providers, industry, academia and the cybersecurity ecosystem to deliberate on emerging cyber threats and evolving challenges in digital investigations and cyber resilience. The conference will focus on strengthening coordination among agencies, enhancing capacity in cybersecurity and digital forensics, facilitating policy dialogue and exploring the application of emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Blockchain Security and Cyber Intelligence.

NCCDFI 2026 is supported by a strong group of industry partners, bringing together leading organisations in digital forensics, cybersecurity and investigative technologies. The knowledge partners includes Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C), CERT-In, Delhi Police, CyberPeace, Standardisation Testing and Quality Certification (STQC), Military College of Telecommunication Engineering (MCTE), Mhow, Maharashtra Cyber, Manipur Police, Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB), Hyderabad, Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) and Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). The industry partners includes STELLAR, Power Forensics & Digital Intelligence, Magnet Forensics, MSAB, Cyint Technologies, 3rd Eye Techno Solutions, Advanced Digital Forensic Solutions, Inc., Oxygen Forensics and VERTEXON LABS. Their participation will contribute industry expertise, technology demonstrations and practical insights, strengthening the conference’s focus on advancing capabilities in cybersecurity, digital forensics and digital investigations.

The conference will focus on 10 key tracks covering the evolving cybersecurity landscape: Cybersecurity, Digital Forensics, AI Security, Critical Infrastructure, Threat Intelligence, Blockchain & Crypto, Drone & IoT Forensics, Digital Evidence, Cyber Law, and Cloud Security. These tracks will bring together experts and practitioners to explore emerging threats, technological advancements, investigative techniques, regulatory developments and strategies for building a secure and resilient digital ecosystem.

The two-day conference will feature an inaugural session, technical and business sessions, panel discussions, an industry exhibition and Cyber Kushti 2026 – Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon. The technical sessions will cover key areas including national cybersecurity and critical infrastructure, incident response, AI-enabled cyber threats, automated digital investigations, cyber threat intelligence, financial cybercrime, advanced device and multimedia forensics, law-enforcement readiness, international cooperation, digital evidence, quantum computing, autonomous systems, frontier technologies, capacity building and the national cyber ecosystem. The exhibition during the conference will showcase technologies and solutions in digital forensics, cybersecurity, drone technology, surveillance systems and AI-driven security, with opportunities for technical interactions and business-to-business engagements.

A key highlight of NCCDFI 2026, “Cyber Kushti 2026- Cybersecurity & AI Hackathon”, will be organised alongside the technical sessions. The three-level competition is structured around the themes of Review, Attack and Defend, reflecting critical aspects of modern cybersecurity operations. The hackathon has received an overwhelming response, with 1,031 teams comprising 3,093 participants registering for the competition. Of these, 923 teams (2,769 participants) have been shortlisted for Level 1, while 50 teams have qualified for Level 2 and 10 teams for Level 3.

NCCDFI 2026 will also feature the signing of MoUs between NIELIT and industry partners, aimed at strengthening institutional partnership, knowledge exchange, joint initiatives, research and development, and capacity building in the fields of cyber security, digital forensics & intelligence, etc. These collaborations are envisaged to establish a framework for long-term cooperation and facilitate industry-academia engagement and promote future collaborative initiatives in these critical domains.

Through NCCDFI 2026, NIELIT along with its supporting organisations and institutional partners, seeks to contribute towards strengthening professional competencies, fostering institutional collaboration and supporting the development of a secure, resilient and trusted digital ecosystem in the country.

***

Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma

2336427.title: COAS GENERAL DHIRAJ SETH DEPARTS ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO CZECH REPUBLIC
2336427.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
COAS GENERAL DHIRAJ SETH DEPARTS ON AN OFFICIAL VISIT TO CZECH REPUBLIC
Visit to Strengthen Bilateral Defence Cooperation and Military-to-Military Ties
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 10:28AM by PIB Delhi

General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), proceeded on an official visit to the Czech Republic from 16 to 19 November 2026. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation, enhance military-to-military engagement and explore opportunities for collaboration in defence technology and industry.

During the visit, the COAS will hold discussions with senior military leaders of the Czech Armed Forces, including Lieutenant General Petr Čepelka, First Deputy Chief of the General Staff and the Deputy Chief of Defence at General Staff Headquarters (GSHQ) in Prague. The COAS will pay tribute to fallen soldiers during a wreath-laying ceremony at the GSHQ. He will call on senior officials of the Ministry of Defence. These engagements will focus on matters of mutual interest, including military cooperation, training, modernisation and emerging security challenges.

As part of the programme, General Dhiraj Seth will visit the Defence University in Brno and the NATO Joint Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defence Centre of Excellence to gain insights into specialised training, operational capabilities and future readiness of the Czech Armed Forces.

The COAS will interact with representatives of Inter-governmental Defence Cooperation Agency (AMOS), the Defence and Security Industry Association and leading defence manufacturers to explore opportunities for cooperation in defence technology and industry.

The visit reflects the shared commitment of India and the Czech Republic to strengthening bilateral defence relations through sustained military dialogue, professional exchanges and industrial partnerships.

2336426.title: Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum
2336426.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum
Preserving India’s Civilisational Heritage for Future Generations
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 10:23AM by PIB Delhi

 

Yuge Yugeen Bharat: A Museum for the Ages

India's civilisational heritage, spanning over 5,000 years, reflects a rich legacy of art, architecture, knowledge systems, traditions and cultural practices that have evolved over centuries. To preserve and present this heritage, the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is being developed as a landmark national cultural institution at the historic North and South Block Complex in New Delhi. Envisaged as a museum of the people, it will showcase the continuity, diversity and richness of India's civilisational journey through an integrated presentation of its tangible and intangible cultural heritage.

First announced by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 18 May 2023, the project received approval from the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on 11 November 2026, with an estimated total project cost of ₹3,230 crore. Being developed by the Ministry of Culture, the museum will transform the historic North and South Blocks, formerly housing key government offices, into public cultural spaces through adaptive reuse while preserving their architectural character. Planned as a museum of global scale, it will bring together historical collections, thematic galleries and modern exhibition technologies to make India's cultural heritage accessible to citizens, researchers and visitors from across the world.

From Historic Buildings to a World-Class Museum

The Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum will transform the historic North and South Blocks in New Delhi from centres of governance into public cultural spaces. Developed through adaptive reuse, the project will preserve the architectural heritage of these landmark buildings while creating modern exhibition spaces and visitor facilities. The museum is envisaged as a major cultural destination, combining heritage conservation with contemporary museum infrastructure.

Preserving Heritage Through Adaptive Reuse

  • Historic Significance: The North and South Blocks served as centres of government administration until 13 February 2026, nearly 95 years after the inauguration of South Block. The South Block housed the Prime Minister's Office since Independence, and Cabinet meetings under 16 Prime Ministers were held in these buildings.
  • Transformation into Public Spaces: Following the relocation of government offices to Seva Teerth, the new Prime Minister's Office, and the Kartavya Bhavans, the two buildings are being repurposed as part of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum.
  • Architectural Conservation: The project will preserve the buildings' historic character, façades and architectural integrity through minimal intervention.
  • Reimagining Existing Spaces: Courtyards, corridors and rooms will be adapted into galleries and exhibition areas, creating a unified museum experience.
  • Sustainable and Inclusive Design: The redevelopment will prioritise sustainable resource use and universal accessibility.

A Museum of Global Scale

The proposed museum will rank among the world's largest cultural institutions in terms of exhibition space, with infrastructure designed to accommodate a substantial number of visitors.

  • Proposed Built-up Area: Approximately 1,78,509 square metres across the North and South Block Complex.
  • World's Largest Display Area: The museum plans to offer more than 1 lakh square metres of display space. This would exceed the display areas of the Louvre (73,000 sq. m), the British Museum (70,000 sq. m) and the Hermitage (66,800 sq. m).
  • Visitor Capacity: Designed to accommodate 30,000 visitors per day and 1 crore visitors annually.
  • Visitor Management: Timed entry and crowd management systems are planned to facilitate convenient movement through the museum.
  • Public Amenities: Proposed facilities include children's zones, food courts, souvenir shops and performance spaces, alongside accessible public areas.

The museum's development will thus combine the conservation of two historically significant buildings with the creation of a large-scale, accessible cultural institution for citizens and visitors from India and abroad.

Bringing India's Civilisational Journey to Life

The Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum will present India's civilisational journey through curated thematic galleries, historical collections and immersive experiences.

Phased Development and Implementation

The museum will be developed in phases, allowing galleries and exhibitions to be introduced progressively.

  • Implementation Period: FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31.
  • First Gallery: The Adornment gallery is expected to open to the public in the North Block in the later part of 2027.
  • Expansion of Galleries: A modular approach is being formulated to add further thematic galleries in subsequent phases.
  • Project Oversight: Implementation will involve coordinated project management, design and technical oversight, quality assurance and periodic monitoring.

The museum is expected to strengthen the preservation and public presentation of India's cultural heritage while creating opportunities for education, research, cultural engagement and tourism.

Thematic Galleries and Exhibitions

The museum will feature galleries on themes such as Architecture and Cityscapes, Mathematics and Astronomy, Languages and Scripts, Faith and Spirituality, and Bharat Connects - Trade and Ideas, among others.

These are among the themes identified for the museum, with additional galleries planned through a modular approach.

A Collection Reflecting India's Cultural Diversity

  • Approximately 18 lakh objects have been identified for potential display at the museum, bringing together collections from different institutions across the country.
  • The identified objects are drawn from the National Museum, other museums under the Ministry of Culture, 52 Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) site museums, various State museums and private collections.
  • Content and collection analysis is underway to determine how these objects will be incorporated into the museum's exhibitions.
  • The project also includes dedicated collection storage and conservation facilities to support the preservation and management of heritage objects.

Technology and Interactive Experiences

The museum will integrate contemporary technologies to make its exhibitions more engaging and accessible.

  • Immersive Experiences: Planned use of Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support interactive interpretation and storytelling.
  • Digital Documentation: The Ministry of Culture's collaboration with Google Arts & Culture, announced on 5 November 2026, includes digitisation efforts relating to the museum's historic buildings and collections.
  • Modern Museum Infrastructure: Integration of intelligent building systems, exhibition technologies and conservation facilities to support museum operations and visitor experiences.

A Cultural Institution for Generations to Come

Beyond preserving and showcasing India's civilisational heritage, the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum is expected to contribute to cultural tourism, education and research while creating opportunities for public engagement. As a national cultural institution, it will benefit a wide range of visitors, including students, researchers, scholars, cultural practitioners, the general public, and domestic and international tourists, offering opportunities to explore and appreciate India's diverse cultural legacy.

The project is expected to generate direct and indirect employment during its construction and operational phases. It is expected to create opportunities for artisans, craftspeople, researchers, museologists, designers, performers and other creative professionals, and to support livelihoods in the hospitality and tourism sectors. To promote Make in India, the project will encourage domestic manufacture of world-class museum materials and products through structured vendor development, creating opportunities for Indian artisans, manufacturers, conservation professionals and technology providers.

The museum is also expected to generate recurring revenue through ticket sales, food and beverage facilities, events and venue rentals, digital experiences, guided tours, retail outlets and other visitor services. With infrastructure planned to accommodate up to 1 crore visitors annually, the project aims to combine long-term cultural preservation with public accessibility and revenue-generating visitor services. Its educational, cultural and tourism-related benefits are intended to extend to visitors from across India and abroad.

2336424.title: Adi Vaani
2336424.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Adi Vaani
Bringing India’s Tribal Languages into the Digital Age
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 9:55AM by PIB Delhi

 

Adi Vaani is an AI-powered platform of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs that makes tribal languages more accessible through translation and digital tools. As on 15 October 2026, it supports text translation in nine tribal languages and has recorded over 35,000 Android downloads. State Tribal Research Institutes have contributed approximately 13.9 lakh text sentences and around 300 hours of speech data to train its models. The Working Group on Tribal Languages, which first met on 15 October 2026, discussed positioning Adi Vaani as the National Tribal Language Repository. By reducing language barriers, it can support mother-tongue education, healthcare communication, access to public services and cultural preservation.

 

Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is observing Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada across the country from 1 to 15 November 2026, culminating in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas on 15 November, the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The Government of India designated 15 November as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas in 2021. The Pakhwada is a focused, time-bound drive to accelerate the Ministry’s flagship programmes and take their benefits to tribal families at the last mile. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, over 300 projects for tribal communities across States are being taken up, with 228 ready for inauguration and 74 for foundation stone laying. Two national digital initiatives, the Jan-HIT Portal and the National FRA Digital Platform, are also being launched. Tribal Research Institutes have planned more than 160 activities in 19 States/UTs.

Click to Read More: Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026: Nationwide Celebrations to Honour Tribal Heritage, Empower Communities and Accelerate Last-Mile Delivery of Welfare Schemes

 

A language is more than a means of communication. It carries the history, identity and knowledge of a community. Across India, tribal languages have carried folk tales, songs and valuable knowledge of forests, farming and medicine across generations. Yet many are low-resource languages, spoken by relatively small communities and passed down largely through oral traditions. With limited written records and very little digital text or speech data, these languages have remained largely unsupported by modern language technologies. Adi Vaani aims to bridge this gap by using artificial intelligence. It uses technology to document, translate and promote tribal languages, creating new opportunities for their preservation, learning and everyday use.

 

Adi Vaani: Connecting Language with Technology

Adi Vaani is an AI-powered translation and language platform built with tribal communities, for tribal communities. Launched by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs on 1 September 2025, it was developed by a national consortium led by IIT Delhi, along with BITS Pilani, IIIT Hyderabad, IIIT Nava Raipur and the Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) of Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Meghalaya. Over time, several other State Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) also joined the initiative, further expanding its collaborative reach across the country.

 

Bridging the Digital Divide: Mission and Vision

Adi Vaani aims to bridge the digital divide for tribal communities through AI-powered translation. Its vision is a digitally inclusive India where no citizen is left behind due to language barriers. The initiative is guided by respect, collaboration, authenticity, innovation and empowerment through digital inclusion.

 

Expanding Language Coverage and Digital Reach

Starting with Santali, Bhili, Mundari and Gondi, Adi Vaani has expanded to offer text translation in nine tribal languages as on 15 October 2026. It also provides speech translation, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), video subtitling and access to more than 300 language primers. Primers are basic language learning resources designed to help new learners understand and practise tribal languages easily. The platform has recorded over 35,000 Android downloads and around 6,500 monthly users, indicating its growing digital reach.

 

 

Building AI with Tribal Communities

What makes Adi Vaani different is its community-based approach. Native speakers contribute words, sentences and voice recordings through TRIs and AdiKosh. These are checked by language experts before being used to train AI models. The project aims to collect around 1,00,000 sentence pairs and 100 hours of speech recordings per language. As on 15 October 2026, State TRIs had contributed approximately 13.9 lakh text sentences across ten languages and around 300 hours of speech data. This approach combines modern technology with community knowledge to support the preservation, learning and everyday use of tribal languages. Each language passes through five phases, from data collection to integration on the platform, and the models are retrained as the community contributes more data.

 

What Are TRIs and AdiKosh?

Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) are research bodies established at the State level under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. They serve as centres of knowledge and research, functioning as think tanks for tribal development. TRIs preserve tribal cultural heritage, while providing research-based inputs to States for evidence-based planning and appropriate legislation. They build the capacity of tribal communities, as well as of individuals and institutions associated with tribal affairs. They also disseminate information and create awareness on tribal issues.

AdiKosh is the word bank of Adi Vaani. It holds dictionary entries and spoken sentences, recorded by verified speakers and reviewed by the language team. Speech recorded through AdiKosh is validated by TRIs before it is used to train the models.

 

The platform’s key features include:

  • Text-to-text translation: Translation between supported tribal languages and languages such as Hindi and English.
  • Speech-to-text: Converts spoken words into text, supporting oral-language documentation.
  • Speech-to-speech translation: Translates speech by linking speech recognition, translation and speech synthesis.
  • Optical Character Recognition (OCR): Extracts text from images and scanned documents for translation.
  • Video subtitling: Supports translation of video content and public information into tribal languages.
  • Digital dictionaries and primers: Provide vocabulary, meanings and basic learning resources.

 

Tribal Languages: Preserving Knowledge and Identity

According to Census 2011, India has about 10.45 crore Scheduled Tribe people, accounting for about 8.6% of the country’s population. These communities have distinct languages and cultural traditions. Preserving these languages is important as they carry centuries of folklore, traditional knowledge and community identity. They also support early learning in the mother tongue and help pass knowledge of forests, farming, medicine and biodiversity to future generations. Making these languages digitally accessible can further reduce language barriers and improve access to education, healthcare information and public services.


 

 

Tribal Languages Covered by Adi Vaani

Adi Vaani works with a total of 13 tribal languages across different regions of India. The table shows the State named on the portal for each language, with its corpus size and script. Some languages are spoken in several States beyond the State identified for the Adi Vaani project.

Adi Vaani’s Impact: Beyond Language Translation

The usefulness of Adi Vaani extends to education, healthcare awareness and public communication, where language can influence how information is understood and used.

 

Supporting Mother-Tongue Education

The National Education Policy 2020 recommends the use of the home language, mother tongue or local language as the medium of instruction wherever possible, at least until Grade 5 and preferably until Grade 8 and beyond.

Adi Vaani provides access to more than 300 language primers prepared by Tribal Research Institutes, along with 24 dictionaries and other learning resources.

The National Education Society for Tribal Students has also highlighted the potential use of these resources across more than 525 Eklavya Model Residential Schools, serving over 1.7 lakh students. Their integration into school learning could support mother-tongue-based multilingual education and encourage students to engage with their linguistic heritage.

 

Improving Healthcare Communication

Language accessibility can play an important role in public health programmes, particularly in explaining diseases, screening procedures and preventive measures.

Adi Vaani includes translated awareness resources on Sickle Cell Disease, a major health concern among several tribal communities.

The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission, launched on 1 July 2023, aims to eliminate the disease as a public health problem by 2047. By 16 July 2026, more than 7.24 crore screenings had been conducted in tribal-dominated areas. Adi Vaani can complement such health initiatives by supporting awareness and communication in local languages.

 

Economic Empowerment: Improving Access to Markets

Language barriers can limit access to market information, digital services and business opportunities. Adi Vaani aims to address this gap by making online information more accessible in tribal languages. Its translation tools can support tribal entrepreneurs in understanding market information and government support programmes.

India is also expanding market opportunities for tribal producers. As on 13 August 2026, 4,712 Van Dhan Vikas Kendras had been sanctioned in 28 States and UTs, covering 12.94 lakh beneficiaries. These centres support tribal livelihoods through processing, packaging, branding and marketing of products.

Digital market access is also growing. As on 18 March 2026, around 6,000 tribal products were available on the Tribes India e-commerce platform, and 1,339 products had been onboarded onto the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC).

By reducing language barriers, Adi Vaani could complement these efforts and help tribal communities participate more easily in the digital economy.

 

Public Services: Making Government Information Accessible

Language barriers can make it difficult to understand government schemes, official documents and public services. Adi Vaani helps address this through AI-powered translation in tribal languages.

The Ministry also launched Jago, its official AI conversational assistant, on 24 August 2026, to make information on tribal welfare schemes, programmes and initiatives easier to find and understand. Together, these initiatives aim to make public information more accessible, particularly in remote tribal areas.

 

Cultural Preservation: Keeping Tribal Traditions Alive

Adi Vaani brings together technology and community knowledge to document tribal languages, folk songs, stories and oral traditions. Native speakers, elders and linguists contribute language data, which is reviewed by experts to ensure accuracy and reflect local usage.

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs also provides financial assistance to 29 TRIs to preserve, document and promote tribal heritage, including languages, oral traditions and indigenous knowledge systems. By involving communities directly, Adi Vaani helps build authentic digital resources and makes tribal cultural heritage more accessible to future generations.

 

Building a National Tribal Language Repository

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is taking steps to expand Adi Vaani beyond translation into a broader national resource for tribal languages.

On 15 October 2026, the Ministry convened the first meeting of the Working Group on Tribal Languages, chaired by Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The group includes representatives from the Central Institute of Indian Languages, IITs, universities, language organisations and experts working on endangered languages.

The meeting discussed positioning Adi Vaani as the National Tribal Language Repository, bringing together corpora, primers, dictionaries and community stories. The Ministry will circulate the agenda items and prepare a roadmap for the work ahead.

 

Proposals placed before the Working Group include:

  • Preparing a national baseline of tribal languages and available resources.
  • Developing digital archives and multilingual educational material.
  • Establishing district-level community resource groups involving trained tribal youth.
  • Strengthening cooperation among TRIs, academic institutions and language experts.
  • Implementing a two-year action plan with quarterly reviews.

Earlier, at the National Conclave on Tribal Languages and Museums in Mysuru on 24 August 2026, an upgraded version of Adi Vaani was introduced, along with an iOS application and the addition of five languages. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs also signed an MoU with the Central Institute of Indian Languages on language documentation and corpus development. The Government of Karnataka and the Karnataka State Tribal Research Institute released Class 1 primers in Jenukuruba at the Conclave.

These initiatives aim to bring existing linguistic research and community resources together within a common national framework.

 

Towards a More Inclusive Digital India

Adi Vaani has established an initial digital foundation for tribal languages through translation tools, educational resources and community-generated language data. As each language’s corpus grows, the models are retrained and translation accuracy improves.

As India advances towards Viksit Bharat 2047, the initiative connects the preservation of linguistic diversity with the wider goal of digital inclusion. Making tribal languages accessible through modern technologies can support both cultural continuity and participation in education and public services.

The next step is to ensure that these digital resources become useful tools in the everyday lives of the communities whose languages they represent.

2336423.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal arrives in Cairo, Egypt, on an official visit to strengthen bilateral economic and commercial ties
2336423.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal arrives in Cairo, Egypt, on an official visit to strengthen bilateral economic and commercial ties
Shri Piyush Goyal pays homage to Indian soldiers at the Heliopolis War Cemetery and meets members of the Indian community in Cairo
Visit aims to deepen the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership and expand cooperation in trade, investment and industrial development
Business delegation comprising over 130 business leaders and start-ups accompanies the Commerce and Industry Minister
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 9:55AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal arrived in Cairo, Egypt, on 14 November 2026, for an official visit aimed at strengthening the India–Egypt Strategic Partnership, deepening bilateral trade and investment relations, and exploring new opportunities for industrial and commercial cooperation between the two countries.

India and Egypt share a longstanding relationship rooted in historical, civilizational and people-to-people ties. Over the years, this relationship has evolved into a multifaceted partnership encompassing political, economic, security and cultural cooperation. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India–Egypt relations have gained renewed momentum, culminating in the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership, with a shared commitment to enhanced cooperation, including in the economic domain.

At the beginning of his visit, Shri Piyush Goyal paid homage to Indian soldiers at the Heliopolis War Cemetery in Cairo, honouring their sacrifice and contribution. Of the 4,000 soldiers buried or commemorated at the cemetery, 3,727 were Indian soldiers. Nearly 2,000 of them lost their lives during the First World War and around 1,700 during the Second World War.

The Minister also addressed an Indian community event organised by the Indian Community Association in Egypt. The interaction provided an opportunity to engage with members of the Indian diaspora and acknowledge their role in strengthening economic, cultural and people-to-people ties between the two countries.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Piyush Goyal highlighted the strength of India–Egypt relations, noting that bilateral trade of around US$6.5 billion represents only the beginning of the partnership between the two ancient civilisations. Describing the Indian community as a living bridge between the two countries, he underscored the contribution of nearly 70 Indian companies operating in Egypt, with investments exceeding US$5 billion and generating direct and indirect employment for Egyptians.

The Indian community in Egypt continues to serve as an important bridge between the two nations, contributing to commercial exchanges, professional cooperation and the broader India–Egypt relationship.

The visit will feature the 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC), the India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) Meeting and the India–Egypt Business Forum. The 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee will be co-chaired by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh on 15 November 2026 in Cairo.

The programme will also include bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers, interactions with leading business representatives and meetings with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), the Egyptian Junior Businessmen Association and the Egypt–India Startups Forum. These engagements are expected to provide platforms for reviewing bilateral economic cooperation, addressing trade and investment-related issues, and identifying new avenues for business partnerships, while giving fresh impetus to bilateral trade, investment, industrial cooperation and innovation linkages.
