2336418.title: Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Arrive at Golden Pagoda, Namsai, Marking the Final Phase of Exposition in Arunachal Pradesh
2336418.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Arrive at Golden Pagoda, Namsai, Marking the Final Phase of Exposition in Arunachal Pradesh
Governor of Arunachal Pradesh Inaugurates the Exposition at Namsai; Sacred Relics to Remain Open for Public Darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026
Over 35,000 Devotees Pay Homage to the Sacred Relics at Bomdila; Cumulative Footfall at Tawang and Bomdila Exceeds 66,000
Two Special Exhibitions on Buddhist Heritage Inaugurated at Golden Pagoda
Posted On: 15 NOV 2026 7:32AM by PIB Delhi

The Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha arrived at Namsai, Arunachal Pradesh, on 14 November 2026, marking the commencement of the third and final phase of their exposition in the State. The Sacred Relics were ceremonially received and enshrined at the Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham), one of the prominent centres of Buddhist faith and heritage in eastern Arunachal Pradesh.

The Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, Lt Gen Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik (Retd.), received the Sacred Relics at Nalung Helipad in Namsai. He was accompanied by Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, State Ministers, public representatives and religious leaders. Devotees and members of the local community gathered along the ceremonial route to the Golden Pagoda to pay their respects to the Sacred Relics.

The exposition was formally inaugurated at the Golden Pagoda following the reception and enshrinement ceremony. The Governor graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein, Shri Raghav Prasad Bhatnagar, Director General, International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), venerable members of the Buddhist Sangha and other distinguished guests were present on the occasion.

Governor Highlights the Contemporary Relevance of Lord Buddha's Teachings

Addressing the gathering, the Governor described the exposition as an occasion of profound spiritual and cultural significance. He observed that the Sacred Relics symbolise the life, enlightenment and timeless teachings of Lord Buddha.

The Governor highlighted the relevance of Buddhist teachings in addressing contemporary challenges. He noted that the message of peace, compassion, wisdom and non-violence assumes particular significance at a time when humanity faces conflict, intolerance and violence.

He urged people to imbibe these values in their daily lives and contribute to building a society founded on harmony, dignity and mutual respect.

The Governor appreciated the collective efforts of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the National Museum, New Delhi, the International Buddhist Confederation and all those associated with the exposition. He acknowledged their contribution in bringing the Sacred Relics closer to devotees across Arunachal Pradesh.

Deputy Chief Minister Shri Chowna Mein highlighted the rich and diverse Buddhist heritage of Arunachal Pradesh. He underlined the significance of the exposition in a State where Mahayana, Vajrayana and Theravada Buddhist traditions have flourished across generations. He described the arrival of the Sacred Relics at Namsai as a rare opportunity for devotees to offer prayers and reconnect with the teachings of Lord Buddha.

On the occasion, two special exhibitions organised by the National Museum, New Delhi, and the International Buddhist Confederation were inaugurated at the Meditation Centre of the Golden Pagoda.

The exhibition titled “Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery”, organised by the International Buddhist Confederation, presents the historical, archaeological and spiritual significance of the Piprahwa Relics. It traces the archaeological discoveries at Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh and the enduring tradition of Buddhist relic veneration.

The exhibition also highlights the journey of the Piprahwa jewel collection and its return to India in 2025 after more than a century. It provides visitors with an opportunity to understand the importance of preserving and protecting India's Buddhist heritage.

The second exhibition, titled “Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives”, curated by the National Museum, New Delhi, showcases the rich artistic, historical and cultural heritage of Buddhism. It highlights the evolution of Buddhist traditions and their continuing influence on art, culture and society.

Together, these exhibitions complement the spiritual experience of the Sacred Relics Exposition. They offer devotees, students, scholars and visitors an opportunity to deepen their understanding of the life and teachings of Lord Buddha and India's rich Buddhist heritage.

The arrival of the Sacred Relics at Namsai follows the successful conclusion of the six day exposition at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery, also known as Lower Gompa, in Bomdila, West Kameng district.

The exposition, held from 8 to 13 November 2026, witnessed an overwhelming response from devotees. More than 35,000 devotees visited the monastery during this period to offer prayers, seek blessings and pay homage to the Sacred Relics.

Buddhist monks, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and devotees from different parts of West Kameng district and neighbouring regions participated in the public darshan with deep faith and reverence.

The district administration made arrangements for constituency wise participation to facilitate orderly public darshan and ensure that devotees from different areas had an opportunity to visit the exposition.

The large turnout at Bomdila reflected the deep spiritual significance of the Sacred Relics and the enduring Buddhist traditions of the region.

Following the conclusion of public darshan on 13 November, the Sacred Relics were accorded a ceremonial farewell on the morning of 14 November for their onward journey to Namsai.

The exposition of the Sacred Relics in Arunachal Pradesh commenced at the historic Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) on 31 October 2026. The inaugural ceremony was attended by Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh Shri Pema Khandu, venerable Buddhist monks and other dignitaries.

The exposition at Tawang continued until 7 November 2026 and witnessed participation by more than 31,000 devotees.

With over 35,000 devotees visiting the subsequent exposition at Bomdila, the cumulative footfall at the two venues has exceeded 66,000.

The return of the Sacred Relics to Arunachal Pradesh after a gap of 13 years has provided Buddhist communities across the State with a cherished opportunity to pay homage to Lord Buddha.

The exposition has brought together devotees from different Buddhist traditions and cultural backgrounds. It has also reaffirmed the enduring spiritual and cultural bonds that connect the people of Arunachal Pradesh with India's wider Buddhist heritage.

The Sacred Relics will remain enshrined at the Golden Pagoda (Kongmu Kham), Namsai, for public darshan from 14 to 20 November 2026.

The Golden Pagoda is an important centre of Theravada Buddhist faith and practice in Arunachal Pradesh. The exposition at Namsai will provide devotees from eastern Arunachal Pradesh and neighbouring regions an opportunity to offer prayers and pay homage to the Sacred Relics.

Following the conclusion of the exposition, the Sacred Relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on 21 November 2026.

The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the National Museum, New Delhi, and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi.

The initiative reflects the Government of India's sustained commitment to the protection, preservation and promotion of India's Buddhist heritage. It seeks to bring this sacred heritage closer to devotees and strengthen cultural and spiritual connections across Buddhist communities.

The exposition at Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai also celebrates the diversity of Buddhist traditions in Arunachal Pradesh and reinforces the universal message of Lord Buddha — peace, compassion, wisdom, non-violence and harmony.

2336332.title: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to perform Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society in Pune, Maharashtra
2336332.body_html:
Ministry of Cooperation
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to perform Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society in Pune, Maharashtra
Shri Amit Shah to virtually inaugurate the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies and launch Bharat Taxi services for Pune
Cooperative sector in Maharashtra to receive a fresh impetus towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’
Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society project marks a significant initiative towards promoting cooperative-led industrial and economic activities
Inauguration of the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies to facilitate improved administrative and regulatory services for Multi-State Cooperative Societies at the regional level
Launch of Bharat Taxi services in Pune to encourage the expansion of cooperative-based transport services and greater participation of Sarathis
Letter of Intent to be exchanged between NHEC and IDMC Limited
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 9:06PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant initiative towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and further strengthening, modernising and making the cooperative movement in the country more inclusive, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will perform the Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society at a programme to be held in Talegaon Dabhade, Pune district, Maharashtra, on Sunday, 15 November 2026. On the occasion, Shri Amit Shah will also inaugurate the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS) and launch Bharat Taxi services for Pune. Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol, Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra Smt. Sunetra Ajit Pawar, Deputy Chief Minister Shri Eknath Shinde and other dignitaries will be present at the event.

Under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, the Ministry of Cooperation has been making sustained efforts to strengthen cooperative institutions financially, enhance transparency and accountability in their functioning, promote cooperative-based enterprises and create new economic opportunities in the cooperative sector. The programme in Pune marks another important step towards advancing these initiatives.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will begin the programme by performing the Bhoomi Pujan of NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society. The foundation-laying ceremony of the NHEC Multi-State Cooperative Society project marks a significant initiative towards expanding cooperative-led industrial and economic activities. On the occasion, a Letter of Intent (LoI) will also be exchanged between NHEC and IDMC Limited. This initiative is expected to promote institutional collaboration and open up new opportunities in the cooperative sector.

During the programme, Shri Amit Shah will virtually inaugurate the Western Regional Office of the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS). The initiative marks an important step towards making administrative and regulatory services more accessible to Multi-State Cooperative Societies at the regional level, while promoting ease of operations, transparency and accountability in the functioning of cooperative institutions.

On the same occasion, the Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation will launch Bharat Taxi services for Pune, Maharashtra. The initiative, aimed at expanding cooperative-based transport services, is expected to encourage greater participation of Sarathis (driver-partners) and further strengthen the cooperative model in the transport sector. During the programme, share certificates will also be presented to four Bharat Taxi Sarathis, underscoring the principles of member participation and ownership that lie at the heart of the cooperative model.

The programme in Pune represents a significant initiative towards strengthening cooperative institutions, promoting cooperative-based entrepreneurship and expanding new economic activities. Guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, the Ministry of Cooperation continues to work towards making cooperative institutions across the country more capable, competitive and people-centric.

2336326.title: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Showcases Artisans’ Products at 45th India International Trade Fair 2026
2336326.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Showcases Artisans’ Products at 45th India International Trade Fair 2026
Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Participate in IITF 2026; Showcase Handicrafts, Handlooms and Traditional Products
TULIP Brand Promoted to Expand National and International Market Access for Traditional Artisans
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 8:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, is participating in the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, being organised at Bharat Mandapam, in the National Capital here.

The Ministry’s pavilion, located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, showcases the rich craftsmanship, traditional skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of artisans and beneficiaries associated with the Ministry’s Apex Corporations.

The participation reflects the Government’s continued commitment to promoting inclusive economic growth and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for disadvantaged and marginalized sections of society.

Guided by the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas’, the Ministry is providing a national platform to artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs) to exhibit, promote and directly market their products.

A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in this year’s edition through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

He said the participating artisans are displaying an extensive range of handicrafts, handloom products, handmade articles and other traditional products, reflecting India's diverse cultural heritage and indigenous craftsmanship.

The initiative provides artisans with an important opportunity to connect with customers, explore new market opportunities, showcase their products to a wider audience and generate income through direct sales, he said.

The Official noted that by facilitating participation in prestigious national-level exhibitions and trade fairs, the Ministry is working towards strengthening market linkages, encouraging entrepreneurship and enabling beneficiaries to move towards greater economic self-reliance.

A major highlight of the Ministry’s participation is the promotion of the TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) brand, the Official said.

 

The Official said Hon’ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, launched the TULIP initiative recently during the Shilp Samagam Mela at Dilli Haat, in National Capital.  He said TULIP seeks to provide traditional artisans with an enhanced platform for showcasing and marketing their products.

The Official added the TULIP initiative aims to strengthen the visibility and market reach of artisan-made products at both national and international levels. It seeks to establish sustainable livelihood opportunities by connecting traditional craftsmanship with emerging market demands, while preserving and promoting India's rich artistic and cultural traditions, he said.

Through the brand, the Ministry endeavours to provide artisans with greater recognition, improved market access and opportunities to expand their entrepreneurial activities, the Official said.

The Official said the Ministry’s participation in IITF 2026 also underscores the importance of inclusive market development, where traditional skills and indigenous knowledge are linked with contemporary marketing opportunities.

The Ministry’s participation adds a social empowerment dimension to the event by bringing the products and entrepreneurial potential of artisans and beneficiaries from marginalised communities into the mainstream marketplace, he added.

The Official remarked that such platforms enable artisans from diverse social and geographical backgrounds to showcase their capabilities, strengthen their market presence and become active contributors to the country's economic development.

Through its continued efforts, the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment remains committed to advancing social and economic inclusion, promoting traditional artisanship, strengthening livelihood opportunities and ensuring that the benefits of development reach all sections of society, the Official concluded.

The India International Trade Fair, was inaugurated on 13th November Friday, that provides a prominent national and international platform for trade, commerce, industry and cultural exchange.

2336272.title: A journey through a divided homeland: Paweł Pawlikowski’s ‘Fatherland’ to mark the beginning of global cinematic celebrations in Goa
2336272.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
A journey through a divided homeland: Paweł Pawlikowski’s ‘Fatherland’ to mark the beginning of global cinematic celebrations in Goa
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 6:46PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 14 November 2026

 

Some journeys cross landscapes, while others travel through the complexities of memory, identity and belonging. Bringing together history and deeply personal relationships, Fatherland (Ojczyzna), directed by acclaimed Polish filmmaker Paweł Pawlikowski, has been selected as the Opening Film of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), setting the tone for nine days of cinematic celebration in Goa.

Set in the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, Fatherland explores the relationship between Nobel Prize-winning German writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, an actress, writer and rally driver. Returning to Germany after sixteen years of exile in the United States, Thomas Mann embarks on a challenging road trip with his daughter in a black Buick. Their journey takes them across a country devastated by war, from US-dominated Frankfurt to Weimar under Soviet control.

As father and daughter travel through a divided Germany, they encounter more than the visible scars of a nation torn apart by conflict. Their journey also brings them face to face with the deep divisions within their own family. Through this emotionally layered narrative, the film explores the intersections of personal relationships, history and the idea of home.

Featuring Sandra Hüller and Hanns Zischler in leading roles, the 82-minute drama is a collaborative production involving Poland, Germany, Italy and France. Presented in black and white, the film will have its India Premiere at the 57th IFFI.

Fatherland continues director Pawel Pawlikowski’s exploration of history and human relationships through an intimate narrative set against a significant moment in European history. The film has already travelled to major international festivals, including Cannes, San Sebastián and Telluride in 2026, earning Pawlikowski the Best Director Award at Cannes.

With Fatherland, the 57th IFFI begins its journey through stories that transcend geographical and cultural boundaries. As cinema brings together different worlds and perspectives, the opening film offers a fitting beginning to this year’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’.

 

* * *

2336270.title: DRI seizes 20 kg meth tablets hidden in specially fabricated cavity of tipper truck in Assam; one arrested
2336270.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 20 kg meth tablets hidden in specially fabricated cavity of tipper truck in Assam; one arrested
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 6:43PM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its major crackdown on trafficking of contrabands in the North Eastern region of the country, officers of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), in an intelligence led operation conducted jointly with the personnel of the 38 Battalion of Assam Rifles, seized 20 kg methamphetamine tablets (commonly known as yaba) from a tipper truck on 12th November 2026.

Acting on an intelligence input, DRI officers intercepted a Tata tipper truck near Borkhola in Cachar district and during its detailed inspection, with the assistance of a mechanic, officers detected a specially concealed cavity in the upper inner portion of the truck's right-side panel. The panel bore signs of cutting and welding, which had been camouflaged with cement and paint.

Upon opening the cavity, officers recovered 32 packets containing pinkish-orange tablets suspected to be methamphetamine. The recovery comprised 17 brick-shaped packets weighing 1 kg each and 15 rectangular packets weighing 200 grams each. Preliminary field tests on representative samples using an NDPS Field Detection Kit indicated the presence of amphetamine.

The recovered tablets, weighing 20 kg in total, along with the truck, were seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. The occupant of the truck was arrested under the provisions of the Act.

The operation has exposed an innovative concealment method involving a fabricated cavity inside the side panel of a tipper truck, with the opening camouflaged using cement and paint to evade detection during routine checks.

DRI remains committed to dismantling drug trafficking networks and curbing the flow of illicit narcotics through sustained intelligence-led operations and inter-agency cooperation.

2336269.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan announces five lakh PMAY-G houses for Odisha
2336269.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Shivraj Singh Chouhan announces five lakh PMAY-G houses for Odisha
29 lakh women in Odisha become Lakhpati Didis; more support for women entrepreneurs
Every panchayat in Odisha to receive up to ₹2 crore for development
Balangir agriculture college to be developed as the country’s best institution
No eligible poor family in Odisha will be left without a pucca house
Solar-powered homes to help rural families cut bills and earn additional income
Women entrepreneurs to get loans without guarantees
Viksit Bharat–G RAM G scheme to accelerate rural development in Odisha
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 6:41PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today announced five lakh pucca houses for poor families in Odisha under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Gramin. Addressing a state-level program of the scheme in Balangir in the presence of Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi. The program also witnessed the foundation stone laying for a new agriculture college in Balangir. Deputy Chief Minister and Agriculture Minister Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Panchayati Raj and Drinking Water Minister Shri Ravi Narayan Nayak, Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr Mukesh Mahaling, Member of Parliament Smt Sangeeta Kumari Singh Deo, and local legislators Shri Naveen Kumar Jain, Shri Laxman Bag and Ms Rupa Mishra were among those present.

Shri Chouhan said that a fresh and proper survey had now been completed and no poor family would be left living in a kutcha house. All eligible families would receive pucca houses in a phased manner. He also announced that the Centre and the state government would jointly provide subsidies for installing solar panels on houses. This would help beneficiaries bring their electricity bills down to zero and earn additional income by selling surplus electricity.

29 lakh women become Lakhpati Didi in Odisha; ₹10 lakh crore credit initiative for women

Paying tribute to the strength and contribution of women, Shri Chouhan said that the Subhadra Yojana, under which women receive ₹10,000 annually, had strengthened their confidence and enhanced their dignity. He appreciated Odisha for achieving the target of 27 lakh Lakhpati Didis a year ahead of schedule, with 29 lakh women now having attained this status under the leadership of Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi. The Union Minister said that, over the next five years, loans worth ₹10 lakh crore would be extended through banks to women across the country to help more women become Lakhpati Didis. He added that access to credit would no longer be limited to members of self-help groups. Women who wish to start their own businesses or livelihood activities individually would also be able to obtain loans without the requirement of a guarantee.

Balangir agriculture college to become the country’s leading institution; solar power to support farmers

Describing service to farmers as akin to worshipping God, Shri Chouhan assured that the new agriculture college in Balangir would be developed into the country’s finest agricultural institution with the support of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Government of India. Leading agricultural scientists from across the country would work with farmers and help address their needs. He said that a comprehensive roadmap is being prepared in coordination with the Odisha government to modernise agriculture in the state. Under a proposed initiative, solar panels would be installed above agricultural fields, allowing farmers to cultivate fruits and vegetables beneath them. This would enable farmers to earn from both agriculture and solar power. Shri Chouhan also said that the names of eligible farmers who had been left out of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme had now been added to the beneficiary list.

Every panchayat to receive ₹1–2 crore for development; mafia networks dismantled

Outlining the government’s plans for rural development, Shri Chouhan said Odisha would receive approximately ₹4,000 crore this year under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G scheme. This would provide every panchayat with ₹25 lakh to ₹50 lakh annually. Over five years, smaller panchayats would receive up to ₹1 crore and larger panchayats up to ₹2 crore for development works. The funds could be used to build roads, drains, schools and panchayat buildings, improve road connectivity to farmers’ fields and construct ponds for water conservation. He further said that, following the approval of 1,700 kilometres of roads under the fourth phase of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, all remaining villages would also be connected through pucca roads.

‘Viksit Odisha’ vision rooted in the state’s culture and people

Paying tribute to Balangir’s rich cultural heritage, including its Nuakhai festival and Dalkhai and Rasarkeli dances, Shri Chouhan called upon the people to work together towards building a developed Odisha. Addressing the large gathering in his characteristic warm and personal style, he said he had not come as a distinguished guest or visitor, but as a humble public servant in his capacity as Minister for Agriculture and Rural Development. He said he saw Lord Jagannath in the living and vibrant people of Odisha and the image of Subhadra Maiya in the women of the state. Praising Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Shri Chouhan described him as a simple, approachable and dedicated public servant who worked tirelessly. He said that, with the objective of realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat, the Chief Minister was working towards building a Viksit Odisha.

2336265.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
MoU Between DoSJE and DGDE to Extend Senior Citizen Welfare Schemes to Cantonment Boards Across the Country
Union Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar to Witness Signing of MoU on November 16 Monday
New Day Care Centres, Senior Citizen Homes and Geriatric Caregiver Training to Strengthen Elderly Care Infrastructure
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) under the  Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, will sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Directorate General Defence Estates (DGDE), Ministry of Defence, in the National Capital here on November 16 Monday.

The signing ceremony will take place in presence of the Hon’ble Raksha Mantri, Shri Rajnath Singh, and the Hon’ble Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar.

The MoU aims to establish a framework for cooperation, coordination and convergence between the two organisations for implementing senior citizen welfare schemes under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) in Cantonment Boards across the country.

The partnership will leverage the infrastructure and administrative network of Cantonment Boards, along with the scheme support, financial assistance and technical expertise of the Department, to facilitate access to care, support and opportunities for active and dignified ageing.

The event will also be attended by Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; Smt. Shobha Gupta, Director General Defence Estates, and other senior officials of both the Ministries and departments.

Speaking about the initiative, Sajeesh Kumar N, Joint Secretary in the Ministry said the MoU represents a Whole-Of-Government approach towards the welfare of senior citizens. He said the well-established infrastructure and community-level presence of Cantonment Boards, in collaboration with the DGDE, will help extend senior citizen welfare services quickly to these areas.

The collaboration will also provide financial support for Senior Citizen Homes with residential facilities of 25/50-bed capacity, wherever feasible, to  help strengthen institutional care facilities and expand access to residential support for senior citizens, the Official said.

The official said the MoU builds on the momentum of the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, a national campaign on intergenerational bonding launched by the Ministry on November 4, 2026.

The participation of young people as trained caregivers and their engagement in activities promoting intergenerational relationships will contribute towards creating a supportive and inclusive environment for senior citizens, the Official said.

Shri Kumar N said the MoU will further promote intergenerational bonding through a pledge to be administered to students of schools run by Cantonment Boards, along with activities encouraging meaningful interaction between young people and the senior citizens.

He said the initiative seeks to foster respect and understanding between generations while recognising senior citizens as valuable sources of experience, wisdom and values.

The Official said India's population aged 60 years and above is projected to increase from approximately 10 Crore in 2011 to around 23 Crore by 2036. He said with changing family structures and increasing urbanisation, community-based facilities such as Day Care Centres and access to trained caregivers close to home are becoming increasingly important, he added.

The partnership with DGDE is expected to strengthen the availability of such services for senior citizens residing in Cantonment areas across the country, Shri Kumar N said.

Under the MoU, new Day Care Centres and related facilities for senior citizens will be established in Cantonment Boards under AVYAY, the Official said. Existing Day Care Centres being operated by Cantonment Boards will also be strengthened with support and assistance from the Department, he added.

Shri Kumar N said another key component of the partnership will be skill training for youth as geriatric caregivers through the training and channel partners of the Department which will contribute towards creating a trained workforce for elderly care while opening up new livelihood opportunities for young people.

The Official said that awareness camps will also be organised to disseminate information about the Ministry’s welfare schemes for senior citizens. Public representatives, prominent social workers and local communities will be mobilised to strengthen awareness and participation, he said.

Through this collaboration, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment continues its efforts to strengthen institutional support, expand community-based care facilities and promote the socio-economic well-being of senior citizens by enabling them to lead dignified, secure and self-reliant lives, Shri Kumar N remarked.

It is pertinent to mention that Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) is the umbrella scheme of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment for the welfare of senior citizens. It aims to ensure that senior citizens lead healthy, happy, empowered, dignified and self-reliant lives. Its key components include the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens, Senior Citizen Homes, Geriatric Caregiver Training, the National Helpline for Senior Citizens (Elderline – 14567), Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana and other initiatives promoting active and healthy ageing.

2336260.title: IICA Stakeholder Consultation held in New Delhi, experts emphasize Public Policy must Shift from ‘Control to Trust’
2336260.body_html:
Ministry of Corporate Affairs
IICA Stakeholder Consultation held in New Delhi, experts emphasize Public Policy must Shift from ‘Control to Trust’
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 6:22PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), established under the aegis of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, organised a high-level Stakeholder Consultation on ‘Public Policy & Corporate Affairs: Evolving Roles & Professional Development’ at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, recently.

The consultation was convened to define the scope of the public policy function within organisations, identify the capabilities its professionals require, and consider how learning pathways can be strengthened to meet both organisational expectations and national priorities.

Delivering the inaugural theme address, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA, underscored the need for continuous and meaningful dialogue between the public and private sectors. He placed the consultation within IICA’s wider mandate of building capacity across government and industry for better-informed engagement between the two. He observed that the way organisations understand policy, contribute to its development and use it to guide their decisions bears on the quality of governance and the wider business environment, and that the consultation was intended to identify practical ways of strengthening the skills this work demands.

The inaugural session had special addresses from retired senior beurocrats and corporate leaders like Shri Amarjeet Sinha, IAS (Retd.), former Secretary, Government of India, who called for collaborative governance and predictable policy, with business engaging the regulator before, during and after a policy shift. It is important to focus the systems thinking approach in the professional framework evolving in public policy function.

Dr. Anup K. Pujari, former Secretary, Government of India, stressed the need to build the capacity of mid- and late-career professionals into a cadre able to bridge the public and private sides of the regulatory system. Shri Arun Goyal, former Secretary, Government of India, noted the growing part the private sector plays in the working of regulatory bodies and the development of regulation, which takes the function well beyond liaison. Shri Rajiv Agarwal, IAS (Retd.), Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, Tata Consultancy Services, emphasised communication and behavioural skills and the alignment of policy work with internal stakeholders and corporate strategy. Shri Richard Rekhy, Vice Chairman, Grant Thornton Bharat, said policy professionals need financial acumen and a view of national and global value chains to advise corporate leaders, with evidence as the basis of trust.

The deliberations that followed were organized in three tracks, (i) on the public policy and corporate affairs function, (ii) the evolving role of its professionals, and (iii) their education and professional development.

Participants examined the evolution of the function in business eco-system and how is it placed between the private sector and regulatory framework. They noted that twin tasks of the public policy function is to help the organisation understand what policy means for its strategy and of contributing credibly to policy discussions, the division of responsibility with legal, compliance and business teams, and how early it is brought into strategic business decisions.

The consultation also sketched the professional acumen for the public policy professionals of the country with the skills expected of practitioners at different career stages, among them a working knowledge of how governments and regulators take decisions, economic and data-based reasoning, and risk and stakeholder management, joined by the judgement to balance institutional priorities with the public interest. On capacity building, the conclusions favoured a multidisciplinary, case-based curriculum, flexible delivery suited to working professionals and internships with government.

The consultation drew 50+ senior representatives from listed and multinational companies, consulting and advisory firms, think tanks, industry associations, academia and civil society, along with senior government officials and policy researchers.

Setting the context, Dr. Niraj Gupta, Head, School of Corporate Governance & Public Policy, described the consultation as the start of a sustained effort by IICA to give this emerging profession an institutional anchor. He laid out the key questions for the consultation on emergence of public policy, and how capability can be built through education and practice. The consultation was coordinated by Mr. Manoj Singh, Chief Program Executive, IICA.

The deliberations concluded with a roadmap for IICA to work with industry bodies and academic institutions in support of this emerging profession, so that public policy professionals are equipped to work at the interface of corporate affairs and national development.

The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA) is a think tank under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, dedicated to serving the corporate sector through knowledge, governance, and transformation.

2336254.title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Celebrates World Diabetes Day with Enthusiastic Participation of Indian Diaspora in Italy; Highlights India's Scientific and Healthcare Progress
2336254.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Dr. Jitendra Singh Celebrates World Diabetes Day with Enthusiastic Participation of Indian Diaspora in Italy; Highlights India's Scientific and Healthcare Progress
Minister calls for prevention of diabetes, particularly among youth – Stresses lifestyle modification and control of obesity
Minister says ‘Early Action on Diabetes’, the theme of World Diabetes Day, captures the essence of diabetes management through early detection, timely intervention and strict control of blood glucose levels
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 6:11PM by PIB Delhi

Union World Diabetes Day was observed in Rome with enthusiastic participation from members of the Indian diaspora in Italy, representing diverse sections of society, including students, women, entrepreneurs and professionals from different walks of life. The participants joined the programme with great enthusiasm and expressed happiness and pride over India’s remarkable progress in science, technology, research and healthcare during the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The gathering reflected the growing confidence of the Indian community in India’s scientific capabilities, healthcare initiatives and its expanding contribution to global scientific advancement.

The enthusiastic participation of the Indian diaspora, comprising students, women, entrepreneurs and members of the professional community, reflected the strong interest of Indians living abroad in India’s scientific and healthcare journey. The participants appreciated the country’s progress in scientific research, technological innovation and healthcare delivery under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, expressing pride in India’s growing global standing and its commitment to addressing important public health challenges such as diabetes.

Addressing the event organised at the Embassy of India in Rome on the occasion of World Diabetes Day, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Dr. Jitendra Singh, a noted diabetologist and Professor, called for greater emphasis on the prevention of diabetes, particularly among young people, stressing that lifestyle modification, healthy dietary habits, physical activity and control of obesity remain the fundamental measures for tackling the growing burden of the disease.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that although several new groups of anti-diabetic drugs have emerged for the treatment of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, the basic mantra of diabetes management continues to be lifestyle modification and obesity control.

Referring to this year’s theme, ‘Early Action on Diabetes’, the Minister said it captures the entire spirit of the management strategies required to check the rapid spread of diabetes in society. He emphasised that proactive early detection and timely action, followed by strict control of blood glucose levels through both pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical measures, are essential to reducing the growing burden of diabetes.

Dr. Jitendra Singh expressed concern over the changing age profile of diabetes, noting that a disease previously associated largely with middle and old age is increasingly affecting young people in the prime of their lives. Diabetes at a younger age can have implications for an individual’s professional productivity and quality of life, while also requiring sustained attention to blood glucose control over a longer period to prevent damage to vital organs such as the kidneys, eyes and heart.

The Minister highlighted the close metabolic association between obesity, diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension and heart disease, stating that the Government of India has accorded priority to addressing these interconnected health concerns. He recalled that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has repeatedly emphasised the importance of controlling obesity.

Pointing to the particular vulnerability of Indians to central obesity, which is an independent risk factor for metabolic disorders, including diabetes mellitus, Dr. Jitendra Singh underlined the need to strengthen preventive healthcare and encourage healthier lifestyles.

The Minister also highlighted the integrated and holistic approach adopted by the Government of India since 2014 towards the management of metabolic disorders and lifestyle-related diseases. He referred to the establishment of the Ministry of Ayush, the introduction of wellness centres and the observance of the International Day of Yoga on June 21 every year, following the proposal of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, which was unanimously accepted by the United Nations. These initiatives, he said, contribute in different ways to reducing the burden of diabetes in society.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also referred to measures aimed at strengthening early detection and access to treatment, including provisions for mass screening for diabetes and initiatives under Ayushman Bharat to make healthcare more accessible and affordable.

Emphasising the importance of dietary discipline and physical activity, the Minister said that proper eating habits and an optimum level of physical activity are essential components of diabetes prevention and management. He also drew attention to physical and mental stress as contributing factors that require attention.

The Minister observed that India, with its large number of people living with diabetes, has considerable experience in managing the disease. Indian experts, he said, are well placed to share their experience and knowledge with counterparts in other countries and contribute to wider international efforts to address the challenge.

Dr. Jitendra Singh reiterated that the message of World Diabetes Day goes beyond treatment and calls for a stronger focus on prevention, early diagnosis and sustained management, particularly among the younger population.

The event was organised at the Embassy of India in Rome as part of the Minister’s official visit to Italy from November 11 to 15, 2026. The programme also included an interaction with members of the Indian community in Italy.

2336242.title: NSS organises block-level sports meets across the country to mobilise youth against substance abuse
2336242.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
2336242.body_html:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
NSS organises block-level sports meets across the country to mobilise youth against substance abuse
Week 9 of ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ campaign witnesses participation of over 87,000 youth and community members across more than 130 institutions
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, through the Directorate of MY Bharat-National Service Scheme (NSS), organised Cluster of Block-Level Sports Meets across the country under Week 9 of the 100-Week ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan’. Held under Month 3 of the campaign, themed ‘Strong Communities, Healthy Youth’, the initiative brought together thousands of student volunteers, local youth clubs and community members from neighbouring villages, blocks and colleges to promote discipline, teamwork and an addiction-free lifestyle through sports. A total of 992 activities were organised, mobilising 87,481 student volunteers, local youth club members and community spectators across the country.

Launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 02.08.2026 under the umbrella of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, the Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat campaign aims to promote a drug-free and healthy society by encouraging young people to stay away from drugs, alcohol, tobacco and other addictive substances.

Field reports from more than 130 institutions across 10 Regional Directorates – Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chandigarh, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Jaipur, Lucknow and Trivandrum – included a range of sporting activities, including 100-metre and 400-metre sprints, marathons, Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Volleyball, Football and Basketball. Traditional games such as Tug of War (Rassa-Kassi), Rumal Jhapat and Lemon Races were also organised. In Lakshadweep, participants took part in traditional island games organised under Regional Directorate Trivandrum.

The campaign also placed emphasis on gender inclusion, with 42,190 female participants taking part in sporting events and awareness activities. The sporting events were integrated with anti-addiction awareness activities to reinforce the message of the campaign. Each competition commenced with a collective Nasha Mukt Sankalp, with athletes, referees, coaches and spectators taking a pledge to uphold fair play and lead an addiction-free lifestyle.

Health awareness kiosks were set up at major clusters across Bhopal, Punjab, Rajasthan and Delhi. These kiosks disseminated Information, Education and Communication (IEC) materials on mental health and provided information about the national de-addiction helpline (14446). The events were further supplemented by Nukkad Nataks (street plays), anti-drug rallies and slogan-writing competitions to raise awareness about substance abuse, peer pressure and pathways to recovery.

Local administration and specialists also extended support to the initiative. Senior police and Narcotics Cell officers from Bathinda, Kasaragod and Coimbatore, psychiatrists, de-addiction specialists and local civic representatives, including Panchayat Sarpanches, participated in the activities.

2336218.title: BRICS Cinema takes centre stage at 57th IFFI with 21 films from across the world
2336218.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
BRICS Cinema takes centre stage at 57th IFFI with 21 films from across the world
Showcase brings diverse cinematic narratives on democracy, freedom, identity, history and contemporary global concerns
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 4:24PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 14 November 2026

 

The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 will feature 'Films from BRICS', a showcase of cinema from BRICS countries that engages with questions of democracy, freedom, identity, history and contemporary global concerns. Drawing on histories, social realities and personal journeys, the films offer perspectives from the societies they emerge from.

Featuring 21 films, the selection moves across countries, languages and genres, bringing narratives that engage with questions of freedom, identity, social inequality, family, conflict, displacement and belonging. Several of these films look back at defining moments of struggle and change, from pro-democracy movements to the fight against slavery and colonial rule.

Brazil’s ‘Amadeo and the Hypothetical New World’ imagines an African inventor in 1830s Brazil whose invention becomes part of the struggle to liberate enslaved people. Indonesia’s ‘The Sea Speaks His Name’ follows the disappearance of a student activist during the country’s 1998 pro-democracy movement and his family’s search for answers. South Africa’s ‘The Trek’ takes viewers across the Kalahari Desert in the mid-19th century, confronting the brutality of the colonial frontier.

Contemporary concerns also find a place in the selection. ‘Dreaming of Serenada’, a Uganda-UK documentary, explores climate change through a father-daughter relationship and the impact of flooding on a rainforest landscape. ‘Faya Dayi’, from Ethiopia and the United States, examines communities connected to khat cultivation and consumption, bringing into focus livelihoods, social realities and the aspirations of young people. Iran’s ‘Poultry Farm’ follows an undocumented child from Iraq whose search for a missing friend puts his own life at risk.

Family, identity and personal choices form another strong theme. Saudi Arabia’s ‘Hijra’ follows a young girl, her grandmother and her missing sister on a journey that uncovers family secrets and generational differences. China’s ‘Embers’ traces the consequences of a mix-up involving cremated ashes, bringing two women face to face with loss and mortality. ‘The Condor Daughter’, a Bolivia-Peru production, portrays a young woman from an indigenous Andean community torn between inherited musical traditions and her dream of becoming a performer. Nigeria-UK production ‘Lady’ follows a young taxi driver in Lagos whose encounter with a group of sex workers leads her towards solidarity and self-discovery.

The Indian entry, ‘Article 370’, directed by Aditya Dhar, is set against the backdrop of the 2016 Kashmir unrest and follows a mission to abrogate Article 370. The film received three honours at the 72nd National Film Awards in the categories of Best Film, Best Actress and Best Music.

The complete line-up also includes ‘Kindik (The Cord)’ (Kazakhstan), ‘Baracoa’ (Cuba and Italy), ‘Bo Bo’ (Russian Federation), ‘Safe Exit’ (Egypt, Germany, Libya, Qatar and Tunisia), ‘9 Temples to Heaven’ (Thailand, Singapore, France, Norway, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia and Qatar), ‘Cotton’ (Uzbekistan), ‘Baga: Tomorrow Belongs to No One’ (Malaysia), ‘1982’ (Vietnam), ‘And the Snow Was Falling’ (Belarus) and ‘Baab’ (United Arab Emirates).

Together, the 21 films offer audiences a cross-section of cinematic perspectives, with stories that move beyond national boundaries while engaging with shared questions of freedom, belonging, memory, resilience and change.

Scheduled from 20th-28th November 2026 across multiple venues in Goa, the 57th International Film Festival of India will showcase over 150 international films from 86 countries. The festival will bring together films across genres, countries and languages through its competitive and non-competitive sections, curated packages, retrospectives, tributes and thematic showcases, providing a platform for cross-cultural exchange and cinematic excellence.

2336214.title: PM to participate in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme on 15 November
2336214.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
PM to participate in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme on 15 November
Programme marks the 151st Birth Anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda
PM to inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of development projects worth around ₹3,000 crore
Projects aimed towards tribal empowerment with focus on strengthening education, healthcare, livelihoods, preservation of tribal heritage and community infrastructure
PM to also inaugurate Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Mizoram
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will participate in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra on 15th November 2026 at 11 AM via video conferencing. He will also address the gathering on the occasion of the 151st Birth Anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda.

During the programme, Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of 246 development projects worth around ₹3,000 crore. These projects are aimed at strengthening education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country.

Prime Minister will inaugurate 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for tribal students and 100 Multi-Purpose Centres under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), which will serve as hubs for service delivery and community activities. He will also inaugurate various other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA).

Other key projects to be inaugurated include the Tribal Research Institute (TRI) building at Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh, and the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum at Aizawl, Mizoram, aimed at preserving tribal culture and heritage. The museum commemorates the courage, valour and sacrifices of Mizo tribal freedom fighters, while showcasing the rich cultural traditions, historical legacy and heritage of the Mizo people. It is named after Ropuiliani, a nineteenth-century Mizo chieftainess who courageously resisted British colonial rule and is remembered as a symbol of tribal resistance and sacrifice.

Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of 19 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools, further strengthening the commitment to providing quality education to tribal children. He will also lay the foundation stone of 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs) to strengthen market access for tribal producers. In addition, Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stone for 42 other projects under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA.

The programme will mark the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, being observed across the country from 1st to 15th November 2026. During the Pakhwada, a range of national and grassroots-level programmes have been organised, including the President's interaction with EMRS students, the National Tribal Literary Festival, training programmes for tribal healers, health and nutrition camps for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), and community service drives in tribal villages under the Dharti Aaba Janbhagidari Abhiyan.

2336212.title: Indian Railways Approves Weekly Train Service Connecting Janakpur Dham in Nepal with Ayodhya in India
2336212.body_html:
Ministry of Railways
Indian Railways Approves Weekly Train Service Connecting Janakpur Dham in Nepal with Ayodhya in India
A Major Step Towards Strengthening Cross-border Connectivity, Religious Tourism and India-Nepal Friendship
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal connectivity, Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new weekly train service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, India.

The service will establish an important rail link between two destinations deeply associated with the Ramayana tradition – Janakpur Dham, revered as the birthplace of Mata Sita, and Ayodhya, the birthplace of Prabhu Shri Ram. The initiative will provide passengers from both countries with improved access to these prominent religious and cultural centres while reinforcing their shared civilizational heritage.

Connecting Key Destinations Across the Border

Covering approximately 604 kilometres, the weekly service will connect Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt., passing through several important towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.

The train will have commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations.

The service will operate once a week, with its originating days being Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya Cantt.

Boost to Tourism, Trade and Regional Development

The new service is expected to make cross-border travel more convenient for pilgrims, tourists and other passengers. It will facilitate religious journeys between Janakpur and Ayodhya, encourage tourism circuits associated with the Ramayana and provide greater mobility to people travelling for education, business and family-related purposes.

Improved rail access is also expected to benefit local economies along the route by creating opportunities for tourism operators, hospitality establishments, local traders and traditional artisans. For communities in the border regions of Bihar and Nepal, the service will offer an additional passenger transport option and strengthen economic and social linkages.

Strengthening India-Nepal Friendship

India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer.

Through this initiative, Indian Railways continues to expand passenger connectivity while supporting regional tourism, economic activity and the enduring friendship between the two neighbouring countries.

2336202.title: ‘I Matter’: A Powerful Story of Identity, Belonging and Second Chances to be Screened as Mid-Fest Film at IFFI 2026
2336202.body_html:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
‘I Matter’: A Powerful Story of Identity, Belonging and Second Chances to be Screened as Mid-Fest Film at IFFI 2026
Indian Premiere of Alina Șerban’s acclaimed film which won the Armani Beauty Audience Award at the Venice International Film Festival
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 3:44PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 14 November 2026

 

I Matter (Eu Contez), a multilingual drama written and directed by acclaimed filmmaker Alina Șerban, will have its Indian Premiere as the Mid-Fest film at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). A co-production of Romania, Germany and Belgium, the 101-minute film explores identity, family, belonging and the pursuit of a future beyond the circumstances of one's past. Featuring dialogues in Romanian and Romani, the film brings a distinctive European cinematic perspective to the festival.

The film follows Rebeca, a young Roma woman preparing to leave the orphanage she has called home. With her father's impending release from prison, she hopes to find the family she has always longed for and begin a new chapter in her life. Her admission to university to study acting brings fresh hope and the possibility of shaping her own future. However, as she navigates an unfamiliar world, unresolved experiences from her past resurface, confronting her with difficult choices.

Through Rebeca's journey, I Matter explores the emotional challenges of growing up without a stable family environment, the search for acceptance and the determination to find one's place in society. Set against the experiences of a young Roma woman, the film also engages with questions of social inclusion, dignity and individual freedom.

The film marks the feature-directorial debut of Alina Șerban, an accomplished actress and playwright. A graduate of the National University of Theatre and Film in Bucharest, she has also trained at the Tisch School of the Arts, New York University, and the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, London. Her earlier works include Alone at My Wedding, which premiered at the Cannes Film Festival, and Gipsy Queen, for which she received several Best Actress honours. She also appeared in Housekeeping for Beginners, screened at the Venice Film Festival.

I Matter premiered in the Venice Spotlight section of the 83rd Venice International Film Festival in September 2026, where it received the prestigious Armani Beauty Audience Award. The film stars Denisa Farcaș as Rebeca, alongside Sorin Mihai, Angelina Pavel, Vanessa Dancea, Raisa Mihai, Alexandru Stancu, Alina Berzunțeanu and Natalia Călin.

As the Mid-Fest presentation at IFFI 2026, I Matter will be screened simultaneously at 4:30 PM on November 24, 2026, at PVR INOX Panjim (Audi 1) and PVR INOX Porvorim (Audi 1). Director Alina Șerban and lead actress Denisa Farcaș will attend the festival as special guests. A red-carpet event featuring the film's guests is also scheduled at PVR INOX Panjim on the day of the screening.

Scheduled from November 20 to 28 across multiple venues in Goa, the 57th International Film Festival of India will showcase over 150 international films from 86 countries. The festival will bring together films across genres, countries and languages through its competitive and non-competitive sections, curated packages, retrospectives, tributes and thematic showcases, providing a platform for cross-cultural exchange and cinematic excellence.

2336206.title: First Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 concludes in Tiruchirappalli, emphasising sustainable drinking water services and community ownership
2336206.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
First Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 concludes in Tiruchirappalli, emphasising sustainable drinking water services and community ownership
Five teams, led by senior officials, including Secretary DDWS and AS&MD NJJM, visit water supply infrastructure and participate in Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations across five villages
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, today visited rural drinking water supply infrastructure and participated in the Jal Arpan Diwas celebration at Palamaneri Village in Tamil Nadu, as part of the second day of the Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 held at Tiruchirappalli. The visit began at the historic Grand Anicut (Kallanai) on the Cauvery River, followed by field visit of the riverbed collector wells and headworks at Vadugakudi. At Palamaneri Village, the Secretary joined the community in celebrating, Jal Arpan Diwas, the formal handover of drinking water infrastructure to the Gram Panchayat, participated in a plantation activity and interacted with VWSC members, who shared how household tap connections had improved their daily lives. Women from the Sujalam Shakti Group also demonstrated water quality testing using Field Test Kits.

Reflecting on these experiences while addressing the concluding session of the Conference, the Secretary emphasised that Jal Arpan should not be viewed merely as a ceremonial handover of infrastructure, but as the beginning of a sustained partnership between the State Government, implementing department and Gram Panchayat. He stressed that JJM 2.0 aims to move beyond providing household tap connections towards ensuring regular, reliable and safe drinking water services, with the long-term aspiration of 24×7 potable water supply directly from household taps. He also suggested that officials participating in Jal Arpan should drink water directly from village taps to strengthen community confidence in water quality.

The Secretary further emphasised that Gram Panchayats require continued technical support, handholding and capacity building to effectively manage drinking water services. He highlighted the importance of training elected Panchayat representatives and adapting training materials to local conditions. Referring to growing water stress, he urged States to utilise the Decision Support System (DSS) for planning rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and other source sustainability measures. Appreciating the Government of Tamil Nadu for successfully organising the Conference, he encouraged participating States to continue exchanging experiences and learning from one another.

Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), emphasised the importance of translating JJM 2.0 reforms into effective field-level implementation and strengthening coordination among concerned departments. During his visit to the village on the occasion of Jal Arpan Diwas, he personally drank water directly from a household tap, reinforcing community confidence in the quality and safety of the drinking water being supplied. He encouraged officials to adopt similar practices during field visits to build public trust in rural drinking water services. He further emphasised that Jal Arpan should be communicated as a step towards shared responsibility for sustainable water service delivery, rather than merely the handover of infrastructure. He also underscored the need to reassure Gram Panchayats of continued technical support from implementing departments, particularly for major repairs and infrastructure breakdowns, to strengthen their confidence in managing village water supply systems.

Shri D. Senthil Pandian, Joint Secretary, DDWS, while summarising the two-day Conference deliberations, highlighted the systematic follow-up undertaken after the Departmental Summit held in September 2026. He informed that specific action points, responsible stakeholders and timelines had been identified, followed by inter-ministerial consultations with the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Tribal Affairs and Rural Development to strengthen convergence in financing, skilling, tribal drinking water coverage and source sustainability. Elaborating on the reforms under JJM 2.0, he emphasised institutional accountability, formal handover of infrastructure to Gram Panchayats, effective implementation of O&M policies, capacity building of VWSCs, dedicated District Technical Units, water quality monitoring, digital mapping through Sujalam Bharat and source sustainability planning using DSS. He urged States to adhere to their committed reform timelines ahead of the proposed national-level review in February 2027, with five Regional Conferences planned as part of the structured review process.

Shri Hari Narayanan M., Director, NJJM, while proposing the Vote of Thanks, expressed gratitude to Secretary DDWS, Additional Secretary & Mission Director and Joint Secretary, NJJM, for their leadership and guidance. He appreciated the Government of Tamil Nadu, TWAD Board and other concerned departments for the excellent arrangements, and thanked participating States and Union Territories, Central Ministries, technical institutions, SPM-NIWAS and the NJJM team for their contributions towards making the Conference meaningful and productive.

Field Visits and Jal Arpan Diwas Celebrations

Earlier in the day, five teams led by senior officials, including Secretary DDWS, Additional Secretary & Mission Director NJJM, Joint Secretary DDWS, Director NJJM and Director SPM-NIWAS, along with representatives from participating States and Union Territories, visited rural drinking water supply infrastructure at Vadugakudi, Thiruchinampoondi, Thindukarai, Nochiyam and Keelaanbil headworks. The teams subsequently participated in Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations across five villages—Palamaneri, Ambedkar Nagar, Theeranmanagar, Ayyampalayam and Puthu Uthamanur, respectively, witnessing community participation and the formal handover of water supply infrastructure to Gram Panchayats.

 

The visits provided practical insights into source-to-tap drinking water infrastructure, including riverbed collector wells, pumping and distribution arrangements, and community-led operation and maintenance. Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations witnessed enthusiastic participation by Gram Panchayats, VWSC members, women's Self-Help Groups, schoolchildren and local communities. Activities included cultural performances, rangoli and painting competitions, demonstrations of water quality testing using Field Test Kits, community pledges, and the formal handing over of scheme documents and as-built drawings to Gram Panchayats.

During the subsequent debriefing session, representatives of all five teams shared their observations, highlighting innovative technical practices, women's participation in water quality surveillance, community ownership and the importance of sustainable O&M financing.


As part of the follow-up to the Departmental Summit held in September 2026 in the gracious presence of the Hon’ble Prime Minister, the first Regional Conference brought together seven participating States and Union Territories to exchange experiences, review progress on JJM 2.0 reforms and identify opportunities for convergence and collective action. On the first day, Shri C. R. Paatil, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, emphasised the need to accelerate the completion of remaining works and operationalise key structural reforms to ensure sustainable rural drinking water services. Deliberations involving Central Ministries, technical institutions and participating States/UTs focused on institutional strengthening, interdepartmental convergence, sustainable O&M financing, source sustainability, capacity building and Gram Panchayat-led water governance. The second day complemented these deliberations through field visits and Jal Arpan Diwas celebrations, providing practical insights into community ownership and sustainable management of rural drinking water systems. The outcomes of the Conference, combining policy deliberations with field-level learning, are expected to strengthen interstate cooperation, accelerate implementation of JJM 2.0 reforms and facilitate the transition from infrastructure creation to sustainable, community-managed and reliable rural drinking water services.

2336151.title: Consent Manager Registration Framework Comes into Effect; MeitY Secretary Launches Online Registration Portal
2336151.body_html:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
Consent Manager Registration Framework Comes into Effect; MeitY Secretary Launches Online Registration Portal
Eligible Indian Companies Can Now Apply For Registration As Consent Managers Through dpbi.gov.in; Minimum Net Worth
Requirement Set At ₹2 Crore
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 12:41PM by PIB Delhi

The registration framework for Consent Managers under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023, came into effect on 13 November 2026. As part of this phase of implementation, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), launched the online portal https://dpbi.gov.in to enable eligible companies to apply for registration as Consent Managers.

The framework marks an important step towards operationalising a system that enables Data Principals to exercise greater control over consent relating to their personal data. It forms part of the phased implementation of the DPDP framework and enables eligible entities to seek registration and prepare to offer consent management services.

Role and Accountability of Consent Managers

A Consent Manager is an entity registered with the Data Protection Board of India (Board) that enables Data Principals to give, manage, review and withdraw consent through an accessible, transparent and interoperable platform. The framework seeks to strengthen trust and accountability in the digital ecosystem, with Consent Managers being accountable to the Data Principals.

Eligibility and Registration Process

Companies incorporated in India with adequate technical, operational and financial capacity, including a net worth of not less than ₹2 crore, may seek registration as Consent Managers. These requirements are intended to ensure that registered entities have the resources and capabilities to provide secure, reliable and accountable services.

Eligible companies may apply to the Board for registration through the newly launched portal. The Board will assess applications against the applicable requirements and may register qualifying companies. The list of registered Consent Managers will be made publicly available on the Board’s website.

Other key provisions concerning the rights of Data Principals, the obligations of Data Fiduciaries, and the Board’s inquiry and penalty processes are scheduled to come into effect on 13 May 2027.

Further information on the DPDP Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025 is available on the Ministry’s website at https://www.meity.gov.in/. For related queries, the email address secretary[at]dpbi[dot]gov[dot]in may be contacted.

2336134.title: DRI seizes 10.8 kg amphetamine concealed in postal parcel from Europe foiling a syndicate's attempt to misuse legitimate postal trade channels
2336134.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 10.8 kg amphetamine concealed in postal parcel from Europe foiling a syndicate's attempt to misuse legitimate postal trade channels
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 11:34AM by PIB Delhi

Continuing its relentless vigilance across diverse trade streams, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has successfully intercepted a international drug smuggling attempt, seizing 10.8 kilogram amphetamine. The operation foiled a bid by a narcotics syndicate to exploit legitimate postal channels to smuggle contraband into India.

Acting on specific intelligence, DRI officers intercepted and examined a suspicious parcel at the Foreign Post Office, New Delhi, which had arrived from a European country and was declared to contain "Kleren" (clothes). While an initial inspection revealed standard household garments stuffed inside a shipping carton, a meticulous examination of the packaging uncovered an intricate concealment method: two plastic pouches were ingeniously concealed on each of four sides of the carton.

In total, officers recovered eight concealed packets containing a pink-coloured powdery substance, which tested positive for amphetamine. All eight packets of the suspected contraband have been seized under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, and further investigation is underway to trace the wider network behind the operation.

Through intelligence-led enforcement and heightened scrutiny of cross-border logistics, the DRI remains steadfast in its resolve to detect, disrupt, and dismantle illicit trafficking networks operating under the guise of legitimate trade. DRI remains committed towards safeguarding both India’s economic frontiers and national security.

2336127.title: Coordination between Industrial Development and Environmental Protection is the Foundation for Building a Developed India: Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh
2336127.body_html:
Ministry of Textiles
Coordination between Industrial Development and Environmental Protection is the Foundation for Building a Developed India: Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh
Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh Visits Welspun World’s State-of-the-Art Manufacturing Units in Kutch, Plants a sapling and Conveys the Message of Environmental Protection
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 11:01AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Textiles Giriraj Singh visited the state-of-the-art manufacturing complex of Welspun World located in Anjar, Kutch district, Gujarat. During the visit, the Union Minister observed the entire production process, from spinning to the manufacturing of towels and bedsheets. He expressed his satisfaction after witnessing the fully integrated value chain developed within a single campus, modern production technology and manufacturing facilities aligned with global quality standards.

The Union Minister of Textiles appreciated Welspun’s commitment to green manufacturing, water recycling and the conservation of natural resources in an arid region like Kutch. He said that this industrial complex, developed amidst greenery, brings the concept of ‘A Manufacturing Facility in a Garden’ to life. It is an excellent example of how industrial progress and environmental protection can go hand in hand.

On this occasion, Union Minister Giriraj Singh also planted a sapling on the premises and conveyed the message of environmental protection, conservation of natural resources and building a green future. He said that trees are an invaluable heritage of our planet. Their protection and preservation are the collective responsibility of all of us. Every section of society should play an active role in protecting nature.

He said that to realise Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a Developed India, environmental balance, sustainable manufacturing and the judicious use of natural resources are equally essential alongside modern industrial development. The Union Minister said that India’s textile industry is strengthening its global identity while setting new benchmarks for development by adopting sustainable and environmentally friendly manufacturing processes.
