2336126.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit Egypt from 15–16 November 2026
2336126.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Visit Egypt from 15–16 November 2026
Shri Piyush Goyal to Co-Chair 7th India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee Meeting
Business Forum to Strengthen Bilateral Trade and Investment Ties
Indian Business Leaders and Start ups to participate in the India–Egypt Business Forum
India Egypt Start up Forum to Explore New Trade, Investment and Joint Venture Opportunities
Large business delegation comprising 130+ business leaders and Start-ups to accompany Commerce and Industry Ministry
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 10:54AM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will undertake an official visit to the Arab Republic of Egypt from 15 to 16 November 2026. The visit aims to further strengthen the longstanding India–Egypt partnership, with particular emphasis on expanding bilateral trade, promoting investment, enhancing industrial cooperation and strengthening business-to-business engagement.

India and Egypt share longstanding historical, civilizational and people-to-people ties, which have evolved into a multifaceted partnership encompassing political, economic, security and cultural cooperation. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India–Egypt relations have gained renewed momentum, culminating in the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership, with a shared commitment to enhanced cooperation, including in the economic field.

The visit will comprise the 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC), the India–Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC) Meeting and the India–Egypt Business Forum. The programme will also include bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers, interactions with leading business representatives and meetings with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), the Egyptian Junior Businessmen Association and the Egypt–India Startups Forum. These engagements are expected to provide fresh impetus to bilateral trade, investment, industrial cooperation and innovation linkages.

The 7th Session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) will be co-chaired by Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh on 15 November 2026 in Cairo.

The JTC has been elevated to the Ministerial level, reflecting the importance both countries attach to strengthening their economic and commercial partnership. The meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket. Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics, among other areas of mutual interest.

Bilateral merchandise trade during April–September 2026 stood at USD 5.04 billion, registering a growth of 64 per cent over the corresponding period of the previous year. India's exports to Egypt during FY 2025–26 amounted to USD 3.87 billion, while imports from Egypt stood at USD 2.60 billion. India's major exports to Egypt include meat and poultry products, petroleum products, organic chemicals, cotton and machinery, while its major imports include crude petroleum, fertilisers, cotton and mineral products. (Source: DGCIS)

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships. Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions. Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 130 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors will participate in the India–Egypt Joint Business Council Meeting and the India–Egypt Business Forum. The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

The visit reflects India's continued commitment to strengthening its economic engagement with Egypt, an important partner in North Africa and a strategic gateway to regional markets. Both countries have significant opportunities to expand cooperation in manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, automobiles, textiles, chemicals, engineering goods, food processing, renewable energy, logistics and emerging technologies. The visit is expected to provide fresh momentum to the India–Egypt economic partnership, strengthen institutional cooperation and create new opportunities for Indian and Egyptian businesses.

2336101.title: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission
2336101.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission
Unlocking India’s Tribal Forest Economy
Posted On: 14 NOV 2026 8:55AM by PIB Delhi

Many of India’s 10.4 crore Scheduled Tribes derive 20–40% of their annual income from Minor Forest Produce (MFP). Historically, tribals sold this produce to middlemen at distress prices, earning below the cost of their own labour. To address this, the government runs the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM). The mission organises tribals into community-owned Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), moving them from raw produce sellers to value-adding entrepreneurs. As of March 2026, 4,172 VDVKs have been sanctioned covering 12.48 lakh beneficiaries. The government also buys MFP at a pre-determined Minimum Support Price (MSP). PMJVM provides enterprise funding and helps tribals access markets through fairs, e-commerce platforms, and exhibitions.

Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is observing Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada across the country from 1 to 15 November 2026, culminating in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas on 15 November, the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The Government of India designated 15 November as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas in 2021. The Pakhwada is a focused, time-bound drive to accelerate the Ministry’s flagship programmes and take their benefits to tribal families at the last mile. On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, over 300 projects for tribal communities across States will be taken up, with 228 ready for inauguration and 74 for foundation stone laying. Two national digital initiatives, the Jan-HIT Portal and the National FRA Digital Platform, will also be launched. Tribal Research Institutes have planned more than 160 activities in 19 States/UTs.

Click to Read More: Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026: Nationwide Celebrations to Honour Tribal Heritage, Empower Communities and Accelerate Last-Mile Delivery of Welfare Schemes

Protecting Tribal Forest Economies

For millions of forest-dwelling tribal families, Minor Forest Produce (MFP)—such as honey, tendu leaves, mahua flowers, tamarind, lac, bamboo and wild herbs—is not merely a forest resource. It is a primary source of livelihood. About 20% to 40% of their annual income is from selling MFP. Yet, despite directly procuring and selling MFP, tribals receive only a fraction of its market value. This is because they often sell MFP to intermediaries at low prices.

The Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) seeks to change this equation. Launched in 2021-22, the Mission provides a systematic way for them to improve MFP’s value by skilling the tribals in newer technology and practices. The scheme links the communities to the larger national and digital markets to help them get more exposure and sell more products. It also guarantees Minimum Support Prices (MSP) to tribals by directly procuring the produce from them.

These efforts are helping forest gatherers become owners of their community enterprises while strengthening India’s tribal economy at the grassroots level.

Minor Forest Products & Minimum Support Price

While the government manages most of India’s forests to preserve ecology and wildlife, tribals and other traditional forest-dwelling communities are given access to these areas for the preservation of their livelihoods.

 

In 2006, the government enacted the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act — also called the Forest Rights Act. The Act defines minor forest produce as “all non-timber forest produce of plant origin including bamboo, brush wood, stumps, cane, tussar, cocoons, honey, wax, lac, tendu or kendu leaves, medicinal plants and herbs, roots, tubers and the like.” The government has notified Minimum Support Price for 87 MFP items under PMJVM.  

The Forest Rights Act recognises that forest-dwelling communities have historically depended on forest products for sustenance and livelihood. The Act gives tribals rights to procure and sell non-timber minor forest produce. Separately, the Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act (1996) grants tribal Gram Panchayats ownership rights over minor forest produce.

The Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED), mandated with the marketing and development of tribal products, purchases non-timber forest produce at the pre-determined price (MSP) regardless of the market price of the product. It does so through a network of state implementing agencies — including tribal development cooperatives and forest development corporations. Since 2013–14, state governments have procured 2,67,954 metric tonnes of MFPs worth Rs. 693.98 crore under the scheme.

How Does PMJVM Support Tribals?

Beyond MSP procurement, the PVJM scheme also provides skilling, technological, marketing, and infrastructural support to tribals.

Organising Tribals into Van Dhan Vikas Kendras

The Mission mobilises tribal gatherers into self-help groups (SHGs). A group of 15 SHGs, comprising about 300 tribals, are clustered together into one Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK). At least 60% of VDVK members must be from Scheduled Tribe communities.

The Van Dhan Yojana, launched on April 14, 2018, is a part of PMJVM. It forms the foundation of the VDVK model and powers its implementation across tribal communities.

Skilling, Funding and Technological Support

The Government organises skilling and other training programmes for MFP gatherers, including trainings on scientific harvesting practices, at Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs).

The SHGs are also provided with:

  • Infrastructural support, established in a beneficiary’s home or a government or gram panchayat building
  • Primary processing equipment — cutting and sieving tools, decorticators, dryers, and packaging tools — based on locally available MFPs
  • Training for 30 members on sustainable harvesting and value addition, with raw materials and trainee kits provided
  • Working capital, facilitated through tie-ups with financial institutions, banks, and the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC)
  • Storage and transportation support on a rental basis.

Marketing and Business Support

Apart from value addition, VDVKs are also centres for market linkages – both local and distant – for the final products.

  • VDVKs are established around local Haat Bazaars, the primary MFP procurement points, to make it easier for tribals to sell products they produce.
    • There are over 5,000 Haats in tribal areas.
    • Haats are being modernised in a phased manner— with permanent structures, storage, drinking water, shade, and weighing equipment.
  • VDVKs may partner with private entities or non-profits for value addition or marketing of their products.
  • TRIFED disseminates market intelligence — including daily rates and e-commerce avenues —to VDVKs to improve their decision-making on business deals.
  • PMJVM also provides:
    • Branding, promotion, and advertisement of tribal products through festivals, exhibitions, and artisan melas
    • Geo-tagging of VDVKs and other scheme assets
    • Geographical Indicators for tribal produce (GI is a sign used on products that have a specific geographical origin and possess qualities or a reputation that are due to that origin)
    • Building and upgrading IT and e-commerce platforms
    • Research and development support

Under the PMJVM scheme:

  • 4,172 VDVKs have been sanctioned and 2,911 VDVKs are functional, with reported sales of around Rs. 168 crores (as on July 31, 2026).
  • 12.48 lakh tribal members have been linked to the VDVKs.

VDVKs Help in Tribal Women Empowerment

Most collections and sales are carried out by women, making PMJVM a key instrument of tribal women’s financial empowerment.

The Nyigamane, Ho Yorbe, Medumhagdum VDVK in Arunachal Pradesh’s Leparada district was established in October 2021 with 300 women SHG members and farmers. This VDVK converts locally available non-timber forest and agricultural produce into processed, marketable goods. The products created are:

  • King Chilli Pickle from King Chillis (Bhut Jolokia — a north eastern Indian specialty)
  • Bamboo Shoot Pickle from bamboo shoots (a common MFP in north-eastern India)
  • Turmeric Powder from locally grown turmeric
  • Ginger Powder from locally grown ginger
  • Pineapple Jam from Pineapples (abundant in Arunachal Pradesh)
  • Pineapple Squash from Pineapples
  • Orange Squash from Oranges

The VDVK has sold Rs. 11 lakh worth of these products from 2022-23 onwards. It has empowered the women, who no longer need to depend on only seasonable agriculture for income throughout the year. The women jointly own the business – they are not mere workers but also have a stake in the brand and the enterprise.

 

Towards A Sustainable Forest Economy

Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM) provides livelihood opportunities to forest-dwelling tribals, offering a systematic way to produce and market non-timber forest produce. These products are locally sourced and rooted in traditional practices — representing a forest-based economy balancing community ownership with market competitiveness.

In a world increasingly driven by mass-manufactured and plastic-packaged goods, they are India’s distinctive offering: natural, community-owned, and forest-born. PMJVM embodies Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikaas- ensuring India’s growth story reaches its most remote forests and the communities who call them home. This will eventually contribute to India’s vision of a Viksit Bharat@2047.

2336069.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal inaugurates 45th India International Trade Fair 2026
2336069.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal inaugurates 45th India International Trade Fair 2026
IITF has emerged as a platform that brings together India’s states, businesses, products and capabilities: Shri Goyal
30 States and Union Territories showcasing their strengths, 3,500 exhibitors and participation from 11 countries at 45th IITF
India records all-time high exports of almost $90 billion in October 2026 showing strong resilience and growth: Shri Goyal
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 9:44PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today inaugurated the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, calling upon Indian businesses, manufacturers, exporters, artisans and entrepreneurs to leverage the opportunities created by India's Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and expand their presence in international markets. He emphasised that with markets across the developed world opening up for Indian goods and services, businesses must seize these opportunities and contribute to India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Goyal highlighted that India had recorded an all-time high in exports of nearly $90 billion in October 2026, comprising approximately $50 billion in merchandise exports and $40 billion in services exports. Describing this as a historic milestone, he said that India was well on track to achieve its $1 trillion export target in the current year. Exports during the first seven months up to October had reached $570 billion, an unprecedented achievement.

The Minister expressed confidence that India's international trade would grow by 15-16 per cent during the current year, despite two ongoing wars, global volatility and uncertainty, and subdued international trade growth, which is expected to remain around 3.5 per cent. He said India's performance reflected the strength of its economy, the confidence of its exporters and the country's ability to face global challenges with determination and self-respect.

Shri Goyal said that the 45th edition of IITF reflected five dimensions of Bharat: its economy, exports, infrastructure growth, the demand generated by 1.4 billion Indians and the country's rich diversity. He observed that the fair had evolved beyond an event focused largely on Delhi and had emerged as a platform bringing together India's states, businesses, products and capabilities.

Highlighting the new initiatives introduced at this year's fair, the Minister said that more than 30 States and Union Territories were showcasing their strengths, with over 3,500 exhibitors and participation from 11 countries. The One District, One Product Pavilion initiative, would showcase products from different parts of the country, highlighting India's strengths in arts, handicrafts, handloom and food products.

Another major attraction, the Hall of Inspiration, will showcase 600 startups and their innovations. The IITF mobile application will provide visitors with information about the entire fair, enabling them to navigate the exhibition and identify exhibitors of interest. Shri Goyal noted that visitors would need to set aside two to three days to explore the entire exhibition, given its extensive spread across Bharat Mandapam.

The Minister also announced that the Government would soon launch the next phase of expansion of Bharat Mandapam, which would almost double the available exhibition space for exhibitors. He said that the success of recent exhibitions, including IITF, had demonstrated that even the significantly expanded facilities available today were no longer adequate to meet growing demand.

Shri Goyal said that IITF would now be taken across the world, with the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) planning several international fairs, both sector-specific and multi-dimensional. These fairs would provide Indian goods, services and startups opportunities to showcase their capabilities and engage with markets in developed countries and other international markets, particularly those with which India has entered into Free Trade Agreements. He called upon businesses and exhibitors to actively participate in these initiatives and contribute to India's global engagement.

Emphasising the importance of quality and sustainability, the Minister said that India's focus must remain on two key elements: quality and sustainability. Adopting the principle of Zero Defect, Zero Effect would help ensure equitable and inclusive growth across the country. He said every Made-in-India product must reflect high quality and reinforce India's reputation in international markets.

He further stressed the need to adopt high-quality standards in manufacturing and services while embracing sustainable practices, promoting a circular economy, using natural products and giving greater importance to biodegradable products. He said that ensuring economic growth without damaging the environment would position India as a global winner in the race to capture international markets and improve the prosperity of its people.

Highlighting the growing strength of India's domestic economy, Shri Goyal referred to the strong business activity witnessed during the recent festive season, including Diwali, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj, as well as Navratri, Dussehra and Dhanteras. He said that stores across the country had witnessed significant consumer demand and business activity had been considerably higher. The October GST collections had already registered an all-time high for the month, and he expressed confidence that November would also witness record collections.

The Minister said that these developments reflected the strength of India's growth story, with every section of the economy contributing to the country's progress. Farmers, fishermen, workers, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), manufacturers, service providers, artists, artisans and handloom and handicraft producers were all demonstrating growth and confidence. From neighbourhood kirana stores and e-commerce businesses to artisans and major brands, every segment was looking to benefit from the expanding economic opportunities.

He observed that India's young entrepreneurs and businesses were increasingly reaching out to global markets, expanding production and looking towards a brighter future. Citing examples of emerging export opportunities, he referred to the export of Kiwi from Arunachal Pradesh, where exports had earlier been negligible, and Sindhuri pomegranates from Kullu reaching Dubai. He urged exhibitors and businesses at IITF to identify products with export potential and take advantage of the opportunities available through India's FTAs, emphasising that international markets were now open and Indian businesses must take the initiative to access them.

Shri Goyal said that India's growth was being powered by a young population aspiring for a better quality of life, improved education and healthcare, and greater opportunities to develop skills and talent. He noted that India had, in a span of 12 years, brought nearly 50 crore people, or 500 million people, out of extreme poverty. This had created a sense of achievement as well as aspirations for a brighter future among people across the country.

He said India was confidently facing global adversities, remaining focused on commerce, economic growth and the well-being of its people, irrespective of conflicts and uncertainties around the world. He attributed this confidence to decisive leadership and the country's growing economic strength.

Referring to India's long-term economic ambitions, the Minister said that the country's current four trillion dollar economy aspired to become a $30 trillion economy by 2047, when India would celebrate 100 years of Independence. He said that the country's young population, expanding businesses and growing export capabilities would play an important role in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.

The Minister also underlined the importance of preserving India's heritage and traditions while pursuing development. He said that the theme of this year's IITF aptly reflected the India story, as development remained incomplete without respect for heritage. Referring to the experience of developed nations, he observed that countries which had achieved prosperity had also protected, encouraged and promoted their traditions, heritage and culture.

The Minister also referred to the recently approved establishment of the world's largest museum, the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, in the North Block and South Block complex. He said that  Honourable Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi recognised the importance of presenting India's diversity, long history, contributions to the world over several thousand years, rich cultural heritage and traditions to the global community. Referring to the fact that India had once contributed more than 30 per cent to the global economy, Shri Goyal said that understanding and recognising the country's past was essential to reclaiming its rightful position in the comity of nations and realising the vision of a developed India.

He expressed confidence that the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, being developed at the North Block and South Block complex, would showcase India's history, traditions and contributions to the world and serve as a source of inspiration for future generations, particularly the country's youth.

Shri Goyal said that the 45th IITF had moved beyond incremental improvements and taken a significant leap towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. He expressed confidence that the fair would become a trendsetter and mark the beginning of a new era in how India presented itself to the world and engaged with international markets to promote Indian goods, services, arts and culture.

He said that initiatives led by ITPO and the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, in coordination with State Governments and other Central Government Ministries through a whole-of-government approach, would create greater opportunities for Indian businesses and entrepreneurs across the world.

Concluding his address, Shri Goyal declared the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 open and called upon all stakeholders to actively contribute to India's journey of economic progress and global engagement.

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Garima Singh/ Ishita Biswas

2336057.title: Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Results Announcement
2336057.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Results Announcement
Dept. of Urban Development, MoHUA Announces Swachh Shehar Jodi Results
Cities recognized for exemplary peer learning, collaboration and replication of best practices as part of Swachh Shehar Jodi under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 9:24PM by PIB Delhi

President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu honoured India’s cleanest cities at the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 Award Ceremony in New Delhi for the 10th edition of the world’s largest urban sanitation survey - Swachh Survekshan held on 11th November 2026. The theme for SS 2025-26 is Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel- Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath (स्वच्छता की नई पहल बढाएं हाथ, करें सफाई साथ). All SS 2025-26 award winners were felicitated in the presence of Sh. Manohar Lal, Union Minister for MoHUA & Power and Shri Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for MoHUA.

As part of the 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan, 4,751 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) were assessed across 176 sub-indicators in 10 sections. Over 3,000 trained field assessors from across the country conducted on-ground surveys covering all ULBs, supported by real-time, GPS-enabled monitoring. The entire process, from evidence submission to verification, is digital, transparent, and rigorously quality-checked at all stages.

This year 60 national awards were announced under 7 categories:

    • Top 3 Swachh Shehar Jodi (SSJ)

    • Top 3 Clean Cities (this category excludes award-winning cities in Swachh Shehar Jodi)

    • Swachh Shehar Rank 1, 2, 3 in 5 population categories

    • Swachh River Front Town Rank 1, 2, 3

    • Swachh Coastal Town Rank 1, 2, 3

    • Clean Himalayan City Rank 1, 2, 3

    • State/UT First Swachh City

On 11th November 2026, MoHUA announced the top three performing city pairs under the 'Swachh Shehar Jodi' initiative, a flagship peer-learning programme under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U) 2.0. Swachh Shehar Jodi was launched by the Hon’ble Union Minster, Shri Manohar Lal on 27th September 2025 as the first-ever urban waste management mentorship initiative involving 70 high-performing mentor cities and around 191 mentee cities from 33 States/UTs, based on Swachh Survekshan 2024-25 rankings. A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between the mentor and mentee cities in a national event at Sonipat in September 2025.

Of the 191 Jodis announced by the Ministry, only the best-performing Jodi of each mentor city was considered.

The SSJ initiative promotes the principle of Each One - Teach One and is rooted in India’s timeless Guru–Shishya tradition, where knowledge, experience, and best practices are passed on from one city to another to collectively advance  the  journey  towards urban excellence and cleanliness.

The Top 3 award winning Swachh Shehar city Jodis have been identified based on their combined total scores as Mentor and Mentee cities. The aggregate score reflects the joint performance and collaborative efforts of both cities under the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative, thereby recognizing mentorship outcomes along with overall cleanliness and service delivery improvements.

The Top 3 ‘Swachh Shehar Jodi’ Initiative Award winners are:

  • Swachh Shehar Jodi Rank 1: Ahmedabad (Million Plus Population Category) and

2336047.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales of Over ₹ 88.36 Lakh, as of November 12, 2026; Highlighting Appreciation for Traditional Handicrafts, Indigenous Products And Growing Market Opportunities for Artisans
2336047.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales of Over ₹ 88.36 Lakh, as of November 12, 2026; Highlighting Appreciation for Traditional Handicrafts, Indigenous Products And Growing Market Opportunities for Artisans
More Than 130 Stalls Across Seven Thematic Zones Showcase India's Rich Handloom, Handicraft and Cultural Heritage
Daily Cultural Performances Featuring Folk Dances, Traditional Music and Regional Art Forms Continue to Enthral Visitors
Mela to Continue Until November 15, Providing Artisans with Opportunities for Direct Consumer Engagement and Livelihood Promotion
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi

The ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA, in the National Capital here, continues to witness an encouraging response from visitors, with cumulative sales reaching ₹88,36,416 (approximately ₹88.36 lakh) as of November 12, 2026.

The impressive sales performance reflects growing public appreciation for traditional handicrafts, handloom products and indigenous creations, while highlighting the Mela's role in providing meaningful market opportunities to artisans and entrepreneurs from beneficiary communities.

The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will continue at Dilli Haat, INA, until November 15, 2026, offering visitors further opportunities to explore India's diverse handicraft traditions, interact with artisans and enjoy cultural performances.

Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, the 15-day Mela has emerged as a vibrant platform celebrating India's rich cultural heritage, artistic excellence and traditional craftsmanship.

The event continues to attract families, young visitors, art enthusiasts and shoppers, offering them an opportunity to explore authentic handmade products while directly supporting the livelihoods of participating artisans.

A senior official of the Ministry said that the four participating National Corporations under the Ministry have collectively recorded sales of ₹88,36,416 up to November 12, 2026.

The encouraging sales figures underline the growing consumer interest in indigenous products and the importance of creating accessible marketing platforms for artisans belonging to socially and economically disadvantaged communities, he said.

The Official said the four participating corporations include the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC).

He said the Mela features more than 130 stalls, showcasing a diverse collection of traditional handicrafts, handloom textiles, ethnic garments, decorative items, handmade accessories, lamps, home décor products and other indigenous creations.

Visitors are actively engaging with artisans, exploring traditional craftsmanship and purchasing products representing the distinctive cultural identities of different regions of the country, he further said.

The Official said the Mela has been organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, and designed around seven thematic zones — कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच.

These zones bring together diverse elements of India's artistic and cultural traditions, offering visitors an immersive experience encompassing traditional crafts, festive decorations, regional culinary traditions and cultural performances, he said.

The Official said beyond its commercial significance, the Mela continues to provide a lively cultural experience through evening programmes featuring traditional music, folk dances and regional performances by artists from different States.

The cultural activities organised at the Manch have become a major attraction, drawing enthusiastic audiences and creating an atmosphere of celebration, cultural exchange and national unity, the Official added.

The Official said the performances highlight India's diverse artistic expressions and provide visitors with an opportunity to experience the richness of regional traditions.

The combination of traditional shopping experiences and cultural entertainment has transformed the Mela into a vibrant destination for families and visitors from different walks of life, he added.

The Official noted the Shilp Samagam Mela also serves as an important initiative for promoting inclusive entrepreneurship and socio-economic empowerment.

It provides artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamchari communities and persons with disabilities with opportunities to showcase their skills, establish direct connections with consumers and expand their market reach, he said.

To facilitate wider participation, the Ministry provides support in the form of free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for goods, the Official said.

These measures help reduce financial and logistical barriers, enabling participating artisans to concentrate on promoting their products, strengthening their enterprises and improving their livelihood opportunities, the Official remarked.

The Official said the growing sales and sustained public participation at the ongoing Mela demonstrate the significance of institutional support in connecting traditional artisans with wider consumer markets.

Such initiatives contribute to preserving indigenous craftsmanship while creating opportunities for economic independence, enterprise development and sustainable livelihoods, he added.

He said the initiative further complements efforts to promote market accessibility through platforms such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce opportunities, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity, capabilities and contributions of persons with disabilities while encouraging greater inclusion and equal opportunities.

The Official said since 2022, the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas to strengthen livelihood opportunities for artisans from beneficiary communities.

These initiatives have benefited more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karmachari communities by providing platforms for exhibiting and marketing their products, promoting self-employment and encouraging entrepreneurship, he added.

Through its emphasis on traditional craftsmanship, inclusive market access, cultural celebration and livelihood promotion, Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 continues to advance the Ministry's commitment to socio-economic empowerment and the vision of an inclusive, self-reliant and Viksit Bharat.

2336039.title: Launch of Web-Portal for Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration 2026
2336039.ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
2336039.body_html:
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
Launch of Web-Portal for Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration 2026
For the year 2026, the scheme for Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration aims to recognize the contribution of civil servants under three categories through 16 Awards.
Category and Awards Details: Category -1- Holistic Development of Districts under 12 priority sector programmes (05 awards); Category 2: Aspirational Blocks Programme (05 awards); Category 3: Innovations for Central Ministries/Departments, States/UTs and Districts (06 awards).
Under Holistic Development of Districts category, 9 new schemes added for the assessment of the Districts
The Central Ministries/Departments and the State/UT governments and the Districts will participate in their respective Innovation Category
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 9:06PM by PIB Delhi

The Web-Portal (https://pmawards.gov.in/) for the Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration 2026 was officially launched to begin the registration process on 13th November 2026 by the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances. The launch ceremony, was conducted via video conferencing, and was attended by officials from Ministries/Departments of Government of India, Principal Secretaries (Administrative Reforms) of States and Union Territories and District Collectors/District Magistrates (DCs/DMs). The session was attended by more than 2000 officers from across 750 different locations.

The total number of Awards under the Prime Minister’s Awards for Excellence in Public Administration 2026 would be 16. The Period of consideration is 1st April, 2024 to 30th November, 2026.  

The Holistic Development of Districts category has been revamped comprehensively. For PMA 2026, the 9 newly added schemes are- SBM (Urban) and AMRUT, Gyan Bharatam, PM Matsya Sampada Yojana, TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, Crop Diversification under three components, PM SHRI, Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), National Mission on Natural Farming and Capacity Building under IGOT. The 3 schemes from PMA 2025 that have been continued for PMA 2026 include Har Ghar Jal Yojana, PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0.

The schemes approved under Prime Minister’s Awards 2026 will also continue for the Prime Minister’s Awards 2027.

Districts with Aspirational Blocks will participate in Aspirational Blocks Programme category covering 513 Aspirational Blocks, across 331 districts of India.

The Ministries were requested to submit their Quantitative, Qualitative, and Governance parameters to DARPG by November 17, 2026 to facilitate the formulation and uploading of the application form on the PM Awards portal to be submitted by the Districts.

The Prime Minister’s Awards, 2026 will consist of: (i) Trophy, (ii) Scroll and (iii) an incentive of Rs. 20 lakhs to the awarded District/organization to be utilized for implementation of project/programme or bridging resources gaps in any area of public welfare.

2336031.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister condoles the loss of lives in the mishap in Golaghat district of Assam
PM announces ex-gratia from PMNRF
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 8:41PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has expressed deep anguish over the loss of lives in the mishap in the Golaghat district of Assam. Extending his condolences to the bereaved families in this hour of grief, he prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured.

The Prime Minister has announced an ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives, while the injured would be given Rs. 50,000.

The Prime Minister's Office posted on X:

"Deeply anguished by the loss of lives in the mishap in Golaghat district of Assam. I extend my condolences to the bereaved families in this hour of grief. Praying for the speedy recovery of the injured.

An ex-gratia of Rs. 2 lakh from PMNRF would be given to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. The injured would be given Rs. 50,000: PM @narendramodi"

2336026.title: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Takes Swachhata Beyond Office Walls as Special Campaign 6.0 Concludes
2336026.body_html:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Takes Swachhata Beyond Office Walls as Special Campaign 6.0 Concludes
Clean neighbourhoods, innovative e-waste reuse and greener workplaces mark the campaign
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 8:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), along with its organisations, undertook a series of initiatives during Special Campaign 6.0 (2–31 October 2026), focusing on cleanliness, pendency reduction, record management and environmental sustainability across its offices and field establishments.

The campaign covered 142 locations, resulting in the reclamation of 1,500 sq. ft. of space and generation of ₹2,47,156 through the disposal of scrap and obsolete items, including e-waste. Beyond office premises, the campaign also promoted cleanliness in public spaces, community participation and innovative approaches to e-waste reuse. The campaign also recorded significant progress in reducing pendency and improving record management, with the following key outcomes:

Campaign Scorecard

The Ministry undertook cleanliness drives at 142 locations, resulting in the reclamation of 1,500 sq. ft. of office space and generation of revenue amounting to ₹2,47,156 through the disposal of scrap and obsolete items, including e-waste. Significant achievements were also recorded in pendency reduction and records management, including:

  • Disposal of 11 PMO references, 29 references received from Members of Parliament and 2 Parliamentary Assurances.
  • Redressal of 1,973 public grievances and 84 grievance appeals.
  • Review of 2,924 physical files, of which 233 files were weeded out.
  •  Review of 355 e-files, of which 87 e-files were closed.

Swachhata Pledge and Public Participation

The campaign commenced with a Swachhata pledge administered to around 250 officials of the Ministry and its field offices, building on the momentum of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 (17th September–2nd October). Citizens were also encouraged to take the online pledge through the Ministry's website: https://dashboard.msme.gov.in/events/pledge.aspx.

Cleaning the Neighbourhood: Swachhata Beyond Office Premises

Extending cleanliness drives to public spaces, NSIC's Head Office team, along with Safai Mitras, undertook cleaning activities at nearby public places including metro stations, parks etc. Shopkeepers, students and residents were sensitised about waste segregation and keeping public spaces clean.

At Rajajinagar Industrial Area, Bengaluru, NSIC's Branch Office and local volunteers cleared litter, cleaned public walkways and segregated biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste. Neighbouring industrialists were also sensitised about sustainable waste management.

Before: litter heap at Rajajinagar, Bengaluru

After: the same stretch, cleared

 

Similarly, MGIRI organised a cleanliness drive at the river ghat in Yelakeli village, Wardha district, Maharashtra, on 13th October 2026.

 

Before Dirty river ghat Wardha, Maharashtra

After: the same ghat, cleaned

From E-Waste to a Working Charkha

MGIRI, Wardha, demonstrated the potential of e-waste reuse by developing a functional Charkha almost entirely from discarded electronic components. Motherboards, PCB strips, pulleys from old DVD drives, bearings and other discarded components were repurposed to create the working model. The initiative exemplifies the principles of Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, showcasing innovation in converting electronic waste into useful products.

Greener and More Welcoming Workplaces

The Ministry introduced greenery across its office workspaces by placing potted plants along workstation partitions, creating a fresher and more welcoming environment.

Potted plants along the workstations, M/o MSME office

NSIC’s Branch Office at Naini developed a Swachhata Selfie Point by creatively shaping its garden lawn into the letters “N S I C”. The initiative was executed in-house at zero cost, without the use of plastic or flex materials, presenting a simple, sustainable and replicable model for other offices. Additionally, NSIC Head Office enhanced its reception areas by incorporating greenery, further promoting a clean, green and welcoming workplace environment.

Taking Swachhata to Villages, Schools and Communities

Citizen engagement remained an important component of the campaign. On 6th October, MGIRI organised a Swachhata and hygiene awareness programme involving staff and villagers at Go-Vigyan Anusandhan Kendra, Devlapar.

Similarly, KVIC engaged with students and local communities through awareness programmes. On 5th October, it organised a seminar, debate and essay competition for over 100 students at Nandkishore Kailash Chandra Mahavidyalaya, Sitapur, Uttar Pradesh, along with Charkha and pottery-wheel demonstrations. Swachhata pledges were also administered at schools and colleges, during a PMEGP awareness camp in Ooty and at Mohamed Sathak College, Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu.

Pledge in a school assembly

Awareness and Capacity Building

Standees and banners were displayed across offices to spread awareness about the campaign among officials and visitors. Ministry officials were also encouraged to undertake identified courses on e-waste management and record management through the i-GOT Karmayogi platform.

Sustaining the Momentum

Special Campaign 6.0 reaffirmed the significance of collective participation in promoting cleanliness, sustainability and environmental responsibility. The Ministry of MSME remains committed to institutionalising these initiatives through regular cleanliness drives, expeditious disposal of pending matters, effective records management and scientific disposal of e-waste. These sustained efforts aim to foster cleaner, greener and more efficient workplaces across the MSME ecosystem.

***

2336006.title: From Financial Hardship to Academic Excellence NFSC Fellowship Empowers a Research Scholar
2336006.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Financial Hardship to Academic Excellence NFSC Fellowship Empowers a Research Scholar
National Fellowship For Scheduled Caste Students Enables A Scholar To Complete PhD In Anthropology, Works As Assistant Professor At Utkal University, Bhubaneswar
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 7:54PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of Mr. Arjun Naik (name changed) from Narasinghpur, Cuttack district, Odisha reflects the role of targeted financial assistance through the NFSC in helping scholars overcome economic and social barriers to higher education.

Through the NFSC, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to support educational advancement and create opportunities for Scheduled Caste students to pursue their academic aspirations.

Access to quality higher education and research opportunities can open pathways to academic achievement, professional growth and social contribution. The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC), provides financial support to eligible scholars pursuing advanced studies and research.

Despite financial hardship and social challenges, he aspired to pursue higher education, build a career in research and teaching, and contribute to society through Anthropology.

Limited economic resources, lack of academic exposure and social marginalisation had created barriers to accessing quality higher education and research opportunities. These challenges also made it difficult to meet academic expenses and sustain research activities.

In 2017, Arjun began receiving assistance under the National Fellowship (SC). The support included a fellowship of ₹16,000 per month, along with House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency assistance. It helped meet his academic expenses, fieldwork requirements and research-related costs, reducing financial stress and enabling him to focus on his higher studies.

 

The fellowship addressed key barriers relating to financial resources, access to educational facilities, research expenses and academic continuity. It also enabled greater participation in academic activities and supported his research and professional development.

With the support of the fellowship and his continued efforts, Arjun successfully completed his Ph.D. in Anthropology. He is currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at Utkal University, Bhubaneswar, where he is engaged in teaching, research and mentoring students.

His academic progress has translated into professional advancement and improved economic circumstances for his family. The fellowship also strengthened his confidence and enabled him to contribute to academic and social development through his work at the university.

Through the NFSC, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to support educational advancement and create opportunities for Scheduled Caste students to pursue their academic aspirations.

2336005.title: ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Records Participation of 28,876 Citizens
2336005.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ Records Participation of 28,876 Citizens
Quiz to Remain Open for Participation Until November 25, 2026
Campaign Reaches Over 35.89 Crore People, Including 14.36 Crore Youth and 11.34 Crore Women
Over 34.08 Lakh Activities Conducted in Educational Institutions; 39.91 Lakh Persons Treated and Rehabilitated; More Than 755 DoSJE-Supported De-addiction Centres Working Across the Country
Over 48.21 Lakh Nasha Mukt Pledges Taken; More Than 2 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras Registered
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 7:50PM by PIB Delhi

 

The online ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ has witnessed an encouraging response, with total participation reaching 28,876 citizens as of November 13, 2026. The growing participation reflects increasing public engagement, particularly among young people, in the collective endeavour of building a drug-free India.

The quiz was launched on October 26, 2026, by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA). The initiative aims to promote awareness about the harmful effects of substance use and encourage citizens, especially youth, to actively contribute towards creating a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

MY Bharat Quiz QR

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the quiz is being conducted from October 26 to November 25, 2026, and remains open to all citizens.

He said that interested participants can access the quiz through the MY Bharat portal and take part in this nationwide awareness initiative.

The Official said the interested citizens may click at the participation Link https://mybharat.gov.in/quizzes/yuva/detail/Url9dlIwCinQVSf8lwPB9w/

 

Launched on August 15, 2020, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan aims to strengthen drug demand reduction efforts through preventive education, awareness generation, treatment, rehabilitation and community participation, he added.

NMBA Mobile App

Initially launched in 272 vulnerable districts, the Abhiyaan has since expanded its reach to cover all districts across the country, he further said.

The Official noted that the campaign has reached over 35.89 crore people, including 14.36 crore youth and 11.34 crore women, reflecting the nationwide scale of its awareness and outreach initiatives.

Nasha Mukti Mitr Registration QR Code
 

Under the Abhiyaan, over 33.57 lakh activities have been conducted in educational institutions, while 39.91 lakh persons have been treated and rehabilitated through a network of more than 755 Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE)-supported de-addiction centres working across the country, the Official said.

The total number of Nasha Mukt pledges taken has crossed 48.21 Lakh, with more than 2 Lakh Nasha Mukti Mitras registered, he added.

Noting that the Abhiyaan has entered its seventh year, the Official said the ongoing quiz seeks to deepen public understanding of the harmful effects of substance use, promote informed decision-making and encourage young people to become active ambassadors of awareness and prevention.

The initiative reinforces the vision of a Nasha Mukt Bharat and Viksit Bharat, recognising the importance of healthy individuals, families and communities in the country's development, the Official further said.

Giving details, the Official informed that the quiz comprises 20 Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs), which participants are required to answer within 10 minutes.

A participation certificate is generated for every participant who successfully submits the quiz, he said.

He added the participants can also view the correct answers upon completion, enabling them to enhance their understanding of substance use prevention.

Underscoring the importance of this digital initiative, the Official said the Ministry aims to strengthen community participation, encourage responsible choices and mobilise citizens, especially youth, to contribute to the movement against substance use.

NMBA e-pledge QR Code

He said the Ministry appeals all citizens, particularly young people, to participate in the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva, Viksit Bharat Quiz’ before November 25, 2026, and become active contributors to the collective vision of a drug-free India.

2335999.title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium in Mysuru, Karnataka
2335999.body_html:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium in Mysuru, Karnataka
The new COSMOS Planetarium in Mysuru brings the wonders of the universe closer to young minds: PM
There were many great astronomers in India like Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya, and Nilakantha Somayaji; Advanced instruments and technology like today were not available at that time; Despite this, they made great discoveries and performed difficult calculations: PM
Our government has opened up the space sector; This has created new avenues for private sector, providing Indian startups with the opportunity to showcase their potential: PM
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 7:31PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated the COSMOS-Mysuru Planetarium, India's first LED dome planetarium, in Mysuru, Karnataka. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister extended his greetings in Kannada, and expressed his delight at returning to Mysuru to dedicate the COSMOS Planetarium to the nation just months after inaugurating the Viveka Smaraka. Pointing out that while the Viveka Smaraka inspires introspection and spiritual pursuit, the COSMOS Planetarium directs our gaze skyward to unravel the mysteries of the vast universe, he emphasized the profound cultural message conveyed by both landmarks. “This is an example of the fact that in India, the traditions of spirituality and science have always moved forward together,” remarked Shri Modi.

Recalling how ancient Indian ancestors minutely studied the skies, understood planetary and stellar movements, created calendars, and calculated solar and lunar eclipses, the Prime Minister highlighted the legacy of great Indian astronomers such as Aryabhata, Varahamihira, Bhaskaracharya, and Nilakantha Somayaji. “Advanced instruments and technology like today did not exist at that time; despite this, they made great discoveries and performed difficult calculations,” noted PM Modi.

Highlighting Mysuru's rich tradition of fostering knowledge institutions,including the establishment of the University of Mysore under Maharaja Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar and the Wadiyar royal family's pivotal role in laying the foundation of the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru to empower generations of scholars, the Prime Minister noted that Mysuru is adding a new chapter to India's scientific journey with the dedication of this state-of-the-art planetarium to the youth and citizens. Sharing that watching a show inside the LED dome was a wonderful experience in itself, he congratulated the nation on the milestone. “I felicitate the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, the University of Mysore, various departments of the government, and all the people associated with its construction,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Tracing the evolution of India's national motto from ‘Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan’ to Atal Bihari Vajpayee's addition of ‘Jai Vigyan’ and his own addition of ‘Jai Anusandhan’ guiding 21st-century India, the Prime Minister praised the enthusiastic participation of Indian youth when Mumbai hosted the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics last year and highlighted their stellar performance at this year's edition in Vietnam. “Five students from India went to Vietnam; out of them, four won gold medals and one won a silver medal, which is a matter of pride for the entire country,” observed PM Modi.

Spotlighting the record-breaking achievements of young Indian students who won gold or silver medals across Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology at this year's International Olympiads, the Prime Minister emphasized that young Indians achieve extraordinary milestones whenever they are provided with learning resources, technology, tools, and institutional support. “This COSMOS Planetarium is now also going to help immensely in giving shape to their dreams,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Emphasizing that no nation can afford to move slowly amid rapid global technological change, the Prime Minister detailed India's unprecedented pace over the past decade in astronomy, astrophysics, and space exploration through new telescopes and landmark ISRO missions, including becoming the first country to land near the Moon's South Pole with Chandrayaan-3 and launching India's first space solar observatory, Aditya-L1. “Last year itself, India became the fourth country in the world to demonstrate the capability of docking and undocking in space,” noted PM Modi.

Pointing out that an Indian astronaut recently traveled to the International Space Station and conducted novel experiments during this period, the Prime Minister highlighted the strategic value of the mission's findings. “The experience gained from this mission is also proving useful for our own human spaceflight program, Gaganyaan,” observed Shri Modi.

Highlighting the government's decision to open the space sector to private participation, which has enabled Indian startups and youth to showcase their capabilities by launching private rockets, placing satellites into orbit, and undertaking unprecedented space ventures, the Prime Minister stated that this reflects the scientific approach of New India. “Where new discoveries are being encouraged, new technology is being developed, and new opportunities are being created for our youth,” asserted PM Modi.

Underscoring that India has always been guided by the mantra of ‘Humanity First’ and dedicated its space program to human welfare, the Prime Minister cited the ISRO-developed satellite communication system for fishermen. “With the help of this system, for the boats fitted with receivers, officials can deliver timely alerts to them during a storm and can also track their safe return to the shore,” noted Shri Modi.

Detailing everyday applications of space technology such as the Real-Time Train Tracking System developed by Indian Railways and ISRO for checking live train locations and the use of satellite data alongside field inputs under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana to estimate crop yields and settle farm insurance claims, the Prime Minister highlighted the dual impact of India's space assets. “Today our satellites are touching the heights of space, and at the same time, they are being used to make the lives of people better on Earth,” observed PM Modi.

Emphasizing that the government's guiding philosophy of ‘Science for Society’ drives its sustained push for research and innovation across the country, the Prime Minister noted that over one crore students have already benefited from more than 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs nationwide. “In these labs, children are getting opportunities to work on their ideas, conduct new experiments, and innovate,” noted Shri Modi.

Stating that advancing research requires giving students and scholars access to the world's finest scientific literature, the Prime Minister highlighted the launch of ‘One Nation One Subscription’ to help domestic institutes access leading global journals alongside the creation of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation. “Through this, we are helping the maximum number of universities to conduct new research,” asserted PM Modi.

Recalling last year's launch of the one lakh crore rupee Research, Development, and Innovation Scheme to ensure sustained funding for domestic researchers, the Prime Minister highlighted the practical impact of the initiative. “This is helping in taking new technology out of the lab and reaching it to practical use,” observed Shri Modi.

Concluding his address by stating that planetariums and science centers play a vital role in sparking youth curiosity within India's burgeoning science and research ecosystem, the Prime Minister urged those associated with COSMOS to continuously invite school and college students from across the region and extended his best wishes for the journey ahead. “The children who come here to learn about the universe, it is possible that some of them may return here one day and tell us what new discoveries they have made about the universe, and this alone will be the biggest success of this COSMOS Planetarium,” remarked PM Modi.

2335993.title: Ministry of Rural Development’s NRIDA Selected for Prestigious U.P. Medal 2025 for Innovation in Road Technology by Indian Road Congress
2335993.body_html:
Ministry of Rural Development
Ministry of Rural Development’s NRIDA Selected for Prestigious U.P. Medal 2025 for Innovation in Road Technology by Indian Road Congress
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 7:08PM by PIB Delhi

National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA) under The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India, has achieved a significant recognition in the field of sustainable rural infrastructure, selected for the prestigious U.P. Medal for Innovative Technology in Roads for the year 2025. The award recognises NRIDA's initiative in promoting the innovative use of steel slag in rural road construction under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY).

The award will be presented during the Indian Road Congress Annual Function of the 85th Annual Session on November 19, 2026, at Hyderabad, Telangana.

For this prestigious recognition, the Ministry of Rural Development and NRIDA submitted a nomination highlighting the innovative use of steel slag in the construction of PMGSY-III road works in the State of Jharkhand, sanctioned during 2022-23.

The project covers a substantial road length of 381.57 km, demonstrating the adoption of steel slag as an alternative construction material in rural road infrastructure. The initiative has helped achieve a 26 per cent reduction in overall construction costs. The proximity of industrial steel plants has also contributed to optimising transportation costs.

The initiative demonstrates the effective utilisation of steel slag, an industrial waste material, as an alternative resource for rural road construction, thereby promoting resource efficiency and sustainable infrastructure development.

MoRD and NRIDA's Commitment to Sustainable Rural Infrastructure

The Ministry of Rural Development and NRIDA have so far sanctioned 1,81,923 km of road works using sustainable technologies, of which 1,39,901 km have been completed.

This recognition reflects NRIDA's continued commitment to encouraging the use of locally available, marginal and waste materials in road construction. It also acknowledges the efforts of the Ministry of Rural Development and NRIDA in facilitating the adoption of innovative and green technologies under PMGSY.

The initiative reinforces the Government's vision of developing sustainable, resilient and environmentally responsible rural road infrastructure across the country.

2335989.title: INS SAHYADRI CONCLUDES VISIT TO YOKOSUKA FOLLOWING MALABAR 2026
2335989.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INS SAHYADRI CONCLUDES VISIT TO YOKOSUKA FOLLOWING MALABAR 2026
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Navy's indigenous Guided Missile Stealth Frigate, INS Sahyadri, departed Yokosuka Naval Base, Japan, on 12 Nov 2026, following the successful conclusion of Exercise MALABAR 2026.

The exercise brought together the navies of India, Japan, the United States and Australia for professional engagements during the Harbour Phase and coordinated maritime operations during the Sea Phase https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=2333046.

The Sea Phase featured a range of maritime operations and drills, including Anti-Submarine Warfare, Visit, Board, Search and Seizure (VBSS) drills, Maritime Interdiction Operations, gunnery exercises, replenishment approaches and cross-deck landings. These engagements provided valuable opportunities to enhance interoperability, operational coordination and mutual understanding among participating navies.

The Harbour Phase witnessed operational synchronisation, cross-deck visits, sporting engagements and cultural activities, fostering camaraderie and strengthening bonds among participating personnel.

The successful culmination of the exercise reaffirmed the shared commitment of participating navies to maritime cooperation and collective security in the Indo-Pacific, in consonance with India's vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

2335988.title: From Safer Working Conditions to Improved Livelihood:  A NAMASTE Success Story from Puducherry
2335988.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Safer Working Conditions to Improved Livelihood:  A NAMASTE Success Story from Puducherry
NAMASTE Scheme Enables Sanitation Worker to Adopt Safer Working Practices Through Protective Equipment, Safety Training and Social Security Support
Monthly Income Increases by 50 Per Cent from ₹8,000 to ₹12,000, Strengthening Financial Stability and Family Well-Being
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of Mr. Ramasamy (name changed), a 56-year-old sanitation worker belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, employed with Oulgaret Municipality in Puducherry,   reflects the role of targeted interventions in addressing occupational risks and improving the livelihoods of sanitation workers.

Through the NAMASTE Scheme, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote safer working conditions, social security and dignified livelihoods, contributing to a more inclusive, sustainable and mechanised sanitation ecosystem.

Ensuring safe working conditions, occupational health and dignified livelihoods for sanitation workers, is an important step towards building an inclusive and sustainable sanitation ecosystem.

The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment seeks to strengthen the safety, dignity and socio-economic well-being of sanitation workers through access to protective equipment, safety training and institutional support.

For several years, Mr. Ramasamy worked as a sewer and septic tank cleaner, often without adequate personal protective equipment (PPE), exposing himself to occupational hazards and associated health risks.

Prolonged exposure to hazardous working conditions resulted in recurring skin infections, injuries and physical discomfort. These health concerns frequently disrupted his work attendance, leading to loss of wages and financial difficulties. Alongside occupational health challenges, he also experienced the social stigma associated with sanitation work.

With a family of four dependent on his earnings, maintaining household stability while managing health-related expenses remained a significant challenge. Despite these difficulties, Ramasamy aspired to work in safer conditions, secure a stable livelihood and provide better opportunities for his children.

A significant turning point came in 2025 when he received assistance under the NAMASTE Scheme. As part of the intervention, he was provided with a comprehensive PPE kit comprising protective overalls, gloves, safety boots, a face mask and a safety helmet. He also underwent structured training on safe sewage handling practices, occupational safety, hazard prevention and the proper use of protective equipment. In addition, he was linked with social security support to strengthen his overall well-being.

The intervention enabled Ramasamy to adopt safer working practices and develop greater awareness of occupational hazards. Access to appropriate protective equipment contributed to a reduction in recurring skin infections and work-related injuries, improving his health and enabling more regular attendance at work.

The improvement in his working conditions also contributed to greater financial stability. His monthly income increased from approximately ₹8,000 to around ₹12,000, registering a 50 per cent rise. Improved work attendance and fewer health-related disruptions enabled him to contribute more consistently towards household expenses and the needs of his family.

With improved occupational safety, greater financial security and increased awareness of safe sanitation practices, Ramasamy has experienced a positive transformation in his professional and personal life. The support received under NAMASTE has helped him continue his work with greater confidence while strengthening his ability to provide for his family.

2335973.title: CBDT actively implements Special Campaign 6 for swachhata and administrative efficiency
2335973.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
CBDT actively implements Special Campaign 6 for swachhata and administrative efficiency
Posted On: 13 NOV 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, achieved significant results under the Special Campaign 6. Conducted across all field formations of the Income Tax Department, the campaign focused on institutionalizing Swachhata, streamlining record management and ensuring disposal of pending matters, in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) and as a continuation of the successful campaigns undertaken since 2021.

During Special Campaign 6, the Income Tax Department achieved remarkable progress across all key parameters. Through systematic weeding out and space optimisation initiatives, the CBDT freed up 1.54 lakh sq. ft. of office space and earned revenue of ₹36.9 lakh from sale of scrap and obsolete materials. In the area of records management, more than 90,000 physical files were weeded out, while more than 24,000 e-files were closed. Cleanliness campaigns were conducted across all Income tax offices across India and also in various public places reinforcing Department’s commitment to cleanliness and sustainability.

On the citizen-centric front, the CBDT disposed of 29,153 public grievances, surpassing the initial target of 15,081 cases. These achievements collectively reflect the CBDT’s unwavering commitment to efficiency, citizen centric tax administration and ease of doing business.

To promote wider public awareness of the Special Campaign, extensive outreach was carried out through social media. More than 200 tweets and posts were shared by the field formations of the Income Tax Department on their official handles, highlighting campaign milestones and local initiatives.

In addition to meeting the operational targets, different regions undertook a series of unique and innovative initiatives under Special Campaign 6. Some of the noteworthy best practices implemented during the campaign are as follows:  

E-Waste Disposal

Various Income Tax Offices across India - at Bengaluru, Chennai, Gujarat, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Odisha and Delhi undertook initiatives for the proper disposal of e-waste generated in office premises, promoting environmentally responsible waste management and ensuring the systematic handling of discarded electronic items, in addition to generation of a revenue to the tune of Rs. 17,66,225/-.

The freed-up area is now available for multipurpose official use, including better space allocation and storage arrangements. This initiative has reduced clutter, improved cleanliness and hygiene, enhanced workplace organization and enabled more efficient utilization of departmental infrastructure. The exercise also promotes environmentally responsible e-waste management and contributes to a cleaner, safer and more functional working environment.

                      

'Waste to Art' Initiatives and Exhibitions showcasing Creativity and Sustainability in Kolkata, Odisha and Gujarat

  • Gaj-Garuda Symbolic Structure: The office of the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Bhubaneswar, Odisha organised a ‘Waste to Art’ exhibition.  A symbolic structure titled Gaj-Garuda - depicting the mythical Garuda holding an elephant by its trunk was installed by the Pr. CCIT, Odisha region. The structure was built at zero cost, by using office scrap like broken steel grills, discarded plastic paint containers, single-use plastic water bottles, and broken pieces of plastic water coolers. The initiative beautifully aligns with the "Waste to Art" mission under the Special Campaign-6, while visually projecting the institutional values of strength, vigilance, and environmental stewardship.

                                                                                                                                                                                                    

           

 

  • The office of the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, West Bengal & Sikkim organised a ‘Waste to Art’ exhibition from 01.10.2026 to 06.10.2026 at the Rooftop, Aayakar Bhawan Annexe, Kolkata, featuring innovative artworks made from discarded household/office materials. Used plastic bottles, cans, containers and other scrap materials were transformed into striking depictions of human figures, animal replicas, planters and decorative artefacts alongside a photograph gallery. 

 

 

  • An exhibition on the theme “Waste to Wealth” was organised by Aaykar Bhavan, Vejalpur, Ahmedabad, to promote awareness regarding the productive utilisation and recycling of waste materials for making reusable articles of value.

 

 

The above initiatives beautifully blended artistic creativity with environmental consciousness, promoting the message of waste-to-art and waste-to-wealth, alongside the message of sustainable living.

Creation of a ‘Sports Recruitment Portal’ at Delhi

The Office of the Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Delhi, has developed an online recruitment portal for Sports Quota Recruitment - 2026 to facilitate candidates in submitting their applications online as part of the digitization initiative under Special Champaign 6. The portal is an innovative practice, aims to ensure a transparent, efficient and streamlined recruitment process, while reducing paperwork, physical documentation and storage requirements. It also enables easier access to application records, faster verification and improved monitoring of the recruitment process, in line with the vision of Digital India and e-Governance.

 

 

Citizen Centric Initiatives by Income Tax Department in West Bengal & Sikkim, Mumbai, UP(East) and Gujarat Regions

Under the campaign, the Income Tax Offices at West Bengal & Sikkim, Mumbai, UP(East) and Gujarat, carried out a cleanliness drive at various public places such as St. John’s Church, a renowned tourist spot in Kolkata; Kamudini Homes Higher Secondary School, Kalimpong; Municipal Girls High School, Darjeeling; pilgrim place, Mehsana; Vastrapur Railway Station, Ahmedabad etc., in addition to the respective Income Tax Offices. These initiatives reinforced the Department's commitment to cleanliness and sustainability.

 

A ‘Laghu Pustakalaya’ set up via space optimization at Delhi

The Office of the Director General of Income Tax (Investigation), Delhi converted an under-utilised floor area into a ‘Laghu Pustakalaya’, a mini library with a reading lounge, book cabinets, suitable lighting, seating and indoor plants. The initiative promotes optimal space utilisation and provides a conducive environment for reading and staff well-being.

The CBDT reaffirms its commitment to institutionalizing Swachhata through regular review and disposal of old records, digital record management and scientific office waste management. It also remains dedicated to sustainability and ease of living initiatives.
