2335598.title: Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Addresses First Regional Conference on JJM 2.0 at Tiruchirappalli
2335598.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C. R. Paatil Addresses First Regional Conference on JJM 2.0 at Tiruchirappalli
Seven Southern States and Union Territories deliberate on accelerating implementation and ensuring long-term functionality of rural drinking water supply schemes
Inter-ministerial convergence, source sustainability, institutional strengthening and Gram Panchayat-led water governance emerge as key priorities
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 7:53PM by PIB Delhi

Shri C. R. Paatil, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, addressed the first Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0, organised by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, in collaboration with the Government of Tamil Nadu. The two-day conference, being held on 12–13 November 2026, brings together senior officials and representatives from seven southern States and Union Territories namely, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Keralam, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry and Lakshadweep  to review progress, address challenges and strengthen sustainable rural drinking water services. implementation

Chairing the Ministerial Session at the Conference, Hon’ble Union Minister of Jal Shakti, recalled the transformative vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister behind the launch of Jal Jeevan Mission in 2019, aimed at ensuring access to tap water for every rural household. He highlighted the remarkable progress achieved under the Mission, with household tap water connections reaching approximately 16 crore rural households, significantly improving the lives of rural communities, particularly women.

The Union Minister noted that the Regional Conference was being organised as a follow-up to the Departmental Summit on Water held on 1–2 September 2026, to translate the deliberations and decisions of the Summit into concrete action at the State, district and village levels. He emphasised that the remaining works must be completed within the approved Mission timeline of December 2028 and appealed to States to make concerted efforts towards completing them by December 2027, wherever feasible.

Hon’ble Minister underscored that JJM 2.0 represents a transition from infrastructure creation to assured and sustainable drinking water service delivery. He stressed the need for States to operationalise the prescribed structural reforms, particularly those relating to operation and maintenance (O&M), institutional accountability and long-term functionality of rural water supply systems. He reiterated the Government of India's commitment to providing financial support for eligible works, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed reform conditions, and urged States to accelerate implementation and effective utilisation of available resources.

Emphasising the importance of water security, the Union Minister called for greater attention to groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and community-led water conservation. Referring to Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari, he highlighted the potential of decentralised water conservation structures and urged States to strengthen convergence among departments and actively involve communities in source sustainability measures. He also encouraged participating States to exchange successful practices and adopt practical solutions to overcome implementation challenges.

Shri Thiru N. Anand, Hon’ble Minister, Rural Development and Panchayati Raj,  and Water Resources in the Government of Tamil Nadu, highlighted the State's progress in expanding rural household tap water connections and strengthening drinking water infrastructure through combined water supply schemes and improvement of existing systems. He outlined initiatives relating to O&M, periodic cleaning of overhead tanks, community-based water quality testing, collection of water service charges and district-level monitoring of drinking water services. He reaffirmed Tamil Nadu's commitment to JJM 2.0 and emphasised continued Centre–State cooperation for completing the remaining works and sustaining drinking water services.

Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, stated that the Tiruchirappalli conference was the first in a series of five regional conferences aimed at translating the outcomes of the Department al Summit on Water held in September 2026 into actionable measures. He emphasised source sustainability, effective O&M arrangements, financial sustainability, skilled local workforce and strengthened Gram Panchayat-led governance as key priorities. He also highlighted the importance of digital platforms, including Sujalam Bharat, and inter-ministerial convergence to support sustainable service delivery.

Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary and Mission Director, NJJM, during his interactions across various presentations, emphasised the need to translate reforms into effective field-level implementation and strengthen interdepartmental coordination among Rural Development, Panchayati Raj and Rural Water Supply Departments.

He highlighted the need for regular assessment of drinking water sources, effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, strengthening Gram Panchayat own-source revenue and ensuring sustainable financing for operation and maintenance.

During the Ministerial Session, Shri D. Senthil Pandiyan, Joint Secretary, DDWS, apprised the Hon’ble Union Minister on the objectives and key deliberations of the Regional Conference. He highlighted the importance of regional conferences as platforms for mutual learning, sharing of best practices and strengthening coordination among States/UTs. Referring to the historical significance of the Kallanai Dam and the Cauvery water management system, he emphasised community ownership, effective operation and maintenance, and interdepartmental convergence for ensuring sustainable rural drinking water services under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

The conference commenced with a welcome address by Shri Dinesh Ponraj Oliver, Mission Director, JJM, Tamil Nadu. Senior officials of the Government of Tamil Nadu and representatives of participating States and Union Territories also attended the deliberations.

Shri Hari Narayan Murugun, Director, DDWS, presented the vision and key structural reforms under JJM 2.0 and reviewed the progress of participating States and Union Territories on various reform parameters. The presentation highlighted institutional strengthening, service utility arrangements, source sustainability, water quality governance, digital monitoring, capacity building and skilled human resources.

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, represented by Dr. M Jayaprakashan, Regional Director, RDSDE, highlighted the importance of developing a skilled local workforce for the operation and maintenance of rural drinking water systems, including training and certification of village-level functionaries.

Shri Y. K. Singh, Director, DDWS, highlighted convergence opportunities with major tribal development initiatives, including PM-JANMAN and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DA-JGUA), to address drinking water requirements in tribal and particularly vulnerable tribal group habitations.

The Ministry of Rural Development, represented by Ms. Deeksha Supyaal Bisht, Assistant Commissioner, VB-G RAM G and Shri Gauri Shankar, Project Officer, MoRD, presented opportunities for convergence under VB-G RAM G for water conservation, groundwater recharge, source sustainability and eligible maintenance-related interventions.

Shri Vipul Ujwal, Director, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, highlighted the central role of Gram Panchayats in sustaining rural drinking water services, with particular emphasis on O&M financing, integration of drinking water requirements into Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) and utilisation of Finance Commission grants. The discussions also emphasised convergence of capacity-building modules developed under JJM 2.0 with the training framework of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA).

Phani Kumar, Project Director, National Institute of Ocean Technology, highlighted its indigenous Low Temperature Thermal Desalination (LTTD) technology, with eight plants established in Lakshadweep to provide safe drinking water with minimal environmental impact. It also showcased an innovative Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) project integrating renewable energy generation with desalination to strengthen island water security.

Representatives from seven States/UTs—Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Puducherry and Lakshadweep presented their achievements, key challenges, best practices and progress on reforms under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The presentations covered physical and financial completion of schemes, Sujalam Bharat digital initiatives, geo-tagging of water supply assets, Jal Arpan and Har Ghar Jal certification, drinking water service delivery assessment, capacity building and skilling, community participation, and institutional, financial and source sustainability measures. States/UTs also shared innovative approaches, implementation challenges and time-bound action plans for accelerating reforms and ensuring sustainable rural drinking water services.

The conference provides an important platform for strengthening Centre–State coordination, promoting inter-departmental convergence and accelerating the implementation of JJM 2.0 reforms towards sustainable drinking water services for every rural household.

2335584.title: Andhra Pradesh Eyes Global Maritime Hub Status with Major Push for Ports and Shipbuilding
2335584.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2335584.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Andhra Pradesh Eyes Global Maritime Hub Status with Major Push for Ports and Shipbuilding
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal highlights state’s 1,053-km coastline
Four greenfield port projects & proposed ₹30,000-crore shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam
Andhra Pradesh today has the opportunity to become India's Maritime Gateway to the East: Sarbananda Sonowal
Smart ports powered by artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, automation and digital logistics platforms would be central to improving efficiency and competitiveness: Sarbananda Sonowal
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi

Andhra Pradesh is poised to emerge as a globally competitive maritime and logistics hub, with a major push towards port infrastructure, shipbuilding and ship repair, Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said in Visakhapatnam at the 31st CII Partnership Summit held in the city today.

Addressing at the summit, Sonowal highlighted the state's strategic advantages, including its approximately 1,053-kilometre coastline along the Bay of Bengal, access to key international shipping routes and proximity to major Asian manufacturing and trading economies. He said these strengths position Andhra Pradesh to become India's principal maritime gateway to ASEAN, East Asia and the wider Indo-Pacific.

Sonowal credited the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the able support from Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for creating the conditions to accelerate the state's maritime ambitions. He said the Centre was committed to working closely with the state government, industry and global investors to unlock its potential.

“If Hyderabad became Cyberabad, Andhra Pradesh today has the opportunity to become India's Maritime Gateway to the East,” Sarbananda Sonowal said, drawing a parallel between the state's technology-led growth and the opportunities emerging in the maritime sector.

Sonowal also highlighted the foundation stone laid on Wednesday for projects worth more than ₹560 crore at Visakhapatnam Port. These projects are expected to build and augment capacity, enhance ease of doing business and create employment opportunities.

The state's port infrastructure is set for further expansion with four major greenfield port projects under construction at Mulapeta, Machilipatnam, Ramayapatnam and Kakinada SEZ. These projects are expected to strengthen cargo-handling capacity and support industrial development.

Identifying shipbuilding and ship repair as major opportunities for Andhra Pradesh, Sonowal highlighted the proposed greenfield shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam. The project has received in-principle approval under the National Shipbuilding Mission and envisages an investment of approximately ₹30,000 crore, with a targeted annual capacity of 1.2 million gross tonnes.

A Centre-State special purpose vehicle (SPV) involving the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board and Visakhapatnam Port Authority has been formed for the project. He invited global shipbuilders, technology companies, equipment manufacturers and maritime investors to explore Andhra Pradesh as a preferred investment destination.

Sarbananda Sonowal said, “Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India had set an ambitious objective of becoming one of the world's top five shipbuilding nations. We have been taking major steps to develop the capacity, technology and industrial ecosystem required to achieve this goal. The Modi government has allocated ₹70,000 crore in financing support for shipbuilding and other maritime activities, creating opportunities for domestic and international investors.”

Sonowal said Andhra Pradesh's maritime development was part of India's wider transformation under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Initiatives such as Sagarmala, Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 are laying the foundations for a globally competitive maritime economy, with an envisaged investment of ₹80 lakh crore.

Sonowal also highlighted the ₹10,000-crore Container Manufacturing Scheme to promote indigenous container production and the proposed ₹10,000-crore Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme to harness the potential of India's 12,000-kilometre coastline. The ₹80,000-crore deep-draft, all-weather mega container port at Vadhavan in Maharashtra is another major initiative aimed at strengthening the country's maritime infrastructure.

The four Global Maritime Investment Summits held under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi have attracted investments worth approximately ₹25 lakh crore in India's maritime sector, he said.

Emphasising the role of technology in the next phase of maritime development, Sarbananda Sonowal said, “Smart ports powered by artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, automation and digital logistics platforms would be central to improving efficiency and competitiveness. Andhra Pradesh has the opportunity to take a leading role in this transformation.”

He called for a strong partnership between the Central and state governments, industry and global investors to accelerate port development, shipbuilding, ship repair, cruise tourism, coastal shipping and maritime industrialisation.

Sonowal outlined three key ambitions for Andhra Pradesh: becoming a leading destination for port-led development in the spirit of the prime minister's Saptadhara roadmap for Viksit Bharat 2047; emerging as a globally competitive shipbuilding and ship repair hub; and positioning itself as India's eastern maritime gateway to ASEAN, East Asia and the Indo-Pacific.

The state already has an established maritime presence through Visakhapatnam, Gangavaram and Krishnapatnam ports. Visakhapatnam Port handled a record 91.17 million tonnes of cargo in FY 2025-26, registering growth of approximately 10% over the previous year. It has maintained a continuous growth trajectory for four consecutive years since FY 2021-22.

The 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 is being held in Visakhapatnam on Nov. 12-13 under the theme “Navigating the New World Order: Trade | Technology | Trust | Thought Leadership.” The summit brings together government leaders, industry representatives and international participants to explore opportunities in trade, investment, technology and global partnerships.

2335582.title: Bhagni Nivedita Chhatri Niwash in Tripura
2335582.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Bhagni Nivedita Chhatri Niwash in Tripura
Strengthening Educational Opportunities for OBC Girls
Ministry-Supported Hostel Project Aims to Improve Access to Safe Residential Facilities for OBC Girl Students Pursuing Higher Education
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi

Access to safe and affordable accommodation is an important enabler of higher education, particularly for young women travelling from distant and rural areas.

Bhagni Nivedita Chhatri Niwash, located at Krishnanagar, Agartala West, Tripura, is a hostel initiative to support girl students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community as they pursue college and university education.

The initiative highlights the role of targeted hostel infrastructure in advancing inclusive educational opportunities. On completion, the proposed 54-seat facility is expected to support OBC girl students travelling from distant areas and contribute to a more enabling environment for higher education.

For students living far from educational institutions, finding suitable accommodation can present a practical challenge to continuing their studies. A dedicated hostel facility is meant to ease this difficulty and provide a more supportive environment in which students can focus on their academic goals.

Bhagni Nivedita Chhatri Niwash has a planned capacity of 54 seats. The project information reports 20 current residents or beneficiaries. The facility is meant to provide accommodation to eligible OBC students and strengthen boarding arrangements.

The project is being implemented by the Rural Development Department, Government of Tripura, on behalf of the OBC Welfare Department. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is the funding and supporting agency. The facility reflects the importance of coordination between the Central and State Governments in supporting educational infrastructure.

The hostel has essential planned amenities including electricity, proper sanitation and hygiene, safe drinking water and suitable security arrangements. Together, these facilities shall support a safe and conducive residential environment for students pursuing higher education.

Beyond its immediate accommodation purpose, the hostel project represents an effort to strengthen educational access for OBC girls by providing the physical infrastructure needed to support their studies. Such residential facilities can help create conditions in which students are better able to pursue their academic aspirations.

2335554.title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs launches national initiative for conservation of medicinal plants and promotion of sustainable livelihoods in 16 tribal hotspots across 13 States/UTs
2335554.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
Ministry of Tribal Affairs launches national initiative for conservation of medicinal plants and promotion of sustainable livelihoods in 16 tribal hotspots across 13 States/UTs
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, in collaboration with the CSIR–National Botanical Research Institute (CSIR-NBRI), Lucknow, formally launched the project “Integrated Conservation, Agro-Technology and Bioresource Enterprise Development for Sustainable Tribal Livelihoods in Tribal Hotspots of India” at the Central University of Odisha, Koraput, on 12 November 2026.

The inaugural programme was attended by Additional Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, senior officials of the Ministry, Dr. Ajit Kumar Kumar Shasany, Hon’ble Vice-Chancellor of the Central University of Odisha, Dr. Sharad Kumar Srivastava, Chief Scientist and Principal Investigator, CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute, Lucknow, Ms. Snehaprabha Majhi, ITDA Project Administration, Koraput, scientists from ICMR-National Institute of Health Research, Bhubaneshwar, scientists, experts, industry representatives, faculty members, and tribal community representatives.

The three-year initiative aims to conserve the rich medicinal plant biodiversity of tribal regions while harnessing traditional knowledge and indigenous bioresources to create sustainable livelihood and enterprise opportunities for tribal communities. The project covers 16 selected tribal hotspots across 13 States/Union Territories: Alluri Seetharama Raju (Andhra Pradesh), Kokrajhar (Assam), Narayanpur (Chhattisgarh), Navsari (Gujarat), East Singhbhum (Jharkhand), Kodagu (Karnataka), Wayanad (Kerala), Kargil (Ladakh), Anuppur (Madhya Pradesh), Gadchiroli and Nashik (Maharashtra), Kandhamal, Balangir and Koraput (Odisha), Sonbhadra (Uttar Pradesh), and Dharchula (Uttarakhand).

The major interventions under the project include documentation of approximately 200–300 medicinal plant species, scientific propagation of 30–40 rare, endangered and threatened (RET) species, establishment of 16 community nurseries and 16 seed banks, and development of community-level capacities for medicinal plant cultivation and bioresource-based enterprises. The project also envisages distribution of 40,000–50,000 quality planting materials to support conservation, propagation and sustainable cultivation.

As part of the initial implementation, CSIR-NBRI has already undertaken fieldwork in Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh during October 2026. The field team interacted with 146 tribal knowledge holders across 12 villages and documented traditional medicinal practices. A total of 97 field numbers, representing approximately 200 medicinal and economically important plant samples, were collected. Additionally, 25 live orchid samples were collected for germplasm conservation and multiplication at the CSIR-NBRI Botanical Garden.

The initiative seeks to establish strong linkages between scientific institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVKs), State Tribal Welfare and Forest Departments and local communities. Special emphasis will be placed on involving tribal farmers, traditional healers, women and rural youth in conservation, capacity building, cultivation and value-chain development.

A special technical session titled “From Tribal Knowledge to Enterprise” was organised as part of the programme, bringing together experts and stakeholders to deliberate on translating traditional knowledge and medicinal plant resources into sustainable economic opportunities. The programme also includes interaction with tribal farmers and traditional knowledge holders, followed by a field visit to the Koraput tribal hotspot on 13 November 2026.

Through this initiative, the Ministry aims to create a replicable institutional model that integrates biodiversity conservation, scientific research, preservation of indigenous knowledge and community-led enterprise development. The project represents an important step towards recognising tribal communities as custodians of India’s biological and traditional knowledge heritage while enabling them to derive sustainable economic benefits from their local bioresources.

2335536.title: From Risk to Respect
2335536.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Risk to Respect
 Mr Muthuvel in Puducherry Experiences Safety, Dignity and Earn Livelihood under NAMASTE Scheme
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 6:11PM by PIB Delhi

The journey of the sanitation worker from Puducherry, Mr Muthuvel (name changed) highlights how NAMASTE Scheme has contributed to improved workplace safety, livelihood security and social recognition.

Through initiatives such as NAMASTE, the Government of India continues to reaffirm its commitment to protecting, respecting and empowering sanitation workers who play an indispensable role in maintaining public health and cleanliness across the country.

The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, continues to strengthen occupational safety, dignity and livelihood opportunities for sanitation workers across the country.

Demonstrating the positive impact of the Scheme, Mr Muthuvel, a 58-year-old sanitation worker from Oulgaret Municipality, Puducherry, has experienced significant improvements in his working conditions, health and financial stability following the provision of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and occupational safety orientation under the initiative.

Belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community, the beneficiary has been engaged in sewer line cleaning for more than ten years. Having studied up to Class 5, he relied on his occupation to support a family of four, earning approximately ₹9,000–10,000 per month.

Despite his dedication to providing essential sanitation services, the absence of adequate protective equipment exposed him to hazardous waste, harmful gases and other occupational health risks. Frequent health complications and associated medical expenses further affected his ability to maintain regular employment and financial stability.

The challenges extended beyond occupational hazards and economic difficulties. Social stigma associated with sanitation work also affected his professional recognition and sense of dignity. With limited access to essential safety resources, he aspired to secure healthier working conditions, reduce occupational risks and provide greater financial security for his family.

A significant turning point came in 2025 when he was identified as a beneficiary under the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme. Through the intervention, he received a comprehensive Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kit comprising protective gloves, gumboots, overalls, a face mask and a safety helmet. He was also provided orientation on safe sanitation practices, appropriate use of protective equipment and measures to prevent occupational hazards.

The support brought a meaningful improvement in his everyday working conditions. With access to protective equipment and increased awareness of workplace safety, he became better equipped to perform his duties while reducing direct exposure to hazardous substances. The adoption of safer working practices contributed to fewer health complications, improved attendance and greater consistency in his professional responsibilities.

The positive impact of the intervention was also reflected in his financial circumstances. His monthly earnings, which previously ranged between ₹9,000 and ₹10,000, increased to approximately ₹13,000–14,000. Improved health and more regular attendance enabled him to maintain greater work continuity and contribute more consistently to his family's financial needs. The increase in earnings also helped strengthen household financial stability and reduce the burden associated with recurring medical expenses.

Beyond the improvements in occupational safety and income, the intervention contributed to strengthening his confidence and professional dignity. Access to protective equipment and institutional support reinforced the importance of recognising sanitation workers as essential contributors to public health and community well-being. The beneficiary also experienced greater recognition of his work within the community, reflecting a positive shift towards safer and more dignified sanitation practices.

For the beneficiary, the PPE kit represented more than protective equipment. It provided greater confidence in carrying out his responsibilities, strengthened his understanding of occupational safety and reinforced the assurance that his health, well-being and contribution to society are valued.

The NAMASTE Scheme seeks to promote the safety and dignity of sanitation workers through interventions aimed at reducing occupational hazards, encouraging mechanised sanitation practices and strengthening access to appropriate safety measures and institutional support. By facilitating protective equipment and safety orientation, the initiative contributes to healthier working environments and improved socio-economic opportunities for sanitation workers.

2335529.title: DRI busts red sanders smuggling syndicate at Chennai Port; seizes around 13,000 kg red sanders worth Rs. 7.72 crore; three arrested
2335529.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI busts red sanders smuggling syndicate at Chennai Port; seizes around 13,000 kg red sanders worth Rs. 7.72 crore; three arrested
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

Acting on specific intelligence regarding an attempt by a Chennai-based syndicate to smuggle Red Sanders logs to Malaysia, officers of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), intercepted an export container at Chennai Port during 9–11 November 2026, before its loading onto the vessel.

The container, declared to contain “Paper Laminate Rolls”, was subjected to detailed examination on 9–10 November 2026. Examination revealed 12.87 metric tonnes of high-grade Red Sanders logs, valued at approximately Rs. 7.72 crore, concealed alongside a small quantity of the declared cargo and gravel stones. The Red Sanders and cover cargo were seized under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

Preliminary investigation revealed that the syndicate had exploited the self-sealing facility available to a manufacturer-exporter. The syndicate arranged an export consignment through the exporter, diverted the container to a private godown and replaced the declared paper laminate rolls with Red Sanders logs before dispatching it for export.

A subsequent search of the godown led to the recovery of the original declared cargo, an industrial weighing scale and traces of Red Sanders, providing further evidence of the modus operandi.

Three key members of the syndicate involved in the smuggling operation have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.

Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) is a protected species listed under Appendix II of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) and Schedule IV of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. Its export from India is prohibited under the Foreign Trade Policy.

The operation highlights the misuse of legitimate export channels and trade facilitation measures for organised wildlife trafficking. DRI remains committed to dismantling such smuggling networks and protecting India’s rich biodiversity through intelligence-led enforcement.

2335516.title: DRI seizes 22 kg cocaine from passenger arriving from Sierra Leone in New Delhi
2335516.body_html:
Ministry of Finance
DRI seizes 22 kg cocaine from passenger arriving from Sierra Leone in New Delhi
Foreign female passenger arrested for attempting to smuggle contraband under guise of diplomatic persona
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

In a major crackdown on international drug syndicates, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has intercepted a foreign female passenger arriving from Sierra Leone and seized 22 kg (net) of cocaine from her possession. The seized narcotics are estimated to have a value of several crores of rupees in the illicit international market. The operation exposed a sophisticated and brazen modus operandi involving the use of forged diplomatic credentials to bypass airport security.

The passenger claimed to be a diplomatic courier and was carrying a large briefcase-type box bearing markings such as “Diplomatic Mail” and “Do Not Open Without Authority”. She also produced apparently forged documents claiming that the consignment belonged to a United Nations diplomatic courier, evidently to evade scrutiny.

Acting on the intelligence input, DRI officers conducted a thorough examination of the briefcase in accordance with due procedure. The examination resulted in the recovery of 22 packets, concealed within multiple layers of plastic wrapping. The white, brick-shaped substance recovered from the packets tested positive for cocaine during field testing.

The entire contraband, comprising 22 packets of cocaine, was seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. The passenger was arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985 and produced before the competent court.

The DRI remains firmly committed to dismantling novel trafficking routes, leveraging intelligence-led enforcement, and dismantling international syndicates attempting to exploit institutional privileges for illicit trade.

2335501.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA INTERACTS WITH MERITORIOUS EMRS STUDENTS AT RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN
2335501.body_html:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs
PRESIDENT OF INDIA INTERACTS WITH MERITORIOUS EMRS STUDENTS AT RASHTRAPATI BHAVAN
President Droupadi Murmu urges students to pursue excellence, remain connected with their roots and contribute to the development of their communities
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, interacted with meritorious students and alumni of Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre (RBCC), Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi, on 12 November 2026. The programme was organised by the National Education Society for Tribal Students (NESTS), Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India, as part of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026, commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.

The interaction provided an opportunity for students from different parts of the country to share their academic achievements, educational journeys, experiences and aspirations with the Hon’ble President. The programme also highlighted the role of EMRS in providing quality education and enabling tribal students to pursue higher education and professional careers.

Referring to the significance of Eklavya, the Hon’ble President encouraged students to understand the values associated with his life and draw inspiration from them. She observed that EMRS are providing tribal students with opportunities to develop their abilities and talents. She also noted that the equal representation of boys and girls in EMRS reflects progress towards inclusive development.

The Hon’ble President particularly emphasised the importance of remaining connected with one's roots, identity and cultural heritage. She encouraged them to take pride in their tribal heritage and maintain a strong connection with their villages and communities.

The Hon’ble President further advised students that, after acquiring higher education and establishing themselves as doctors, engineers, administrators and professionals in different fields, they should contribute to the welfare and development of their villages and communities. She stressed that their education would have greater significance when its benefits reach the people and regions from where they come.

Shri Jual Oram, Union Minister of Tribal Affairs, delivered the welcome address. Addressing the gathering,  Union Minister encouraged students to aim high and pursue their aspirations with dedication, discipline, hard work and self-confidence.

A total of 146 meritorious students and alumni from EMRS across the country participated in the programme. The participants included Class X and XII toppers and students who had secured admission to premier institutions such as IITs, NITs, National Law Universities (NLUs), NIFT and government medical colleges.

On the occasion, NESTS showcased a five-minute short film featuring the success stories of EMRS students and their journeys from their schools to the realisation of their dreams. Students also shared their educational journeys and experiences with the gathering, highlighting the role of EMRS in providing a supportive learning environment, academic opportunities, exposure and facilities that have contributed to their personal and academic development.

The programme also recognised the contributions of officials and institutions associated with the implementation of the EMRS initiative. The Hon’ble President felicitated the Secretaries/Principal Secretaries of the Tribal Welfare Departments of Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha; five District Magistrates; and Principals of five best-performing EMRS. Awards were also conferred upon best-performing tribal startups in recognition of their contributions to entrepreneurship and innovation.

The interaction highlighted the importance of providing quality education, equal opportunities and appropriate institutional support to tribal students. It also reinforced the role of EMRS in nurturing academic excellence, confidence, leadership and professional aspirations among tribal youth, while encouraging them to preserve their cultural identity and contribute to the development of their communities.

2335498.title: Union Environment Minister holds interaction with LeadIT Industry Members and Project Partners
2335498.ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
2335498.body_html:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Union Environment Minister holds interaction with LeadIT Industry Members and Project Partners
India is committed to Climate Action with focus on Multilateral Collaboration through initiatives like LeadIT: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi

In the run up to participation in UNFCCC COP31 at Antalya (Turkiye), Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav held an interaction with industry representatives from hard to abate sectors like steel, cement and transport, and academic research institutes, today in New Delhi.

The gathering brought together Indian member companies of the Leadership Group for Industry Transition (LeadIT), including Tata Steel, JSW Steel, SAIL, Synergy Advanced Metals, Adani Ambuja Cement, Dalmia Cement, JK Cement, JSW Cement, UltraTech Cement, Volvo Group and Spicejet. The participating project partners under the India-Sweden Industry Transition Partnership (ITP) included Jindal Steel and Power Ltd, Prism Johnson, Höganäs India and MyHome Industries. Further, premier research institutions working on low carbon technologies as project partners were also present, including National Council for Cement and Building Materials, IIT Bombay, IIT Bhubaneshwar, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, IIT Hyderabad and IIT Kharagpur.

Speaking at the interaction, Shri Yadav said, “The MoEFCC and Government of India are committed to support collaborative climate action. LeadIT 3.0 will be an implementation-oriented platform, translating ambition into tangible impact”. He emphasized that India's approach to climate action is firmly rooted in the power of collaboration among government, industry, and academia. The Minister highlighted India’s efforts towards climate action through ambitious policies and programmes.

Chaired an interaction with Indian LeadIT (Leadership Group for Industry Transition) member companies and project partners in New Delhi today. Launched by India and Sweden in 2019 to achieve industrial decarbonisation in heavy and hard-to-abate sectors by, LeadIT brings together 19 countries and 33 companies, including 13 from India. During the interaction, reaffirmed the strong commitment of the Government led by PM Shri @narendramodi ji to LeadIT, with a clear focus on building impactful partnerships for a low-carbon industrial future.

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) November 12, 2026

LeadIT industry members and project partners shared their experiences of engaging with LeadIT and highlighted the importance of collaboration with government and academia. Industry members appreciated the support that the platform has provided in formulating project partnerships, assessing technology feasibility and sharing knowledge. Industry representatives also expressed the need for further support for pre-competitive project preparation, pilot projects and capacity building.

The Governments of India and Sweden launched LeadIT in 2019 at the UN Climate Action Summit in New York, with the support of the World Economic Forum. Prime Ministers of India and Sweden announced the renewed mandate for LeadIT in May 2026. It is a public-private partnership that now has 19 countries and 33 companies as members. Shri Yadav and the Swedish Ministry of Climate and Enterprise would be launching the third phase of the initiative, LeadIT 3.0, on 17.11.2026, at the LeadIT Industry Leaders Roundtable at COP31 in Antalya.

2335497.title: National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students Enables Research Scholar to Complete Ph.D. in Genetics and Plant Breeding
2335497.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students Enables Research Scholar to Complete Ph.D. in Genetics and Plant Breeding
Financial Assistance of Approximately ₹11 Lakh Under NFSC Scheme Supports Doctoral Research and Higher Education
Ms. Anjali Kumari Completes Ph.D. and Pursues Professional Career at APMC, Kangra Himachal Pradesh
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi

The academic and professional journey of 29 year research scholar Ms. Anjali Kumari (name changed) demonstrates how access to educational support can contribute to individual achievement, family advancement and wider social progress.

Through initiatives such as the NFSC Scheme, the Government of India remains committed to expanding opportunities for students from Scheduled Caste communities and enabling them to contribute meaningfully to the nation's development.

The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, continues to facilitate access to higher education and advanced research opportunities for students from Scheduled Caste communities.

Demonstrating the positive impact of the Scheme, Ms. Anjali Kumari successfully completed her Ph.D. in Genetics and Plant Breeding with financial assistance of approximately ₹11 lakh received under the NFSC Scheme during 2022–2025.

Coming from a Scheduled Caste community, Ms. Anjali Kumari aspired to establish herself in the field of academics and scientific research. Despite her determination and academic commitment, financial constraints posed significant challenges in pursuing advanced studies. The substantial expenses associated with higher education and research, coupled with limited financial resources, created barriers to achieving her educational aspirations.

A significant turning point in her academic journey came through the financial assistance provided under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme. The support of approximately ₹11 lakh during 2022–2025 helped ease the financial burden associated with her doctoral studies, enabling her to concentrate on academic learning, research activities and the successful completion of her Ph.D. in Genetics and Plant Breeding.

Following the completion of her doctoral studies, Ms. Anjali Kumari is currently working as a Market Supervisor at the Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC), Kangra in Himachal Pradesh. Her academic achievement and professional progress reflect how targeted financial assistance can enable students from disadvantaged backgrounds to overcome economic barriers, develop specialised knowledge and pursue meaningful career opportunities.

The benefits of the Scheme have extended beyond her individual academic achievements. The financial assistance and subsequent professional opportunities have contributed to improving the socio-economic standing of her family, while strengthening her confidence and financial independence. Her journey highlights the importance of sustained institutional support in enabling students to realise their academic and professional potential.

Ms. Anjali Kumari has also been encouraging and supporting other students who aspire to pursue higher education but face financial difficulties. Drawing from her own experiences, she continues to motivate aspiring scholars to explore educational opportunities and pursue their academic goals with determination and confidence.

The National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students Scheme seeks to promote higher education among students belonging to Scheduled Caste communities by providing financial assistance for pursuing advanced studies and research. Through such interventions, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to strengthen educational inclusion, promote academic excellence and create opportunities for socio-economic empowerment.

2335496.title: CCRAS-CARI and University of Delhi sign MoU to document medicinal plant diversity of DU North Campus
2335496.body_html:
AYUSH
CCRAS-CARI and University of Delhi sign MoU to document medicinal plant diversity of DU North Campus
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS) - Central Ayurveda Research Institute (CARI), New Delhi and the University of Delhi signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on 10 November 2026 to undertake a collaborative project titled “Inventory of Phyto-diversity of Medicinal Importance Used in Ayurveda of North Campus of Delhi University.”

The MoU was formally signed by Prof. (Vd.) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS, and Dr. Vikas Gupta, Registrar, University of Delhi, at the VC Office, North Campus, New Delhi.

The project aims to systematically document, identify and conserve the medicinal plant diversity available across the 250-300 acres of the University of Delhi's North Campus. The initiative seeks to explore the rich botanical heritage of the campus and document plant species of medicinal importance described in Ayurveda.

The major activities under the project will include comprehensive field surveys, identification and documentation of medicinal plant species, preparation of herbarium specimens, and installation of QR-code-enabled name boards across the campus to facilitate easy identification and access to information about medicinal plants.

The project will also result in the preparation of an illustrated pictorial book documenting the medicinal flora of the North Campus, along with joint research publications to disseminate the scientific findings.

Prof. K. Ratnabali, Dean of Academic Affairs, Delhi University; Prof. (Dr.) Shobha Bagai, Director of the Cluster Innovation Centre (CIC), Delhi; Dr. Hemanta Panigrahi, Director in Charge, CARI, New Delhi; Dr. Sakshi Sharma, Research Officer and PI of the Project, CARI, New Delhi; Prof. (Dr.) Suresh Kumar, PI of the Project, Cluster Innovation Centre (CIC), University of Delhi; and Prof. (Dr.) Vandana, Department of  Chemistry, Dyal Singh College, Delhi University, were also present on the occasion.

This collaborative initiative represents an important step towards strengthening institutional cooperation in the fields of Ayurveda, biodiversity conservation, medicinal plant research and scientific documentation. It is expected to contribute significantly to raising awareness about the medicinal wealth of the university campus and promoting the conservation and sustainable utilisation of medicinal plant resources.

2335471.title: Raksha Rajya Mantri launches revamped Gallantry Awards portal
2335471.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Raksha Rajya Mantri launches revamped Gallantry Awards portal
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 5:07PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth launched the revamped Gallantry Awards portal (https://gallantryawards.gov.in) in New Delhi on November 12, 2026. The portal is a dedicated digital initiative to honour the courage & supreme sacrifices of the Gallantry Awardees and preserve their legacy for future generations.

The re-developed portal features an enhanced, citizen-centric User Interface and User Experience, with intuitive navigation, responsive design and improved accessibility. The key features include dedicated sections on Events, Memorials and Museums, Warpedia, Awardees, Gallantrypedia (Articles), Media and an interactive Tribute Section enabling citizens to explore the nation’s military history & pay homage to its bravehearts.

The Gallantry Awards Portal also hosts Veer Gatha as a dedicated digital space, with a page for every edition that brings its introduction, topics, timeline, evaluation criteria, rewards, resources, results, felicitation ceremony, media gallery and student activities together in one place. Through this, Veer Gatha connects students directly with the stories of the Gallantry awardees. Students learn about the courage and sacrifice of these heroes and express what they learn through their own entries.

The programme has grown from about 8 lakh students and 4,788 schools in the first edition to over 1.92 crore students and 1.9 lakh schools in the fifth. It includes 28,005 students from 91 CBSE-affiliated schools across 18 countries.

The initiative aims to create a comprehensive and authentic digital repository of information on Gallantry Awards, Awardees, wars and military operations since independence, while promoting patriotism and raising awareness about the rich military heritage, particularly among the youth.

Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh and other senior officials of the Ministry of Defence were present on the occasion.

2335459.title: Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 22 bids for 10 GWh Advanced Chemistry Cell manufacturing capacity under PLI ACC Scheme
2335459.body_html:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) receives 22 bids for 10 GWh Advanced Chemistry Cell manufacturing capacity under PLI ACC Scheme
Strong Industry Response Reflects Growing Interest in Establishing Domestic ACC Manufacturing Capacity
Bid opening marks a significant step towards strengthening India’s Domestic ACC Manufacturing Ecosystem
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 4:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has received 22 bids from prospective bidders for 10 GWh capacity offered under the Global Tender floated on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal for selection of beneficiary firms to establish giga-scale Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) manufacturing facilities in India. The 10 GWh capacity is earmarked for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage (GSSS) applications and forms part of the overall targeted 50 GWh ACC manufacturing capacity under the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage.

 

Request for Proposal (RFP) was floated on CPP portal on 15th July 2026. The pre-bid conference was held on 29th July 2026. The last date for receiving bids was 10th November 2026 on CPP portal and the Technical Bids were opened on 11th November 2026 in the presence of the bidders at MHI. The bidding is being conducted online through a transparent two-stage Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) mechanism. The list of bidders who have submitted their bids is as follows:

The allocation of 10 GWh for GSSS applications is expected to support the country’s rapidly growing energy-storage requirements arising from the expansion of renewable energy. It will contribute to enhancing energy security and deepening the domestic value chain for ACC technologies.

The strong participation in the tender reflects growing industry interest in India’s ACC manufacturing potential and reinforces the Government’s commitment to building a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive and sustainable ACC ecosystem, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

2335454.title: Dr. P.K. Mishra addresses the 22nd Foundation Day of PPVFRA and Plant Genome Saviour Award Ceremony
2335454.body_html:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
Dr. P.K. Mishra addresses the 22nd Foundation Day of PPVFRA and Plant Genome Saviour Award Ceremony
Dr. P.K. Mishra calls for linking farmers’ traditional knowledge with scientific research, seed systems and markets
Farmers must be recognised as custodians and innovators of India's agricultural biodiversity: Dr. P.K. Mishra
India's National Genebank is the world's second largest; around 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties developed: Dr. P.K. Mishra
“An award honours a farmer once; a seed chain, a market and a fair share of benefits sustain the farmer every season”: Dr. P.K. Mishra
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi

Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, Dr. P.K. Mishra, today called for recognising farmers as custodians and innovators of India's agricultural biodiversity and linking their traditional knowledge with scientific research, seed systems and market opportunities. Addressing the 22nd Foundation Day of the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPVFRA) and the Plant Genome Saviour Award Ceremony, Dr. Mishra noted that the occasion marked 25 years of the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001.

He said India's rich agricultural biodiversity was vital for developing crops resilient to climate change, water stress, pests and diseases, while preserving traditional knowledge, food cultures and community livelihoods. He highlighted India's 22 agro-biodiversity hotspots and cited Koraput in Odisha, recognised by FAO in 2012 as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System, as an example of community-led conservation.

Highlighting India's distinctive framework for farmers' rights, Dr. Mishra said the Act balanced plant breeders' rights with recognition of farmers as conservers, cultivators and developers of plant varieties. Nearly half of the varieties registered under PPVFRA were farmers' varieties. He also emphasised the role of benefit-sharing provisions and the National Gene Fund in ensuring fair returns to communities conserving genetic resources.

Referring to India's scientific capabilities, he noted that the National Genebank at ICAR-NBPGR was the second largest in the world and that around 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties had been developed under the National Agricultural Research System. He also highlighted the potential of Geographical Indications in creating economic opportunities for distinctive agricultural products.

Dr. Mishra highlighted India's contribution to international efforts on farmers' rights through its engagement with the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, the 2022 Governing Body session in New Delhi and the 2023 Global Symposium on Farmers' Rights. He also referred to the Indore Declaration adopted by BRICS Agriculture Ministers and the establishment of a Global Forum on Farmers' Rights in Seed Systems.

Calling for a shift from recognition to empowerment, Dr. Mishra emphasised strengthening community seed banks and field gene banks, connecting traditional knowledge with modern scientific research, and linking farmers' varieties with quality seed systems, Farmer Producer Organisations and wider markets. He called for promoting farmer entrepreneurship and ensuring fair and transparent benefit-sharing so that conservation translated into sustainable economic opportunities.

Concluding his address, Dr. Mishra said farmers must be recognised not merely as participants in India's agricultural transformation but also as contributors and beneficiaries of it.Emphasising the need for sustained economic returns for farmers conserving traditional varieties, he observed: “An award honours a farmer once; a seed chain, a market and a fair share of benefits sustain the farmer every season.” He said safeguarding agricultural diversity was a shared responsibility of farmers, scientists, universities, industry, the State and society, and congratulated the Authority and all award recipients.

2335430.title: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Reaches Over 35.88 Crore People; Over 14.35 Crore Youth, 11.33 Crore Women Reached Through Nationwide Awareness Campaign
2335430.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan Reaches Over 35.88 Crore People; Over 14.35 Crore Youth, 11.33 Crore Women Reached Through Nationwide Awareness Campaign
More Than 2 Lakh Citizens Enrolled as Nasha Mukti Mitr
Persons Seeking Treatment and Counselling Increase from 2.08 Lakh in 2020-21 to Over 9.11 Lakh in 2025-26
Total Number Of District De-Addiction Centres In The Country Is 198 As On Date
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 4:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on 15 August 2020, has evolved into a nationwide people's movement against substance abuse, reaching over 35.88 crore people across the country as on 12 November 2026.

The campaign has connected with more than 14.35 crore youth and 11.33 crore women, reflecting its expanding outreach among key sections of society. More than 2 lakh citizens have also enrolled as Nasha Mukti Mitr, strengthening community participation in the collective effort to build a drug-free India.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Abhiyaan was initially launched in 272 districts identified as particularly vulnerable to substance use, that was subsequently expanded to 372 districts in August 2022 and extended to all districts of the country with effect from 15 August 2023.

He said over the past six years, NMBA has evolved from an initiative driven by institutional participation into a community-led movement, with States, districts, educational institutions, civil society organisations and local stakeholders actively contributing to its implementation.

The Official said the Campaign has reached over 35.88 crore people as on date, marking a significant expansion from approximately 1.4 crore people reached in 2021. Its growing footprint reflects sustained efforts towards awareness generation, community mobilisation and encouraging citizens to actively participate in the movement against substance abuse, he further said.

The Official noted that more than 34.07 lakh awareness activities have been conducted in educational institutions, engaging students and young people in discussions on the harmful consequences of substance use.

These activities aim to promote informed choices, encourage healthy lifestyles and strengthen awareness about substance abuse prevention among the younger generation, he added.

He said the NMBA’s expansion is rooted in the need to address substance dependence as a complex psycho-social and medical challenge affecting individuals, families and communities.

The Official informed the first National Survey on the Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India, conducted in 2018, highlighted the scale of the challenge, indicating that more than 7 crore people in the country were affected by substance use disorders, including nearly 1.2 crore children and 58 lakh women.

Recognising the need for a comprehensive and sustained response, the Ministry launched NMBA as the flagship awareness initiative under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), which focuses on prevention, treatment and rehabilitation, the Official said.

Alongside awareness generation, the Ministry has strengthened the treatment and counselling ecosystem under NAPDDR, the Official noted.

Emphasizing that the expansion of these services highlights the importance of accessible treatment, timely intervention and sustained rehabilitation in addressing substance dependence, the Official said the number of persons seeking treatment and counselling has increased from 2.08 lakh in 2020-21 to over 9.11 lakh in 2025-26, reflecting the growing reach and utilisation of support services. The total number of District De-Addiction Centres in the country is now 198 as on date, he added.

The Official further said a key component of NMBA is the Nasha Mukti Mitr initiative, which encourages citizens to become active participants in the movement against substance abuse.

With more than 2 lakh citizens enrolled as Nasha Mukti Mitr as on 12 November 2026, the initiative is fostering a network of community volunteers who contribute to awareness generation, encourage individuals to seek assistance and support the creation of drug-free communities, he added.

Through sustained awareness campaigns, strengthened treatment and rehabilitation services and active citizen participation, the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan continues to advance the vision of a healthier, informed and drug-free society.

2335428.title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Inaugurate 45th India International Trade Fair on November 13
2335428.body_html:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal to Inaugurate 45th India International Trade Fair on November 13
45th India International Trade Fair to be Held at Bharat Mandapam from November 14–27, 2026
IITF 2026 to Bring Together 32 States/UTs and 11 Countries, Featuring Over 3,500 Exhibitors Across 17 Halls to Showcase India's Development and Heritage
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 4:10PM by PIB Delhi

The 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 14 to 27 November 2026. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, will inaugurate the Fair as the Chief Guest on 13 November 2026. The inauguration ceremony will also feature an Odissi performance by Padma Shri awardee Guru Madhavi Mudgal and her group.

Themed ‘Vikas aur Virasat’, IITF 2026 will bring together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad across 17 halls, covering over 1,00,000 square metres of exhibition space. The Fair will witness participation from 32 States and Union Territories and 51 Central Ministries, Government Departments, PSUs and Public Sector Banks. Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh are the Partner States, while Assam, Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal are the Focus States. The participating States and UTs will showcase their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, culture, tourism potential and development initiatives.

International participation will include 11 countries, with pavilions featuring exhibitors from Thailand, Iran, Ghana, Nepal, Afghanistan, the UAE, Turkey, China, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, providing opportunities for international business engagement and trade linkages.

Chairman, India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), Shri Jawed Ashraf, said that IITF 2026 will celebrate India's progress, diversity and heritage, with a special focus on youth through around 600 start-ups at the Hall of Inspiration and district-level crafts, cuisine and culture at the ODOP Pavilion.

Visitors will find country pavilions in Hall 1, Partner and Focus States, Central Ministries, PSUs and Public Sector Banks in Halls 2 to 5, and a wide range of consumer categories across Halls 8 to 14. These will include electronics, consumer durables, textiles, footwear, kitchen equipment, processed food, spices, agricultural produce, handicrafts, home furniture, cosmetics and jewellery.

IITF 2026 will introduce new experiences for businesses and visitors alike. The Hall of Inspiration in Hall 14 will showcase around 600 Indian start-ups across deep-tech, agri-tech, drones, space, healthcare and edtech, providing young enterprises with visibility and opportunities to connect with wider markets.

The One District One Product (ODOP) Pavilion will feature participation from 21 States and showcase signature crafts, cuisine, culture and products from districts across the country, highlighting local enterprise, traditional skills and the artisans behind them.

Playverse@Mandapam will offer an immersive and interactive digital experience combining entertainment and education, designed particularly to engage young visitors and families. Together, these initiatives reflect the spirit of ‘Vikas aur Virasat’, bringing India's technological progress, entrepreneurship and traditional strengths onto one platform.

A world-class food court featuring more than 90 outlets will serve Indian and international cuisines, with an emphasis on food quality, hygiene, zero-waste practices and reduced plastic usage.

Beyond its role as a major trade exhibition, IITF continues to strengthen market access for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), start-ups and small traders by providing opportunities to showcase products, connect with potential buyers and explore new markets. ITPO is also facilitating the participation of Indian start-ups at international platforms such as VivaTech in Paris and the upcoming Singapore FinTech Festival, creating opportunities for global exposure and collaboration. The initiative aims to encourage entrepreneurship across the country, including the growing start-up ecosystem in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

Reflecting the growing scale of Bharat Mandapam, the venue will feature LED mesh installations measuring approximately 1,000 square metres each at Hall 1 and Hall 14, alongside plans for around 100 LED screens across the complex, with more than 30 expected to be installed during the Fair. ITPO is also working towards developing Bharat Mandapam as a year-round destination for exhibitions, cultural programmes and public engagement, including a proposed cultural hub with a seating capacity of approximately 2,000.

To ensure a seamless and comfortable experience for visitors, exhibitors, delegates and media representatives, ITPO has put in place a range of dedicated support facilities across the venue. A dedicated Media Lounge will provide workspace for journalists, while a Protocol Lounge will facilitate hospitality for VIPs and dignitaries. Additional arrangements include internal mobility assistance, shuttle services, golf carts, designated cab and parking zones, B2B networking facilities, exhibitor assistance and lost-and-found services.

Food court operations will be subject to round-the-clock monitoring, with prescribed food safety, hygiene and food-handling standards applicable to all outlets, including State-operated stalls. Security arrangements, supported by Delhi Police and ITPO, particularly for the international pavilions in Hall 1, along with medical centres, first-aid facilities and emergency response services, will further strengthen visitor safety and convenience throughout the Fair.

Complementing the exhibition, 87 cultural performances, recitals and shows across seven venues will celebrate India's diversity, spanning classical and folk traditions and featuring acclaimed masters alongside young and upcoming talent. Highlights include The Manganiyar Seduction, Tal Fry, Hariharan & Prithvi Gandharva, Shahzad Ali, Salim–Sulaiman and Ruhaniyat, featuring performers from Nigeria, with tickets available on BookMyShow. Other cultural performances from 19 States and organisations will be free with IITF entry.

The first five days, from 14 to 18 November, will be Business Days reserved for B2B visitors, and the Fair will open to the general public from 19 to 27 November. Fair timings will be from 10:00 AM to 7:30 PM, with general public entry until 5:30 PM. Entry tickets can be booked at booking.indiatradefair.com, through the official IITF 2026 mobile app, or offline at 55 DMRC Metro stations. Season tickets are available for both Business Days and General Days. Senior citizens and persons with disabilities can enter free on General Days with a valid government-issued ID. General visitors can enter through Gate Nos. 3 and 4 on Bhairon Road and Gate Nos. 6 and 10 on Mathura Road.

2335423.title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh’s visit to Italy begins with follow-up on Special Strategic Partnership decided during PM Modi’s visit in May 2026
2335423.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh’s visit to Italy begins with follow-up on Special Strategic Partnership decided during PM Modi’s visit in May 2026
India and Italy to deepen scientific cooperation through bilateral engagements, Science & Innovation Dialogue and institutional partnerships
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian delegation led by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State for PMO, Department of Atomic Energy, Department of Space, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Dr. Jitendra Singh, began its official visit to Italy with engagements aimed at taking forward the Special Strategic Partnership decided during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit in May 2026, with particular emphasis on strengthening bilateral cooperation in Science, Technology and Innovation.

The initial interaction with representatives of the scientific fraternity and officials of the Embassy of India reaffirmed the traditional relationship between the two countries and the importance of further reinforcing bilateral scientific and technological cooperation.

The Minister's visit from November 11 to 15, 2026, includes a series of high-level bilateral engagements and institutional interactions aimed at providing further momentum to India-Italy scientific collaboration.

As part of the India-Italy Science & Technology Dialogue 2026, Dr. Jitendra Singh is scheduled to hold a meeting with the Italian Minister of University and Research on November 12. The Minister will also participate in the Second Science & Innovation Dialogue with Italian Minister of University and Research Anna Maria Bernini. The engagement will provide an important platform for taking forward scientific and innovation cooperation between the two countries.

The Indian delegation will undertake visits to leading science and technology institutions in Trieste on November 13, including the Elettra Synchrotron Facility, ICTP and ICGEB. The visits are part of the programme to familiarise the delegation with the scientific and research facilities and explore avenues for institutional interaction and cooperation.

The Minister's programme also includes an event marking World Diabetes Day at the Embassy of India in Rome on November 14, followed by an interaction with the Indian community in Italy.

The Indian delegation includes Ms. Vani Rao, Ambassador of India to Italy; Mr. Gaurav Gandhi, Deputy Chief of Mission, Embassy of India; Dr. Praveenkumar Somasundaram, Head (IC), Department of Science and Technology; Dr. Dhananjay Tiwary, Global Innovations (Scientific Decision Unit), Department of Science and Technology; Mr. Rajeev Kumar Choudhary, APS to the Minister; Ms. Lakshmi Swaminathan, First Secretary, Embassy of India; Mr. Anuj Jain, ASO, Embassy of India; and Ms. Silvia Buffa, Local Staff, Embassy of India.

The delegation also includes representatives of India's research institutions, academic centres and innovation ecosystem, including Dr. R. Vijay, Director, International Advanced Research Centre for Powder Metallurgy and New Materials (ARCI), Hyderabad; Prof. Sanjay Behari, Director, Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology, Thiruvananthapuram; Prof. Venu Gopal Achanta, Director, National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi; and Prof. Vibha Tandon, Director, Indian Institute of Chemical Biology, Kolkata. The innovation and technology ecosystem is represented by Prof. Kasturi Saha, Project Director, Qmet Tech Foundation, IIT Bombay; Dr. Ashutosh Agnihotri, CEO, Incubator & Technopark, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kanpur; and Dr. Satya Dash, Chief Executive Officer, IKP Knowledge Park, Hyderabad.

The participation of senior representatives from government, research institutions, academic centres and technology incubators reflects the broad institutional representation in India's scientific engagement with Italy.

2335399.title: Ministry of Jal Shakti Extends Timeline for Citizen Feedback on Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) 2.0
2335399.body_html:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Ministry of Jal Shakti Extends Timeline for Citizen Feedback on Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) 2.0
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Jal Shakti has extended the timeline for submitting Citizen Feedback on the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) 2.0 Portal until 30 November 2026. The Citizen Feedback Portal has been open to the public since 26 January 2026, providing citizens across the country an opportunity to share their feedback on water conservation, rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and storage works reported under the JSJB 2.0 initiative. The extension will enable citizens to continue providing feedback on the artificial recharge and storage structures created under the initiative.

The second phase of JSJB has marked a significant milestone in advancing the nationwide water conservation movement envisioned by the Prime Minister on 6 September 2024 at Surat, Gujarat, with the objective of transforming water conservation into a true Jan Andolan through active public participation. As of 31 May 2026, more than 1.5 crore rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge, water conservation and storage structures have been reported across the country under the initiative.

The Citizen Feedback mechanism on the JSJB 2.0 Portal seeks to further strengthen Jan Bhagidari by enabling citizens to provide feedback on the reported works. Through their valuable inputs, citizens can help identify maintenance requirements, monitor the functionality of structures and contribute to improving their long-term effectiveness.

Feedback from citizens will also support the verification and assessment of assets reported under the initiative. Since recognition is provided to Districts, States/UTs and other stakeholders based on the number of artificial recharge and storage works completed under the initiative, citizen participation in feedback is particularly significant. The mechanism is expected to enhance the quality and credibility of reporting, promote transparency in implementation, and encourage Districts and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) to ensure proper maintenance and sustained functionality of the structures created.

Citizens and stakeholders may submit their suggestions and feedback through the JSJB 2.0 Portal at:

https://jsjb.mowr.gov.in/DashboardJsjb.aspx

Through this initiative, the Ministry aims to strengthen community ownership of water conservation structures and further advance the nationwide movement towards sustainable water management and water security.

2335376.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA INTERACTS WITH MERITORIOUS STUDENTS FROM EKLAVYA MODEL RESIDENTIAL SCHOOLS
2335376.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA INTERACTS WITH MERITORIOUS STUDENTS FROM EKLAVYA MODEL RESIDENTIAL SCHOOLS
AIM HIGH AND STRIVE TO REALIZE YOUR DREAMS WITH DEDICATION, DISCIPLINE, AND SELF-CONFIDENCE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU TO STUDENTS
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 2:56PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu interacted with a group of meritorious students from Eklavya Model Residential Schools at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (November 12, 2026). This interaction was organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs as part of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, observed every year to commemorate the birth anniversary of Bhagwan Birsa Munda.

 

Addressing the students, the President said that the nation is moving forward to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat by the year 2047. The development of every region of the country and every section of society is essential. The Eklavya Model Residential Schools are not only providing quality education to tribal students but also offering them opportunities to hone their multifaceted talents. She stated that there is no dearth of talent in our country. What the students require are the right opportunities, a conducive environment, and proper guidance. She was happy to note that the ratio of boys and girls in Eklavya Model Residential Schools is equal. She said that it is a testament to country’s progress toward inclusive development.

 

The President urged students to aim high and strive to realize their dreams with dedication, discipline, and self-confidence. She said that education should not only be a means to earn a livelihood for themselves; rather, their goal should also be to create employment opportunities through their knowledge. She underlined that when our youth become job creators, the country’s inclusive development will gain further momentum.

 

The President advised students to be well-informed about current affairs and the changes taking place in the country and the world. This will help them develop logical thinking and analytical skills. She advised students that whenever they visit their village, they should share with their family members, relatives, and neighbours, the knowledge of current affairs and information about public welfare schemes being implemented by the government. Such efforts on their part will benefit their family and society, and will also add greater meaning and purpose to their education.
