2335351.title: Element of Surprise, Technological Superiority & Jointness key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Raksha Mantri at Air Force Commanders’ Conference
2335351.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
Element of Surprise, Technological Superiority & Jointness key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Raksha Mantri at Air Force Commanders’ Conference
Shri Rajnath Singh launches in-house Al applications developed by UDAAN for operations, administration & aerospace safety
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 2:04PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to strengthen and sustain both offensive and defensive dimensions of the ‘element of surprise’ to maintain operational readiness against conventional and emerging threats arising from rapid technological advancements and the evolving nature of modern warfare. Addressing the Air Force Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi on November 12, 2026, he emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities, enhance integration among systems and identify potential threats before they unfold.

“Our Defence Forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy. Surprise can manifest in various forms, both conventional and electronic. Our intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened and operational preparedness enhanced to ensure that our personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge,” said the Raksha Mantri.

Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role. Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, he stated that drones and air defence systems have emerged as critical components of modern warfare. He exhorted the Commanders to remain prepared for emerging challenges such as kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations.

Raksha Mantri called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space. He emphasised that enhanced preparedness in these domains would strengthen the ability to address future challenges. “Victory in future conflicts would depend not merely on the number of aircraft, but also on technological sophistication, speed of response and precision of preparations,” he said, urging the Commanders to make these emerging challenges a core priority, with focus on integrating them into institutional thinking, planning and operational processes.

Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the Defence Forces are undergoing a transformative phase, encompassing reforms in wide-ranging areas, including organisational structures, jointness & integration, and operational concepts. He added that the changing security environment necessitated continuous adaptation and a forward-looking approach to military preparedness.

Raksha Mantri commended the IAF for effectively implementing its doctrines and operational methods during and after Operation Sindoor, appreciating the professionalism, restraint & judgement demonstrated by the air warriors in successfully executing their assigned tasks. He stated that the lessons learnt during the operation were clearly reflected in the IAF's evolving operational procedures, particularly through the increased emphasis on drones and air defence systems, which are vital to national security. These lessons, he added, are shaping the pace and direction of the transformative changes underway in the Defence Forces.

Highlighting the coordinated and complementary contributions of all the three Services effectively demonstrated during Op Sindoor, Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Defence Forces for the synergy and integration. He underlined that jointness and integrated efforts must continue to guide military planning and operational execution.

While appreciating the IAF for enhancing the skills and capabilities of its personnel in keeping with rapid technological advancements, Raksha Mantri urged the Commanders to sustain efforts towards training air warriors in emerging technologies. He underscored the importance of leveraging the technological knowledge and expertise of young recruits, stating that their capabilities could contribute significantly to stronger decision-making and organisational development.

On the Second Tour of Duty for Agniveers, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that the decision was taken following feedback received from the Defence Forces, reiterating the Government's commitment to incorporating the Services’ suggestions into policy decisions. He expressed confidence that the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ initiative would contribute to further bolstering the three Services.

As part of this conference, Raksha Mantri launched a suite of Artificial Intelligence (Al) applications developed in-house by the IAF's Al Centre of Excellence of the Unit for Digitisation, Automation, Artificial Intelligence and Application Networking (UDAAN). The applications will be utilised to automate and expedite tasks across the domains of operations, administration and aerospace safety, and are deployed on the IAF’s secure network. The initiative marks a significant milestone in the IAF's pursuit of technology-driven transformation and enhanced operational capabilities.

The inaugural session was also attended by Raksha Rajya Mantri Shri Sanjay Seth, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary (Defence Production) Shri Sanjeev Kumar, and Secretary (Defence Finance) Shri Vishvajit Sahay. Air Officers Commanding-in-Chief of all Commands of IAF, all Principal Staff Officers & all Director Generals. The two-day conference is being attended by the Air Officers Commanding-in-Chief of all Commands of IAF, all Principal Staff Officers & all Director Generals.

The theme of this year’s conference is ‘The Year of Empowerment: Maximising Efficiency Through Decentralisation’. The conference provides a forum to the senior leadership of the IAF to discuss critical issues pertaining to operations, maintenance and administration.

2335323.title: INSA endorses G20 Science Academies’ Joint Statement, reaffirming commitment to science-led solutions to global challenges
2335323.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
INSA endorses G20 Science Academies’ Joint Statement, reaffirming commitment to science-led solutions to global challenges
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 12:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian National Science Academy (INSA), an institution of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), actively participated in the S20 2026 process and endorsed the Joint S20 Statement, released by the science academies of the G20 countries, on November 10, 2026, under the leadership of the U.S. National Academy of Sciences (NAS), as part of the Science20 (S20) engagement process.

Through its endorsement of the Joint Statement, which highlights opportunities for governments to harness advanced technologies to strengthen preparedness and response to natural hazards and disasters, INSA reaffirmed its commitment to promoting science-based approaches to address global challenges.

The Statement, developed through consultations and contributions from science academies across G20 nations, is intended to inform discussions within their respective governments. It will also be presented to the G20 ahead of the G20 Summit scheduled to be held in Miami, Florida, in December 2026.

Natural hazards such as heavy rainfall, earthquakes, droughts, wildfires, and extreme heat and cold events are increasingly posing significant challenges to populations, ecosystems and economies. The Statement highlights the potential of emerging technologies, including Earth observation, remote sensing, early warning systems, digital twins, drone technologies and artificial intelligence, to improve decision-making and strengthen disaster preparedness and resilience.

It also recognises that the effective application of these technologies depends on addressing gaps in data availability, infrastructure, technical capacity and institutional coordination, while ensuring equitable access and readiness for deployment.

The Joint S20 Statement identifies five key areas for action. These include strengthening data collection and understanding of risk, enabling safe, secure and equitable access to data and technology, building local skills and capacity and designing context-specific solutions, strengthening human decision-making and governance, and advancing international and cross-sector collaboration.

The Statement underscores that technology should enhance, rather than replace, human expertise and that effective disaster resilience requires locally relevant solutions supported by strong scientific collaboration and institutional partnerships.

As India's national science academy, INSA will endeavour to bring the recommendations of the Statement to the attention of relevant national stakeholders and facilitate engagement among scientific experts, research institutions and government agencies. Through its national and international networks, INSA will continue to encourage interdisciplinary research, knowledge exchange and collaboration in areas relevant to disaster preparedness and resilience.

The S20 2026 process has provided an important platform for science academies across G20 nations to exchange perspectives and contribute collectively to addressing a shared global challenge. INSA looks forward to continuing this engagement under the leadership of the Royal Society in 2027.

KEY AREAS OF ACTION

  1. Strengthening data collection and understanding of risk: Improving observation systems and the availability of reliable data on hazards, exposure and vulnerability to support preparedness, response and recovery.
  2. Enabling safe, secure and equitable access to data and technology: Promoting data sharing, common standards, interoperability and resilient systems, while respecting national responsibilities for data governance, safety, security and privacy.
  3. Building local skills and capacity and designing context-specific solutions: Investing in education, workforce development, training and community engagement to ensure that technologies are adapted to local needs and can be effectively sustained.
  4. Strengthening human decision-making and governance: Ensuring that advanced technologies complement human expertise through appropriate oversight, local validation, transparency, accountability and effective communication of risks.
  5. Advancing international and cross-sector collaboration: Encouraging sustained partnerships among governments, academia, industry, civil society, communities and international organisations, with an emphasis on co-producing knowledge and technology.

2335322.title: TDB-DST signs agreement with Astrome for ₹64.05 crore RDI support to develop sovereign space-based AI-ELINT constellation
2335322.body_html:
Ministry of Science & Technology
TDB-DST signs agreement with Astrome for ₹64.05 crore RDI support to develop sovereign space-based AI-ELINT constellation
Project to advance indigenous electronic intelligence, AI-based ground processing and inter-satellite communication technologies towards TRL-9
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening India's indigenous space-based intelligence and advanced satellite technology capabilities, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Astrome Technologies Pvt Ltd, Bengaluru, Karnataka for financial support of ₹64.05 crore under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The project, with a total project cost of ₹128.11 crore, aims to develop a sovereign space-based Artificial Intelligence-enabled Electronic Intelligence (AI-ELINT) constellation for national security applications. The programme seeks to advance critical technologies from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-9, with financial support being provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).

As the strategic importance of space-based systems continues to grow, the ability to develop and deploy indigenous technologies for intelligence gathering, communication and data processing has become increasingly important. Space-based constellations can provide persistent coverage over large geographical areas, while advances in artificial intelligence are enabling faster processing and interpretation of complex data. Astrome's project seeks to address this emerging technology requirement through the development of an integrated AI-ELINT satellite constellation. The programme brings together three key technology components: an Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) payload, AI-based ground processing software, and      inter-satellite communication links.

The project envisages the development and progressive deployment of AI-ELINT microsatellites in the 50 kg class, designed to operate as part of a constellation architecture. The proposed system aims to provide enhanced coverage and increased observation frequency, supporting persistent surveillance      of identified areas of interest. The ELINT payload forms a key component of the proposed system and is intended to support the detection and analysis of signals across a broad frequency range. Complementing the satellite hardware, the AI-based ground processing software is designed to enable the efficient processing and analysis of information generated by the constellation.

The project also includes the development of an inter-satellite communication link, an important capability for enabling satellites within a constellation to exchange information and operate as an integrated network. The proposed constellation architecture is designed around satellites operating in a low Earth orbit, with an objective of progressively increasing coverage and revisit capability as additional satellites are deployed. The programme will undertake technology development, engineering, integration, testing and validation activities required to advance the core systems towards TRL-9.

The project falls under the Deep Technology sector, with Space Technology as its sub-sector. It represents the convergence of several frontier technologies—satellite engineering, electronic intelligence, artificial intelligence and secure space-based communications.

Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, Technology Development Board, said, “India's growing capabilities in space technology are creating new opportunities to develop advanced systems that combine indigenous engineering with artificial intelligence and next-generation communications. Building such complex technology platforms requires sustained innovation, rigorous validation and long-term investment. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting Indian enterprises working on frontier technologies that can strengthen the country's strategic technology capabilities. The project with Astrome reflects the potential of India's deep-tech ecosystem to develop sophisticated space-based solutions for emerging national requirements.”

An authorised representative of Astrome Technologies said, “The support from TDB under the RDI Fund will help us accelerate the development and integration of critical technologies for our AI-enabled space-based intelligence programme. By bringing together indigenous ELINT payloads, AI-based data processing and inter-satellite communications, we aim to develop an integrated constellation capability that can address emerging requirements in the space and national security domains. This partnership will support our efforts to advance these technologies towards TRL-9.”

2335313.title: Naturopathy Day 2026: Scientific Research Strengthens India's Nature-Based Healthcare Ecosystem
2335313.body_html:
AYUSH
Naturopathy Day 2026: Scientific Research Strengthens India's Nature-Based Healthcare Ecosystem
9th National Naturopathy Day to be observed on 18 November at Nagamangala, Karnataka, under the theme ‘Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 12:12PM by PIB Delhi

Naturopathy in India is gradually moving beyond its traditional association with nature cure towards a more structured ecosystem of scientific research, clinical evaluation and preventive healthcare. With growing attention to lifestyle-related disorders, obesity, stress and healthy ageing, its emphasis on nutrition, natural therapies and lifestyle modification is finding renewed relevance.

The 9th National Naturopathy Day will be observed on 18 November 2026 at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy (CRIYN), Nagamangala, Karnataka, under the theme “Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat.” The day is observed to promote awareness of naturopathy and its role in health promotion, disease prevention and the adoption of healthy lifestyles. This year's theme emphasises preventive and promotive healthcare through appropriate dietary practices, physical activity, yoga, stress management and other evidence-informed naturopathic approaches. It also seeks to strengthen public awareness about obesity prevention and lifestyle-related disorders, encouraging individuals and communities to adopt healthier and more sustainable lifestyles. The observance aligns with the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister for a Fit and Healthy India, emphasising preventive healthcare, healthy living and collective responsibility towards public well-being.

Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, reiterated, “Naturopathy encourages us to recognise the close relationship between lifestyle, nature and overall health. Our emphasis is on strengthening its scientific foundation through credible research, quality education and responsible integration with conventional healthcare. This approach can contribute to preventive healthcare while advancing the vision of a Fit and Healthy India.”

Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, highlighted, “Scientific validation is essential for strengthening the credibility and wider application of naturopathy. Through CCRYN and other institutions, we are encouraging systematic research, clinical evaluation and collaboration so that naturopathic practices can be assessed through appropriate scientific methods and translated into responsible healthcare approaches.”

The Central Council for Research in Yoga and Naturopathy (CCRYN) published Various research papers in peer-reviewed journals during FY 2025–26, while five research councils under the Ministry collectively published 653 papers. The Council also has 22 units across India, reflecting its institutional presence in research, education and outreach.

India's institutional infrastructure has expanded through postgraduate institutes dedicated to Yoga and Naturopathy education and research, along with 200-bed Yoga and Naturopathy hospitals at Jhajjar in Haryana and Nagamangala in Karnataka. The Bachelor of Naturopathy and Yogic Sciences (BNYS) College at Nisarg Gram, National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune, the first such college established under the Central Government, further strengthens this ecosystem through academic and clinical training, research-based learning and practical exposure in naturopathy and yoga, preparing graduates for careers in healthcare, research, academics and private practice.

The National Institute of Naturopathy (NIN), Pune, has further strengthened its research framework through a dedicated Research Department and an Institutional Ethics Committee registered with the Department of Health Research. Its initiatives include research methodology workshops, Good Clinical Practice training, observational studies, systematic reviews and collaborative research.

The growing research emphasis is particularly relevant as naturopathy promotes healthy dietary practices, physical activity, adequate rest and stress management. These lifestyle measures can support preventive healthcare across different age groups and contribute to greater awareness of lifestyle-related risk factors.

On National Naturopathy Day, the focus remains on strengthening the scientific foundation of naturopathy, expanding institutional capacity and encouraging healthier lifestyles. Through sustained research, quality education and public participation, India aims to further develop a credible and accessible naturopathy ecosystem that complements its wider preventive healthcare efforts and contributes to the vision of ‘Prakrutik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’.

2335306.title: One Nation, One Ration Card
2335306.body_html:
PIB Backgrounder
One Nation, One Ration Card
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 11:48AM by PIB Delhi

Food Security Without Boundaries

 

From Portability to Inclusion: Transforming Foodgrain Access

The One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) scheme was launched in 2019 by the Department of Food & Public Distribution. It is a major reform of the Public Distribution System (PDS), enabling nationwide portability of ration cards and beneficiaries covered under the National Food Security Act (NFSA). NFSA establishes legal entitlements for subsidized food grains, while TPDS distributes these grains to eligible beneficiaries. Under Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) reforms, ONORC uses technology to enable beneficiaries to access their entitled foodgrains anywhere in the country. The initiative has strengthened social protection for migrant populations and advanced the vision of a more integrated, inclusive, and beneficiary-centric welfare delivery system.

  • Enables access to foodgrain entitlements from any Fair Price Shop across the country without needing a new ration card. Makes foodgrain entitlements portable across States.
  • Supports migrant workers and families in accessing PDS benefits after changing residence.
  • Ensures subsidized foodgrain access for beneficiaries wherever they reside.
  • Strengthens PDS access for NFSA beneficiaries across the country.

 

Portability Milestones

ONORC has transformed PDS by making foodgrain access seamless, portable, and nationwide.

  • ONORC has been implemented across all 36 States/UTs, covering 100% of PMGKAY beneficiaries.
  • ONORC facilitates approximately 3.27 crore portability transactions every month.
  • Since its inception, it has recorded over 233 crore inter-state and intra-state portability transactions, distributing more than 614 LMT of foodgrains.

Strengthening Transparency and Delivery Under PDS

The Government has complemented ration portability with digital authentication, data-driven targeting and technology-enabled distribution to improve transparency and last-mile delivery.

 

  • 100% Digitisation: Ration card and beneficiary databases are 100% digitised across all States/UTs as of October 2026, covering around 78.65 crore beneficiaries, and are accessible on public transparency portals of States/UTs. Out of 20.51 crore ration cards in the Central System, 98.8% (20.27 crore) have been Aadhaar-seeded. The total number of beneficiaries seeded with Aadhaar stands at 76.97 crore.  As on 30 September 2026, e-KYC has been done in respect of 71.52 crore beneficiaries i.e., 91% of total beneficiaries.
  • Transparent Grievance Redressal: Transparency portals, online grievance systems and toll-free helplines operate across all States/UTs.
  • Computerised Supply Chain: Online foodgrain allocation is implemented nationwide, while supply chains are computerised in 31 States/UTs.
  • ePoS-enabled FPSs: Out of a total of 5.51 lakh Fair Price Shops (FPSs), 99.8% (5.50 lakh) are operational with e-PoS devices.
  • Rightful Targeting & De-duplication: Advanced Aadhaar and PDS data analytics flagged 5.95 crore suspicious records, leading to the deletion of 2.58 crore duplicate or ineligible entries for Rightful Targeting V1. Rightful Targeting Version 3.63 flagged and 68 lakhs Deleted.
  • NIRMAL & SAKSHAM: Under the Scheme for Assistance in Ration Transport and Handling-Income with Automation in PDS (SARTHAK-PDS) umbrella Scheme, these initiatives strengthen data architecture/analytics (NIRMAL) and real-time data integration, including Vehicle Location Tracking Systems (SAKSHAM), from procurement to distribution. SARTHAK-PDS provides financial support for intra-State movement, handling, and FPS dealer margins, while creating a unified, citizen-centric, and interoperable PDS architecture. The scheme aims to ensure last-mile delivery, minimise leakages, and strengthen food security under NFSA through 31 March 2031.
  • Scheme for Modernisation and Reforms through Technology in Public Distribution System (SMART-PDS): Under the SARTHAK-PDS, SMART-PDS digitally integrates ration cards, distribution, supply chains and grievance redressal, while addressing State/UT-level technology gaps through an integrated central system.

Mera Ration App: Foodgrain Access at Your Fingertips

As part of technology-driven TPDS reforms under ONORC, the Department launched the Mera Ration mobile application. Available in 13 languages, the app helps beneficiaries access important ration-related information and services.

Key features include:

  • Check monthly foodgrain entitlement details
  • View past transaction details
  • Verify Aadhaar-seeding status
  • Check eligibility for national portability
  • Register voluntarily for ONORC
  • Locate nearby Fair Price Shops (FPSs) using GPS
  • Navigate to the nearest FPS through the map

 

Mera Ration app helps beneficiaries, particularly migrants, locate nearby FPSs and access their foodgrain entitlements in a new area.

Toward Inclusive and Dignified Food Security

ONORC has transformed the Public Distribution System by making foodgrain access portable, nationwide and technology-enabled. Its implementation across all 36 States/UTs, along with extensive portability transactions, reflects its growing role in strengthening food security.  With digitalised beneficiary databases, ePoS-enabled Fair Price Shops, SARTHAK-PDS framework, and the Mera Ration app, the system is becoming more transparent, integrated, and beneficiary-centric.

Collectively, these reforms are strengthening last-mile delivery and ensuring that food security reaches beneficiaries wherever they live and work.

2335304.title: Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Receive Devout Homage from Nearly 50,000 Devotees Across Arunachal Pradesh So Far
2335304.body_html:
Ministry of Culture
Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha Receive Devout Homage from Nearly 50,000 Devotees Across Arunachal Pradesh So Far
Exposition continues at TGL Monastery, Bomdila, until November 13 and at Golden Pagoda, Namsai, from November 14 to 20, 2026
Posted On: 12 NOV 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi

The exposition of the Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha in Arunachal Pradesh has evoked deep devotion and religious reverence, with nearly 50,000 devotees having visited the exposition across the State so far to pay their respects to the holy relics. As the exposition enters its second week, it continues to provide  an opportunity for devotees from different parts of Arunachal Pradesh to offer prayers, seek blessings and experience the spiritual significance of the Sacred Relics.

The exposition commenced at Gaden Namgyal Lhatse Monastery (Tawang Monastery) on October 31, 2026, and concluded there on November 7, 2026. During this period, more than 31,000 devotees from Tawang and neighbouring areas visited the monastery  to offer prayers and pay their respects to the Sacred Relics.

Following the conclusion of the exposition at Tawang, the Sacred Relics arrived at Thubchog Gatsel Ling (TGL) Monastery, also known as Lower Gompa, in Bomdila, on November 8, 2026. The exposition has received an encouraging response from the local community and devotees from neighbouring areas. People have been visiting the monastery in large numbers to offer prayers and pay their respects to the Sacred Relics with deep faith and devotion. The participation of the local community reflects the strong Buddhist traditions and spiritual heritage of the region.

The public exposition at TGL Monastery, Bomdila, will continue until November 13, 2026, providing devotees with further opportunities to have darshan of the Sacred Relics. Following the conclusion of the Bomdila exposition, the Sacred Relics will proceed to the Golden Pagoda in Namsai, where they will be open for public veneration from November 14 to 20, 2026.

The exposition is being organised by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the National Museum, New Delhi, the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, and the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC), New Delhi. The initiative reflects the Government of India's continued commitment to preserving and promoting India's rich Buddhist heritage and strengthening the country's cultural and spiritual ties with Buddhist communities.

2335224.title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS SWACHH SURVEKSHAN AWARDS
2335224.body_html:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA PRESENTS SWACHH SURVEKSHAN AWARDS
CLEANLINESS IS NOT MERELY A MATTER OF MAINTAINING THE AESTHETIC APPEAL OF PUBLIC SPACES; IT IS ALSO AN INDICATOR OF OUR HEALTH, SOCIAL CONSCIOUSNESS, AND ADMINISTRATIVE ACCOUNTABILITY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:52PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 in New Delhi today (November 11, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that a single organization alone cannot achieve the goals of cleanliness. It requires the participation of every citizen, every household, every community, and every city. She underlined that cleanliness is not merely a matter of maintaining the aesthetic appeal of public spaces. It is also an indicator of our health, social consciousness, and administrative accountability. It is a reflection of our habits at home too. 

The President said that every citizen, especially youth, women, Resident Welfare Associations and community organizations, should engage with various aspects of cleanliness. They should share their experiences and report any shortcomings, the resolution of which could help make our cities cleaner and healthier. This should foster an ongoing dialogue between the municipal administration and the citizens, thereby strengthening trust, transparency, and accountability.

 The President said that citizens are the best judges when it comes to assessing the cleanliness of their surroundings. Therefore, the use of citizen feedback should not be limited merely to surveys or rankings. Instead, this feedback should serve as a vital tool for improving municipal services and addressing local challenges.

 The President said that there is a need to develop effective, affordable and safe technologies in the field of sanitation. She was happy to note that various institutions, including several IITs and other scientific research organizations, are actively working in this direction.

 The President noted that several startups have emerged in the sanitation sector. She said that such enterprises can contribute significantly toward solving real-world sanitation challenges while also creating employment opportunities.

 The President said that there is a need to place special emphasis on enhancing the capacities of Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, as these are the fastest-growing urban centers. They have distinct needs and challenges. Their development should take place within a national framework designed to address their specific problems and challenges. She said planners in Tier-2 cities can learn from the issues faced by Tier-1 cities, and to do so, they should study the experiences of planners in Tier-1 cities.

 The Swachh Survekshan Awards, organized by the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, honours India’s cleanest cities and recognizes their outstanding contributions to Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban.

2335212.title: Sarbananda Sonowal Lays Foundation Stones for Projects Worth Rs 560 Crore at Visakhapatnam Port
2335212.ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
2335212.body_html:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Sarbananda Sonowal Lays Foundation Stones for Projects Worth Rs 560 Crore at Visakhapatnam Port
Sonowal Dedicates Port Promenade in Visakhapatnam to the nation, open for public
New Contracts to employ about 500 local people
Sonowal ties projects to PM Modi's vision of Citizens as Active Partners of development
It opens up the port to the city: Sonowal on the newly inaugurated Promenade
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal, in Visakhapatnam, dedicated a waterfront promenade at the Visakhapatnam Port to the public and laid foundation stones for four new projects, bringing the port’s package of new works to about Rs 560 crore.

The Rs 19 crore Port Promenade runs about 710 meters (2,330 feet) along the water from the Venkateswara Temple to the International Cruise Terminal and covers about 5.5 acres. The promenade gives residents a regulated, safe place to watch ships and port operations for the first time. "It opens up the port to the city," Sonowal said. "This project is dedicated to the people of Visakhapatnam.”

The promenade has a waterfront walkway and two view decks, one a Titanic-style viewpoint, along with a park, a public plaza, a children's play area, a food court and visitor parking. It was built on existing port land without affecting cargo operations. Its location beside the cruise terminal is also meant to add to the terminal's appeal for cruise passengers.

Sonowal tied the project to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of inclusive development, in which citizens are not just beneficiaries but active partners in building the nation. A port that was once closed to outsiders now invites residents in, he said, and the new terminal contracts will give about 500 local people jobs running its berths.

"Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision is a development in which every citizen has a place and a part to play," Sarbananda Sonowal said. "A port that opens its gates to the people, and gives local youth the work of running its berths, is that vision in action.”

Sonowal also laid foundation stones for three contracts to operate and maintain existing cargo terminals, together worth about Rs 580 crores. They cover the WQ-1 and WQ-1RE berths; WQ-2 and WQ-3; and EQ-3. Operators must mechanise the berths with cranes and conveyors, with environmental controls, and will employ about 500 local people. "Through these projects, VPA will secure assured cargo throughput and achieve optimum capacity utilisation in these berths," Sarbananda Sonowal said.

The Union Minister also laid the foundation stone for upgrading the port's sewage treatment plant from 10 million liters a day to 15 million liters, including a new 5 million-liter plant, at an estimated cost of about Rs 11 crores. Treated water is used for dust suppression, wetting roads and sprinkling at stockpile yards, and the upgrade supports the ministry's Harit Sagar green port initiative.

Sonowal said the port handled a record 91.17 million metric tons of cargo in the 2025-26 fiscal year, about 10% more than a year earlier and its fourth straight year of growth. From April 1 to Oct. 31, cargo rose by 4.44 million metric tons, or 8.88%, over the same period last year. "You must beat last year's target of 10% growth," Sonowal encouraged the port employees as he spoke and interacted with them.

The initiatives were launched as Sonowal is going to speak at the 31st CII Partnership Summit–2026, which the Andhra Pradesh government is hosting on November 12 and 13, which is themed under ‘Navigating New World Order: Trade, Technology, Trust.’

The port has taken up four Public-Private Partnership (PPP_ projects worth about Rs 800 crores, which are under construction and expected to be commissioned by 2027. It has one of the deepest container terminals among India's major ports, with a permissible draft of 16 meters, and is shifting to a landlord-port model to cut vessel turnaround time and logistics costs.

Sonowal credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership for transforming Indian ports into world-class facilities as the country works toward becoming a developed nation by 2047. He described the day's projects, from a public promenade to a cleaner sewage system, as examples of the Prime Minister's call for development that includes every section of society.

"When citizens are partners and not spectators, development lasts," Sonowal said. "That is the spirit of Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas, and it is the surest road to a Viksit Bharat by 2047.”

Sonowal also thanked Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and the state government for their support.

Visakhapatnam Lok Sabha member M. Sribharat, Rajya Sabha member Golla Babu Rao, Andhra Pradesh BJP president P.V.N. Madhav, legislators Ch. Vamsi Krishna Srinivas and P. Vishnu Kumar Raju, and port Chairperson Jasmeet Singh Bindra attended among other officials and employees of the port.

2335207.title: Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26
2335207.body_html:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26
President of India Smt. Droupadi Murmu Awards the Nation’s Cleanest Cities after the Swachh Survekshan 2025–26
AHMEDABAD (Mentor) – SANAND (Mentee), INDORE (Mentor) - DEPALPUR (Mentee) & TIRUPATI (Mentor) - KUPPAM (Mentee) rank top 3 in ‘Swachh Shehar Jodi category for accelerating urban waste management excellence
NAVI MUMBAI, SURAT & VIJAYAWADA Declared Top 3 in Clean Cities of Super Swachh League
GVMC VISAKHAPATNAM, JABALPUR and LUCKNOW Emerge as India’s top 3 Swachh Shehar in the Million Plus population category
This year awards were given for the first time to Swachh River Front Town, Swachh Coastal Town and Clean Himalayan City,
350+ ULBs jump 500 ranks to move up in Swachh Survekshan 2025-26
Smaller Cities Lead the Change: 1,700+ ULBs with population under 50k Improve Their Rankings Over 2024–25
State-Level Winners to Be Honoured in Award Ceremonies in respective States
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:31PM by PIB Delhi

 Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Hon’ble President of India, honoured India’s cleanest cities at the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025–26 held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, convened by the Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Winners were felicitated in the presence of Sh. Manohar Lal, Union Minister for MoHUA & Power and Shri Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for MoHUA. This year 60 national awards have been announced, under 5 categories:

  • Swachh Shehar Jodi (SSJ)
  • Clean Cities of Super Swachh League
  • Swachh Shehar in 5 population categories
  • Swachh River Front Town
  • Swachh Coastal Town
  • Clean Himalayan City
  • State First Swachh City

Speaking at the event, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Hon’ble President of India, underscored that cleanliness cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single institution alone and requires active participation from all stakeholders. She emphasized the importance of citizen participation, behavioural change, administrative accountability, and sustained public engagement. Highlighting the need to inculcate cleanliness values from an early age, she called for integrating issues such as plastic waste management into school curricula and fostering continuous dialogue with children and youth. The President noted that meaningful progress in sanitation is possible when citizens, local administrations, and sanitation workers work together, and when the on-ground suggestions of sanitation workers and citizen feedback are given due importance. She also appreciated the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative as a new dimension of collaborative learning, enabling cities to share innovations, test solutions, and support one another in achieving higher standards of urban cleanliness.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs Shri Manohar Lal said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Swachh Bharat Mission has evolved into a nationwide people's movement, transforming urban sanitation and encouraging greater citizen participation. Highlighting the progress achieved since 2014, he stated that urban waste processing has increased from 16% to 80%, while door-to-door waste collection coverage has risen from 44% to over 96%. He further noted that the remediation of legacy waste dumpsites has freed nearly 11,000 acres of urban land for productive use.

The Hon’ble Minister also encouraged States to conduct Swachh Survekshan competitions at the State level to rank cities and towns within their respective States, fostering healthy competition among Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and encouraging smaller towns to improve their cleanliness standards.

Shri Manohar Lal highlighted the growing scale and impact of Swachh Survekshan, which has expanded from 73 cities in 2016 to 4,751 cities in 2025–26. He informed that 2.70 crore citizens provided feedback during this year's survey, while over 1,700 smaller cities improved their rankings and more than 350 cities registered improvements of over 500 positions. Emphasising the importance of behavioural change, the Minister said that the real success of Swachh Survekshan lies not merely in improving rankings but in making cleanliness a permanent habit and collective responsibility. He also highlighted the participation of nearly 2.10 crore citizens in Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, the benefits extended to around 17 lakh SafaiMitras through over 33,000 special camps, and the participation of nearly 4 lakh children in Gyan Yatras.

The Minister further highlighted several new initiatives aimed at strengthening collaboration and encouraging excellence in urban sanitation. He stated that under the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative, 70 mentor cities have been paired with 191 mentee cities to facilitate knowledge-sharing and improve sanitation outcomes. He also referred to the introduction of special award categories for River Front Towns, Coastal Towns and Himalayan Cities, along with recognition across five population categories to ensure wider participation. Highlighting the PRAGATI-50 initiative, Shri Manohar Lal said that 50 cities would be developed as Model Clean Cities through technology-driven interventions and continuous monitoring. Congratulating all award-winning cities, urban local bodies and SafaiMitras, he reiterated the Government's commitment to making cleanliness an integral part of urban life and realising the vision of a Swachh and Viksit Bharat.

Sh. Satendra Singh, Secretary, DoUD, MoHUA, highlighted how Swachh Survekshan has, over the past decade, strengthened the assessment and improvement of urban sanitation services while driving tangible on-ground outcomes under the Mission. Secretary, MoHUA, further mentioned that Swachh Survekshan is much more than an assessment; it is the collective voice of millions of people committed to the vision of a Swachh Bharat. He said, “today is a celebration of the outstanding efforts made by our cities and citizens in advancing the cause of cleanliness.”

The Swachh Survekshan 2025–26 results reflect a strong upward momentum across urban India, with over 350 ULBs improving their position by more than 500 ranks. Smaller cities have emerged as key drivers of this transformation, as 1,700+ ULBs with populations below 50,000 population improved their rankings compared to 2024–25, demonstrating that sustained efforts and citizen participation are accelerating the Swachhata movement across towns of all sizes.

Showing excellence in collaborative efforts and peer-learning, Mentor city Ahmedabad & Mentee city Sanand, Mentor Indore & Mentee Depalpur and Mentor Tirupati & Mentee Kuppam, were declared the top-ranked jodis under Swachh Shehar Jodi award. The Top 3 Swachh Shehar Jodis have been identified based on the combined score of the Mentor City (SS 2024-25 awardee) and its paired Mentee City. It reflects the joint performance and collaborative efforts of both cities under the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative, thereby recognizing mentorship outcomes along with overall cleanliness and service delivery improvements. The intention of Jodi award is that the best performing cities should handhold cities with low scores to improve their performance. The initiative started after 2024-25 award ceremony with the motive of Each One - Teach One and rooted in India’s timeless Guru–Shishya tradition, where knowledge, experience, and best practices are passed on from one city to another to collectively advance the journey towards urban excellence and cleanliness.

 

Maharashtra’s Navi Mumbai, Gujarat’s Surat and Andhra Pradesh’s Vijayawada emerged as top 3 Clean Cities of Super Swachh League.

Marking the rise of a new generation of clean cities, GVMC Visakhapatnam, Jabalpur and Lucknow emerged as India’s top Swachh Shehar in the million plus population category.

Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025-26 expanded its coverage to include the Hills and Himalayan cities as well as River front and coastal towns. Rudrapur in Uttarakhand, Jammu & Shopian in J&K have been declared as the top 3 Clean Himalayan Cities. Riverfronts, coastlines and water bodies, are an integral part of the natural and cultural heritage. Their cleanliness is essential not only for environmental sustainability but also for the health and livelihoods of communities. In line with the same, the top 3 ranks for the Swachh River Front Town have been bestowed upon Rewa (MP), Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) & Varanasi (UP) consecutively, while awards for Swachh Coastal Town went to Odisha’s Puri, Kerala’s Alappuzha and Maharashtra’s Ratnagiri.

To recognize and reward excellence across States and Union Territories, the State First Swachh City Award was conferred on 30 top-performing cities. Union Territories have been classified into two categories for awards: (i) Up to 5 ULBs and (ii) more than 5 ULBs.

As part of the 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) were assessed across 43 indicators covering 10 critical domains, including Segregation, Collection & Transportation of Waste, Solid Waste Management, Visible Cleanliness, Access to Sanitation, Mechanisation of Desludging Services, Ecosystem Strengthening & Institutional Parameters, Used Water Management, Advocacy for Swachhata, Overall Welfare of Sanitation Workers, Citizen Feedback & Grievance Redressal. Over 3,000 trained assessors undertook extensive on-ground evaluations nationwide, supported by real-time GPS-enabled monitoring. From evidence submission to verification, the entire assessment process was conducted through a fully digital, transparent, and rigorously quality-assured framework, ensuring credibility and consistency at every stage.

2335194.title: Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales Cross Rs 73.49 Lakh, Reflecting Growing Public Appreciation for Artisans' Products
2335194.body_html:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat Records Cumulative Sales Cross Rs 73.49 Lakh, Reflecting Growing Public Appreciation for Artisans' Products
Mela Draws Enthusiastic Public Participation, Celebrates India's Cultural Diversity
More Than 130 Stalls Showcase Traditional Handicrafts, Handloom Products and Indigenous Creations Across Seven Thematic Zones
Daily Cultural Performances, Traditional Music and Folk Dances Create a Vibrant Festive Atmosphere
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi

The ongoing Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA, in the National Capital, is witnessing enthusiastic participation from citizens, families and young visitors, offering a vibrant celebration of India's traditional craftsmanship, cultural heritage and artistic diversity. The growing public interest is also reflected in the sales recorded during the Mela.

 

A Senior Official in Ministry said the four participating National Corporations under the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment, have recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹ 73.49  Lakh between November 1 and November 10, 2026. The sales reflect the encouraging response from visitors and the increasing market opportunities for products created by beneficiary communities.

The four participating corporations include National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC) and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation (NDFDC), he said.

Organised by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, the 15-day Mela has emerged as an engaging platform where visitors explore indigenous products, experience regional art forms and connect with the country's rich cultural traditions.

Organised around the theme ‘प्रकाश और परंपरा – ज्योति से ज्योति जलाएँ’, the Mela brings together traditional craftsmanship and cultural heritage through seven thematic zones: कला आँगन, प्रकाश चौक, पूजा पथ, सजावट बाज़ार, घराना, स्वाद चौक and मंच. Each zone offers visitors a distinctive experience, covering traditional crafts, festive decorations, home décor, cultural products and regional culinary traditions.

The Official said the Mela features more than 130 stalls showcasing a diverse range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, lamps, festive decorations, home décor items and other indigenous creations.

 

The visitors are enthusiastically exploring the stalls, appreciating the craftsmanship of participating artisans and purchasing products that reflect India's rich artistic traditions, he added.

A major attraction of the Mela is its lively cultural programme organised every evening at the Manch.

Artists and performing troupes from different States are presenting colourful folk dances, traditional music and regional art forms, bringing together diverse cultural expressions on a common platform.

These performances offer visitors an opportunity to experience India's cultural richness and regional traditions while creating a festive atmosphere of celebration and cultural exchange.

The cultural evenings have added a distinctive dimension to the Mela, making it more than an exhibition and shopping destination.

Visitors are enjoying the performances, discovering different regional traditions and experiencing the artistic diversity that reflects India's pluralistic cultural identity.

The Mela provides a valuable marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase their products and connect directly with consumers.

The Ministry facilitates their participation by providing free stalls, travel expenses, daily allowances and transportation facilities for their goods, helping them overcome logistical and financial barriers.

The initiative also promotes wider market access through platforms such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce opportunities, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while encouraging inclusion and equal opportunities.

Since 2022, the Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas, benefiting more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamchari communities by providing opportunities to exhibit and market their products. The initiative aims to encourage self-employment, strengthen entrepreneurship and promote socio-economic empowerment through sustainable livelihood opportunities.

The Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 will continue at Dilli Haat, INA, New Delhi, until November 15, 2026.

Through its combination of traditional products, cultural performances and public participation, the Mela offers a meaningful platform for celebrating India's artistic diversity while advancing the vision of an inclusive and self-reliant India.

2335193.title: INDIAN NAVY AND ROYAL NAVY OF OMAN CONDUCT 15TH EDITION OF BILATERAL MARITIME EXERCISE NASEEM AL BAHR (SEA BREEZE)
2335193.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVY AND ROYAL NAVY OF OMAN CONDUCT 15TH EDITION OF BILATERAL MARITIME EXERCISE NASEEM AL BAHR (SEA BREEZE)
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:57PM by PIB Delhi

The Indian Navy and the Royal Navy of Oman conducted the 15th edition of their bilateral maritime exercise, Naseem Al Bahr (Sea Breeze), aimed at enhancing interoperability, strengthening professional cooperation and promoting mutual understanding between the two navies.

During the harbour phase, Subject Matter Expert Exchanges (SMEE) were conducted between specialist teams of the two navies. The exchanges covered key areas of mutual interest, including Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD), Mine Countermeasure Operations and Hydrography. These interactions facilitated the exchange of professional knowledge and operational experience in specialised maritime domains.

The sea phase featured joint operational activities between Indian Naval Ship Surat and Royal Navy of Oman Vessel Al-Mu’azzar. These included joint Visit, Board, Search and Seizure (VBSS) drills and cross-deck operations, providing opportunities for personnel of both navies to practise coordinated procedures and enhance operational interoperability.

Exercise Naseem Al Bahr (Sea Breeze) reflects the close maritime partnership between India and Oman and the shared commitment of the two navies to strengthening maritime cooperation. The exercise also reinforces the Indian Navy’s engagement with regional maritime partners in furtherance of the Government of India's vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).

2335192.title: INDIAN NAVAL SHIP TRISHUL CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT SAFAGA, EGYPT
2335192.body_html:
Ministry of Defence
INDIAN NAVAL SHIP TRISHUL CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT SAFAGA, EGYPT
Posted On: 11 NOV 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Naval Ship (INS) Trishul concluded her port call at Safaga Naval Base, Egypt, on 09 Nov 2026, as part of her ongoing operational deployment.

The port call further reinforced the growing India–Egypt defence and maritime partnership , in the backdrop of the 11th India–Egypt Joint Defence Committee (JDC) meeting held in Cairo in Apr 2026 (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2254773). The 11th JDC meeting provided an institutional framework for advancing defence commitments under the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Defence Cooperation signed in Sep 2022, following the elevation of bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership in 2023.

During the visit, the Commanding Officer of INS Trishul called on RAdm MD Abd El Maksoud, Commander, Red Sea Naval Base, Egypt. Discussions covered maritime security in the Gulf of Suez and the strategic significance of the Red Sea. The ship's crew also visited Egyptian Naval Ship ENS Port Said (976), gaining insights into its operational capabilities and the best practices followed by the Egyptian Navy.

The visit further featured reciprocal interactions between personnel of the Indian and Egyptian navies, along with joint diving training activities. These professional engagements provided opportunities for exchange of operational experience, sharing of Best Practices and furthering mutual understanding between the two navies.

The port call reaffirmed the longstanding defence ties between India and Egypt and their shared commitment to maritime security and regional stability. Following completion of the engagements, INS Trishul proceeded for the next phase of her operational deployment.
